summary: Creates a voluntary grant program to help public high schools without computer science courses offer them, funded by donors, with reporting requirements.

title: California Safe Homes grant program.
summary: Creates a Department of Insurance wildfire home-retrofit grant program funded through a new Sustainable Insurance Account, with performance reporting starting in 2027.

title: Prevailing wage: per diem wages.
summary: Tightens prevailing wage credit rules by ending annualization exceptions and requiring employers to prove calculations, while allowing full credit for certain defined contribution pension contributions.

title: Interscholastic sports: gender equity.
summary: Requires the California Interscholastic Federation to bar students assigned male at birth from participating on girls' sports teams.

title: Nonminor dependents: county of residence.
summary: Allows a nonminor dependent to request transfer of juvenile court jurisdiction to a new county where they live, with court timelines and review-hearing consideration.

title: Transportation: Quick-Build Pilot Program.
summary: Creates a Quick-Build Pilot Program to speed low-cost state highway improvements, requiring Caltrans guidance by 2027 and funding at least six projects by 2028.

title: Captive wild animals: direct contact: prohibition.
summary: Prohibits allowing the public to have direct contact with covered captive wild animals, adds civil penalties, and allows permit suspension or revocation for violations.

title: Housing development projects: objective standards: campus development zone.
summary: Expands streamlined ministerial housing approval to mixed-income projects in campus development zones, limits local review to the disturbed construction area, and widens CEQA's ministerial exemption.

title: General acute care hospitals: patient directories.
summary: Requires general acute care hospitals to notify patients they can restrict patient directory disclosures of their health information, with written acknowledgment.

title: Personal Income Tax Law: Corporation Tax Law: credits: fast food restaurants.
summary: Creates a $12,000 per-restaurant tax credit for qualified fast food franchisees and independent operators for 2026 through 2030.

title: Foster care: placement transition planning.
summary: Requires counties to adopt placement transition planning policies for foster children and directs state guidance on best practices for successful transitions.

title: Trespassing: removal of trespassers on residential property.
summary: Creates a misdemeanor crime of unlawful squatting on property, requiring police citations and allowing removal and fines.

title: The Family Urgent Response System.
summary: Makes the statewide hotline the primary entry point for the foster family crisis response system, adds data collection and biennial county plan updates, and authorizes mobile response staff use.

title: Beverage containers: recycled glass: market development.
summary: Raises the cap on recycled-glass market development payments to $150 per ton and authorizes $20 million annually from 2028 to 2030.

title: Budget Act of 2024.
summary: Budget trailer bill declaring utility undergrounding plan approvals not a CEQA project, while still requiring environmental review before physical project approvals.

title: Public postsecondary education: overnight student parking.
summary: Requires community college districts to adopt overnight parking programs for eligible students, with basic needs coordinators and campus security involved and no-cost permits.

title: Environmental protection: 30x30 goals: land conservation: stewardship.
summary: Requires the Natural Resources Agency to develop stewardship strategies for conserved lands and add a stewardship section with recommendations to its 2027 30x30 progress report.

title: Veterans’ preferences: eligible spouses.
summary: Extends state civil service veterans' preferences to active duty members and eligible spouses of active duty members, veterans, and disabled veterans.

title: Transportation projects: barriers to wildlife movement.
summary: Requires lead agencies to include wildlife passage features in transportation projects in designated connectivity areas, with exemptions and mitigation credits allowed.

title: School accountability: local control and accountability plans: education technology: best practices: School Technology Empowerment Advisory Committee.
summary: Requires CDE to compile technology best practices and a model LCAP policy, plus surveys, webinars, and an advisory committee, without direct restrictions.

title: Carpet recycling.
summary: Revises California's carpet stewardship and producer responsibility programs, including penalties, governing board makeup, reporting, and the carpet definition.

title: State general obligation bonds: disclosure requirements.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Requires state general obligation bond acts approved from 2026 onward to include expenditure objectives, public notices, and agency reports on bond projects.

title: Planning and zoning: housing elements: affirmatively furthering fair housing.
summary: Removes a housing element sites analysis requirement and requires local programs to distribute housing sites to affirmatively further fair housing, with rezoning.

title: State Air Resources Board: board members: compensation.
summary: Gives air district members on the Air Resources Board the same annual salary as other members and ends the $100 daily payments to elected members.

title: Instructional materials: compliance review.
summary: Requires the State Department of Education to monitor school districts' compliance with diverse instructional materials and social sciences instruction requirements.

title: Financial abuse of an elder or dependent adult: fraudulent transactions: liability.
summary: Limits elder fraud victims' liability to $50, requires banks to investigate fraud claims, and raises elder financial abuse reporting penalties.

title: State and local agencies: demographic data.
summary: Requires state and local agencies collecting ancestry data to separately tabulate and publish Middle Eastern and North African group data starting in 2029.

title: Criminal procedure: sentencing.
summary: Expands vacatur relief and the coercion defense to nearly all offenses except murder, and requires broader record sealing by law enforcement and corrections agencies.

title: Emergency telecommunications medium- and heavy-duty zero-emission vehicles.
summary: Exempts emergency telecommunications vehicles used for 911, Emergency Alert System, and outage connectivity from Advanced Clean Fleets zero-emission requirements.

title: Vallejo Flood and Wastewater District: trustees.
summary: Revises the membership and size of the Vallejo Flood and Wastewater District board, changes trustee pay, and extends appointment list rules to public members.

title: Housing programs: financing.
summary: Lets the housing department transfer excess reserves between same-owner rental developments and waive certain loan payments.

title: Air pollution: indirect sources.
summary: Requires the state air board to adopt and enforce indirect source pollution rules, funded by fees on facilities and mobile sources.

title: Dam safety: state supervision: exceptions.
summary: Exempts certain water storage facilities tied to a Kern County compressed-air energy storage project from state dam safety supervision.

title: Safer Soap Act.
summary: Bans benzalkonium chloride and other listed ingredients in consumer body wash and hand soap from 2028, with registration and penalties.

title: County offices of education: school districts: average daily attendance of less than 250 pupils: permanent status.
summary: Extends automatic permanent employee status for certificated staff to all school districts and county offices, regardless of attendance size.

title: Personal Income Tax Law: exclusions: first responders.
summary: Excludes from state income tax wages earned by local first responders providing mutual aid outside their jurisdiction, for 2025-2029 tax years.

title: Confidentiality of voter information: cognitively impaired individuals.
summary: Lets people with power of attorney apply for confidential voter status for cognitively impaired individuals, with exclusions from voter lists and an annual report.

title: Patient visitation.
summary: Requires health facilities to allow specified family visitors and limits facility visitor bans, including in end-of-life situations, with PPE requirements for visitors.

title: Permit Streamlining Act: housing development projects: centralized application portal.
summary: Requires cities and counties over 150,000 residents to offer an online portal for housing permit applications that tracks application status.

title: Generators: air pollution regulations: sales and use taxes: exemptions.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Exempts backup generators from air emissions rules during loss-of-power emergencies, and creates sales tax exemption and income tax credit for generator purchases.

title: University of California: employees, volunteers, and contractors: background checks.
summary: Lets the University of California require Department of Justice background checks for staff, contractors and volunteers, and adds rules for terminating and verifying arrest notifications.

title: Detention and incarceration of pregnant and postpartum defendants.
summary: Creates a presumption against detaining pregnant or postpartum defendants, allows sentence stays, and requires county jails to provide pregnancy tests on request.

title: Leases: termination of tenancy: abuse or violence: security deposit.
summary: Requires landlords to refund a calculated security deposit share to a tenant who leaves due to another tenant's abuse, making remaining tenants jointly liable.

title: Mobilehome parks: emergency preparedness.
summary: Requires mobilehome park emergency preparedness plans and staff from 2027, and raises the per-lot inspection fee to $10 until 2030.

title: Juvenile court: visitation.
summary: Requires juvenile courts to order frequent, presumptively unsupervised parent-child visitation and contact within 72 hours, with social workers reporting on reunification barriers.

title: County superintendent of schools: inspection of public schools.
summary: Extends the textbook review deadline to the 8th week for listed schools and prioritizes early county visits to schools with textbook or facility safety problems.

title: Roosters: restrictions.
summary: Bans keeping more than 25 movement-constrained roosters from 2028, with civil penalties of up to $2,500 per violation.

title: Abandoned endowment care cemeteries: County of Marin.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Lets Marin County transfer the Mount Tamalpais cemetery to a nonprofit or authority, shielding successors from the prior owner's debts and liabilities.

title: Water resources: data centers.
topics: AI and technology; Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Requires data centers to estimate and report water use to their suppliers and self-certify this when applying for city or county business licenses.

title: Elections and voting procedures.
summary: Extends the deadline for mailed ballots to count as timely to 7 days after election day, and adds recount, voting-system security, and notice rules.

title: State Bar Act: consumer legal funding.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Labor and employment
summary: Defines consumer legal funding, sets contract requirements and penalties, and bans attorney fee-sharing with certain out-of-state nonlawyer-owned entities until 2030.

title: Community youth athletics programs: sex or gender discrimination.
summary: Extends sex and gender discrimination bans on community youth athletics and facilities to school districts, county offices of education, and charter schools.

title: Disability benefits: duration: postchildbirth.
summary: Requires disability benefits for pregnancy-related disability to cover at least 12 weeks following childbirth, and renames and expands organized camp regulation.

title: Community colleges: degrees and certificates: education plans.
summary: Requires community colleges to identify students near degree completion, award degrees retroactively, and give education plans to new and returning students.

title: State agencies: complaints: demographic data.
summary: Requires the Superintendent and Civil Rights Department to collect and publish demographic data on discrimination complaints, while keeping that data confidential.

title: CalFresh Fruit and Vegetable Supplemental Benefits Program.
summary: Renames the Fruit and Vegetable EBT Pilot Project as a permanent CalFresh supplemental benefits program, with funding allocation rules and quarterly utilization reporting.

title: The Cannella Environmental Farming Act of 1995: Organic Transition Program.
summary: Creates a state Organic Transition Program offering grants to help farmers and ranchers convert land to certified organic production.

title: Criminal procedure: sentencing.
summary: Expands post-conviction vacatur and record sealing to nearly all offenses except murder, and extends the coercion defense to violent felonies except murder.

title: Housing development: density bonuses: affordability of for-sale units.
summary: Allows density bonus developers to meet for-sale affordability rules by having a nonprofit buy units for low-income families in a below-market loan program.

title: Recall elections: successors.
summary: Prohibits a recalled local officer from being appointed to fill the vacancy and makes clarifying changes to statewide recall successor rules.

title: Economic development: industry strategies.
summary: Requires the Governor's economic development office to develop industry strategies for Jobs First strategic sectors, including quantum technology, by July 2026.

title: California Environmental Quality Act: electrical infrastructure projects.
summary: Sets a 270-day deadline and expedited review for priority electrical infrastructure projects' CEQA environmental reports at the Public Utilities Commission.

title: Electricity: climate credits.
summary: Excludes low-bill residential customers not enrolled in CARE or FERA from receiving the California Climate Credit.

title: Insurance agents: prelicensing education.
summary: Eliminates the 20-hour prelicensing study requirement for insurance agent license applicants and adds a fee for the 12-hour ethics course certification.

title: State government: emergency services: nonprofit service providers.
summary: Lets nonprofits under state contracts modify service methods and seek funding flexibility during emergencies, with notice and documentation requirements.

title: Density Bonus Law: incentives and concessions: green housing developments.
summary: Requires cities and counties to grant extra density bonus incentives for green housing developments and bars them from requiring parking.

title: Natural resources: equitable outdoor access: 30x30 goal: urban nature-based projects.
summary: Directs state agencies and the Legislature to prioritize 30x30 and Outdoors for All goals, maximizing investment in historically underserved urban communities when distributing resources.

title: Agriculture: Cannella Environmental Farming Act of 1995.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Renames and expands California's environmental farming program into a sustainable agriculture program with research, technical assistance, and incentive grants, and expands its advisory panel.

title: School facilities: task-order procurement contracting.
summary: Extends task-order procurement to small school districts and county offices, requiring skilled-workforce commitments and project labor agreements for large projects.

title: Small Business Retail Theft Solutions Grant Program.
summary: Creates a grant program in the Office of the Small Business Advocate to help small businesses prevent and recover from retail theft, subject to appropriation.

title: California Education Interagency Council.
summary: Creates a subject-to-appropriation education interagency council and office within the Government Operations Agency to coordinate education and workforce policy and report recommendations.

title: Political Reform Act of 1974: advertisements.
summary: Creates the Billboard DISCLOSE Act, letting campaign ads shorten committee and contributor names and shortening independent-expenditure disclaimers.

title: Health care coverage: behavioral diagnoses.
summary: Bars insurers from requiring rediagnosis of autism or pervasive developmental disorder to keep behavioral health treatment coverage.

title: Youth Offender Program Camp Pilot Program.
summary: Makes the Youth Offender Program Camp Pilot Program permanent and lets the secretary expand it to some or all conservation camps.

title: Political Reform Act of 1974: contributions and expenditures by foreign nationals.
summary: Extends bans on foreign government and foreign principal election contributions and spending to foreign nationals, excluding LPRs and certain DACA recipients.

title: Interregional transportation strategic plan: bicycle highways.
summary: Creates a pilot program for numbered bicycle highway networks in two major metro areas, programmed through the state transportation improvement program.

title: Mexican prepaid health plans.
summary: Expands licensed Mexican prepaid health plans' group coverage to all legal workers in San Diego and Imperial counties and raises their net equity requirement to $2.3 million.

title: Accessory dwelling units and junior accessory dwelling units.
summary: Requires local approval of two detached new-construction accessory dwelling units on single-family lots and extends the bar on restrictive covenants to lots zoned for single-family use.

title: Cigarette and tobacco products: retail sale: pharmacies.
summary: Prohibits pharmacies from selling cigarettes or tobacco products and bars tobacco retail licenses for retailers containing pharmacies.

title: Trustees of the California State University: gubernatorial and faculty appointees.
summary: Expands the CSU Board of Trustees from 25 to 27 members, adding a Governor-appointed member and a faculty member chosen from Academic Senate lists.

title: Teacher credentialing: administrative services credential: internship program.
summary: Limits administrative services credential internship programs to those run by school districts, county offices of education, or regionally accredited colleges, and requires a later review of internship requirements.

title: Mental health services: peer support specialist certification.
summary: Removes the high school diploma or equivalent requirement for peer support specialist certification.

title: Patient visitation.
summary: Requires general acute care hospitals to let disabled and cognitively impaired patients have a family or friend caregiver present, including outside visiting hours.

title: Hazardous materials: California Land Reuse and Revitalization Act of 2004.
summary: Extends the California Land Reuse and Revitalization Act's liability immunity for innocent landowners and purchasers from 2027 to January 1, 2037.

title: Pupil safety: comprehensive school safety plans: use of smartphones.
summary: Allows schools to prohibit pupil smartphone use during emergencies or threats if the school safety plan explicitly addresses that circumstance.

title: Public works: prevailing wages: access to records.
summary: Requires owners and developers on prevailing-wage work to provide payroll records on request, with penalties for noncompliance.

title: Commission on State Mandates: state mandates.
summary: Requires the Controller to notify claimants in writing within 30 days of audit or review adjustments and lets local agencies offset reduced reimbursements or remit funds.

title: Vehicles: electric bicycles.
summary: Bans selling class 3 electric bicycles to anyone under 16, with a violation punishable as a fine-only infraction up to $250.

title: Dental Practice Act: foreign dental schools.
summary: Extends approval of foreign dental schools pending CODA accreditation and requires graduates to serve in specified practice settings for two years.

title: Physicians and surgeons: licensure: expedite fee.
summary: Requires the Medical Board of California to expedite physician licensure for applicants who pay an expedite fee capped at $250, and repeals these provisions in 2030.

title: Contraceptives.
summary: Expands contraceptive access by letting pharmacists furnish nonhormonal and over-the-counter contraceptives and applying 12-month supply rules to all contraceptives.

title: CalWORKs: family violence option and gender-based violence information.
summary: Requires counties to waive CalWORKs program requirements for domestic abuse victims and creates standardized abuse-information materials and waiver forms.

title: Personal Income Tax Law: Corporation Tax Law: Bobcat Fire: exclusions.
summary: Excludes from state personal and corporate income tax settlement payments for costs and losses from the 2020 Bobcat Fire, for tax years 2024 through 2028.

title: Child abuse and neglect reporting.
topics: Children and families; Government and administration
summary: Creates a two-year Los Angeles County pilot where mandated reporters using a training and decision-support tool are deemed to comply with reporting duties.

title: State Property: San Pasqual Battlefield State Park.
summary: Requires the state to quitclaim about 3.68 acres of San Pasqual Battlefield State Park land to the San Pasqual Band at no cost.

title: Postsecondary education: discrimination: sex.
summary: Adds sex to the list of protected characteristics against discrimination in postsecondary education programs receiving state financial assistance.

title: Recycling: plastic trash bags: plastic packaging and products.
summary: Repeals the existing rigid plastic packaging program and replaces it with registration, recycled-content minimums, and penalties for manufacturers of covered plastic products.

title: Medi-Cal managed care plans: enrollees with other health care coverage.
summary: Lets Medi-Cal fee-for-service providers bill managed care plans for enrollees with other coverage without in-network contracts, with limited plan safeguards and reporting.

title: Lake and streambed alteration agreements: exemptions: culverts and bridges.
summary: Exempts certain small bridge and culvert repairs in Sutter County from streambed alteration permit rules until 2027 after disaster damage.

title: Personal Income Tax Law: Corporation Tax Law: California Retail Security Tax Credit.
summary: Creates a 2026-2027 tax credit for small disadvantaged-community retailers' theft prevention expenses, capped at $10 million annually.

title: California Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act of 2001: California State University: burial sites: human remains.
summary: Requires the California State University to develop a policy for reburying repatriated Native American remains on university-owned land, in consultation with tribes.

title: Department of Transportation and local agencies: streets and highways: recycled materials.
summary: Requires local street standards to keep allowing recycled materials and removes the requirement to use low-greenhouse-gas road materials and methods.

title: California Cybersecurity Integration Center: artificial intelligence.
topics: AI and technology; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Requires the state cybersecurity center to create an AI cybersecurity collaboration playbook by 2027 and makes information shared under it confidential.

title: State property: City of Moreno Valley.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Requires the state to transfer 11 undeveloped open-space parcels in Moreno Valley to the city at no cost for wildfire mitigation and recreation.

title: Health care: medically necessary treatment.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Requires health plans and insurers to cover medically necessary physical-condition treatment on par with other conditions, with utilization review standards and penalties.

title: Vehicles: active intelligent speed assist devices.
summary: Creates a pilot program until 2033 in five counties requiring speed-limiting devices for drivers convicted of speeding, reckless, or exhibition offenses.

title: Mining: The Surface Mining and Reclamation Act of 1975: mining operations status: idle reserve mine status.
summary: Lets idle aggregate mines seek 'Idle Reserve Mine Status' with longer interim plan renewals, exempts that approval from CEQA, and expands mine inspections and reporting.

title: Vehicles: removal and impoundment.
summary: Adds driving over 100 mph to the offenses for which police may impound a vehicle under a magistrate's warrant or order.

title: Personal income taxes: deductions: CalABLE contributions.
summary: Allows a California personal income tax deduction for contributions to CalABLE accounts for taxable years 2026 through 2030.

title: Chiquita Canyon Landfill: property tax reassessment and penalties.
summary: Requires reassessing property near the Chiquita Canyon Landfill to reflect value declines, and suspends tax installment defaults and delinquency there until 2030.

title: State of emergency and local emergency: landslides and climate change.
summary: Adds landslides to the conditions that can qualify as a state of emergency or local emergency under the Emergency Services Act.

title: Vehicles: storage and towing.
summary: Expands the list of presumptively unreasonable towing and storage fees, including holiday storage charges and tow fees during emergency removals.

title: Pupil instruction: statewide dual enrollment framework: advisory board.
summary: Creates a dual enrollment advisory board and requires a statewide dual enrollment framework and best-practices guide by January 2027.

title: State holidays: Native American Day.
summary: Makes Native American Day, the 4th Friday in September, a paid holiday for state employees.

title: Electrical corporations: rates.
summary: Bans electric utilities from proposing systemwide rate increases above inflation, except when the PUC finds costs tied to safety, modernization, or fuel costs.

title: Public water systems: emergency notification plan.
summary: Authorizes and encourages public water systems to notify users in their preferred language when updating emergency notification plans, if resources are available.

title: Sentencing: dismissal of enhancements.
summary: Exempts firearm-related sentence enhancements from the mandatory dismissal rule, leaving courts only general discretionary authority to dismiss them.

title: Peace officers.
summary: Requires most peace officers to earn a college degree within 36 months of basic certification starting in 2031, while repealing a POST education-criteria approval requirement.

title: Hazardous materials management: Rural CUPA Reimbursement Account.
summary: Makes all counties under 150,000 population eligible for Rural CUPA reimbursement funds, regardless of certification date, if the Legislature appropriates money.

title: County jails.
summary: Lets state prisoners facing new charges petition to serve pretrial confinement at their current state prison instead of county jail.

title: Department of Justice: phone scams.
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to create and maintain an online database of known phone scams with a reporting tool, and report on it annually until 2033.

title: Public Resources: sea level rise plans.
summary: Lets coastal commissions accept existing local sea level rise plans as meeting required content and encourages voluntary early consultation.

title: Child health and safety: “Have a Heart, Be a Star, Help Our Kids” license plate program.
summary: Raises fees on Have a Heart license plates and directs the revenue to childcare licensing, training, safety, and child abuse prevention programs.

title: Household hazardous waste: vape pens.
summary: Allows household hazardous waste facilities to disassemble vape pens, bars public materials exchanges from accepting them, and has DTSC study confiscated vape pen disposal.

title: Skydiving or sport parachuting operations.
summary: Makes a nonsubstantive wording change to existing skydiving operator duties regarding federal parachute safety and certification compliance.

title: Stop Politicians from Violating Our Constitutional Rights Act of 2025.
summary: Reduces pay for legislators and governors whose voted-for or signed laws are later struck down as unconstitutional by federal courts.

title: Parole.
summary: Repeals constitutional provisions giving nonviolent felons parole eligibility and giving prisoners credits for good behavior and rehabilitation.

title: California Water Resiliency Act.
summary: Constitutional amendment requiring an annual transfer of 1% of General Fund revenues to a fund for water infrastructure projects.

title: Road usage charges: vote and voter approval requirements.
summary: Constitutional amendment requiring two-thirds legislative and voter approval for road usage charges, which must be uniform and used only for transportation.

title: Public finance: Balanced Budget Accountability Act of 2025.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Requires two-thirds votes for General Fund appropriations and fee increases, caps state employment costs, and mandates competitive bidding of state programs.

title: Taxes and fees: voter thresholds.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget

title: California Physical Fitness and Mental Well-Being Month.
summary: Declares May 2025 as California Physical Fitness and Mental Well-Being Month.

title: Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day.
summary: Commemorates Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. and Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day through a ceremonial resolution.

title: Suicide Prevention Awareness Month.
summary: Proclaims September 2025 as Suicide Prevention Awareness Month. It has no operative effect beyond recognition.

title: Little Saigon Freeway.
summary: Designates a portion of State Route 101 in Santa Clara County as the Little Saigon Freeway and requests signage.

title: Melanoma Awareness Month.
summary: Proclaims May 2025 as Melanoma Awareness Month and encourages statewide awareness activities.

title: Italian American Heritage Month.
summary: Proclaims October 2025 as Italian American Heritage Month and encourages Californians to observe it with ceremonies and programs.

title: Motorcycle Safety Awareness Month in California.
summary: Designates May 2025 as Motorcycle Safety Awareness Month in California.

title: California’s Farm Week.
summary: Designates May 11 to May 17, 2025, as California's Farm Week.

title: California Small Business Month.
summary: Declares May as California Small Business Month.

title: Drowning Awareness and Prevention Month.
summary: Proclaims May 2025 as Drowning Awareness and Prevention Month in California and honors Nadina Riggsbee on her retirement.

title: Maternal Mental Health Awareness Month.
summary: Proclaims May 2025 as Maternal Mental Health Awareness Month.

title: Equestrian Heritage Day.
summary: Proclaims July 15, 2025, and every July 15 after that as Equestrian Heritage Day.

title: Desert ecosystems.
summary: Recognizes the second Saturday of January each year as World Desert Day in California and encourages local desert conservation events.

title: Elder and Dependent Adult Abuse Awareness Month.
summary: Proclaims June 2025 as Elder and Dependent Adult Abuse Awareness Month in California.

title: Border Patrol Agent Daniel H. Salazar Memorial Highway.
summary: Designates a portion of State Route 94 in San Diego County as the Border Patrol Agent Daniel H. Salazar Memorial Highway.

title: Foster Care Month.
summary: Declares May 2025 as Foster Care Month in California.

title: California Maritime Day.
summary: Proclaims May 22, 2025, as California Maritime Day in the State of California.

title: Lyme Disease Awareness Month.
summary: Proclaims May 2025 as Lyme Disease Awareness Month in California.

title: 529 College Savings Day.
summary: Proclaims May 29, 2025, as 529 College Savings Day.

title: National Stuttering Acceptance Awareness Week.
summary: Proclaims May 9-15, 2025 as National Stuttering Acceptance Awareness Week in California.

title: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Awareness Month.
summary: Proclaims May 2025 as Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Awareness Month in California.

title: Men’s Mental Health Month.
summary: Proclaims June 2025 as Men's Mental Health Month through a ceremonial resolution.

title: Military Appreciation Month.
summary: Recognizes May 2025 as Military Appreciation Month and honors current and former service members.

title: National Human Trafficking Awareness Month.
summary: Recognizes January 2025 as National Human Trafficking Awareness Month through a commemorative resolution.

title: Juneteenth.
summary: Recognizes June 19, 2025, as Juneteenth and urges Californians to celebrate it. The resolution has no legal effect.

title: Portuguese Heritage Month: Day of Portugal: Day of the Azores.
summary: Declares June 2025 Portuguese Heritage Month and recognizes June 10 as Day of Portugal and June 9 as Day of the Azores.

title: Electronic Dance Music Month.
summary: Declares June 2025 as Electronic Dance Music Month through a ceremonial resolution.

title: Aromatic L-Amino Acid Decarboxylase Deficiency Awareness Day.
summary: Designates October 23, 2025, as Aromatic L-Amino Acid Decarboxylase Deficiency Awareness Day.

title: Antimicrobial resistance.
summary: Resolution recognizing antimicrobial resistance as a public health crisis and urging agencies to explore research funding.

title: The 2025 International Day of Yoga.
summary: Recognizes June 21, 2025, as the 2025 International Day of Yoga in California.

title: Assembly Member Patty Berg Memorial Highway.
summary: Designates a portion of State Route 101 in Humboldt County as the Assembly Member Patty Berg Memorial Highway.

title: Charlie Barra Memorial Bridge.
summary: Designates the Russian River Bridge on State Route 20 in Mendocino County as the Charlie Barra Memorial Bridge.

title: Law enforcement: immigration actions.
summary: Non-binding resolution urging an immediate end to state policies that obstruct lawful immigration enforcement and urging the Governor to restore law and order.

title: Scleroderma Awareness Day.
summary: Declares June 29, 2025, as Scleroderma Awareness Day in California.

title: Sudan conflict.
summary: Declares the conflict in Sudan an international crisis and urges greater action and aid for its people.

title: United States Forest Service: federal funding.
summary: Urges the President to veto bills defunding the U.S. Forest Service and to work with Congress to protect wildfire and forest management programs.

title: Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities program: federal funding cuts.
summary: Urges Congress and the President to immediately restore full federal funding for Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities projects.

title: Head Start program.
summary: Recognizes May 2025 as Head Start Month and urges Congress and the President to protect and increase Head Start funding.

title: Cuts to safety net programs.
summary: Resolution censuring California U.S. House members who support cuts to social safety net programs.

title: California ports: tariffs.
summary: Urges federal agencies to weigh tariff impacts on California ports and pursue strategies to stabilize trade and port competitiveness.

title: The Major Richard Star Act.
summary: Urges Congress to pass the Major Richard Star Act so disabled veterans receive full military retirement pay and VA disability compensation.

title: Tijuana River: transboundary flow pollution.
summary: Urges Congress and the President to fully fund EPA's Tijuana River infrastructure solution and take further actions on transboundary pollution.

title: The Renewing Immigration Provisions of the Immigration Act of 1929.
summary: Joint resolution expressing support for renewing the immigration provisions of the Immigration Act of 1929; no direct policy change.

title: Recognition of the historical wrongdoing committed against California Native Americans.
summary: Recognizes historical wrongdoing against California Native Americans and urges the federal government to work with tribal leaders on related injustices.

title: United States Department of Education: proposed closure.
summary: Urges Congress and the President to reject dismantling the federal Department of Education and preserve its core functions.

title: Location of missing immigrant children.
summary: Nonbinding resolution urging federal officials to locate missing immigrant children who crossed the southern border and address the crisis.

title: Records: Jeffrey Epstein.
summary: Urges federal agencies to release all Jeffrey Epstein-related records and to investigate and prosecute those named.

title: Redistricting: independent redistricting commissions.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Urges Congress to propose a constitutional amendment requiring all states to adopt independent redistricting commissions.

title: Federal Infrastructure Bank.
summary: Urges Congress to pass H.R. 1235 to establish a federal infrastructure bank to finance urgently needed infrastructure projects.

title: New state formation.
summary: Expresses Legislature consent for specified counties to form a new state within California and urges Congress to accept it.

title: Health care coverage: enhanced premium tax credits: health savings accounts.
summary: Urges Congress to reauthorize enhanced ACA premium tax credits and continue exploring bolstering health savings accounts.

title: Health care coverage: enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits.
summary: Urges Congress and the President to restore and extend enhanced ACA premium tax credits.

title: Secretary of the United States Department of Homeland Security Kristi Noem.
summary: Urges Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem to resign and urges Congress to impeach her if she does not.

title: Federal disaster aid: 2025 Los Angeles fires.
summary: Urges the President and Congress to approve federal disaster aid and supplemental funding for Los Angeles County wildfire recovery.

title: The United States Department of Homeland Security: funding.
summary: Urges the U.S. Senate, especially Democrats, to immediately pass the House-approved Department of Homeland Security funding bill.

title: Voting by mail.
summary: A resolution opposing federal actions that restrict California's vote-by-mail system and urging Congress to reject limits on mail voting.

title: Public social services: Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid.
summary: Urges Congress to repeal federal budget act provisions harming Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid, and oppose privatization.

title: Ending gun violence in the United States.
summary: A resolution commending President Trump's gun violence comments and urging Congress to support legislation and constitutional amendments to end gun violence.

title: Restoration of the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Urges Congress to restore and strengthen Voting Rights Act protections and calls on the President to sign such legislation.

title: 9/11 Remembrance Flag.
summary: Encourages public buildings to display the 9/11 Remembrance Flag each September 11 and allows officials to accept flag donations.

title: Intellectual property enforcement: Priority Foreign Countries.
summary: Urges Congress and the President to temporarily halt enforcement of copyright claims from claimants in Priority Foreign Countries.

title: Public lands.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Non-binding resolution supporting federal stewardship of public lands and opposing efforts that reduce public access, voice, or recourse.

title: Environmental investigations: pediatric cancer clusters.
summary: Urges federal and state agencies to research environmental causes of Ewing Sarcoma and chemical exposures in south Orange County, and to share epidemiological data.

title: Medi-Cal program: audit.
summary: Resolution urging the federal CMS to audit California's Medi-Cal program to restore its fiscal health.

title: Birthright citizenship.
summary: Resolution opposing federal Executive Order 14160 on birthright citizenship and affirming the Legislature's commitment to it.

title: Child nutrition: federal programs: funding cuts.
summary: Urges Congress to keep funding the federal Local Food for Schools and Child Care program and support family farmers supplying school meals.

title: Special education funding: protection.
summary: Urges Congress and the President to oppose special education funding cuts and keep services for students with disabilities uninterrupted.

title: Immigration: Temporary Protected Status.
summary: Urges Congress to create a path to permanent residency for Temporary Protected Status holders and condemns federal TPS terminations; also opposes Social Security cuts.

title: National parks: federal funding.
summary: Urges Congress and the President to restore full, consistent funding and staffing for the National Park Service.

title: Governor’s reorganization plan: reorganization of executive branch of state government.
summary: Governor's plan splits the Business, Consumer Services, and Housing Agency into two agencies and creates a housing finance committee, effective July 1, 2026.

title: Budget Act of 2024.
summary: Amends the 2024-25 Budget Act by changing existing appropriations and takes effect immediately as a Budget Bill.

title: Climate change: plans: gender impacts.
summary: Requires a state gender-impact assessment of extreme heat and allows SANDAG toll revenues to fund Tijuana River sanitation projects.

title: Budget Acts of 2023 and 2024.
summary: Amends the 2023 and 2024 Budget Acts by changing appropriations, takes effect immediately as a Budget Bill, and states legislative intent on 2025 statutory changes.

title: California AI Transparency Act.
topics: AI and technology; Consumer protection and business
summary: Revises California AI Transparency Act provenance rules, adds latent disclosure of AI creation, delays assistive-tech systems, and bans false assistive-technology claims.

title: Local agency, public utility, or mutual water company: personnel access: Personal Identity Verification-Interoperable.
summary: Starting 2028, OES must issue PIV-I credentials so utility and water-agency personnel can enter disaster areas closed to the public.

title: Out-of-state physicians and surgeons: telehealth: license exemption.
summary: Expands out-of-state physician telehealth exemption to cover eligible patients whose life-threatening conditions are in remission.

title: Prohousing enhanced infrastructure financing districts.
summary: Creates a state infrastructure financing program for prohousing cities and counties' enhanced infrastructure financing districts, with loans or grants for housing developments.

title: Law enforcement: masks.
summary: Extends California's mask ban to state peace officers, narrows mask exclusions, and adds liability for masked false arrest or imprisonment.

title: Local agency: payment: rounding amount.
summary: Lets local agencies that adopt a resolution round cash payments and refunds to the nearest five cents.

title: Student financial aid: Cal Grant B access costs award.
summary: Requires the Cal Grant B access costs award to be at least the 2025-26 maximum amount starting in 2027-28, indexed annually to CPI.

title: Common interest developments: annual reports: assessments: discipline.
summary: Requires HOA budget comparisons and management compensation disclosure, caps regular assessment increases at 8% without member approval, and requires evidence access before fines.

title: California Environmental Quality Act: exemption: railroad grade crossing closure.
summary: Exempts from CEQA review the Public Utilities Commission-ordered closure of railroad grade crossings that pose public safety threats.

title: Juveniles: detention.
summary: Limits juvenile hall detention and commitment unless less restrictive alternatives are unsuitable, and requires court review of removals from parental custody.

title: Budget Act of 2025.
summary: Enacts the 2025-26 Budget Act, making general appropriations for state government support and taking effect immediately.

title: Hazardous waste: major appliances: recycling.
summary: Tightens hazardous waste rules for major appliance recyclers, requiring stricter certification, CUPA facility inspections, scrap facility documentation, and recordkeeping.

title: Energy: Utility Infrastructure AI Safety, Oversight, and Workforce Protection Act.
topics: AI and technology; Environment and energy
summary: Requires the PUC to set standards for utilities' AI use, allows prohibiting harmful AI, and requires local utilities to adopt consistent policies.

title: Employment of inmates.
summary: Requires facilitating released conservation camp graduates' entry into construction craft laborer apprenticeships and certifying their eligibility.

title: Automated license plate recognition systems.
topics: AI and technology; Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Restricts how police and public agencies use, share, and retain license plate reader data, with exemptions for some transportation and parking agencies.

title: Development projects: preliminary estimate of required improvements: onsite and offsite improvements.
summary: Requires cities and counties to give housing applicants preliminary estimates and itemized lists of required onsite and offsite improvements within set deadlines.

title: Crimes: minors.
summary: Creates crimes for adults who recruit minors to harm or sexually exploit other minors, and expands extortion liability for minors who coerce other minors.

title: Community Assistance, Recovery, and Empowerment (CARE) Court Program and court-ordered evaluations.
summary: Allows CARE petitioners to seek court-ordered mental health evaluations for respondents unlikely to engage voluntarily.

title: Pupils: foster youth: access to pupil records.
summary: Requires school districts to give foster youth aged 14 and older access to their relevant pupil records, with state reimbursement for mandated costs.

title: Human trafficking: specialized license plates.
summary: Creates a survivors of human trafficking grant program and a human trafficking license plate, with plate revenue subject to legislative appropriation.

title: California Cargo Theft Task Force.
summary: Requires the Attorney General to create a California Cargo Theft Task Force to investigate and recommend prosecution of cargo theft, reporting annually from 2028.

title: Budget Act of 2025.
summary: Amends the Budget Act of 2025 for fiscal year 2025-26 by changing appropriation items and declaring immediate effect as a Budget Bill.

title: State of emergency: Governor’s powers and annual report.
summary: Limits the Governor's emergency powers by requiring justification for overrides, automatically ending emergencies after a fiscal year unless renewed, and mandating an annual report on open proclamations.

title: Fishing and hunting: youth program.
summary: Requires the Fish and Game Commission to adopt regulations expanding fishing and hunting opportunities for resident youth with life-threatening illnesses, contingent on appropriation.

title: Human trafficking: California Multidisciplinary Alliance to Stop Trafficking Act.
summary: Creates a contingent state task force to review anti-trafficking collaboration models and report recommendations annually starting 2029.

title: Health care coverage: antiretroviral drugs, drug devices, and drug products.
summary: Bars health plans and insurers from requiring prior authorization or step therapy for HIV prevention drugs, and requires coverage under medical and drug benefits starting 2027.

title: Firefighter postpartum and recovery leave.
summary: Requires specified fire departments to provide up to 26 weeks of full-pay leave for firefighters disabled by pregnancy or childbirth.

title: Office of Food Security and Affordability.
summary: Creates an independent Office of Food Security and Affordability with a director and a special fund, repealed in 2037.

title: Bail Fugitive Recovery Agent Reform Act.
summary: Requires bail fugitive recovery agents to keep liability insurance on file, suspends licenses for noncompliance, and extends notice-of-appointment filing rules.

title: California Street Prostitution Issues and Options Task Force.
summary: Creates a temporary task force to study street prostitution and human trafficking and recommend revisions to state law, reporting by 2029.

title: Behavioral Health Crisis Response Advisory Group.
summary: Creates an advisory group and requires state reports and recommendations on law enforcement's role in behavioral health crisis response.

title: Vehicle lien sales: proceeds.
summary: Requires DMV to transfer unclaimed vehicle lien sale surplus funds to the Controller after 3 years, treating them as escheated property, operative 2030.

title: Budget Acts of 2022, 2023, and 2024.
summary: Amends the 2022, 2023, and 2024 Budget Acts by changing, adding, and repealing appropriation items, effective immediately as a Budget Bill.

title: CalWORKs: unrelated adult male.
summary: Repeals the requirement that unrelated adult males living with CalWORKs families contribute financially to the family, expanding eligibility starting July 2027.

title: Solid waste: compostable products.
summary: Tightens labeling rules for compostable products, requires plastics meeting ASTM standards to be labeled compostable, and orders an OEHHA study of compostable plastic health effects.

title: Staffing agencies: registration.
summary: Requires staffing agencies to register annually with the Labor Commissioner and show workers' compensation coverage, and bars businesses from using unregistered agencies.

title: Protein products.
summary: Requires heavy metal testing and public disclosure for bulk and packaged protein products sold in California starting 2028.

title: Vehicles: special license plates.
summary: Expands eligibility for disabled veteran special license plates to veterans with qualifying mobility conditions, regardless of service connection.

title: Motor vehicle fuel tax: greenhouse gas reduction programs: suspension.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Suspends the fuel tax and Low Carbon Fuel Standard for one year, requires savings passed to consumers, and transfers General Fund money.

title: Mitigation Fee Act.
summary: Requires development fees on demolition or use-change projects to be offset so they reflect only incremental impacts, and limits water and sewer capacity charges to the change in capacity.

title: Health care coverage: rate review.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Tightens state rate review of health plans and insurers by adding cost-target filing requirements, affordability reports, and a broader unreasonable-rate definition.

title: The Public Employees’ Retirement System.
summary: Requires CalPERS to post audit details online and give written notice to affected employers before starting audits, and specifies report distribution.

title: Air resources: refinery-related community air monitoring system.
summary: Lets refineries petition air districts to exclude pollutants from required fence-line air monitoring, and authorizes districts to grant those exclusions.

title: Budget Act of 2025.
summary: Amends the Budget Act of 2025 by changing, adding, and repealing appropriation items, and takes effect immediately.

title: Veterans Cemetery Maintenance-Endowment Match Act.
summary: Creates a state matching-funds program for veterans cemetery maintenance, matching local contributions up to $250,000 per cemetery annually.

title: Voluntary contractual assessments: wildfire safety improvements.
summary: Extends and expands voluntary PACE-style assessment financing for wildfire safety home improvements, including fire-rated roofs and defensible space.

title: Vehicle registration modernization study.
summary: Requests the Little Hoover Commission study modernizing vehicle registration, including eliminating stickers and two-year or installment options, and report by 2028.

title: FAIR Plan policy reporting.
summary: Requires the Department of Insurance to annually report changes in FAIR Plan policy counts by ZIP Code, starting July 1, 2027.

title: Public contracts: Small Business Procurement and Contract Act.
summary: Raises the no-bid small business contract ceiling for services and IT from $250,000 to $350,000 and allows periodic CPI adjustments.

title: Personal income tax.
summary: Makes a nonsubstantive change to the provision that names the Personal Income Tax Law, with no change in tax policy.

title: Occupational safety: transboundary pollution.
summary: Requires state occupational safety regulators to propose a standard protecting outdoor workers from high or prolonged transboundary pollution exposure by 2030.

title: Neurodegenerative disease registry program.
summary: Extends the neurodegenerative disease registry to cover frontotemporal degeneration and other dementias, and extends its operation to 2032.

title: State Seal of Climate Literacy.
summary: Creates a voluntary State Seal of Climate Literacy for high school graduates, with criteria set by the State Board of Education.

title: Health care claims reimbursement.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Requires health plans and insurers to allow at least 90 days to submit corrected claims and bars denials based on prior filing deadlines.

title: Budget Acts of 2021, 2023, 2024, and 2025.
summary: Amends the 2021, 2023, 2024, and 2025 Budget Acts by changing, adding, and repealing appropriation items, effective immediately as a Budget Bill.

title: False advertising: synthetic performers.
summary: Requires clear disclosure when advertisements prominently include AI-generated synthetic performers, and bars media from running ads a court has ordered taken down.

title: Foster care: childcare.
summary: Lets childcare navigators refer foster children to county welfare departments for eligibility under the Emergency Child Care Bridge Program.

title: State Council on Developmental Disabilities: appointing authorized representatives.
summary: Limits authorized representative appointments for developmental disability clients to one year, adds renewal, investigation, and removal authority.

title: Property taxation: transfer of base year value: disaster relief.
summary: Lets counties extend deadlines for disaster-damaged property owners to transfer tax base year values, without state reimbursement of lost local revenue.

title: Unemployment insurance: reporting requirements.
summary: Requires employers with 10 or more workers to report detailed wage, hours and occupation data, and enables data sharing with public benefit agencies.

title: Pajaro Regional Flood Management Agency: contracts.
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Lets the Pajaro Regional Flood Management Agency use alternative project delivery and job order contracting, with a project labor agreement required for the latter.

title: Criminal procedure.
summary: Requires courts in certain cases to issue protective orders limiting disclosure of sexually explicit material depicting adult victims, while preserving defendants' fair-trial rights.

title: Licensing: certified nurse assistants and home health aides.
summary: Makes criminal convictions and prior discipline discretionary grounds to deny or revoke nurse assistant and home health aide certificates, with a rehabilitation pathway.

title: School districts: contracting: purchases for child nutrition programs.
summary: Removes the requirement that price be the primary award factor for school nutrition purchases and modifies the federal procurement standards districts must follow.

title: Employment Training Panel.
summary: Lets Employment Training Panel contractors keep electronic training records and requires the panel to adopt recordkeeping standards.

title: Budget Act of 2025.
summary: Amends the Budget Act of 2025 by changing one appropriation item and takes effect immediately as a Budget Bill.

title: Alcohol and drug treatment facilities.
summary: Bars alcohol and drug treatment facilities serving more than six residents from operating within 1,000 feet of schools or daycare centers.

title: Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act: relocation.
summary: Allows the Department of Fish and Wildlife to permit relocating up to 10 western Joshua trees per parcel without mitigation fees, with conditions and reporting.

title: Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act: fees.
summary: Requires Fish and Wildlife to consider making western Joshua tree mitigation fees proportionate to project impact and tiered by project type or size.

title: Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act: life-sustaining services: take permit.
summary: Allows Fish and Wildlife to permit taking western Joshua trees for life-sustaining service connections to homes without mitigation fees, with 30-day decisions.

title: Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program: testing.
summary: Limits emissions testing of older, low-use heavy-duty nongasoline trucks to no more than once a year and requires CARB rulemaking.

title: Public works: apprenticeship.
summary: Lets apprentices on public works perform any journeyperson tasks within DIR's scope of work and refines the apprenticeable-trade definition.

title: Unclaimed property.
summary: Extends the time before unclaimed property escheats to the state to seven years and requires the Controller to keep escheated property in its original form.

title: Pupil instruction: math assessments.
summary: Requires the state to set criteria and a list of approved math diagnostic assessments, and requires districts and charter schools to assess K-2 pupils' math knowledge by 2028-29.

title: Water appropriations.
summary: Makes a nonsubstantive change to a provision requiring the State Water Resources Control Board to act on water appropriation permit applications.

title: Motor vehicle pollution control devices: aftermarket parts: approval process.
summary: Allows conditional sale approval of aftermarket emissions-related vehicle parts before final CARB executive order, with deemed approval after 30 days.

title: Budget Acts of 2023, 2024, and 2025.
summary: Amends the Budget Acts of 2023, 2024, and 2025 by changing, adding, and repealing appropriation items, effective immediately as a Budget Bill.

title: Crimes: disturbing religious worship.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Makes disturbing religious worship a felony in addition to the existing misdemeanor, and disclaims state reimbursement for resulting local costs.

title: Death certificates.
summary: Lets families request a corrected death certificate from the State Registrar after a court determines a different manner of death.

title: Housing omnibus.
summary: Housing omnibus bill that repeals expired Napa housing authority, expands Housing Accountability Act timing references, and adds owner notice duties for expiring assisted housing.

title: Income taxes: voluntary contributions: Black Cultural District Voluntary Tax Contribution Fund.
summary: Creates a voluntary tax-return checkoff for a Black Cultural District fund, with a continuous appropriation and a sunset tied to contribution levels.

title: Covered provider: goods and services: self-preferencing conduct.
summary: Prohibits large covered platforms from self-preferencing their own products in rankings and from restricting interoperability or data portability.

title: Air resources: toxic air contaminants: criteria air pollutants: community emissions reduction programs: local community emissions reduction plans.
summary: Expands community emissions reduction programs for toxic air contaminants, requiring state approval and enforcement of local plans, plus reporting and steering committee rules.

title: Admitted insurers: residential property insurance.
summary: Requires admitted insurers to offer and renew residential property coverage for hardened homes, sets minimum coverage, and penalizes non-compliance with five-year license suspension.

title: CalFresh: federal government shutdowns.
summary: Requires CalFresh communications plan, public landing page, and emergency benefit issuance mechanism during federal government shutdowns.

title: Gift certificates: cash redemption.
summary: Lets issuers keep selling pre-2026 gift certificates with lower cash-redemption thresholds until 2028 if they post required notices.

title: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection: Fire Innovation Unit.
summary: Establishes a Fire Innovation Unit in the Department of Forestry and Fire Protection to research, procure, and deploy wildfire technologies, subject to appropriation and sunsetting in 2033.

title: Budget Act of 2025.
summary: Amends appropriation items in the Budget Act of 2025 for fiscal year 2025-26 and takes effect immediately as a budget bill.

title: County clerks: certification of records: signature.
summary: Lets county clerks certify records with a facsimile, electronic, or digital signature if the official seal is affixed.

title: Waste discharge requirements: minimum penalties: exception: publicly owned treatment works.
summary: Expands authority to replace mandatory wastewater discharge penalties with compliance projects for very small publicly owned treatment works with financial hardship.

title: Pupil attendance: interdistrict transfers: agreements: policies.
summary: Requires districts with interdistrict transfer agreements to adopt transfer policies, set notice deadlines, and allow concurrent parent requests.

title: Noncertificated public school employees: private school employees: egregious misconduct: statewide data system: Commission on Teacher Credentialing: adverse actions: contracts and background checks for educational services.
summary: Expands school employer disclosure duties on employee egregious misconduct and allows dismissal for nondisclosure, tied to a statewide data system.

title: Personal income taxes: Fire Safe Home Tax Credits Act.
summary: Creates personal income tax credits for wildfire home hardening and vegetation management costs, capped at $50 million per year, from 2027 to 2031.

title: Water supply planning: housing developments.
summary: Speeds water supply assessments for certain housing projects to 45 days and drops the public-meeting approval requirement.

title: Microschools and micro-education entities.
summary: Directs the state Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation to develop and publish model ordinances for microschools and micro-education entities.

title: Transportation planning: sustainable communities strategies: transportation funding programs.
summary: Revises sustainable communities strategy requirements, sets regional emissions targets for 2035 and 2045, and repeals two regional implementation reporting provisions.

title: Health care decisions: life-sustaining treatment.
summary: Revises POLST and prehospital DNR provisions: renames POLST, allows e-signatures, recognizes out-of-state forms, and bars conditioning care on completing them.

title: Preventive Treatment Health Care Act.
summary: Authorizes state partnerships, subject to appropriation, to lower prices and address supply of GLP-1 antiobesity drugs for Medi-Cal beneficiaries.

title: Budget Act of 2026.
summary: Makes the state government appropriations for fiscal year 2026-27 and takes effect immediately as a Budget Bill.

title: Planning and zoning: housing development projects: urban lot splits: subdivisions: 2025 Eaton Wildfire: Altadena.
summary: Suspends ministerial approval rules for housing developments and maps in Altadena ZIP codes 91001 and 91003 until 2030, as an urgency statute.

title: Community Anti-Displacement and Preservation Program.
summary: Creates a program funding acquisition and rehabilitation of unrestricted housing with long-term affordability restrictions and anti-displacement tenant protections.

title: Mobilehome parks: resident organizations: option to purchase.
summary: Requires park management to notify residents and negotiate in good faith with resident organizations that seek to buy a mobilehome park management intends to sell.

title: Mobilehome parks: disaster assistance.
summary: Requires mobilehome park management to give disaster status updates, allow resident access after evacuations, and evaluate rebuilding costs before closure.

title: Prescription drugs.
summary: Expands pharmacist biosimilar substitution and requires certain plan formularies to include lower-cost biosimilars, and bars insurers from dropping previously covered drugs.

title: Fusion centers.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Government and administration; Immigration
summary: Requires law enforcement MOUs before sharing information with fusion centers, bars immigration-enforcement sharing absent judicial warrant, mandates audits and public records.

title: Personal income tax: senior tax credit: dependents: qualifying child.
summary: Creates a $1,500 per dependent income tax credit for seniors 65+ with no earned income, for tax years 2026 through 2030.

title: California Environmental Quality Act: electrical distribution: exemptions.
summary: Exempts transmission line maintenance and reconductoring from CEQA and creates a modified approval process for certain energy projects.

title: Public Utilities Commission: memorandum and balancing accounts.
summary: Limits utility memorandum and balancing accounts to necessary cases, requiring their review in general rate cases.

title: State and local public benefits.
summary: Clarifies that local governments may provide aid, including health care, to immigrants otherwise ineligible under federal PRWORA rules.

title: Artificial intelligence technology.
summary: Adds AI digital replica provisions to impersonation crimes and publicity rights, requires AI tools to warn users, and has the Judicial Council review AI evidence.

title: Budget Act of 2026.
summary: Budget bill making 2026-27 state government appropriations and amending the Budget Act's list of related appropriation bills.

title: Grand juries: final reports.
summary: Requires court clerks to compile each grand jury's final reports and responses and transfer them to the State Archivist within six months of the term's end.

title: Postsecondary education: sharing personal information: notice.
topics: AI and technology; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Requires colleges to notify students, faculty and staff when personal information goes to federal civil rights office, and limits sharing to legally required cases.

title: Personal Income Tax Law: credit: nurses.
summary: Creates a $2,000 annual personal income tax credit for licensed nurses at rural health facilities, from 2027 through 2031.

title: Large retail stores: immigration enforcement: reporting.
summary: Requires large retail stores to give the Attorney General immigration enforcement records and video from their premises, and to publicly disclose related policies.

title: California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018: data broker registration: accessible deletion mechanism.
summary: Tightens California data broker rules: adds registration disclosures, email requests for offline businesses, and a state privacy preference tool.

title: Law enforcement.
summary: Restricts federal officers' state arrest and peace officer powers and requires interagency agreements to bar racial or identity profiling.

title: Agentic artificial intelligence.
summary: Adds agentic AI to state AI risk-analysis recommendations and to the required inventory of high-risk automated decision systems used by state agencies.

title: School facilities: design-build: shade structures.
summary: Lets school districts bundle shade structure design-build contracts through 2031 and caps accessibility path-of-travel costs for playground-integrated shade structures.

title: Grassland Ecological Area Conservancy.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Creates the Grassland Ecological Area Conservancy within the Natural Resources Agency, with a governing board and a dedicated fund subject to appropriation.

title: Short-term residential therapeutic programs.
summary: Requires annual license renewal from 2027 for short-term residential therapeutic programs with five or more citations in 12 months.

title: Budget Act of 2026.
summary: Sets state government appropriations for fiscal year 2026-27 and amends the Budget Act of 2026, effective immediately as a Budget Bill.

title: Early learning and care: rates.
summary: Changes childcare and preschool reimbursement to tie full contract payment to 85% enrollment and caps administrative costs.

title: Digital replicas.
summary: Extends unauthorized-likeness liability to AI digital replicas, makes digital replica impersonation a crime, and removes the employee likeness presumption.

title: Vehicles: towing companies and storage facilities.
summary: Lets vehicle owners post bond to recover towed or stored vehicles, bars towing and storage profiteering, requires notices, and imposes civil fines.

title: Corporate tax: exclusions: qualifying shipping activities.
summary: Excludes qualifying international shipping income from corporate tax for electing corporations under federal tonnage-tax rules, starting 2026.

title: Data collection: sexual orientation, gender identity, and intersex status: disclosure.
summary: Bans disclosure of sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex data that could identify individuals outside state or local government, with limited exceptions.

title: Public cemetery districts: board of trustees: County of Tulare.
summary: Lets Tulare County cemetery district boards and the county Board of Supervisors remove trustees for misconduct or neglect, with notice and a hearing, and appoint replacements.

title: Planning and zoning: housing development projects: subdivisions.
summary: Expands ministerial housing approvals on subdivided lots by relaxing height, setback, density, and parcel size limits.

title: Accessory dwelling units and junior accessory dwelling units.
summary: Limits impact fees on accessory dwelling units to only the square footage above 750 square feet, applying to all cities including charter cities.

title: Personal Income Tax Law: Corporation Tax Law: tax credits: backup generators: solar batteries.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a 2027–2031 income and corporate tax credit for 50% of backup generator or solar battery costs, capped at $5,000 or $7,500, contingent on appropriations.

title: Companion chatbots: children’s safety.
topics: AI and technology; Children and families
summary: Requires companion chatbot operators to assess risks, undergo independent child safety audits, and face enforcement for minor users, starting July 2027.

title: Budget Acts of 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025.
summary: Amends the 2022 through 2025 Budget Acts by changing, adding, and repealing appropriation items, effective immediately as a Budget Bill.

title: Personal Income Tax Law: Corporation Tax Law: credits: CalCompetes.
summary: Extends the California Competes business tax credit to 2035 and allows strategic-industry taxpayers to elect a refundable credit, with appropriations.

title: Vehicles: commercial electric vehicle safety.
summary: Requires the Office of Emergency Services to develop and post an action plan for responding to electric commercial vehicle battery fires by 2028.

title: Planning and zoning: annual progress report: accessory dwelling unit ordinances.
summary: Requires cities and counties with accessory dwelling unit ordinances to report the ordinance's code section and enactment or update date in their annual housing report.

title: Administrative Procedure Act: major regulations.
summary: Requires agencies estimating regulatory economic impact to count offsetting benefits and savings in their major regulation analyses.

title: Public health.
summary: Requires tobacco retailers from 2028 to display state lung cancer screening awareness signage, with $500 civil penalties for violations.

title: Water Rate Assistance Program.
summary: Creates a Water Rate Assistance Program and fund for low-income ratepayers, contingent on legislative appropriation, with state board guidelines and oversight.

title: Local agencies: financial postings.
summary: Requires local agencies with websites to post audited financial statements or annual comprehensive reports online within 30 days of completion, starting 2028.

title: California State University: terms of employment.
summary: Makes nonsubstantive wording changes to the requirement that CSU trustees set rules governing their appointees and employees.

title: Pupils: technology-based materials: school-issued electronic devices.
summary: Bars schools from requiring kindergartners to take home school-issued devices starting 2027-28, and directs state guidance on screen time and e-waste.

title: State Bar of California: community justice worker program.
summary: Requires the State Bar to report to Judiciary committees on statutory changes needed for a proposed community justice worker program, repealing the requirement in 2031.

title: Budget Act of 2026.
summary: Amends the Budget Act of 2026 by changing, adding, and repealing appropriation items, and takes effect immediately as a budget bill.

title: Invasion of privacy: wearable recording devices.
topics: AI and technology; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Bars recording others in private areas of businesses with wearable devices without consent, requires recording indicators, and bans disabling them.

title: Debt collection.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Requires remote examinations of debt collection licensees, renames the advisory committee as a board, and exempts it from open meeting law.

title: Workforce development: workplace rights training.
summary: Requires the state workforce board to create a workplace rights curriculum and local boards to provide matching training to people using workforce services.

title: Pupil instruction: preventative health instruction.
summary: Requires the Instructional Quality Commission to consider adding evidence-based preventative health instruction to the health framework when it is next revised after 2027.

title: SNAP to Thrive: Shop Nutritiously and Preventatively to Thrive Act.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Directs California to seek federal waivers barring CalFresh use for soft drinks, candy, prepackaged desserts, and certain ultraprocessed foods.

title: California Wildlife Coexistence Act.
summary: Creates wildlife coexistence programs, renames the wolf-livestock pilot, and exempts livestock-guarding dogs from pursuit bans for wolves.

title: Intercity rail and commuter rail: special events service plans: fare system integration.
summary: Requires regional rail fare systems to integrate with intercity rail and adds special events service plans to joint powers board business plans.

title: Personal income tax: deduction: medical expenses.
summary: Creates a temporary state income tax deduction for medical costs exceeding 4% of income for low-income taxpayers, capped at $5,000.

title: Load-serving entities: resource adequacy requirements.
summary: Lets load-serving entities meet resource adequacy requirements through short-term transactions with other load-serving entities, capped at 25% of obligations.

title: Monterey Peninsula Water Management District: nonfunctional turf: noncompliance and enforcement.
summary: Authorizes the Monterey Peninsula Water Management District to impose civil penalties and enforce the nonfunctional turf irrigation ban.

title: Budget Acts of 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025.
summary: Amends the 2022 through 2025 Budget Acts by changing, adding, and repealing appropriation items, effective immediately as a Budget Bill.

title: Pupil safety: limiting school access to unauthorized individuals.
summary: Requires school construction contracts during school hours to include security provisions keeping unauthorized individuals off school property.

title: Public contracts: University of California executives: conflicts of interest: prohibition.
summary: Bars University of California executives from influencing contracts with businesses where they serve on the board or receive consulting pay, and requires voiding affected contracts.

title: Digital Dignity Act.
summary: Creates liability for distributing AI digital replicas used for impersonation and requires large platforms with replica tools to offer reporting and honor court-ordered removals.

title: Children’s advocacy centers: recordings.
topics: Children and families; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Lets children's advocacy center multidisciplinary teams share confidential child abuse investigation information with child welfare agencies.

title: Personal income taxes: exemption credit: dependents.
summary: Raises the state dependent exemption credit from $475 to $700 for 2026 through 2030, with inflation adjustments starting in 2027.

title: California Environmental Quality Act: surplus land disposal requirements: exemption.
summary: Exempts former military base land conveyed to reuse authorities from surplus land rules and streamlines CEQA review for Concord Naval Weapons Station projects.

title: Advertisement claims: health-related consumer products and services: digital replicas and synthetic performers.
topics: AI and technology; Consumer protection and business
summary: Requires disclosure when AI-generated or synthetic health care provider depictions are used in ads for health-related products, enforceable under unfair competition and false advertising laws.

title: Pupil instruction: high school graduation requirements: personal finance.
summary: Lets districts satisfy the high school personal finance requirement with an integrated year-long course and exempt those students from the economics requirement.

title: Security guards: training.
summary: Allows security guards who completed use-of-force and arrest training to finish security officer skills training before registration is issued.

title: Employees: bereavement leave.
summary: Adds employee-designated persons to the bereavement leave family definition, but lets employers limit this to one designated person per 12 months.

title: Budget Act of 2025.
summary: Expresses legislative intent to enact future statutory changes relating to the Budget Act of 2025.

title: Cancer data: notifications.
summary: Requires hospitals treating cancer patients in designated reporting areas to post a department-developed sign about cancer data reporting.
