summary: Creates an income tax credit for hotels and inns that train employees to recognize and report human trafficking, for tax years 2027 through 2032.

title: Relating to antisemitism.
summary: Declares Oregon policy to combat antisemitism and defines the term; the text sets out no operative rules or programs.

title: Relating to crimes involving minors.
summary: Creates a new crime of harmful communication with a minor, punishable by up to five years' imprisonment, a $125,000 fine, or both.

title: Relating to tax incentives for financial institution lending in rural areas; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates temporary tax subtractions and a CAT exemption for banks' interest on rural farm, residence and coastal fishing boat loans, for tax years 2026-2031.

title: Relating to unemployment insurance benefits for nonprofessional educational workers.
summary: Restores former restrictions on unemployment insurance benefits for certain nonprofessional educational workers, reversing a 2023 repeal.

title: Relating to exemption of prescription drug sales; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts receipts from prescription drug sales by licensed retail pharmacies from Oregon's corporate activity tax, starting tax years on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to sustainable investing.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Directs the state investment council and Treasurer to reduce the carbon intensity of certain state investments and report on those investments.

title: Relating to mobile on-demand fueling.
summary: Allows mobile on-demand gasoline delivery, with State Fire Marshal standards and local certificates authorizing the service.

title: Relating to behavioral health.
summary: Clarifies roles and updates terminology for behavioral health service delivery, and directs OHA to study redundancies in ORS chapters 414 and 430.

title: Relating to the safety of behavioral health workers; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires behavioral health employers to adopt written safety plans and worker safety training, offers grants for safety upgrades, and provides reinstatement with back pay for retaliation.

title: Relating to rural health care provider tax credits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands the rural provider income tax credit to podiatrists and removes hospital privilege requirement for optometrists claiming it.

title: Relating to coordinated care organization contracts.
summary: Sets Oregon Health Authority contracts with coordinated care organizations to 10 years, with a performance review after five years.

title: Relating to adult residential mental health services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires OHA to convene a work group to study transferring financial risk and administration of adult residential mental health services for Medicaid enrollees to CCOs, reporting by December 2028.

title: Relating to external quality reviews of coordinated care organizations; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to adopt external quality review standards for coordinated care organizations aligned with NCQA standards, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to community health improvement plans.
summary: Requires CCOs to collaborate on community health assessments and improvement plans, folding in behavioral health plans, and directs OHA to align planning requirements through rulemaking.

title: Relating to coordinated care organization contracts.
summary: Changes the process and adds criteria for amending contracts between the Oregon Health Authority and coordinated care organizations.

title: Relating to coordinated care organizations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to recommend expanding and improving the Oregon Health Authority's provider credentialing database, with no immediate rule changes.

title: Relating to dental subcontractors; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Defines dental subcontractors and directs the Oregon Health Authority to adopt requirements for those contracting with coordinated care organizations.

title: Relating to the prioritized list of health services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study impacts of phasing out the prioritized list of health services and report by February 2026.

title: Relating to coordinated care organizations.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to set an 85 percent minimum medical loss ratio for coordinated care organizations, excluding certain dental care revenue.

title: Relating to coordinated care organizations.
summary: Modifies the minimum financial requirements that coordinated care organizations must meet; the text gives no detail on the changes.

title: Relating to global budgets for coordinated care organizations; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Sets a process, similar to insurer rate review, that the Oregon Health Authority must follow when determining CCO global budgets.

title: Relating to community health workers; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study community health worker payment and offer technical assistance on billing structures, sunsetting January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to medical assistance for children; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Modifies CCO advisory council membership and requires CCOs to partner with Early Learning Hubs on community health assessments and improvement plans for children.

title: Relating to reimbursement rates for inpatient psychiatric services.
summary: Requires OHA and CCOs to pay hospitals for inpatient psychiatric services for Medicaid recipients at no less than Oregon State Hospital psychiatric rehabilitation rates.

title: Relating to reimbursement rates for hospital obstetric services.
summary: Requires OHA and CCOs, where federal law allows, to pay hospitals at least cost for Medicaid labor and delivery services.

title: Relating to hospitals.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study hospitals and report findings to interim health committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to health insurance.
summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study health insurance and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to mobile integrated health care; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs OHA to set Medicaid enrollment criteria for mobile integrated health care providers and to help them apply.

title: Relating to coordinated care organizations; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires coordinated care organizations to contract with out-of-area providers where Medicaid care or services have limited access, and directs OHA to identify those services.

title: Relating to medical assistance; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds local health officials and public health expertise to Medicaid CCO governance and advisory bodies, and lets local health departments receive payment for services.

title: Relating to equitable access to health care services.
summary: Requires OHA and CCOs to set minimum Medicaid reimbursement rates for primary care, optometry, dental and behavioral health services.

title: Relating to bonding.
summary: Directs the State Treasurer to study bonding and report findings to interim ways and means committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to investments.
summary: Directs the State Treasurer to study state investments and report findings to ways and means interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to brassica production; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals Willamette Valley brassica production limits, creating a seed-crop registration system and requiring isolation distances between brassica seed fields.

title: Relating to coordinated care organizations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Extends CCO contract terms to 10 years, limits contract amendments, sets standards for awarding contracts, and conditions new CCOs serving already-covered areas.

title: Relating to explicit digital forgeries.
summary: Creates first- and second-degree crimes for making, possessing, distributing or buying explicit digital forgeries, with prison terms and fines.

title: Relating to seed quality standards.
summary: Defines "quality standard" for certain seed contracts and directs OSU's seed certification service to keep publishing the Oregon Seed Certification Handbook.

title: Relating to off-road vehicle equipment standards; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Moves authority to adopt off-road vehicle equipment standards to the State Parks and Recreation Department and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to public safety; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a program funding legal services for adults in custody at Coffee Creek Correctional Facility, with evaluation and reporting, sunsetting in 2027.

title: Relating to an income tax subtraction for overtime pay received; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a personal income tax subtraction for overtime pay for tax years 2026 through 2031, reducing state income tax on overtime earnings.

title: Relating to a tax credit for security systems; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a 2026–2031 income or corporate excise tax credit for small businesses that install or upgrade security alarm systems.

title: Relating to employment; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets professional employer organizations elect whether to treat client workers as the PEO's or the client's for certain unemployment insurance purposes.

title: Relating to the repeal of provisions of law governing predictive work scheduling.
summary: Repeals Oregon's predictive work scheduling statutes, removing employer scheduling-notice rules for workers.

title: Relating to coordinated care organizations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes Oregon's coordinated care organization model: longer contracts, limits on amendments, entry conditions for new CCOs, a minimum medical loss ratio, and quality measures for fee-for-service providers.

title: Relating to recovery residences; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits state agencies, coordinated care organizations and counties to contracting with recovery residences that a certifying organization has certified for substance use housing supports.

title: Relating to workers' compensation.
summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study Oregon workers' compensation and report to labor interim committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to unemployment insurance.
summary: Requires the Employment Department to study Oregon unemployment insurance and report to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to employment.
summary: Directs the Employment Department to study employment issues and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026; the bill sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to laws concerning job-protected leave from work.
summary: Directs the Employment Department to study the family and medical leave insurance program and report to legislative committees by September 2026, then sunset.

title: Relating to workplace safety.
summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study workplace safety issues and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the Construction Contractors Board.
summary: Requires the Construction Contractors Board to study construction contractors and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the Employment Department.
summary: Requires the Employment Department to study how unemployment insurance law is implemented and report to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to employment standards.
summary: Directs the Employment Department to study employment standards and report findings to interim committees by September 15, 2026; the bill sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to the Bureau of Labor and Industries; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Creates an Employer Assistance Division at BOLI with confidential employer discussions, penalty protection for good-faith reliance, advisory opinions, and alternative dispute settlements.

title: Relating to apprenticeships; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force to identify licensing and apprenticeship challenges for health care providers and report by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to redistricting.
summary: Counts incarcerated adults at their last known addresses for redistricting and apportionment, adjusting census population data used to draw legislative and local boundaries.

title: Relating to student use of personal electronic devices.
summary: Requires school districts to adopt policies prohibiting student use of cell phones and other personal electronic devices.

title: Relating to conditions that apply to registration as a pharmacy benefit manager.
summary: Requires pharmacy benefit managers to prove they are not owned or operated by insurers to register, applying to renewals from 2031.

title: Relating to pharmacy benefit managers.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Requires pharmacy benefit managers to act as fiduciaries to enrollees when negotiating drug prices, with DCBS rules and a complaint process.

title: Relating to wages.
summary: Makes owners and direct contractors jointly liable for construction workers' unpaid wages, sets a limitations period, requires subcontractor payroll records, and allows payment withholding.

title: Relating to interpretation of laws.
summary: Bars courts from deferring to state agency interpretations of statutes or rules and directs them to favor interpretations that limit agency power.

title: Relating to sales of units of land not lawfully established for conservation purposes.
summary: Exempts nonprofit, public body or tribal buyers of land for conservation, and their sellers, from liability for selling certain unlawful land units, but removes the exemption for buyers who resell within five years.

title: Relating to housing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to OBDD for grants to cities building housing-related infrastructure, and extends the program's and cities' reporting sunsets.

title: Relating to housing; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets the state preapprove residential building plans and lets the land commission require local governments to approve matching land use applications; boosts rulemaking funds.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to homelessness.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study homelessness and report findings to interim housing committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to homelessness.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study homelessness and report findings to housing interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to homelessness.
summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to study homelessness and report findings to housing interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to homeownership.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study homeownership and report findings to interim legislative housing committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to homeownership.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study homeownership and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to homeownership.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study homeownership and report findings to interim legislative housing committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to housing development.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing development and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to health care cost sharing arrangements; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires health care cost sharing arrangement sellers to register with DCBS, file annual reports, follow disclosure rules, and face Unlawful Trade Practices Act penalties.

title: Relating to the Oregon State Capitol Foundation; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Restructures Capitol Foundation board appointments, moves financial audits from annual to biennial, lets the Legislative Administrator accept gifts, and closes two foundation funds.

title: Relating to addiction medicine services; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to raise addiction medicine reimbursement rates by 30 percent, with annual commission review and possible later revisions.

title: Relating to employer taxes.
summary: Gives employers a one-year credit against unemployment insurance taxes if their 2025 rate drops at least 2.5 points from 2024.

title: Relating to sports.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to study sports in Oregon and report to economic development interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to telecommunications.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study telecommunications and report findings to economic development interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the Oregon Business Development Department.
summary: Directs the state business development agency to stop using the name 'Business Oregon' and requires a study of its economic development role.

title: Relating to the Oregon Business Development Department.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to study its economic development role and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission.
summary: Requires the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission to study itself and report findings to economic development interim committees by September 15, 2026. The bill sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to the semiconductor industry; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows state CHIPS Fund grants and loans to semiconductor businesses eligible for federal CHIPS Act aid that have not applied for it, and requires a study.

title: Relating to trade.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to study trade and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to utilities.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study utilities and report findings to economic development interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to forest products.
summary: Directs the State Forestry Department to study forest products and report to legislative natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to advanced manufacturing.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to study advanced manufacturing and report to the Legislature by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to alcohol; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires certain individuals to obtain an OLCC retail liquor sales permit, and limits minor decoy operations on distilleries and retail agents to one per year.

title: Relating to the arts.
summary: Directs the Oregon Arts Commission to study the arts and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to broadband.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study broadband and report findings to economic development interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to business services.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study business services and report to the Legislature by September 15, 2026; the study sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to cannabis.
summary: Directs the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission to study cannabis and report findings to interim economic development committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to child care.
summary: Requires the Department of Early Learning and Care to study child care and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to clean technology.
summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Quality to study clean technology and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the Commercialization Gap Fund program.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study the Commercialization Gap Fund grant program and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to county fairs.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study county fairs and report to natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to economic development; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Appropriates money for a festival and event grant program and a study of operating Tom McCall Waterfront Park in Portland.

title: Relating to treatment of human immunodeficiency virus.
summary: Requires health benefit plans and Medicaid managed care plans to cover additional HIV treatment with no cost-sharing and bars prior authorization for it.

title: Relating to pretrial incarceration.
summary: Limits pretrial release for felony and Class A misdemeanor defendants to security release and reimburses counties for pretrial incarceration costs.

title: Relating to theft of firearms.
summary: Directs the Criminal Justice Commission to classify theft of a firearm as a level 8 offense on the sentencing grid.

title: Relating to landowner immunity.
summary: Changes landowner immunity from outdoor-visitor lawsuits to focus on the injured user's activities and location, not intended purposes.

title: Relating to public defense; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Makes counties responsible for public defense, directs them to coordinate services, and revises the Public Defense Commission's duties to set standards and distribute funds.

title: Relating to tendering rent to avoid termination of residential tenancy.
summary: Requires tenants to pay accruing rent to avoid nonpayment termination, and awards landlord attorney fees if rent is unpaid through trial.

title: Relating to expungements.
summary: Changes the timing rules for when a person may obtain an order setting aside a conviction, arrest, charge, or GEI finding.

title: Relating to the unlawful dissemination of intimate images.
summary: Expands the intimate image dissemination crime to cover digitally altered fake images and raises penalties, adding a second-degree offense.

title: Relating to retaliatory actions for communications.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Bars civil suits against individuals who, without malice, make reasonable-belief communications about sexual assault, harassment or sex discrimination, and lets prevailing defendants recover fees and sanctions.

title: Relating to estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Sets Oregon estate tax exclusion at $7 million, flat seven percent rate, plus additional $7 million exclusion.

title: Relating to abuse of vulnerable persons; declaring an emergency.
summary: Expands who can bring civil actions for abuse of vulnerable persons and adds individuals under 18 to the definition of vulnerable person.

title: Relating to judicial review of administrative rules.
summary: Directs courts to invalidate administrative rules that would require a public body to fail to comply with federal law or regulations.

title: Relating to fairs; declaring an emergency.
summary: Redirects lottery money to county fair accounts, requires a county fairground master plan, authorizes emergency-center bonds, and appropriates funds for fairgrounds and consultants.

title: Relating to termination of residential tenancy for repeated violations.
summary: Lets landlords end a residential tenancy after a third violation or a late payment, on 30 days' notice, with no right to cure.

title: Relating to courts.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Lets any county create a justice of the peace district including the county seat, and raises the marriage solemnization fee with CPI indexing.

title: Relating to fluorescent lamps purchased by school districts; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Exempts school districts from the ban on selling certain fluorescent lamps until January 2, 2030, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to parental control filters for consumer products that enable access to the Internet.
summary: Requires makers of internet-enabled consumer devices to include a parental control filter that is automatically on for users under 18, enforced by the Attorney General.

title: Relating to change of name.
summary: Removes the administrative option to change a birth certificate name for gender identity without court approval, and requires clear and convincing evidence for name-change applicants with certain convictions.

title: Relating to the rights of crime victims.
summary: Requires district attorney offices to create a victims' rights form and provide it to all victims when a prosecution begins.

title: Relating to contested case hearings involving the Oregon State Hospital.
summary: Lets the Oregon Health Authority hear Oregon State Hospital contested cases without using Office of Administrative Hearings administrative law judges.

title: Relating to staffing correctional facilities; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Task Force on Staffing at Correctional Facilities to study staffing and report to a legislative interim committee by December 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the protection of health care workers.
summary: Expands assault in the third degree to cover health care workers and requires employers to create notification programs alerting victims when assailants enter workplaces.

title: Relating to a memorandum of understanding concerning oversight of agricultural labor housing standards; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs DCBS and the Department of Agriculture to sign an agreement on administering and enforcing farmworker housing safety and health standards, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to sex offender information.
summary: Directs State Police to release level two sex offender information to certain entities through a department-maintained website.

title: Relating to lands designated for housing; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets DAS designate state and local lands within urban growth boundaries as home start lands for affordable housing, exempting them from local land use laws and property taxes for up to five years.

title: Relating to coordinated care organizations; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires coordinated care organization governing bodies to include a federally qualified health center representative and a senior public health official.

title: Relating to mail order drugs.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to review studies on temperature excursions in mail order drug transit and report findings by September 2026.

title: Relating to veterans' personal information.
summary: Limits who can obtain veteran discharge papers from county clerks and exempts those records from the 25-year public disclosure limit.

title: Relating to cancellation of approval by the Higher Education Coordinating Commission.
summary: Lets the Higher Education Coordinating Commission cancel a school's approval to confer degrees or offer degree-leading services.

title: Relating to ballot measures addressing property taxes; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force and directs a fiscal officer to study the state property tax system and report by late 2026. It changes no tax rules.

title: Relating to economic development; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets state CHIPS Fund grants and loans go to eligible firms that have not applied for federal semiconductor aid, broadens eligible businesses, and renames the fund.

title: Relating to food production.
summary: Directs the State Department of Agriculture to study food and beverage production and report to natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to high technology.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study high technology in Oregon and report to the Legislature by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to industrial site readiness.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to study industrial site readiness and report to the Legislature by September 15, 2026; the section sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to industrial site readiness.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to study industrial site readiness and report to the Legislative Assembly by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to loans.
summary: Requires the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study loans and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to manufacturing.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to study manufacturing in Oregon and report to the Legislature by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to fraudulent schemes targeting the elderly; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study financial scams targeting older Oregonians and recommend legislation, with a list of standard terms based on federal law.

title: Relating to authority to delegate parental decision making.
summary: Prohibits parents of children in DHS care or custody from delegating their parental decision-making rights to someone else.

title: Relating to air curtain incinerators; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars DEQ from requiring Title V air operating permits for certain air curtain incinerators, relaxing their permit obligations.

title: Relating to ballot measures addressing property taxes; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force to study the impacts of Measures 5 and 50 on local governments and report to legislative tax committees by December 2026.

title: Relating to ballot measures addressing property taxes; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force to study how Measures 5 and 50 affected public higher education costs, reporting by December 15, 2026, then sunsetting.

title: Relating to ballot measures addressing property taxes; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a task force to study past and future impacts of Ballot Measures 5 and 50 on taxing jurisdictions, reporting by December 2026, then sunsetting.

title: Relating to internal audits.
summary: Changes the timing of internal audits by state agencies and of DAS reporting on those internal audits.

title: Relating to preferences for small businesses in public procurement; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to create a small business preferences program for state procurement, with reporting and a 2031 sunset.

title: Relating to tax preparation professionals.
summary: Creates a new registered tax aide credential that lets aides assist tax professionals with returns, with education, training, and fee requirements overseen by the state board.

title: Relating to changes to the tax laws of this state; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Makes unspecified changes to Oregon tax laws; the text does not identify which taxes or how they change.

title: Relating to eligibility criteria for the homestead property tax deferral program; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Reduces from five to three years the homestead ownership period needed before a property qualifies for the homestead property tax deferral program.

title: Relating to the Department of Veterans' Affairs.
summary: Adds veterans' and service members' e-mail addresses to the data that state agencies must share with the Department of Veterans' Affairs.

title: Relating to fees concerning wildlife; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Raises wildlife and commercial fishing license, tag and permit fees, allows new ocean endorsements, and creates a Marine Fisheries Enhancement Fund subaccount.

title: Relating to the Columbia Basin endorsement.
summary: Extends sunsets on Columbia Basin endorsement fees for fishing licenses, the fund receiving those fees, and the youth and pioneer license exemptions.

title: Relating to the World War II memorial located in the Capitol Mall.
summary: Requires the Department of Veterans' Affairs to keep the Capitol Mall World War II memorial updated and maintain an educational tool.

title: Relating to Oregon hatcheries.
summary: Renames the Oregon Hatchery Research Center Fund and repeals the statutes creating the Oregon Hatchery Research Center and its board.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Creates an Office of Resilience and Emergency Management in DHS for emergency human services and makes fire-responsible persons liable for state service costs.

title: Relating to land use planning.
summary: Authorizes DLCD to give housing-production planning assistance to federally recognized tribes and makes various technical land use law changes.

title: Relating to economic development programs.
summary: Makes small administrative changes to certain economic development program statutes; the summary gives no specifics on what changes.

title: Relating to industrial development.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets the state Business Development Department provide financing for industrial land projects and creates an Industrial Site Loan Fund in the State Treasury.

title: Relating to financial assistance to small businesses; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs Business Oregon to create a program offering loans and grants to small businesses for enhanced and new commercial projects.

title: Relating to the economic development information of businesses; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Changes how businesses report data from certain state benefit programs and how their economic development information is released.

title: Relating to long term care.
summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study long-term services and supports and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to behavioral health.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study behavioral health services for older adults and people with disabilities, reporting by September 2026, then sunsetting.

title: Relating to long term care.
summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study long-term services and supports and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to district annexations.
summary: Allows annexation petitions covering multiple parcels without an election, and skips the public hearing when a majority of resident electors sign.

title: Relating to a metropolitan service district boundaries.
summary: Adds lands inside Metro's urban growth boundary to the Metro district when annexed by a Metro city.

title: Relating to health care professional interstate compacts; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Joins interstate compacts letting licensed occupational therapists, audiologists and speech-language pathologists from other member states practice here without an Oregon license.

title: Relating to school-based health practitioners; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study student caseloads for school-based speech-language pathologists, occupational therapists and physical therapists, reporting by January 5, 2026.

title: Relating to school starting times.
summary: Requires high schools to start no earlier than 8:30 a.m. and directs the Department of Education to provide technical assistance and grants for implementation.

title: Relating to substance use disorders.
summary: Authorizes involuntary civil commitment of people with substance use disorders who meet the existing mental disorder commitment criteria, and sets standards for treatment without consent.

title: Relating to tax exemption for the property of veterans; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lowers the disability rating veterans need to qualify for a property tax exemption on their homestead or personal property to 10 percent.

title: Relating to exemptions from estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an additional Oregon estate tax exemption that phases out as estate size grows, for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to damage caused by elk; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a pilot program and fund at the Department of Agriculture to prevent and compensate elk damage, with a 2031 sunset and a 2029 report.

title: Relating to the effects of wolves on livestock.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Caps wolf depredation compensation at $15,000 per animal, bases payments on fair market value multipliers, and removes compensation for missing livestock.

title: Relating to rural medical provider tax credits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands the rural provider income tax credit to more provider types and drops a hospital consulting privileges requirement for optometrists.

title: Relating to lottery revenues; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Changes how video lottery revenues are transferred to counties for economic development, using a fixed percentage and adjusting for forecast differences.

title: Relating to telemedicine.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study telemedicine issues and report findings to interim health committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the provision of information about courses of study offered by school districts; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires school boards to post each course's curriculum on district websites, with small districts phased in, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the depredation of livestock.
summary: Lets people appeal wolf depredation compensation findings to a county advisory committee, with no change to wolf protection rules.

title: Relating to fees imposed by the Public Utility Commission; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Raises the annual fee the Public Utility Commission may charge utilities to cover its costs, and takes effect immediately.

title: Relating to waiver of tuition.
summary: Prevents the tuition waived for qualified students from being reduced by specified student aid they receive.

title: Relating to infants born alive.
summary: Requires medical practitioners to provide life-preserving care to any child born alive, including after an induced abortion, and allows private lawsuits for violations.

title: Relating to timeshare sales agents; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Labor and employment
summary: Creates a timeshare sales agent license, prohibits selling or offering timeshares without it, and assigns regulation to the Real Estate Agency.

title: Relating to services to improve school attendance.
summary: Creates the CARE Program within DHS to fund local grants supporting families and reducing barriers to school attendance.

title: Relating to wind energy facilities.
summary: Requires wind energy developers to seek FAA and FCC approval for light-mitigating systems, and bars counties and cities from permitting projects that do not apply.

title: Relating to economic development in Wallowa County; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Wallowa County economic development board with a grant and loan program, and lets the county rezone up to 50 acres from resource to residential use.

title: Relating to ports.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to study Oregon port economic development and report to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to lumber grading training program.
summary: Creates an OSU lumber grading training program, a State Board of Forestry certification for graduates, and a DCBS process for obtaining lumber from certified graders.

title: Relating to dyslexia.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to study effective methods for teaching students with dyslexia and report findings to legislative education committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to cosmetology provisional certificates; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets provisional cosmetology certificate holders work under a supervisor, sets supervisor requirements, and allows supervised practice to count toward certification education requirements.

title: Relating to pregnancy resources; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a state Pregnancy Launch Program and hotline, bars contracts with abortion-referring organizations, and routes callers seeking abortions to program providers.

title: Relating to funding services for pregnant persons other than types of abortions on which federal moneys may not be spent; providing that this Act shall be referred to the people for their approval or rejection.
summary: Limits state Medicaid abortion reimbursement to life-threatening or rape/incest cases and creates a grant program and fund supporting pregnancies carried to term.

title: Relating to mass transit districts.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Lets mass transit district officers be appointed to enforce ordinances and issue tickets, permits optional body cameras, and exempts their recordings from public records disclosure.

title: Relating to fees on the transportation of oil by rail.
summary: Extends the sunset dates for two fees on oil transported by rail and modifies the definitions of "oil" and "tank railroad car" for the tank car fee.

title: Relating to restrictions on 340B covered entities; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars drug manufacturers from interfering with pharmacies acquiring, delivering or dispensing 340B drugs, and creates State Board of Pharmacy civil penalties.

title: Relating to the unclaimed remains of eligible decedents.
summary: Gives the Department of Veterans' Affairs rulemaking authority to implement laws on unclaimed remains of veterans and their families.

title: Relating to psilocybin; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets health care providers licensed by their boards discuss and provide psilocybin services, and become licensed psilocybin facilitators, without facing discipline for doing so.

title: Relating to easements; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows landowners to create easements over their own property for their own benefit by declaration, effective immediately as an emergency measure.

title: Relating to enrollment limit for public universities.
summary: Caps public universities' enrollment growth at five percent per year and requires referring excess applications to community colleges and other public universities.

title: Relating to tax credits for rural medical providers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises the income tax credit for rural medical providers and removes the adjusted gross income limit on eligibility.

title: Relating to an income tax credit for sheriff's deputies in rural counties; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income tax credit for sheriff's deputies employed in rural counties for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to suicide prevention in schools.
summary: Requires school districts to have suicide prevention plans and individualized student protection plans, and has OHSU convene a work group on improving them.

title: Relating to the examination of instructional materials.
summary: Requires school districts to give parents, guardians and district residents equitable access to instructional materials for examination.

title: Relating to an income tax credit for volunteer firefighters; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income tax credit for volunteer firefighters for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to county veterans' service officers; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires ODVA to distribute funds to rural counties under 30,000 population that cannot maintain county veterans' service officer operations due to budget cuts.

title: Relating to firearm purchase permits.
summary: Lets anyone holding a valid concealed handgun license automatically qualify for a firearm purchase permit.

title: Relating to sex offender information.
summary: Directs State Police to release level two sex offender information to certain entities through a department website.

title: Relating to direct admissions to certain institutions of higher education.
summary: Creates a direct admissions program at community colleges and certain public universities, and requires high schools to share graduate information only with student consent.

title: Relating to a grant program for individuals who do public service.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a DAS grant program and Restart Initiative Fund for people who serve in uniformed or public service, with grants exempt from income tax.

title: Relating to family dwelling units; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets owners of rural property outside urban growth boundaries site an additional dwelling for a relative.

title: Relating to providing for the mental health needs of the agricultural workforce; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to support operation of the AgriStress Helpline, a mental health resource for Oregon's agricultural workforce.

title: Relating to administrative rules.
summary: Directs every state agency to review its administrative rules and amend them to simplify and remove redundancy.

title: Relating to a principal Act for predator damage control districts; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets landowners form predator damage control districts that pay county costs for lethal and nonlethal predator control, with set per-acre and flat charges.

title: Relating to student readiness for post-secondary education; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a sunsetting State Board of Education pilot, with Eastern Oregon University, to help students access post-secondary education, plus a December 2026 report.

title: Relating to funding education programs for adults in custody in eastern Oregon; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money for education programs, including university degrees, for adults in custody at eastern Oregon prisons; declares emergency.

title: Relating to career and technical education.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to study career and technical education and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to capital construction.
summary: Bars agencies from changing approved capital project plans and from enforcing rules on issues already addressed in a prior approval or permit.

title: Relating to funding programs at Oregon State University; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through HECC to Oregon State University for its experiment stations, Extension Service and Forest Research Laboratory.

title: Relating to local stewardship of natural resources; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a pilot program for rural local natural resource stewardship technical assistance and planning, funded from the General Fund and sunsetting in 2031.

title: Relating to a small modular reactor energy facility demonstration project; providing that this Act shall be referred to the people for their approval or rejection.
summary: Allows EFSC to site a small modular reactor demonstration project in Umatilla County, requires microgrid capability and tribal consultation, orders a report, and refers the Act to county voters.

title: Relating to industrial development.
summary: Creates an Industrial Site Loan Fund using lottery money so the state can provide financial assistance for industrial land projects.

title: Relating to media production.
summary: Directs Business Oregon to study media production in the state and report to economic development committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the outdoor gear and apparel industry.
summary: Directs Business Oregon to study the outdoor gear and apparel industry and report to legislative economic development committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to permitting.
summary: Directs the Department of Land Conservation and Development to study permitting and report findings to economic development interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to ports.
summary: Replaces the statutory dollar cap on port grants from the Port Planning and Marketing Fund with a maximum set by agency rule, and orders a DAS study of ports.

title: Relating to semiconductors.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study semiconductors and report findings to interim economic development committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to signature research centers.
summary: Appropriates money to the Oregon Business Development Department for grants to signature research centers and requires a study of those centers.

title: Relating to the Small Business Innovation Research matching grant program.
summary: Appropriates state money to Business Oregon for matching grants to small firms under the federal SBIR program, and requires a study of the program.

title: Relating to small business.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to study small business and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to sports funding.
summary: Directs Business Oregon to study sports funding in Oregon and report its findings to interim economic development committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to direct admissions.
summary: Adds private higher learning schools to the state's direct admissions program run by the Higher Education Coordinating Commission.

title: Relating to residential rural use of lands.
summary: Allows denser residential housing on rural lands to count as a rural use and lets counties rezone qualifying rural land accordingly.

title: Relating to health care services in schools; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force to study employment duties of licensed health care providers working in schools and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the Department of Veterans' Affairs.
summary: Lets the Oregon Department of Veterans' Affairs director appoint a deputy director, subject to the Governor's approval.

title: Relating to ensuring that forced labor is not used for electric products that public bodies procure; declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Requires public bodies buying electric vehicles and solar systems to get no-forced-labor certifications, adds penalties for false certifications, and creates a sunsetting procurement task force.

title: Relating to nuclear-fueled thermal power plants; providing that this Act shall be referred to the people for their approval or rejection.
summary: Repeals Oregon's nuclear siting requirements, including the waste-repository precondition and voter approval, and refers the change to voters.

title: Relating to the constitutionality of state laws.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Government and administration
summary: Directs DOJ to review all state statutes and rules for likely unconstitutionality under the SFFA reasoning and report findings to a judiciary committee.

title: Relating to information collected by public bodies.
summary: Bars public bodies from collecting certain information about a person's views, associations or activities without that person's consent.

title: Relating to medical decision-making by individuals under 18 years of age.
summary: Limits minors who can consent to their own health care without parental permission to emancipated minors, modifying existing exceptions.

title: Relating to electric vehicle registration; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Increases the additional registration fee paid for electric vehicles and requires a three-fifths vote for the revenue-raising provision.

title: Relating to electronic records from the Oregon Health Authority for voter registration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals the transfer of certain Oregon Health Authority electronic records to the Secretary of State used for voter registration, and takes effect immediately as an emergency.

title: Relating to the regulation of public property with respect to persons experiencing homelessness; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals the 2021 state standard limiting city and county rules on homeless people using public property, including the related legal challenge and defense.

title: Relating to different treatment of persons by a public body.
summary: Bars public bodies from discriminating or giving preferential treatment based on race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin in employment, education and contracting, with exceptions.

title: Relating to voter registration.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study voter registration in Oregon and report findings to interim election committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to monthly statistical report on voter registrations.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to publish a monthly statistical report on voter registrations for each county.

title: Relating to appointments in state government.
summary: Bars state officials and agencies from discriminating or giving preferential treatment by race, sex, gender identity, color, ethnicity or national origin when appointing people to boards and commissions.

title: Relating to paid compensation claimed as a business deduction; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires taxpayers to report payee names, birth dates and SSNs for deducted compensation, and to add back amounts for payees not reported.

title: Relating to real estate professionals.
summary: Bars anyone from denying a real estate licensee MLS access merely for not belonging to a real estate association, with violations treated as unlawful trade practices.

title: Relating to gender identity.
summary: Removes the term "gender identity" from certain Oregon statutes; the text does not specify which laws or the effect.

title: Relating to unauthorized use of real property.
summary: Lets property owners have police remove unlawful occupants on declaration and fee payment, and raises penalties for property theft.

title: Relating to waiver of tuition.
summary: Prohibits reducing a qualified student's tuition waiver by the amount of certain other student aid received.

title: Relating to providing proof of United States citizenship when registering to vote.
summary: Requires proof of U.S. citizenship for first-time voter registrants and repeals the state's electronic voter registration system.

title: Relating to cancellation of voter registration.
summary: Requires county clerks to cancel a voter's registration if the voter registers in another county, surrenders an Oregon license for another state's, or is excused from jury duty for non-citizenship.

title: Relating to providing proof of United States citizenship when registering to vote; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote, repeals the electronic voter registration system, and takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.

title: Relating to homelessness; declaring an emergency.
summary: Restores the pre-2021 law on removing homeless camps by repealing HB 3124's changes, and takes effect immediately.

title: Relating to massage therapy.
summary: Bans massage facilities from locating within 1,000 feet of a school or similar building.

title: Relating to boats.
summary: Requires the State Marine Board to study motorboat safe operation and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to funding for students eligible for special education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Increases yearly transfers from the State School Fund to the High Cost Disabilities Account for special education, funded by a General Fund appropriation.

title: Relating to support programs in recovery schools.
summary: Requires recovery schools to provide peer group support for students, and directs the State Board of Education to adopt a related requirement.

title: Relating to child care impact statements.
summary: Requires the Department of Early Learning and Care to prepare child care impact statements on request, and the Secretary of State to print them in the voters' pamphlet.

title: Relating to funding for students eligible for special education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Increases state money for school districts serving students with disabilities, through higher High Cost Disabilities Account transfers and a broader eligibility percentage, funded from the General Fund.

title: Relating to financial support for child care resource and referral entities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a DELC grant program for child care resource and referral entities to help families access child care, funded by a General Fund appropriation.

title: Relating to education; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes the requirement that a school district's educational equity advisory committee advise the board and limits that committee's duties; takes effect immediately.

title: Relating to legislative oversight of executive branch actions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a legislative oversight officer who can audit executive agencies, investigate public complaints, and report to the Joint Legislative Audit Committee starting January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to home occupations on lands zoned for resource uses.
summary: Allows homeowners on farm- and forest-zoned land to run businesses from their homes, including owners who do not live on the property.

title: Relating to the Sexual Assault Victims' Emergency Medical Response Fund.
summary: Modifies provisions of the Sexual Assault Victims' Emergency Medical Response Fund; the summary gives no detail on the changes.

title: Relating to the Rare Disease Advisory Council.
summary: Creates a Rare Disease Advisory Council that must report biennially to the Governor and legislative committees with policy recommendations.

title: Relating to reporting requirements for public universities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to study public university reporting requirements and propose cutting unnecessary or duplicative ones.

title: Relating to compensation of state employees.
summary: Starting January 2028, caps pay at certain state agencies at 10 times their lowest full-time salary, allows exemption requests, and requires agency reporting to the Legislative Fiscal Officer.

title: Relating to local courts; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Updates and reorganizes appeal procedures from justice and municipal courts that are not courts of record, with a separate municipal appeal statute, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to remote location testimony.
summary: Changes notice and facility/technology requirements for motions allowing remote location testimony in legislative proceedings.

title: Relating to the periods of time allowed for filing complaints with the Construction Contractors Board; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Revises some time limits for filing complaints with the Construction Contractors Board; the direction of the change is not stated.

title: Relating to small claims.
summary: Gives defendants more time to respond to small claims and clarifies that jury-trial claim amounts include certain interest, fees and costs.

title: Relating to correction of erroneous material in Oregon law.
summary: Makes technical, nonsubstantive corrections to Oregon law, including grammar, punctuation, and conforming language to existing statutes.

title: Relating to the authority of supervising officers; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Makes unlawful departure from a parole or probation officer's custody the crime of escape, and lets those officers view DMV driver license photos.

title: Relating to information sharing between state and federal authorities.
summary: Allows law enforcement to share information for international extraditions and bars agreements sharing data on people in custody with federal immigration authorities.

title: Relating to mental illness.
summary: Changes when courts may civilly commit people with mental illness, defining dangerous to self, dangerous to others, and need for treatment, including chronic mental disorder.

title: Relating to discovery.
summary: Allows a district attorney to charge defendants a fee, based on costs, before providing discovery.

title: Relating to criminal procedure.
summary: Changes criminal procedure: sets a timing limit on indictments, allows grand jury recordings in challenges, requires motions for warrantless-search evidence, and lets courts modify preventive detention.

title: Relating to mental health; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice; Health care
summary: Expands Oregon State Hospital capacity, adds jail-based and community restoration options for defendants unfit to proceed, and modifies extremely dangerous person commitment criteria.

title: Relating to guilty except for insanity; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes when a person may be found guilty except for insanity; the digest gives no detail on the change, and it takes effect on passage or the 91st day after sine die.

title: Relating to juvenile offenders.
summary: Shifts the burden of proof to the state in hearings on whether juvenile offenders must register as sex offenders.

title: Relating to criminal procedures; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Revises criminal procedure: repeals a harassment manner, lets phlebotomists draw blood for DUI evidence, and removes a prosecutor's election deadline.

title: Relating to crime victims who are under 18 years of age; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands criminal offenses and penalties involving minor victims in familial-relationship sexual crimes and raises the age for felony assault and strangulation.

title: Relating to adults in custody.
summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to study adults in custody and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to fitness to proceed.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study fitness to proceed and report to interim legislative committees by December 31, 2026.

title: Relating to animals.
summary: Directs the State Department of Agriculture to study animal-related rules and report to natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to animal cruelty.
summary: Directs the State Department of Agriculture to study animal cruelty and report to natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to attorneys.
summary: Directs the Oregon State Bar to study attorneys and report findings to judiciary interim committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to behavioral health.

title: Relating to universal representation; declaring an emergency.

summary: Creates an Agricultural Workforce Labor Standards Board to set minimum working standards, training requirements, and remedies for farmworkers.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Higher Education Coordinating Commission for distribution to REAP, Inc.'s Young Entrepreneurs Program, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to fire safety systems in public buildings; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires periodic inspection and testing of fire and smoke dampers and smoke control systems in public buildings, with penalties, and worker benefits for publicly funded repairs.

summary: Requires Portland State University and the Legislative Policy and Research Director to study farmworker labor standards and report to legislative committees; makes no rule changes.

title: Relating to rural health care tax credits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands the rural health care income tax credit to cover pharmacist services in rural communities, with certification criteria set by the Office of Rural Health.

title: Relating to qualification for the Oregon Promise program.
summary: Loosens Oregon Promise grant eligibility by dropping the high school, GPA and timing requirements and allowing enrollment in applied baccalaureate or BSN programs.

title: Relating to security on campus.
summary: Requires public university boards to ensure background checks from DPSST are requested and reviewed before commissioning special campus security officers, and lets DPSST share applicant information.

title: Relating to violence in health care settings; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates workplace violence prevention requirements for health care employers, mandates incident data reporting, and funds a grant program for prevention efforts.

title: Relating to qualification for the Oregon Promise program; declaring an emergency.
summary: Keeps Oregon Promise grant eligibility for students who join approved career and technical student organizations or career groups before attending community college, applying to recent enrollees.

title: Relating to a social worker licensure compact; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Joins the interstate Social Work Licensure Compact, letting multistate licensees practice in Oregon without a separate Oregon license.

title: Relating to sentencing; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Makes the Family Sentencing Alternative pilot permanent, renames it, and widens eligibility to all sentences eligible for downward dispositional departure.

title: Relating to Portland State University designation.

title: Relating to octopus.

title: Relating to activities regulated by the State Marine Board; and prescribing an effective date.

title: Relating to the insurance rate review process.

title: Relating to building codes applicable to essential facilities; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires DCBS to adopt fireproofing rules for new essential facilities and lets state boards set licensing standards for masonry and fireproofing work.

title: Relating to conditions of development.
summary: Bars cities and counties from requiring frontage improvements like roads, curbs, and sidewalks as conditions for certain building permits or zone changes, with a population-based phase-in.

title: Relating to the Oregon Vehicle Industry Board; declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Creates the Oregon Vehicle Industry Board and transfers ODOT's dealer and dismantler regulation duties to it, starting January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to trip permits.
summary: Allows vehicle dealers to issue a 30-day recreational vehicle trip permit to out-of-state buyers who will not title the RV in Oregon.

title: Relating to petroleum contamination; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force on containing petroleum contamination to study the issue and report recommendations to a transportation interim committee by December 15, 2026.

title: Relating to law enforcement agencies.
summary: Requires large municipal police agencies, serving 350,000 or more people, to staff patrol vehicles with at least two officers, with an exception.

title: Relating to motor vehicles.
summary: Allows car dealers to issue temporary registration permits for vehicles lacking proof of pollution control compliance, and requires written notice to buyers that plates and stickers need that proof.

title: Relating to housing for veterans.
summary: Directs the Department of Veterans' Affairs to create a program acquiring residential properties to rent to housing-insecure veterans, possibly via private partners.

title: Relating to the establishment of Central Oregon University; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates Central Oregon University as a separate public university, distinct from Oregon State University, effective 91 days after session adjournment.

title: Relating to pretrial detainees; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires each county to operate a jointly managed sheriff and mental health facility to house and treat pretrial detainees with behavioral health disorders or developmental disabilities.

title: Relating to servicemembers.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Creates two new crimes concerning servicemembers: criminal defamation and unlawful appropriation of a servicemember's identity, each punishable by up to 364 days and a $6,250 fine.

title: Relating to search and rescue.
summary: Requires private persons conducting search and rescue to first make specified disclosures to the missing person's family and notify county sheriffs.

title: Relating to part-time faculty at community colleges; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires community colleges to pay part-time faculty a set percentage of full-time pay for comparable courses and appropriates salary equity funds.

title: Relating to education for children with a traumatic brain injury.
summary: Broadens the definition of brain injury as a health impairment, making more children with brain injuries eligible for special education.

title: Relating to highly automated vehicles; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Permits testing of highly automated vehicles on Oregon highways, including without an onboard operator, under a DOT testing permit with insurance, reporting and rule requirements.

title: Relating to open enrollment.
summary: Allows students to attend schools in a nonresident district and establishes an open enrollment process, with the receiving district's consent required.

title: Relating to school business professionals; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to the Department of Education, passed to OASBO, to create a statewide program for school business professionals; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to a task force on high school diploma requirements; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force to study and report on high school diploma requirements, without changing any requirements now.

title: Relating to funding for an after-school program at the Oregon Institute of Technology; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to Oregon Institute of Technology for an after-school program, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to an interstate dental professionals compact; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Joins an interstate dental compact so dentists and hygienists licensed in other member states can practice in Oregon without an Oregon license.

title: Relating to juvenile records; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands juvenile record expunction eligibility, including felonies, requires expunction steps for some violent misdemeanors, and increases Oregon Youth Authority funding for processing.

title: Relating to services for medically complex Oregonians.
summary: Directs state agencies to study complex-needs services and creates a home care worker certification program, without changing eligibility or service rules.

title: Relating to neonicotinoid pesticides; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Restricts certain neonicotinoid pesticides to restricted-use status and bans their application on residential landscapes, with exceptions, operative January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to certifications required for work with fenestration systems in public buildings; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires contractors doing glass and window work on publicly funded projects in public buildings to hold national glazing certifications and employ a certified technician.

title: Relating to funding for career and technical education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Education for career and technical education student organization grants and high-wage job activities.

title: Relating to services for young children with special needs.
summary: Creates an advisory committee to study early intervention and early childhood special education service levels and report recommendations by September 2026, sunsetting January 2027.

title: Relating to documents issued by the Department of Transportation.
summary: Lets people with disabilities that impair police communication request a notation on their ODOT driver or ID card, after health professional verification.

title: Relating to integrated pest management.
summary: Requires school integrated pest management plans to be reviewed every five years and posted publicly online, along with a low-impact pesticide list.

title: Relating to cytomegalovirus; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to set a newborn cytomegalovirus screening protocol by rule, ending that requirement if CMV joins the bloodspot panel.

title: Relating to re-enrollment of residents; declaring an emergency.
summary: Funds the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to grant an organization that runs a statewide strategy to re-enroll residents in certain programs.

title: Relating to a grant program for improving the health and safety of agricultural workforce housing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands eligibility for an agricultural workforce housing health and safety grant program by removing the exclusion of certain temporary agricultural workers; effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to the application of a prevailing rate of wage to off-site custom work for use in public works; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Applies the prevailing wage requirement to off-site custom work fabricated for a specific public works project.

title: Relating to the competitiveness of the Oregon food sector; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Agriculture Department to create a program promoting Oregon-made food sold to out-of-state buyers, study food processing competitiveness, and appropriates General Fund money.

title: Relating to the Health Insurance Mandate Review Advisory Committee; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an interim committee to review proposed health insurance mandates and report findings to the Legislature, sunsetting June 30, 2028.

title: Relating to plant-based foods.
summary: Requires disclosure labels on meat- or egg-suggesting plant-based and manufactured-protein foods, and bars state purchasing and nutrition program eligibility for them.

title: Relating to administrative law.
summary: Modifies unspecified provisions of administrative law governing state agency actions; the summary gives no concrete changes.

title: Relating to levees; declaring an emergency.
summary: Authorizes lottery bond issuance to deposit funds into a Levee Project Grant Fund for levee projects, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to a registry for union representatives.
summary: Requires the Employment Relations Board to create a registry and bars anyone from acting as a union representative unless registered, with civil penalties.

title: Relating to duties of the Oregon Health and Science University Board of Directors.
summary: Requires the OHSU board to include specified people in presidential search and hiring committees and to let campus labor representatives communicate with the board on request.

title: Relating to camping sites on public property; declaring an emergency.
summary: Clarifies that homeless individuals' personal property storage protections apply when property is removed from a public camping site; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to traffic stops.
summary: Repeals the limit on police initiating traffic stops for certain vehicle lighting offenses, widening when officers may stop drivers.

title: Relating to homeownership goal; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Establishes a statewide homeownership goal and requires the Housing and Community Services Department to track progress toward it.

title: Relating to nurse faculty compensation.
summary: Directs the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to study nurse faculty compensation and report to legislative interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to emergency response.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Emergency Management to create and maintain a registry of people willing to provide emergency response services.

title: Relating to emergency preparedness; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires health facilities, providers, public health and safety agencies to maintain 120-day operating capacity under a 25 percent mortality scenario, with agency reporting.

title: Relating to disaster response.
summary: Creates a matching fund letting the state emergency management agency give grants to local governments for federal disaster aid match and disaster response.

title: Relating to an income tax surtax to fund emergency preparedness; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Creates a personal income tax surtax, with proceeds transferred to the Resiliency Grant Fund for emergency preparedness, starting tax year 2026.

title: Relating to redistricting.
summary: Requires adjusting census population data to count incarcerated adults at their pre-incarceration addresses, and uses that adjusted data for redistricting.

title: Relating to patents resulting from public funding of post-secondary institutions of education.
summary: Directs the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to study what rate of return Oregon should receive from patents built on public university and college funding.

title: Relating to businesses regulated by the Department of Transportation.
