summary: Extends dismantler certificate validity by one year, raises the certificate fee, and requires two days' notice before DOT inspects dealer and dismantler records, except for complaints.

title: Relating to testing and inspecting fire safety systems in public buildings; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires owners of public buildings to periodically test and inspect fire and smoke dampers and smoke control systems, with inspector qualifications, compliance certificates, and civil penalties.

title: Relating to workforce development; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Transfers workforce development duties from HECC to BOLI, creates a BOLI workforce office, account and Oregon Workforce Corps, and renames community college office.

title: Relating to a warrantor's obligations with respect to extended warranties for motor vehicles; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars warrantors and sellers from taking fees for motor vehicle extended warranties unless the vehicle qualifies, requires information gathering, mandates coverage if fees were taken, and enforces violations under the Unlawful Trade Practices Act.

title: Relating to participant eligibility in the Address Confidentiality Program; declaring an emergency.
summary: Adds victims of child abduction to the Address Confidentiality Program, allowing them to shield their addresses. Takes effect on passage as an emergency measure.

title: Relating to emergency benefits for independent contractors; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a worker-funded program paying unemployment-style emergency benefits to independent contractors during a governor-declared state of emergency, operative January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to the Judicial Department; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Raises state court judge salaries and gives the Chief Justice authority to set rules promoting judicial accountability and accessible justice services.

title: Relating to funding for calamity preparation; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Imposes income tax surtax and alternative minimum tax to fund disaster resiliency, creating Shaky Day and Resiliency Requirements funds.

title: Relating to support loans for small business activity in this state; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Treasurer-run loan program for small businesses unable to operate normally during emergencies, funded by bonds, with a new fund.

title: Relating to higher education.
summary: Lets public universities offer PhDs with HECC approval, caps some at five programs until 2044, and bars state aid to fraud-found online schools.

title: Relating to vehicle dealers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires ODOT to notify car dealers of missing or incomplete registration or titling papers, allow them to fix errors, and study processing delays.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Authorizes state general obligation bonds to finance construction of a veterans' home in Roseburg, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to vehicle dealers.
summary: Lets vehicle dealers submit vehicle-related documents in person at Department of Transportation field offices.

title: Relating to methods of paying for post-secondary education; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Guaranteed Opportunity Program, operative in 2045, under which students repay funds received for higher education, and sets up a task force and implementation fund.

title: Relating to emergency preparedness.
summary: Expands the duties of the State Resilience Officer, a state emergency preparedness role; the text gives no details.

title: Relating to a public transit incentive surcharge.
summary: Lets cities and counties add a public transit incentive surcharge on top of parking fines for motor vehicle parking violations.

title: Relating to the use of integrators for vehicle-related transactions.
summary: Directs ODOT to enter agreements with qualified providers, or integrators, to help perform certain department functions, including vehicle-related transactions.

title: Relating to backup power sources.
summary: Directs DHS to adopt rules requiring long-term care, dialysis and residential facilities to acquire and maintain backup power sources for outages.

title: Relating to corporate registration for federal selective service.
summary: Requires corporations to annually file an affidavit attesting Selective Service registration, or disallows their state tax subtractions and credits if they do not.

title: Relating to the inclusion of ports in strategic investment program agreements; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits which types of port districts must be parties to strategic investment program agreements for eligible projects in their territory.

title: Relating to the Columbia corridor flood safety project.
summary: Authorizes state lottery bond sales to fund flood safety projects in the Columbia corridor in Multnomah County.

title: Relating to limitations on post-legislative service activity.
summary: Extends restrictions on former legislators, barring compensation for advocacy on policy or funding changes for one year after leaving office.

title: Relating to member data under the Public Employees Retirement System; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires PERS to include information about overtime use in calculating a retiring member's final average salary in the member's letter.

title: Relating to schools; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to fund grants for school-based health centers and mental health and substance use services, adjust grants for inflation, and study reimbursement.

title: Relating to incentives for beginning agricultural operators; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a State Department of Agriculture incentive program and fund for beginning farmers and ranchers, and appropriates money to the fund.

title: Relating to funding for agricultural education.
summary: Lets the Department of Education use existing Fund for Student Success and Statewide Education Initiatives moneys for grants supporting agricultural science and technology programs.

title: Relating to tax credits for crop donation; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Raises the percentage of wholesale crop value that donors may claim as a tax credit for crop donations, starting tax years on or after January 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the concealment of a person's face during criminal activity.
summary: Requires courts to treat a defendant's concealing their face during a crime, to avoid arrest or facilitate the offense, as an aggravating sentencing factor.

title: Relating to the Oregon Public Defense Commission; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Authorizes the Oregon Public Defense Commission to contract with specified individuals and entities to provide public defense services; takes effect 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to individual development accounts.
summary: Raises the annual cap on tax credits for donations to individual development accounts and aligns the donation deadline with the credit's sunset date.

title: Relating to education of students in voluntary placements.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study how school districts serve students voluntarily placed outside their homes, reporting findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to student transportation.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to study ways to help school districts transport students living outside district boundaries, reporting by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the use of leaded fuel; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bans leaded fuel use at race tracks in cities with 500,000 or more people, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to motor vehicles.
summary: Allows vehicle owners to request a registration card notation that the owner or driver has limited English proficiency.

title: Relating to education outcomes.
summary: Directs the Legislative Policy and Research Director to study education outcomes and report findings to interim education committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to public health testing.
summary: Requires Oregon providers to ensure newborn bloodspot screening and reporting, and creates an exemption for parents who object for religious or philosophical reasons.

title: Relating to persons with disabilities.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Labor and employment
summary: Extends disability anti-discrimination rules to local governments, bars screening out disabled workers with physical requirements, guarantees union representation in accommodation talks, and creates mediation.

title: Relating to adult entertainment establishments; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Labor and employment
summary: Requires adult entertainment establishments to register with the state, sets health and safety duties and leasing-agreement terms, and has the state offer entertainer training.

title: Relating to exclusions of insurance coverage for veterinary services on the basis of a preexisting condition; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars insurers from excluding, limiting or reducing pet veterinary coverage based on a pet's preexisting condition, even if the owner knew of it.

title: Relating to benefit payments during employer compliance investigations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets a timeline for paying temporary disability workers' compensation to workers while their employer is under a compliance investigation, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to disclosures of certain information concerning employment-related matters; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires pay and benefit information in job postings, adds employer recordkeeping, and bars retaliation against employees who exercise related rights.

title: Relating to adults in custody; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to give some incarcerated adults access to specific online education programs; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the use of nursing titles.
summary: Prohibits nonhuman entities, such as AI systems, from using nursing titles and abbreviations.

title: Relating to the bridge across Columbia Boulevard; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money through ODOT to Portland to design a bridge across Columbia Boulevard and requires a report on seeking federal funds.

title: Relating to the Task Force on Improving Safety in Health Care Settings.
summary: Creates a task force on improving safety in health care settings and requires it to report to a legislative interim health committee by December 15, 2026.

title: Relating to community health worker services; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs OHA to run a two-year, two-county demonstration testing expanded paid services by community health workers, sunsetting in 2030.

title: Relating to revenue estimates; declaring an emergency; providing for revenue estimate modification that requires approval by a two-thirds majority.
summary: Directs the difference between collected and estimated 2023 revenue to disaster preparedness and PERS unfunded liability; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to emergency preparedness; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Authorizes general obligation bonds to fund the emergency preparedness equipment grant program.

title: Relating to viewpoint discrimination in nonresidential tenancies.
summary: Prohibits nonresidential landlords from barring or limiting tenancies based on a tenant's viewpoint.

title: Relating to funding public safety; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force to plan a statewide public safety funding authority, effective only if a constitutional amendment (HJR 8) is approved by voters.

title: Relating to international economic relations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the state business development department to open trade centers in Taiwan and Vietnam and allows up to five more abroad.

title: Relating to workloads in the Department of Human Services.
summary: Requires ODHS to study aging and disability services case manager workloads and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to tourism districts.
summary: Creates tourism districts, lets them seek grants and temporary land use and building code waivers, and exempts designated live performances from unlawful recording crime.

title: Relating to quality assurance in the Judicial Department.
summary: Creates an independent Office of Quality Assurance in the Judicial Department to audit circuit court noncriminal proceedings and report judicial bias or misconduct.

title: Relating to emergency volunteers; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs ODEM to create a program reimbursing nongovernmental disaster response groups for volunteer-related costs, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to county disaster recovery; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs ODEM to create a grant program so counties can hire disaster mitigation and recovery manager positions, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to traffic violations.
summary: Creates an offense for sleeping in a highway danger zone, punishable by a maximum fine of $250.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Creates the Oregon Individual Assistance Grant Account and continuously appropriates its funds to the Emergency Management department for aid to individuals and households after emergencies.

title: Relating to programs in the Department of Human Services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a legislative work group to develop a multi-sector plan for aging under the Department of Human Services, with three reports due through 2026.

title: Relating to a grant program to prevent fuel spills.
summary: Directs DEQ to create a grant program to prevent fuel spills at fuel facilities and establishes a Fuel Spills Mitigation Fund.

title: Relating to justice courts.
summary: Removes the restriction barring justice courts within 50 driving miles of a circuit court from becoming courts of record.

title: Relating to mitigation planning; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to DLCD for natural hazards mitigation planning and states intent to use it to secure federal matching funds.

title: Relating to philanthropic liaisons for emergency preparedness; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Emergency Management to contract with philanthropic liaisons to help acquire and use resources for emergencies.

title: Relating to emergency management; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs OBDD to create a small business emergency registry, send emergency information, and run grants to strengthen small business emergency resilience.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Creates the Oregon Disaster Recovery Authority, which the Governor can activate during an emergency to coordinate recovery, aid, and temporary hiring of state personnel.

title: Relating to justice of the peace districts.
summary: Removes state prohibitions that barred counties from creating justice of the peace districts that include a county seat or a city with a circuit court.

title: Relating to the emergency alert system; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to counties and Oregon Public Broadcasting to upgrade emergency alert system equipment, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to fishing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Fish and Wildlife grant program for recreational fishing facilities within urban growth boundaries, funded by lottery bond proceeds, sunsetting in 2033.

title: Relating to supervised parenting time.
summary: Bars unsupervised parenting time for a parent who commits certain gun-related acts or abuse involving a firearm.

title: Relating to discounted mortgage loans for installation of energy generation improvements.
summary: Directs state agencies to study discounted home mortgage loans for renewable energy systems and report findings to the legislature by September 2026.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Emergency Management to study its operations, recommend improvements, and report by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to mining.
summary: Exempts certain sample wells from onshore exploration permits and bars extra conditions on permit transfers and certain land use compatibility statements for mining.

title: Relating to innovative water technology; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study innovative water technologies, report by September 2026, and receives General Fund money for the study.

title: Relating to juries.
summary: Bars members of the Legislative Assembly from serving on juries.

title: Relating to firearm purchase permits.
summary: Makes anyone holding a valid concealed handgun license automatically qualified for a firearm purchase permit.

title: Relating to Federal Home Loan Banks; declaring an emergency.
summary: Bars courts from stopping Federal Home Loan Banks from enforcing collateral against insolvent insurer-members, and shields their security-agreement transfers from receiver clawback.

title: Relating to elections.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to study elections and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026; the study sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to squatting.
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to study squatting and report findings to housing-related interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to public safety training.
summary: Requires DPSST to study adding deflection training to police officer training and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the State Department of Geology and Mineral Industries.
summary: Changes some DOGAMI fees and requires an annual report to the legislature on the mined land regulatory and reclamation program.

title: Relating to compensation for accrued leave upon termination of employment.
summary: Requires employers offering sick, vacation or personal leave to pay employees for all earned but unused accrued leave when employment ends.

title: Relating to requirements concerning on-call shifts.
summary: Requires employers to pay employees for on-call and standby time and to post schedules at least 14 days ahead, including on-call shifts.

title: Relating to immigration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates state grants to nonprofits helping noncitizens change immigration status or obtain permanent residency, with a General Fund appropriation and an emergency effective date.

title: Relating to services provided by registered nurses; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets registered nurses bill for certain services without a primary care provider's order, and bars OHA from requiring such orders for Medicaid care management reimbursement.

title: Relating to sick leave for mental health.
summary: Clarifies that sick leave may be used for mental health conditions and mental well-being, and directs the labor commissioner to create training materials and adopt retaliation rules.

title: Relating to workers' compensation.
summary: Lets injured workers receive permanent disability payments and appeal claim closures while in training, and delays training selection until claim closure is final.

title: Relating to the amount a hospital spends for individuals to replace employees during a labor dispute.
summary: Requires hospitals to report how much they spend on replacement workers during strikes or lockouts.

title: Relating to actions by a hospital on labor organizing.
summary: Requires hospitals to report how much money they spend on strategies to discourage, avoid or prevent labor organizing.

title: Relating to the provision of care by health care facilities.
summary: Requires health care facilities to create complaint procedures for staff about unsafe supplies or equipment, retain complaints 10 years, and notify patients and provide copies.

title: Relating to public transportation service providers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Modifies the definition of "qualified entity" for Statewide Transportation Improvement Fund distributions to public transit providers, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Requires Oregon hospitals and hospital systems to publicly disclose certain financial data annually, with OHA able to impose penalties for noncompliance.

title: Relating to the Port of Morrow.
summary: Adds two Governor-appointed commissioners to the Port of Morrow board, requiring trade-sector knowledge or experience.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Requires Oregon hospitals and hospital systems to publicly disclose their prior-year expenses, with OHA able to penalize noncompliance.

title: Relating to litigation costs for prevailing claimants.
summary: Removes or raises the cap on attorney fees and litigation costs awarded to workers who win workers' compensation claim denial disputes.

title: Relating to professional employer organizations under workers' compensation law; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Renames 'worker leasing company' as 'professional employer organization' in workers' compensation law and describes how PEO agreements allocate employer duties. No substantive change.

title: Relating to the time frame for allowing changes to determined claims in the Upper Klamath Basin.
summary: Extends the time window for changes to Upper Klamath Basin water rights, letting the Water Resources Department approve leases and temporary transfers until a final court decree.

title: Relating to lump sum payments of permanent partial disability awards.
summary: Specifies when insurers must make lump sum payments of permanent partial disability awards, such as after a waived reconsideration or a final award.

title: Relating to fees concerning water; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Increases certain water-related fees and declares an emergency, effective on passage.

title: Relating to the Psychiatric Security Review Board; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Children and families; Government and administration
summary: Eliminates the Psychiatric Security Review Board's juvenile panel and restructures the board into a single five-member panel with an alternate member.

title: Relating to food establishment licenses.
summary: Makes permanent the Department of Agriculture's authority to raise food establishment license fees by up to three percent annually.

title: Relating to license fees for commercial instruments.
summary: Makes permanent the Agriculture Department's authority to raise commercial weighing and measuring instrument license fees up to 3% yearly, plus temporary extra increases.

title: Relating to the liability of the Psychiatric Security Review Board.
summary: Grants the Psychiatric Security Review Board immunity from liability for certain functions and for acts of persons under its jurisdiction, except wanton and willful misconduct.

title: Relating to fees concerning wells; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Increases certain fees related to wells and declares an emergency, effective on passage.

title: Relating to pesticide registration fees; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises the maximum fee the state may charge to register a pesticide, with the change taking effect 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to the Oregon Public Defense Commission.
summary: Directs the Oregon Public Defense Commission to study law changes needed to implement SB 337 (2023) and report to lawmakers by May 1, 2026.

title: Relating to encouragement of reading in young children; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a free monthly book program for eligible young children, administered by the Department of Early Learning and Care and funded through a new account.

title: Relating to individually identifiable health information disclosure.
summary: Exempts individually identifiable health information held by the Psychiatric Security Review Board from public records disclosure, with limited exceptions for release.

title: Relating to water right retirement under the Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a groundwater conservation match fund in the State Treasury for water right retirement under CREP and appropriates money to it.

title: Relating to licensing of child care facilities; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets the early learning department waive certain certified child care facility requirements for good cause and directs rules setting children-per-age-group limits for family child care homes.

title: Relating to tribal early learning services.
summary: Creates a statewide tribal early learning plan, a grant program for Oregon's nine tribes, an advisory alliance, and a continuously appropriated fund.

title: Relating to forest products harvest taxation; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Extends three taxes on harvesting merchantable forest products from forestlands and sets their new rates.

title: Relating to forestland closures.
summary: Removes the permit-based closure of forestland due to fire danger, eliminating that closure mechanism.

title: Relating to medical assistance.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study potential changes to the CCO quality incentive program and report findings by September 2026.

title: Relating to fire protection enforcement procedures.
summary: Changes the State Forester's citation standard for fire protection violations from reasonable grounds to probable cause.

title: Relating to compensation ratios in certain nonprofit corporations; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars public agencies from accepting contract bids from nonprofits whose highest-to-lowest pay ratio exceeds 50 to 1, with disclosure and termination penalties.

title: Relating to disclosure of information from executives of businesses receiving public moneys.
summary: Requires executives and directors of businesses receiving $10 million or more in public money over five years to file statements of economic interest.

title: Relating to a report on Canis lupus; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Department of Fish and Wildlife to report on how changes in gray wolf protections over the past decade affected Oregon wolf populations.

title: Relating to patents for inventions in public high schools in this state.
summary: Lets state agencies, including the Oregon Business Development Department, hire attorneys to patent school inventions and take or waive ownership of them.

title: Relating to prescription drugs for veterans.
summary: Requires Medicaid coordinated care organization drug outlets to dispense a free seven-day supply to disabled veterans who cannot obtain the drug through the VA.

title: Relating to preferences for veterans in public employment selection processes.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Government and administration
summary: Limits veterans' hiring preference for public jobs, requires written reasons for some non-hires, and requires BOLI exhaustion before veterans sue for employment discrimination.

title: Relating to veterans' courts.
summary: Creates a grant program, run by the Department of Veterans' Affairs, to fund Oregon counties' veterans' courts.

title: Relating to goods necessary to address emergencies.
summary: Lets the Governor require persons in Oregon to accept and fulfill orders for certain goods during an emergency, with limited grounds to refuse and liability protection.

title: Relating to veterans.
summary: Requires public colleges to grant 12 academic credits to veterans who served two or more years on active duty.

title: Relating to veterans.
summary: Directs the Department of Veterans' Affairs to study its operations, make improvement recommendations, and report findings by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to materials for local water projects; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars local governments from restricting pipe material choices for state-funded water projects that meet specified industry standards.

title: Relating to police oversight boards.
summary: Requires law enforcement agencies to designate a police oversight board that annually reviews agency policies and reports to DPSST.

title: Relating to preferences for veterans in public employment.
summary: Requires veterans to show preference eligibility when applying for civil service jobs and requires public employers to explain in writing any decision not to interview a veteran.

title: Relating to identification of law enforcement.
summary: Extends the existing crowd-management officer identification requirement to cities with over 5,000 residents, down from 60,000.

title: Relating to the military.
summary: Directs the Oregon Military Department to study its operations, recommend improvements, and report its findings by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to veterans; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Veterans' Affairs to fill certain positions and allocates lottery funds from the Veterans' Services Fund for specified veterans' purposes.

title: Relating to statements of economic interest.
summary: Requires heads and board members of nonprofits and businesses that received or sought $1 million or more in state funds to file statements of economic interest.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Emergency Management to study its operations, recommend improvements, and report by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to veterans.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Veterans' Affairs to study veterans and its own operations, then report recommendations by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to the military; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Oregon Military Department to staff the Service Member and Family Support Program for 2025-27.

title: Relating to designated representatives.
summary: Modifies PERS retirement benefit provisions for public employees who serve as designated union representatives while on release time.

title: Relating to instructors at institutions of higher education.
summary: Requires community colleges and public universities to meet minimum full-time instructor credit-hour shares and report compliance to HECC, which reports to the Legislature.

title: Relating to childcare programs for people with governmental business; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money through DAS to an organization and Polk County to run free drop-in childcare for people with government business.

title: Relating to veterans' benefits.
summary: Creates a Veterans' Benefits Economic Development Fund, funded partly by lottery moneys, to help veterans and families apply for federal and state benefits; sunsets 2035.

title: Relating to emergency management; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates statewide emergency preparedness offices, a training commission and facility office, and a task force, and requires agency liaisons and county preparedness reports.

title: Relating to veterans; declaring an emergency.
topics: Education; Government and administration; Health care
summary: Expands the Oregon Department of Veterans' Affairs with new positions, suicide prevention and workforce pilots, a higher education grant cap, and a funding goal.

title: Relating to refinancing options for veterans.
summary: Creates a veterans mortgage refinancing loan and credit guarantee program, funded by a new Veterans Refinancing and Reintegration Services Fund backed by state budget requests.

title: Relating to subtractions for start-up expenditures; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a subtraction from taxable income for start-up expenditures for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to nonprofit corporations that receive public funds; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires nonprofits receiving public funds to follow open meetings and public records laws, post proposed budgets, submit to audits, and meet government ethics standards.

title: Relating to law enforcement.
summary: Requires DPSST to study issues facing law enforcement agencies and report findings to judiciary interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to nepotism laws for members of the Legislative Assembly.
summary: Requires legislators to disclose to the Oregon Government Ethics Commission any relatives or household members on their personal staff and their salaries.

title: Relating to critical infrastructure.
summary: Adds terrestrial cable and wire communication facilities to the definition of critical infrastructure for the domestic terrorism crimes.

title: Relating to emergency preparedness public contracting preferences.
summary: Creates an ODEM certification program for businesses as emergency preparedness partners and directs agencies to prefer certified bidders in contracting.

title: Relating to urban growth boundaries.
summary: Replaces an old industrial siting program with a new one letting cities bring certain lands into urban growth boundaries for light industrial and open space uses.

title: Relating to building code requirements for school facilities within the seismic hazard region; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the building code director to adopt amendments mandating specific seismic design features for new school facilities in a designated seismic hazard region.

title: Relating to public exchange stations.
summary: Directs the Department of State Police to establish public exchange locations, subject to unspecified requirements.

title: Relating to veteran housing services.
summary: Creates a lottery-funded Veterans Housing Construction Cost Reduction Fund so ODVA can give nonprofits grants for unexpected costs of repurposing buildings for veteran housing.

title: Relating to air ambulance services; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an ODEM air ambulance readiness program that subsidizes qualified air ambulance bases to offset operating costs, with biennial reporting to health committees.

title: Relating to emergency management; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates statewide emergency preparedness offices, commissions and training facilities, authorizes lottery bonds for public safety grants, requires county reports, and delays the emergency notification system transfer.

title: Relating to services for veterans.
summary: Requires ODVA's budget requests and the Governor's and Legislature's budgets to fund the veterans department at a set level, unless economic conditions are poor.

title: Relating to the military.
summary: Directs the Oregon Military Department to study its operations, recommend improvements, and report its findings by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to the military.
summary: Directs the Oregon Military Department to study its operations, make recommendations, and report findings by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to interest-only loans to assist small businesses to increase employment.
summary: Creates a state interest-only loan program for small businesses with up to 50 employees to hire, with a fund and appropriation for administration.

title: Relating to capital gains treatment of affordable housing property; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts capital gains from selling affordable housing property in low-income census tracts from Oregon income tax for tax years 2025 through 2030.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Emergency Management to study its operations and report recommendations by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to emergency management; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to state agencies for emergency management and fire protection purposes for the 2025-27 biennium, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to labor organization representation.
summary: Bars compulsory fees from non-union public employees, allowing voluntary in-lieu-of-dues payments only, and makes agreements requiring such payments an unfair labor practice.

title: Relating to veterans.
summary: Directs the Department of Veterans' Affairs to study veterans and its own operations, then report recommendations by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Directs courts to consider it an aggravating sentencing factor when a defendant takes advantage of a natural-disaster emergency or evacuation.

title: Relating to services provided by school districts.
summary: Requires school districts to hold back contract retainage on service contracts required by state or federal law and to keep contract payments until completion.

title: Relating to campaign reform.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Elections and voting
summary: Creates penalties for false campaign statements and a Campaign Review Commission to investigate complaints against candidates and political committees.

title: Relating to tax returns.
summary: Requires businesses getting over 20 percent of gross receipts from public contracts to report that amount on their tax returns, starting 2028.

title: Relating to ensuring the credentials of persons working in regulated building activities.
summary: Requires building permits to list contractor license numbers, inspectors and municipalities to verify that licensed contractors do the regulated work, and state regulators to share violations with the licensing board.

title: Relating to post-secondary student financial aid; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a temporary Oregon work study pilot program run by HECC, sunsetting in 2029, and orders a study of student access to basic necessities.

title: Relating to preferences for veterans in public employment selection processes.
summary: Limits public-employer hiring preference for veterans to applicants within ten years of discharge, requires eligibility proof at application, and adds exhaustion of BOLI remedies.

title: Relating to maker spaces.
summary: Authorizes school districts to create maker spaces and lets school boards take steps to facilitate them.

title: Relating to county governing bodies.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Requires counties to have five nonpartisan commissioners unless county voters opt out, with county ordinances setting details, operative January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to workforce assistance to veterans in the construction industry; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Veterans' Affairs to run statewide pilot programs helping veterans in construction, funded from the Veterans' Services Fund, sunsetting December 31, 2027.

title: Relating to carbon sequestration.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Authorizes $500 million in general obligation bonds and directs the Forestry Department to create a carbon sequestration and forestry program.

title: Relating to seismic event preparation; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study how a major seismic event affects children and recommend school and community preparedness, reporting by September 2026.

title: Relating to grants to small cities for public transit.
summary: Authorizes state grants to certain small cities to study, develop and capitalize public transit systems, with an appropriation for the program.

title: Relating to appointments to the Board of Commissioners of the Port of Portland.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Government and administration
summary: Requires the Governor to interview at least one candidate from an underserved racial, ethnic or minority group when appointing Port of Portland commissioners.

title: Relating to real estate appraisers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a two-year grant program for newly certified or licensed real estate appraisers and lets the board issue temporary appraisal certificates and licenses.

title: Relating to technology support structures; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs DLCD to study ways to mitigate the aesthetic impact of cell towers and report to legislative land use committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to returning hatchery fish.
summary: Requires the Department of Fish and Wildlife to annually assess effects of hatchery fish carcass disposition rules and report results to legislative natural resources committees.

title: Relating to emergency volunteers.
summary: Creates a statewide electronic system to track emergency volunteers, run by ODEM, plus workgroups on volunteerism and a link to OregonServes.

title: Relating to small business resource sharing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study cost savings from small business resource sharing, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to carbon sequestration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Western Oregon carbon sink area run by the Forestry Department, plus a temporary task force and an advisory board.

title: Relating to fish hatcheries.
summary: Requires the state fish and wildlife department to get prior legislative approval before closing certain fish hatcheries.

title: Relating to small employer compliance with the Oregon Safe Employment Act.
summary: Directs the workplace safety agency to offer small employers incentives and maximum allowable fine protection for participating in consultative safety services.

title: Relating to small business economic development in rural areas of the state.
summary: Creates the Oregon Fund for Rural Small Business Development, continuously appropriated to the Oregon Innovation Council for grants and contest awards supporting rural small businesses.

title: Relating to personnel records kept for faculty members at institutions of higher education.
summary: Limits faculty personnel records at higher education institutions, lets faculty respond to records, bars evaluations based on unauthorized records, and allows faculty to sue. Operative 2027.

title: Relating to state funding of county projects.
summary: Bars state agencies from giving counties capital construction money unless the county attests it will remain in Oregon for a specified period.

title: Relating to screening of replacement workers during a labor dispute in an industry involving hazardous materials.
summary: Directs the state occupational safety division to study safety benefits of screening replacement workers during labor disputes at hazardous-materials employers and report findings.

title: Relating to the Oregon Military Department; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Allocates $500,000 in lottery revenue to the Oregon Military Department for tuition waivers for Oregon National Guard members at post-secondary institutions.

title: Relating to tax credits for employing youth workers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income tax credit for employers who hire up to three youth workers, for tax years 2025 through 2030.

title: Relating to state educational goals.
summary: Revises Oregon's state education goals to consider student aspirations, well-rounded education, and sufficient instructional time, and extends the education mission beyond high school.

title: Relating to the eligibility of corporations to serve on juries.
summary: Makes corporations eligible to serve on juries, changing who may sit as jurors in Oregon courts.

title: Relating to a public safety task force; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study public safety funding sources and recommend a strategic resourcing structure to the Legislature; it sunsets December 31, 2026.

title: Relating to tax incentives for firearms safety; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Guns and weapons; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates personal income tax credit and mileage subtraction for costs of required firearm transfer background checks, for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to teachers.
summary: Clarifies teacher probationary and contract definitions, shortens probation for teachers moving districts, and requires a 60-day improvement period for performance problems.

title: Relating to newborn safety devices.
summary: Allows parents to anonymously leave an infant in certified newborn safety devices at authorized facilities, under new device standards.

title: Relating to a tax credit for educator classroom expenses; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income tax credit for unreimbursed classroom expenses of teachers and adjunct instructors, inflation-adjusted, for tax years 2025 through 2030.

title: Relating to adjustment of classification of management service employees during an economic emergency.
summary: Lets the Governor declare an economic emergency, allowing agencies to reclassify management employees as at-will and adjust staffing, then report findings.

title: Relating to education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study the Quality Education Model and sunsets it January 2, 2027; makes no change to funding rules.

title: Relating to the training of police officers.
summary: Lets police units sponsor reserve officers to train with cash or G.I. Bill funds, requires a three-year service commitment, and sunsets in 2032.

title: Relating to housing for veterans; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a sunsetting task force to study innovative housing strategies for veterans and report its findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to tax incentives for investment in community food resources; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income tax credit for investment in community gardens and food banks, applying to tax years starting January 1, 2025.

title: Relating to civics proficiency for a high school diploma.
summary: Lets school districts and public charter schools require civics proficiency through methods other than completing a civics course for a high school diploma.

title: Relating to public utilities.
summary: Creates a homeland security commission in emergency management, a utility disaster fund, and grants plus lottery bonds for consumer-owned utilities' disaster projects.

title: Relating to energy-related improvements; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets local governments add criteria encouraging energy efficiency and generation on property receiving certain ad valorem property tax exemptions.

title: Relating to a paid sick leave tax credit; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Labor and employment; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a temporary income tax credit for employers required to provide paid sick leave, for tax years 2026 through 2029.

title: Relating to accelerated college credit programs; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires dual credit teachers to take graduate-level coursework and sets minimum education requirements for high school dual credit instructors, starting July 1, 2026.

title: Relating to tax credits for veterans services; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a personal income tax credit for military organization members who donate to the Veterans' Educational Aid Account before the organization dissolves, for tax years 2026-2031.

title: Relating to pipeline security; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study pipeline, storage and terminal security and report to interim legislative committees by December 2026.

title: Relating to disclosures of written accounts to the Psychiatric Security Review Board.
summary: Allows health information about conditionally released individuals to be disclosed without authorization to the Psychiatric Security Review Board.

title: Relating to the Fire Policy Committee.
summary: Changes the qualifications required for the fire instructor representative on the Fire Policy Committee of the Board on Public Safety Standards and Training.

title: Relating to medical assistance.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study potential changes to the Oregon Health Plan's prioritized list of health services and report by September 2026.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Requires hospitals to report their daily cash on hand to the Oregon Health Authority quarterly, with penalties for noncompliance.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Requires hospitals to report annually to the Oregon Health Authority on stock investments of medical assistance and other public funds, with penalties for noncompliance.

title: Relating to the disclosure of financial information.
summary: Requires Oregon hospitals to report fiscal and securities disclosure data to the Oregon Health Authority and publish it on a public website.

title: Relating to full-service redemption centers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Modifies siting and approval rules for some full-service bottle redemption centers, with a 91-day post-session effective date.

title: Relating to address confidentiality.
summary: Lets State Parks park managers and rangers have their employer's address, rather than home address, appear in ODOT records.

title: Relating to statements of economic interest.
summary: Specifies additional types of business roles and positions that public officials and candidates must list on statements of economic interest.

title: Relating to the System of Care Advisory Council.
summary: Changes the number and description of members on the System of Care Advisory Council, without altering the council's policy effects.

title: Relating to ocean shore permitting.
summary: Changes ocean shore permitting procedures and lets State Parks issue general authorization permits for limited shoreline activities.

title: Relating to the jurisdiction of the Department of Public Safety Standards and Training in cases of denial; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets DPSST keep investigating and act on officer or instructor certification even after the person changes or leaves their job.

title: Relating to investigations into alleged ethics law violations.
summary: Lets the Oregon Government Ethics Commission extend investigations into alleged ethics or lobbying violations by up to 60 days.

title: Relating to gift limits.
summary: Removes the $50-per-year cap on gifts offered to public officials, candidates, and their relatives or household members.

title: Relating to substance use; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies the membership, functions and powers of the Alcohol and Drug Policy Commission and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to conflict of interest requirements.
summary: Extends Oregon's conflict of interest laws to members of public officials' households, so household members are covered by those rules.

title: Relating to the interstate bridge replacement program.
summary: Modifies, adds and repeals laws on the I-5 bridge replacement project and its tolling, with no specific details given.

title: Relating to exceptions to prohibited use of official position or office.
summary: Creates an ethics-law exception letting public officials be paid by post-secondary institutions for teaching courses.

title: Relating to the Oregon Criminal Justice Commission.
summary: Approves unspecified modifications to Oregon Criminal Justice Commission rules on sentencing guidelines.

title: Relating to the Justice Reinvestment Program.
summary: Changes the membership of the Justice Reinvestment Grant Review Committee and the process for reviewing grant applications.

title: Relating to pretrial release.
summary: Directs the Criminal Justice Commission to study pretrial release and report findings to judiciary interim committees by May 1, 2027.

title: Relating to marketplace affordability.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study health insurance marketplace affordability and report findings to legislative health committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to public health testing.
summary: Directs OHA to run a public health lab and newborn bloodspot screening, requires providers to collect specimens and report results, and adds a religious or philosophical opt-out.

title: Relating to the payment of wages upon termination.
summary: Lets collective bargaining agreements set final-wage due dates and imposes penalty wages on employers who miss those dates.

title: Relating to the provision of health services offered by hospitals.
summary: Requires hospitals to give 275 days' notice before closing, reducing or relocating health services, with OHA civil penalties for violations.

title: Relating to hemoglobinopathies; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs OHA to create a program sending emergency departments real-time alerts identifying patients with hemoglobinopathies, and creates a task force to develop a treatment protocol and report.

title: Relating to projects eligible for federal tax credits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to give school districts technical assistance to plan and develop projects eligible for federal tax credits.

title: Relating to reimbursement of pharmacy services; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires OHA and coordinated care organizations to reimburse pharmacists the same as other health care providers for certain HIV-related services.

title: Relating to public health testing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a voluntary OHA pilot letting ED hospitals offer hepatitis C, HIV and syphilis screening with opt-out notice, requires insurance coverage of those tests, and funds county outreach.

title: Relating to penalties for failure to comply with certain requirements under the laws governing public employee collective bargaining.
summary: Directs the Employment Relations Board to impose civil penalties on public employers with a history of violating public employee collective bargaining requirements, with exceptions and extenuating-circumstance considerations.

title: Relating to zero-emission school buses; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires DEQ rules mandating new zero-emission school bus purchases in certain areas, backed by technical and financial assistance and a new assistance fund.

title: Relating to an audit of the Department of Transportation.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to perform a fiscal audit of the Department of Transportation.

title: Relating to a study of PFAS in biosolids applied to land; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs OSU Extension and its College of Agricultural Sciences to study PFAS in biosolids spread on non-food farm fields and report by 2028.

title: Relating to schools.
summary: Lets non-nurse school staff supervise school nurses for non-nursing purposes, while barring them from directing nursing practice.

title: Relating to financial assurance for certain facilities; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Requires bulk oil and liquid fuel terminal owners to obtain state certificates of financial responsibility for spill costs, and preempts local financial assurance rules.

title: Relating to amending land use planning goals; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires Oregon's land use commission to update the citizen involvement planning goal by 2029, creates a fund, and appropriates money for the work.

title: Relating to notarial acts; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to maintain an online database of notarial acts, which notaries must populate, operative January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to documents.
summary: Requires more information on notarial certificates and certain documents, and lets county clerks refuse documents that may be fraudulent.

title: Relating to funding for students eligible for special education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes caps on State School Fund money for special education students, requires a funding report, and appropriates General Fund money to the State School Fund.

title: Relating to substance abuse prevention; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Oregon Health Authority to distribute to local health departments and tribes for addiction prevention services.

title: Relating to continuous glucose monitors; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the state Medicaid program to cover continuous glucose monitors for specified medical assistance recipients, and takes effect immediately.

title: Relating to adult foster homes.
summary: Creates a pilot letting up to 30 adult foster homes care for up to seven residents, with reporting and a 2039 sunset.

title: Relating to time limitations associated with violations over which the Bureau of Labor and Industries has enforcement authority; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Bans employers from agreements shortening limitation periods for BOLI-enforced violations, and sets deadlines for BOLI notices and civil lawsuits.

title: Relating to earned income tax credits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Increases the earned income tax credit, allows quarterly advance payments, shields the credit from garnishment, and extends its sunset.

title: Relating to infertility; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires health insurers to cover specified fertility services and treatments, with exemptions for certain insurers, and directs agencies to study reproductive access.

title: Relating to certain facilities that convert plastic waste; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Bans establishing or operating plastic conversion or depolymerization facilities in Oregon and bars state and local incentives for them.

title: Relating to the capacity for electric vehicle charging required in certain newly constructed buildings.
summary: Requires newly constructed commercial, multifamily (10+ units) and mixed-use buildings in metro areas to install a set share of parking spaces with EV charging capacity.

title: Relating to minimum wage rates; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Changes how Oregon's minimum wage rate is calculated starting July 1, 2026, with BOLI setting the formula by rule.

title: Relating to electric bicycles; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Environmental Quality Commission to create a rebate voucher program for buyers of electric assisted bicycles, funded through a new Electric Bicycle Incentive Fund.

title: Relating to affordable housing; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to award loans for affordable housing predevelopment costs, adopt rules by June 2026, and appropriates General Fund money.

title: Relating to aquaculture.
summary: Creates the Aquatic Animals Fund, appropriates money to Fish and Wildlife for aquaculture purposes, and sets requirements for raising fish as food.

title: Relating to a public finance task force; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a State Public Finance Task Force to study public banking and other public financing options, reporting to the Legislature by December 31, 2026.

title: Relating to residential applicant screening charges.
summary: Bans residential landlords from charging tenant applicants screening fees.

title: Relating to housing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a state-guaranteed system for deferred development charges paid by housing developers after occupancy, with a fund, appropriation, penalties, and collections.

title: Relating to economic development.
summary: Appropriates state money to the Oregon Coast Visitors Association to replicate a fish-based nonfood manufacturing project, and requires an economic development study report by September 2026.

title: Relating to the use of dogs to hunt wild cats.
summary: Prohibits using dogs to hunt or chase lynx or bobcats, with up to 364 days' jail, a $6,250 fine, and loss of hunting license application privileges.

title: Relating to financial institutions.
summary: Changes which investments certain financial institutions may make and how qualified public depositories calculate net worth.

title: Relating to funding for staffing workforce reentry programs; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Provides Employment Department funding to staff workforce reentry programs for adults in custody, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to funding for marine cleanup.
summary: Directs the Department of State Lands to study funding options for public waterway cleanup and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to crimes involving children; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Changes the definition of "sexually explicit conduct" in certain child-related crimes and raises the sentencing grid category for first-degree invasion of personal privacy when the victim is a minor.

title: Relating to crimes constituting domestic violence; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Provides that a DV-involving crime's admission or finding is not an element for merger purposes, so such convictions may not merge for sentencing.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through the Department of Administrative Services to a nonprofit for indigenous language interpretation purposes.

title: Relating to funding to support species conservation; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Raises the state transient lodging tax and directs the added revenue to a renamed wildlife conservation subaccount.

title: Relating to natural resources.
summary: Directs transportation and wildlife agencies to create an advisory group on wildlife-vehicle collisions and changes related program reporting.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to DAS to distribute to various entities for food production and distribution, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to wildlife.
summary: Creates a Wildlife Stewardship Program and a grant program for licensed wildlife rehabilitation centers, funded by a General Fund appropriation to ODFW.

title: Relating to aquatic invasive species; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to four agencies for aquatic invasive species work, including vessel inspections, monitoring and rapid response, and requires a study and report.

title: Relating to small watercraft.
summary: Raises some boat fees, deposits the money into an aquatic invasive species fund, and requires a waterway access permit for nonmotorized boats with exceptions.

title: Relating to individuals with developmental disabilities.
summary: Directs the Department of Human Services to study transitions of developmentally disabled youth from youth to adult residential settings and report by September 2026.

title: Relating to funding for activities concerning water; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Fish and Wildlife for the Oregon Conservation and Recreation Fund, for water-related activities, effective on passage.

title: Relating to the Public Utility Commission.
summary: Modifies Public Utility Commission administrative proceedings procedures; the summary gives no substantive change to utility rules or rates.

title: Relating to irrigation districts.
summary: Bars irrigation districts from delivering more water than a user requests for a season, with an exception allowing temporary transfer of the water.

title: Relating to compensation for members of certain public entities.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study compensation for state board and commission members and report to interim legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to aquifers.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to take actions on aquifer recharge and storage and recovery and report to interim legislative committees by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to the Law Enforcement Medical Liability Account.
summary: Directs OHA to pay medical costs, including copays and full costs for Medicaid or uninsured people, for injuries from law enforcement activity, using the LEMLA fund.

title: Relating to transportation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires ODOT to report by September 15, 2026 on progress revising the Class C driver license written test; the bill sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to services for assisting low-income individuals with tax navigation; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money to fund outreach on federal tax credits and to provide tax preparation and navigation help for low-income people.

title: Relating to student vision; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates an Oregon Health Authority program to provide eye exams and prescription glasses to low-income students.

title: Relating to linguistically appropriate health care.
summary: Directs the Oregon Medical Board and Nursing Board to offer language education to providers and make patient forms available in patients' languages.

title: Relating to health equity; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to create a medical science liaison position to recommend ways to advance health equity and justice.

title: Relating to a task force on reparations for Oregonians of African-American descent; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Task Force on Reparations to study and propose financial and nonfinancial reparations for Oregonians of African-American descent, sunsetting December 31, 2026.

title: Relating to child abuse arising from neglect.
summary: Bars DHS from substantiating child neglect allegations based solely on a parent's or guardian's financial resources.

title: Relating to higher education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Higher Education Coordinating Commission grant program to expand college access and success programs, with an appropriation and an emergency clause.

title: Relating to behavioral health screening for racial trauma; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs OHA to adopt rules requiring certified or licensed behavioral health providers to screen for racial trauma during initial assessments.

title: Relating to warrants requirements in child abuse investigations.
topics: Children and families; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Requires DHS to give suspected abusers notice of rights and bars entering private property or drawing negative inferences without consent, warrant, or exigent circumstances.

title: Relating to oversight of the child abuse investigation process.
topics: Children and families; Government and administration
summary: Changes the Children's Advocate's appointment to require gubernatorial appointment with Senate confirmation and modifies its complaint review duties.

title: Relating to adults in custody.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Corrections for housing and employment reentry services for Black adults in custody.

title: Relating to demographic data; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Task Force on Data Modernization that must report to an interim legislative committee by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to Department of Human Services annual child welfare reporting.
summary: Changes the list of data the Department of Human Services must include in its annual child welfare report on foster children.

title: Relating to community violence prevention.
summary: Directs the Youth Development Division to review community violence prevention initiatives and report to an education interim committee by December 1, 2027, then sunsets.

title: Relating to expunction of records relating to child abuse; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Changes when DHS may expunge records of reported or founded child abuse, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to the education workforce.
summary: Creates programs and appropriates General Fund money to increase representation of marginalized groups in the education workforce, including scholarships for administrator candidates.

title: Relating to accommodations for students diagnosed with a brain injury; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires public schools to put immediate, temporary accommodations plans in place for students diagnosed with a concussion or other brain injury, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to investments in the child care workforce.
summary: Appropriates money to various agencies to fund investments in the child care workforce.

title: Relating to the Oregon Jail-Based Medications for Opioid Use Disorder Grant Program.
summary: Expands the jail-based opioid treatment grant program so people in other types of county facilities can receive treatment and transition planning.

title: Relating to pesticide education; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs OSU Extension and the Department of Agriculture to develop and publicize Spanish-language pesticide education and precertification materials.

title: Relating to the Early Childhood Education Workforce Development Fund; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates an Early Childhood Education Workforce Development Fund and appropriates money through HECC to community colleges and public universities offering early childhood training.

title: Relating to voting in school district elections.
summary: Allows 16- and 17-year-olds who are registered to vote to cast ballots in school district elections.

title: Relating to the effect of land use provisions that fail to gain acknowledgement.
summary: Voids land use permits and zone changes based on unacknowledged plan or regulation provisions, and requires removal or revocation of resulting improvements or uses.

title: Relating to school facilities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a School District Facility Equity Fund, with grants for school district and ESD facility needs, funded in part by lottery bonds.

title: Relating to school nutrition; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Bans Red Number 3, potassium bromate and propylparaben from food and beverages sold to students in public schools, effective July 1, 2027.

title: Relating to a rebate program for zero-emission landscaping equipment; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Environmental Quality Commission to create rebate vouchers for replacing gas lawn and garden equipment with zero-emission electric models, funded through a new rebate fund.

title: Relating to chemicals in products.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study health risks of chemicals in menstrual, intimate care and incontinence products and report by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to food waste; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires food businesses to separate and recover food waste, mandates local collection service, sets state compost procurement priority, and requires uniform food date label terms.

title: Relating to Oregon Medical Board licensure of medical practitioners trained outside of the United States.
summary: Requires the Oregon Medical Board to study licensing doctors and PAs trained outside the U.S. and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to racing.
summary: Bans wagering on dog races and removes greyhound racing references from animal racing law, operative July 1, 2027.

title: Relating to laws administered by the Employment Department; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Makes unspecified changes to unemployment insurance and paid family and medical leave laws administered by the Employment Department.

title: Relating to information collected by state agencies; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Labor and employment
summary: Allows state agencies to share employer and employee information with the Employment Department for paid leave and related program administration.

title: Relating to racing.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Removes the requirement that horse racing fees and simulcasting and wagering hub fees collected by the Oregon Racing Commission be transferred to the General Fund.

title: Relating to the reduction of unemployment benefits due to disqualification; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Eliminates the reduction in maximum unemployment benefits for workers disqualified for cause who have not earned four times their weekly benefit.

title: Relating to the Oregon Opportunity Grant program.
summary: Restructures the Oregon Opportunity Grant so HECC awards grants to qualified students toward their cost of education, removing the shared-responsibility model.

title: Relating to the Higher Education Coordinating Commission; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies eligibility for a teacher-candidate scholarship, exempts certain Transfer Council subcommittee meetings from public meetings law, and orders several higher-education studies and reports.

title: Relating to injunctions regarding career school regulatory violations.
summary: Lets the Higher Education Coordinating Commission seek court injunctions against career schools or persons violating licensure requirements and standards.

title: Relating to degree authorization by the Higher Education Coordinating Commission.
summary: Lets HECC set rule-based fees to recover its costs of reviewing school degree-authorization applications, replacing fixed statutory fee amounts.

title: Relating to workforce development.
summary: Aligns Oregon workforce development programs, defines 'public workforce system,' sets shortage criteria, renames Prosperity 10,000 as the Prosperity Program, and changes Youth Works board term limits.

title: Relating to grants for diverse school administrator candidates.
summary: Authorizes HECC to award grants to school administrator candidates with experience with diverse populations, for use at approved educator preparation programs.

title: Relating to housing; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a program letting the Oregon Infrastructure Finance Authority fund roads, pipes and other infrastructure supporting housing, with a new fund and a housing study.

title: Relating to homelessness.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study homelessness and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the Emergency Housing Account.
summary: Changes the funding and use of the Emergency Housing Account and modifies the Oregon Housing Stability Council's role in designing its programs.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Expands the Housing and Community Services Department's authority over homeownership housing projects and lending, and lets it refinance housing loans.

title: Relating to tax credits for affordable housing lending; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands permitted uses of bank affordable-housing lending tax credit savings to include resident and supportive services.

title: Relating to state grants awarded by the Department of Education; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes ODE grant rules: sets a minimum grant for small districts, eases grant paperwork, expands grant eligibility, and adjusts certain education grant amounts.

title: Relating to education; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Omnibus education bill adjusting STEM grants, abolishing an account, clarifying recovery school funding, setting Deaf school admission and consent rules, and requiring school safety programs.

title: Relating to expanded learning options.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study ways to expand summer and after-school academic and enrichment programs and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to early literacy.
summary: Changes the early literacy grant program by adding teacher professional development and coaching requirements, widening curriculum grant uses, moving report dates, and expanding state intervention options.

title: Relating to the Educator Advancement Council; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Moves the Educator Advancement Council's legal basis from an intergovernmental agreement into state statute, with no stated change in its function.

title: Relating to Oregon Board of Naturopathic Medicine; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds grounds for the Naturopathic Medicine Board to discipline licensees and lets it order mental, physical, or competency evaluations of those under investigation.

title: Relating to the impaired health professional program; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Clarifies licensee self-referral to the impaired health professional program, defines key terms, lets boards remove certain program participation records, and clarifies evaluator requirements.

title: Relating to nursing; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Modifies Oregon nursing law: defines key terms, clarifies license pathways, lets the board require relicensure competency, drops mandatory CE program approval, and lets it monitor and revoke nursing assistant training approval.

title: Relating to the State Board of Pharmacy; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets the State Board of Pharmacy require a person under investigation to undergo a mental, physical, chemical dependency or competency evaluation.

title: Relating to pharmacy; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Clarifies pharmacists may prescribe and dispense opioid use disorder medications, allows DEA registration for that purpose, and requires certain prescription lockers to register with the Board of Pharmacy.

title: Relating to economic development.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study Oregon's clean technology sector and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to arts and culture.
summary: Abolishes the Oregon Arts Commission and Trust for Cultural Development Board, creates a new arts board and office, and orders a state study of arts and culture.

title: Relating to tax exemptions for business development; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Modifies a corporate excise tax exemption for businesses in economically lagging areas, changing wage calculation and eligibility certification requirements.

title: Relating to ports.
summary: Creates a Business Oregon loan and grant program, administered by the Infrastructure Finance Authority, to provide financial assistance for eligible port projects.

title: Relating to fitness to proceed.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study fitness to proceed and report results to interim legislative committees by May 1, 2026.

title: Relating to PFAS.
