summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Quality to study PFAS and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to summer camp training for certain University of Oregon students; declaring an emergency.
summary: Provides state money via HECC to UO for a pilot training speech-language pathology graduate students to serve children with communication needs at summer camps.

title: Relating to residential tenancies for a space in a facility; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Caps manufactured home park and marina rent increases at six percent from 2026, with a tenant-approved infrastructure exception, and bars certain sale conditions.

title: Relating to statewide summative assessments.
summary: Requires school districts to meet statewide test participation rules and show improved test scores to receive certain state education funds, and removes the waiver directive.

title: Relating to public record request fees.
summary: Requires state agencies to waive public records request fees when the request comes from a member of the Legislative Assembly.

title: Relating to adoption awareness.
summary: Directs DHS to create an Adoption Awareness Program, administered by a nonprofit organization or agency.

title: Relating to commitment for fitness to proceed.
summary: Requires courts to make a dangerousness finding before committing a person who lacks fitness to proceed to a state mental hospital.

title: Relating to the education of youth in residential facilities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Education, with DHS, to study education needs of youth in residential training homes and report to interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to a physician assistant licensure compact; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Joins the PA Licensure Compact so physician assistants licensed in other member states can practice in Oregon under compact privilege, with board data-sharing and fund-use authority.

title: Relating to consideration of criminal convictions in school settings.
summary: Directs the Teacher Standards and Practices Commission to study modernizing background checks and criminal history standards for public school employment, reporting by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to industrial development impact on sensitive uses of land; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires local governments to map sensitive uses and to study and mitigate impacts on nearby sensitive uses before approving new industrial development.

title: Relating to students in hospital educational programs.
summary: Treats students in hospital educational programs as enrolled in their school district and keeps prior-district enrollment to preserve access to curricula and technology.

title: Relating to health care coverage beginning at perimenopause.
summary: Requires certain health insurers and the state employee benefit boards to cover perimenopause, menopause and postmenopause treatment.

title: Relating to local standards to promote housing stability; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires smaller cities to adopt local housing-stability standards by 2027, allows rent control statewide, and requires reviews every 10 years.

title: Relating to the advanced esthetics program at the Coffee Creek Correctional Facility; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Corrections to fund an advanced esthetics program at Coffee Creek Correctional Facility.

title: Relating to the Justice Reinvestment Program.
summary: Directs the Criminal Justice Commission to study repealing the Justice Reinvestment Program's sunset and report to the legislature by May 1, 2026.

title: Relating to community corrections.
summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to study community corrections and report findings to interim judiciary committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to public safety; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Reorganizes CJC grant programs, makes Justice Reinvestment and reentry court provisions permanent, and repeals HB 3194's sentencing increases set for 2033.

title: Relating to the Sexual Assault Task Force.
summary: Appropriates money to the Department of Justice to fund the Oregon SAE/SANE Certification Commission under the Sexual Assault Task Force.

title: Relating to crime victim services.
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to study crime victim services and report findings to judiciary interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to expungements.
summary: Requires the Judicial Department to study ways to improve the efficiency of setting aside convictions and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to crime.
summary: Requires the Criminal Justice Commission to study how different sentence types affect recidivism and report to legislative judiciary committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to firearms.
summary: Requires the State Police to study the efficiency of firearm transfer background checks and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to firearms; declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies Measure 114 permit-to-purchase rules: delays permit requirements for transfers to 2026, raises fees, adds exceptions for officers, and changes magazine defenses.

title: Relating to gun dealer licenses; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a DOJ-run state gun dealer licensing program with inspections, penalties, employee background checks, and an appropriation to fund it.

title: Relating to fire.
summary: Allows local government employees to volunteer to help fight wildland fires during emergencies.

title: Relating to water; declaring an emergency.
summary: Funds a drinking water operator training pilot and a municipal water grant program, funds western juniper treatment, and extends Deschutes groundwater rules to 2039.

title: Relating to youth homelessness.
summary: Requires DHS to update youth homelessness cost estimates and study budget options, and expands emergency housing eligibility; sunsets January 2027.

title: Relating to health care decision making for incapacitated individuals.
summary: Expands who may make health care decisions for incapacitated people who have no appointed representative or advance directive.

title: Relating to energy.
summary: Directs ODOE to create a statewide navigation system and single universal application clearinghouse for energy efficiency incentive programs, and to identify gaps and overlaps.

title: Relating to reporting obligations for patient assistance programs for prescription drug purchases.
summary: Requires drug manufacturers offering patient assistance programs to report to the Department of Consumer and Business Services how many consumers participated, even without price increases.

title: Relating to school safety.
summary: Directs school governing bodies to consider installing panic alarm systems as part of school building security policies.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Directs state agencies to help develop the CORE3 emergency management center, evaluate financial participation, and has DAS issue a grant for it.

title: Relating to behavioral health treatment.
summary: Creates a pilot program in the Oregon Health Authority for timely behavioral health care for children in emergency department crises, with state-funded regional centers, sunsetting in 2032.

title: Relating to drug costs; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the state employee benefit board to count coupon and third-party drug payments toward enrollees' cost-sharing and out-of-pocket maximums.

title: Relating to renewable energy; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a state income or corporate excise tax credit for transmission service costs paid by owners of solar, wind, or storage facilities placed in service 2026–2031.

title: Relating to transportation; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force on sustainable aviation fuel and directs ODOT to study promoting its use, sunsetting December 31, 2026.

title: Relating to a definition of "wildfire" for the purposes of insurance coverage; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Defines "wildfire risk" to determine certain homeowner insurance obligations of insurers; the text gives no detail on the obligations.

title: Relating to homeownership development incubator programs.
summary: Directs the housing department to amend its homeownership development incubator program for specified purposes, with the program sunsetting January 2, 2028.

title: Relating to the Department of Environmental Quality.
summary: Requires DEQ to set clear permit rules, bars applying new requirements to pending permit applications, and expedites applications when DEQ misses a deadline.

title: Relating to drug costs; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Oregon Educators' Benefit Board to count coupon and third-party drug payments toward enrollees' cost-sharing and out-of-pocket maximums.

title: Relating to DNA samples; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Requires police to take DNA samples from people arrested for certain crimes, allows destruction on request after favorable outcomes, and adds DNA analysis to Criminal Fine Account uses.

title: Relating to drug treatment; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Restructures drug treatment grant funding and oversight, moving council duties to a commission and modifying the behavioral health deflection program.

title: Relating to rebuttable presumptions regarding parenting; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a rebuttable presumption that equal parenting time is in a child's best interests, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to a tax credit for apprenticeships; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a new income tax credit for taxpayers that provide apprenticeship opportunities, applying to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to the offense of attempting to elude a police officer.
summary: Increases the crime seriousness and sentencing guidelines for felony attempting to elude a police officer, making sentences longer.

title: Relating to reporting by recipients of public moneys; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Requires recipients of state grants or loans to report annually on spending and political contributions, with contribution disclosure within a set timeframe.

title: Relating to economic development districts; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allocates lottery moneys to Oregon's twelve economic development districts to use as matching funds for federal Economic Development Administration grants.

title: Relating to a unified trade strategy for Oregon; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allocates lottery funds to Business Oregon to develop a unified state trade strategy with the Port of Portland, tourism, and agriculture agencies; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to events that involve livestock; declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes the County Fair Account cap, allocates lottery proceeds to fair and a new horse racing account, and funds a county fairground master plan.

title: Relating to damages incurred as a result of wildfire.
summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study impacts of wildfire damages and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to reliable forest management outcomes; declaring an emergency.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Directs the State Forester to set sustainable timber harvest levels and manage state forestland, allows injunctions for failures, and appropriates General Fund money; declares emergency.

title: Relating to rural community resources; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a statewide rural community resource center, run through a nonprofit or local government association agreement, to help rural jurisdictions pursue and manage grants.

title: Relating to water.
summary: Allows water right certificates to be assigned and requires real estate sellers to notify the Water Resources Department of transactions involving water rights.

title: Relating to water data; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an Integrated Water Data Team led by DOGAMI to build a statewide water data portal, with General Fund money for DEQ's portal work.

title: Relating to Department of Environmental Quality regulatory processes; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands DEQ's authority to agree with regulated entities to expedite or enhance regulatory processes, and directs the EQC to set guiding standards.

title: Relating to aquifer storage and recovery permits.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to adopt additional rules and requirements for reviewing limited license applications for aquifer storage and recovery permits.

title: Relating to the Sustainable City Year Program at the University of Oregon; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money through HECC to the Sustainable City Year Program at the University of Oregon and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to official flags.
summary: Requires flags on public buildings to be flame-hardy or flame-retardant by July 4, 2026, and sets criteria for official state and U.S. flags.

title: Relating to evictions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a mandatory eviction mediation program funded by appropriation, requires landlords to provide program notice, and lets tenants use nonattorneys in eviction proceedings.

title: Relating to the voluntary relinquishment of water rights; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a voluntary, compensated program for groundwater right holders in critical groundwater areas to relinquish rights, funded by a state appropriation.

title: Relating to access to funding; declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a state and federal grants coordinator in the Regional Solutions Program and allocates lottery funds to match federal grants.

title: Relating to the Chewaucan River watershed; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs Oregon Consensus and OSU to support a Chewaucan River watershed water management process and appropriates funds for it; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the state lottery; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Bans selling or transferring certain winning Oregon lottery tickets, bars deducting those purchases for Oregon tax, and exempts winners' names and addresses from public records.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Water Resources Department for place-based water planning and limits grant spending to implement water plans.

title: Relating to funding for responses to natural disasters.
summary: Directs the State Forestry Department to study funding for natural disaster prevention, response and recovery, and report by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to communications services for persons in custody.
summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to contract for free voice communication services for incarcerated people and bars the department from profiting from them.

title: Relating to the delay of certain motor vehicle emissions standards; declaring an emergency.
summary: Bars DEQ from implementing or enforcing Advanced Clean Trucks emissions rules before January 1, 2027, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to earned income tax credits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises the Oregon earned income tax credit percentage, adds an age-of-youngest-dependent tier, and extends the credit's sunset through 2031.

title: Relating to community water systems; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs state funding, via a contract with the Oregon Association of Water Utilities, for technical assistance to small water systems and a training center.

title: Relating to Owyhee Lake Road.
summary: Directs State Parks to seek an agreement with federal agencies to establish and implement an access fee for Owyhee Lake Road.

title: Relating to wildfire.
summary: Creates a Department of Agriculture grant program to reduce wildfire risk and impact on rangeland, awarding grants to eligible local stakeholders.

title: Relating to predator management in drought-stricken regions; declaring an emergency.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Directs the Fish and Wildlife department to reduce predators in drought-affected wildlife areas and appropriates General Fund money for that predator control.

title: Relating to rangeland wildfire resilience; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force on rangeland wildfire resilience and risk reduction, sunsetting December 31, 2026; it changes no rules.

title: Relating to licensure of teachers providing classroom instruction in subjects other than career and technical education.
summary: Directs the TSPC to create a five-year pilot program licensing non-CTE teachers in a manner similar to the career and technical education license, sunsetting in 2031.

title: Relating to reports of death.
summary: Requires death reports to be filed with the Center for Health Statistics through the state's electronic reporting system, starting July 2027.

title: Relating to the use of water for fire response preparedness.
summary: Exempts surface water stored for fire response preparedness from needing a water right application, permit, or certificate.

title: Relating to the behavioral health workforce; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a higher education fund, appropriated by the state, to expand training, employment and retention of behavioral health professionals.

title: Relating to economic interest statements filed by district school board members.
summary: Exempts school board members who receive no stipend from filing economic interest statements, requiring filings only from stipend-receiving members.

title: Relating to the Oregon Agricultural Heritage Fund; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Oregon Watershed Enhancement Board for the Oregon Agricultural Heritage Fund and sets a spending limit, effective immediately.

title: Relating to augmentation of firefighting capacity of airports; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration; Transportation
summary: Directs ODEM to buy vehicles and grants airport infrastructure funds, lets the Transportation director suspend statutes during conflagrations, and lets the Guard move aviation fuel.

title: Relating to farm stands.
summary: Amends the conditions under which counties must approve farm stands on exclusive farm use zoned lands; the direction of change is not specified.

title: Relating to prior authorization.
summary: Adds prior authorization reporting, exempts some providers and surgical procedures from prior authorization, and requires an authorization interface by 2027.

title: Relating to water conservation; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money for grants to soil and water conservation districts in certain counties, plus support and monitoring funds, and takes effect on signing.

title: Relating to composition of planning commissions.
summary: Removes the cap of two real estate professionals on city and county planning commissions with more than five members.

title: Relating to real estate professionals.
summary: Modifies real estate professional regulation, defining managing principal broker and prescribing that role's responsibilities.

title: Relating to an organic policy special assistant to the Director of Agriculture.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Directs the Director of Agriculture to employ an organic policy special assistant to advise on organic policy.

title: Relating to the assessment of rebuilt homesteads; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets counties give rebuilt wildfire-destroyed homesteads a specially assessed value matching the destroyed home's market value, with conditions.

title: Relating to recreation; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets recreation operators require participants to release them from ordinary negligence claims, and funds an OBDD study of the recreation industry.

title: Relating to Oregon Farmer and Rancher Day; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Designates the third Tuesday of March each year as Oregon Farmer and Rancher Day, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to employment subject to unemployment insurance taxes; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts employers from unemployment insurance tax on wages of H-2A agricultural workers who are not eligible for UI benefits.

title: Relating to fostering coexistence with beavers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a beaver coexistence grant subaccount and appropriates General Fund money for Fish and Wildlife block grants to private landowners, with a 2027 report.

title: Relating to dwellings.
summary: Bars planned communities from banning manufactured dwellings or prefabricated structures, and extends the mobile home park dispute resolution program to 2031.

title: Relating to factory-produced housing; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets the housing department use LIFT fund money for factory-built homes, requires a contractor to support that industry, and requires a report, with a 2028 sunset.

title: Relating to emergency housing for individuals awaiting residential substance use disorder services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a sunsetting OHA pilot providing low-barrier emergency housing to unhoused or unsafely housed people waiting for residential substance use treatment, with biennial reporting.

title: Relating to broadband service infrastructure; declaring an emergency.
topics: AI and technology; Environment and energy
summary: Directs state agencies to expedite permits and approvals for building, siting, and operating broadband infrastructure, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the availability of residential telecommunication services for low-income customers; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Makes the Oregon Lifeline telecom assistance plan permanent, renames it, and adds a one-time benefit for low-income customers to buy an internet-enabled computer.

title: Relating to state moneys for school districts impacted by wildfires; declaring an emergency.
summary: Extends by one school year the authority to spend state money on school districts affected by wildfires, instead of four years.

title: Relating to an income tax credit for volunteer firefighters; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income tax credit for volunteer firefighters for tax years 2026 through 2031, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to State School Fund distributions; declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes the cap on State School Fund money for special education students and adds a funding weight for homeless students in district distributions.

title: Relating to candidate filings.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to create an electronic system for city and county candidates to file portraits and statements, posted online and listed in voters' pamphlets.

title: Relating to cougars.
summary: Allows dog-assisted cougar hunting on private property and directs the Fish and Wildlife Commission to set chronic-depredation thresholds and reduce cougar populations as needed.

title: Relating to defining buildable lands.
summary: Removes certain lands from the definition of buildable lands, narrowing which lands may be counted for urbanization.

title: Relating to all-terrain vehicles.
summary: Allows Class I, III and IV all-terrain vehicles on non-interstate highways if they meet equipment standards and are registered, and creates optional highway registration.

title: Relating to utilities.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Requires public utilities to include PUC consumer contact numbers and a complaint website on each utility bill; PUC to study utilities and report.

title: Relating to an income tax credit for blood donations; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a refundable personal income tax credit for blood donations made during a declared emergency, for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to photovoltaic solar power generation facilities on lands zoned for exclusive farm use.
summary: Allows certain solar power facilities on exclusive farm use land to operate alongside farm or allowed nonfarm uses on the same tract.

title: Relating to public utility rates.
summary: Caps how much a public utility may raise rates or rate schedules in a calendar year, limiting increases to the average CPI change.

title: Relating to funding for fire districts.
summary: Directs the State Fire Marshal to study fire district funding and report to legislative natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to public utility liabilities arising out of wildfire litigation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Prohibits public utilities from raising rates while they carry wildfire-litigation liabilities that have been outstanding or contingent for three or more years.

title: Relating to financial support for child care; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Education to grant to schools for before- and after-school child care, with a report due June 30, 2027.

title: Relating to a specially assessed value for the residences of seniors; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets counties opt to give owner-occupied primary residences of homeowners aged 62 and older a specially assessed property tax value.

title: Relating to temporary signs on private property.
summary: Raises the allowed size of temporary signs on private property from 12 to 32 square feet.

title: Relating to state moneys for school districts impacted by wildfires; declaring an emergency.
summary: Transfers Fund for Student Success moneys to a subaccount and raises spending limits so the Education Department can grant funds to wildfire-impacted school districts.

title: Relating to elections.
summary: Places all candidates for partisan and nonpartisan office on one unified primary ballot, advancing the top five vote-getters to the general election.

title: Relating to regulating sales of admission tickets to entertainment events.
summary: Bars bots and software that evade ticket sale controls, requires total-price disclosure and reseller possession, and bans misleading ticket-related domain names, enforceable under the Unlawful Trade Practices Act.

title: Relating to residential developmental disabilities services; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires DHS rules for enhanced staffing ratios at agencies serving people with disabilities, and requires high-needs residential homes to file staff safety plans.

title: Relating to school-based health centers; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to adjust school-based health center grant amounts for inflation, effective July 1, 2025, with an emergency declaration.

title: Relating to community resilience; declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies definitions and grant requirements for disaster Resilience Hubs and Networks and appropriates General Fund money to DHS for those grants.

title: Relating to county energy resilience plans; declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes the required contents of county energy resilience plans and extends the deadline and sunset of a county planning grant program.

title: Relating to reducing the vulnerability of structures to wildfire; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a State Fire Marshal grant program to help retrofit dwellings against wildfire damage and appropriates General Fund money for it.

title: Relating to the OregonFlora Program at Oregon State University; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates the OregonFlora Program at Oregon State University on plant life in Oregon and appropriates money to OSU for it, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to driving while under the influence of intoxicants; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises DUII-related fees and lets the Intoxicated Driver Program Fund cover more indigent defendants, including non-residents completing treatment out of state.

title: Relating to county recording fees.
summary: Removes the cap on county recording fees, letting counties charge more to fund public land survey corner activities.

title: Relating to staffing plans for home health care entities; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires home health agencies and hospice programs to create staffing committees and plans, adds OHA enforcement and penalties, and lets workers seek enforcement of meal and rest break rules.

title: Relating to offers for used motor vehicles; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires used motor vehicle sellers to check the VIN against NHTSA's recall database and repair safety recalls before advertising or offering the vehicle.

title: Relating to conditions for financing a transaction involving a motor vehicle.
summary: Requires motor vehicle sellers to make good-faith efforts to sell installment contracts on negotiated terms, bars certain trade-in loan payoffs before lender approval, and adds disclosures and penalties.

title: Relating to public utilities; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Adds rate-increase limits and reviews for residential electric and gas customers, including a winter moratorium, and authorizes utility securitization bonds.

title: Relating to the Washington County Courthouse Replacement Planning Project; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money to the Judicial Department to plan a replacement Washington County courthouse, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to a task force on youth apprenticeships; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Task Force on Youth Apprenticeship that reports to legislative committees by December 1, 2026, then sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to aid to students in higher education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates HECC grant programs for student basic needs and affordable housing support, plus a task force studying student housing barriers.

title: Relating to the Open Educational Resources Program; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to the Higher Education Coordinating Commission for the Open Educational Resources Program and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to the homestead exemption.
summary: Bars forced sale of a homestead to satisfy a judgment that does not exceed the homestead exemption amount.

title: Relating to post-secondary students working at nonprofit corporations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a pilot program reimbursing nonprofits up to 100% of wages paid to participating public university students, and removes the $5 million budget cap for eligible nonprofits.

title: Relating to the State Board of Towing.
summary: Renames the State Board of Towing the Oregon State Board of Towing and declares it an independent board. It does not change towing rules.

title: Relating to age-based employment discrimination; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands age-based employment discrimination protections by barring employers from requesting age and graduation-date information and removing the apprentice age-limit exception.

title: Relating to guarantees against losses in mortgage loans extended to first-time home buyers; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a state loan-guarantee program for first-time home buyers' mortgages, a Welcome Home Assistance fund, and an appropriation to the housing department.

title: Relating to the Oregon Arts Commission; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Oregon Business Development Department for Oregon Arts Commission grants to certain organizations; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to historic property special assessment; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits the historic property special assessment tax break to commercial property and makes other structural program changes.

title: Relating to support of cultural organizations.
summary: Appropriates state money to support arts and cultural organizations in Oregon.

title: Relating to newborn bloodspot screening.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Oregon Health Authority to screen newborns for five specific diseases through the regional bloodspot program.

title: Relating to farmworker disaster relief.
summary: Creates a permanent Oregon Health Authority program giving money to farmworkers who lose income from disasters, funded by a General Fund appropriation.

title: Relating to farmworker camps.
summary: Makes landowners and farmworker camp operators jointly liable for unregistered camps, with a rebuttable presumption for landowners who show a lease prohibiting such use.

title: Relating to children's advocacy centers; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes the cap on how much a children's advocacy center can receive from a one-time grant fund and changes grant eligibility rules.

title: Relating to state finance; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money to the Department of Justice for purposes related to federal Victims of Crime Act grants, backfilling reduced grant funding, effective on passage.

title: Relating to revenues derived from sale of alcoholic beverages.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Directs the Legislative Revenue Officer to study taxation of beer and wine sales and report to interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to missing and murdered indigenous people.
summary: Directs OHA to dedicate tribal affairs staff to missing and murdered indigenous people work and requires a DOJ study reporting by September 2026.

title: Relating to school attendance; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Orders studies of school attendance initiatives, convenes an advisory committee to recommend a State Board attendance policy, and sets up attendance data and coding work.

title: Relating to education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies a teacher-candidate scholarship program and directs the Department of Education to allocate a specified amount from a fund to it.

title: Relating to food served under the Child and Adult Care Food Program; declaring an emergency.
summary: Provides financial support for child care food under CACFP, creates a supplemental fund, and appropriates money for culturally specific menus.

title: Relating to school attendance; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to convene an advisory committee on improving school attendance, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to school attendance; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to convene an advisory committee on improving school attendance, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to student attendance data.
summary: Requires quarterly collection and compilation of student attendance data, including regular attenders and chronically absent students, and makes that data public.

title: Relating to vehicles used to transport children from home to school.
summary: Authorizes school activity vehicles to transport students from home to school, expanding how those vehicles may be used.

title: Relating to the recording of student absences.
summary: Directs ODE to review attendance recording and response procedures, and requires districts to report students without regular attendance.

title: Relating to an early warning system for students.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to use Statewide Education Initiatives Account money to give school districts technology for early warning data systems.

title: Relating to school attendance; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study ways to improve school attendance and report findings to interim legislative committees by December 31, 2025.

title: Relating to motor vehicles; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Adds a 10-year surcharge on certain RV registration fees and trip permits, deposited in a fund to tow and dispose of abandoned RVs.

title: Relating to funding the manufacture of electric vehicles in Oregon; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the state to give federal small business credit funds to Lit Motors, Inc., to fund electric vehicle manufacturing in Oregon.

title: Relating to health directives.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to develop and make available a nonopioid directive form for people who do not want certain drugs given.

title: Relating to pharmacy benefits.
summary: Adds new rules and requirements for pharmacy benefit managers and for health insurance policies covering prescription drug reimbursement.

title: Relating to public records disclosure by public university foundations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Subjects public university foundations to state public records laws and requires them to post an annual report publicly on their website.

title: Relating to marijuana for medical use; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands qualifying conditions for medical marijuana, requires caregiver organizations to adopt staff policies and training, and bars nurse discipline for discussing medical marijuana.

title: Relating to sponsorship of public charter schools.
summary: Allows chambers of commerce, community groups, trade associations, corporations and nonprofits to sponsor public charter schools, broadening who can authorize them.

title: Relating to a system for submitting certified statements required for reporting compliance with the prevailing wage laws; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Bureau of Labor and Industries to study a centralized electronic system for prevailing wage compliance reporting and report by September 2026.

title: Relating to education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a scholarship program, lifts the virtual charter cap, opens cross-district enrollment, and requires proficiency in Essential Learning Skills for diplomas.

title: Relating to school attendance.
summary: Directs the Commission on Indian Services and Department of Education to study the Tribal Attendance Promising Practices grant program and report by September 2026.

title: Relating to the Oregon Hazards Lab at the University of Oregon.
summary: Appropriates state money through HECC to the Oregon Hazards Lab at the University of Oregon.

title: Relating to nursing education.
summary: Directs the Oregon State Board of Nursing to adopt rules requiring a set student-to-faculty ratio in nursing education clinical components.

title: Relating to urgent care centers; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Creates optional OHA registration for urgent care centers with minimum standards, and bars unregistered entities from using "urgent" or "urgent care" in names or advertising.

title: Relating to academic assessments administered to students by school districts.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to update its survey of school district academic assessments and submit a report by December 15, 2026.

title: Relating to prescription drugs; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits when mail-order, specialty, or online pharmacies may transfer prescriptions to in-state pharmacies, and bars PBMs from forcing pharmacies to accept such transfers.

title: Relating to background checks; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Human Services to study state background check requirements, report on consolidation options, and study a 12-month reuse exemption.

title: Relating to control of a professional corporation organized for the purpose of practicing medicine; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires physicians who hold majority control of a medical professional corporation to meet specified qualifications; takes effect 91 days after session.

title: Relating to organizations that provide services related to obtaining prescription drugs; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Brings pharmacy services administrative organizations under pharmacy benefit manager laws and requires them to register with DCBS as third-party administrators, with some exemptions.

title: Relating to restrictive covenants in employment contracts for medical professionals; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Voids noncompete, nondisclosure, nondisparagement and nonsolicitation agreements between medical care businesses and medical professionals, and bars retaliation against workers who violate them.

title: Relating to cybersecurity; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs a cybersecurity council to study why public bodies cannot get cyber insurance and creates a fund to help them meet insurance and incident requirements.

title: Relating to provider enrollment in the medical assistance program; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Speeds Medicaid enrollment and CCO contracting for behavioral health providers, with a 30-day decision deadline and retroactive reimbursement; also studies an automated enrollment tool.

title: Relating to information technology; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires an independent contracted assessment of executive-branch IT, with recommendations and a report to the Governor and legislative committees; takes effect on passage.

title: Relating to passenger rail; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires Oregon's passenger rail plan to include track upgrade and capacity strategies and federal grant information, with DOT status updates every even-numbered year.

title: Relating to exemption of property owned by a limited equity cooperative; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Removes the requirement that limited equity co-op property be built or converted after a local body adopts the low-income rental housing property tax exemption.

title: Relating to rail; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs ODOT to coordinate with Washington and British Columbia on rail planning, adds quarterly and biennial performance and planning reports, and authorizes shared regional agreements.

title: Relating to business practices that reduce access to health care in this state; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Lets the Attorney General investigate and sue health insurers for antitrust violations and unlawful trade practices that reduce competition.

title: Relating to a grant program to support accelerated mortgages for first-time home buyers; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a grant program, run through Housing and Community Services, that supports first-time home buyers with reduced-rate, accelerated-term loans to build equity faster.

title: Relating to tax credits for lending for affordable housing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands the corporate excise tax credit for bank lending for affordable housing, including credits for buyer mortgage loan funds and distressed-property rehabilitation loans.

title: Relating to public safety answering points.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Emergency Management to run a grant program funding consolidation and upgrades of 911 public safety answering points, sunsetting in 2045.

title: Relating to cybersecurity.
topics: AI and technology; Government and administration
summary: Directs the Office of Enterprise Information Services to study cybersecurity and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to criminal records checks; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state funds to DHS, OHA and State Police to implement criminal records check programs, including Rap Back, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to development of staging areas for emergency response.
summary: Directs ODEM to develop emergency response staging areas, creates a public places investment fund with continuous appropriations, and sets up an advisory committee.

title: Relating to events on lands zoned for exclusive farm use.
summary: Allows certain events to be held on lands zoned for exclusive farm use, loosening farm-zone land use limits.

title: Relating to in-network credentialing; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires health insurers to pay providers joining an in-network practice at in-network rates during credentialing, with provider repayment if criteria or a complete application aren't met.

title: Relating to billing for ground ambulance services.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Bans balance billing for ground ambulance services in certain cases, sets insurer reimbursement rules, and requires providers to report local rates to DCBS.

title: Relating to municipal solid waste incinerators; declaring an emergency.
summary: Replaces continuous air-emissions monitoring at municipal solid waste incinerators with annual monitoring and lets DEQ modify the monitoring plan.

title: Relating to coordinated care organization global budgets; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study how to calculate coordinated care organization global budgets and report findings to the Legislature.

title: Relating to circular economy; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs Business Oregon to develop a voluntary industrial symbiosis roadmap, funds six pilot communities, and lets certain county water districts charge for services.

title: Relating to the supply of electricity in this state; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires utilities to secure replacement reliable power before retiring a plant, and directs the PUC to seek waivers or injunctions against federal rules that raise plant costs.

title: Relating to abortion restrictions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bans abortion at 15 or more weeks gestational age except for medical emergency, rape or incest, adds facility rules, reporting, and private lawsuits.

title: Relating to an exemption from property taxes for the homesteads of seniors; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a partial property tax exemption for the owner-occupied home of people 65 or older and their surviving spouses.

title: Relating to consideration of nonfinancial factors in managing state investments.
summary: Bars the Oregon Investment Council, State Treasurer and managers from considering nonfinancial factors when investing Public Employees Retirement Fund moneys.

title: Relating to leasing land for the placement of cell phone towers in rural areas; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the State Board of Forestry to allow cell tower leases on state land in Clatsop and Tillamook counties at $1,500 yearly, switching to federal forest rates in 2036.

title: Relating to administrative rules regarding agricultural labor housing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Limits how certain administrative rules apply to farmworker housing on livestock operations, bars retroactive enforcement, and blocks forced relocation or demolition absent immediate hazard.

title: Relating to technology support structures.
summary: Sets county review criteria for telecom tower siting and requires existing towers to comply by January 1, 2032.

title: Relating to veterans.
summary: Requires the Department of Veterans' Affairs to annually report federal dollars received per state dollar spent on veterans, plus federal moneys received by veterans.

title: Relating to requirements for online businesses to provide contact methods to respond to customer concerns.
summary: Requires online businesses to maintain phone and email contact for customer concerns, with Secretary of State enforcement, civil penalties, and possible dissolution or revocation for repeated violations.

title: Relating to motor vehicle pollution control systems.
summary: Exempts motor vehicles eight model years old or newer from the requirement to have a certified pollution control system.

title: Relating to licensure portability for military families.
summary: Directs the Oregon Military Department to study interstate licensure portability for military families and report findings by September 2026.

title: Relating to economic development.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study economic development and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to public safety answering points.
summary: Directs ODEM to run a grant program supporting consolidation and upgrades of public safety answering points, sunsetting in 2045.

title: Relating to a grant program to improve the resiliency of community facilities.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a grant program at ODEM to harden community facilities against disasters and establishes a Community Facility Hardening Fund.

title: Relating to diesel fuel; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force to study renewable diesel availability, demand, incentives, and effects of removing petroleum diesel, sunsetting December 31, 2026.

title: Relating to wildfire recovery; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a wildfire recovery fund financed by an annual insurer surcharge on property policies and a property tax filing fee, sunsetting in 2033.

title: Relating to carbon sequestration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Western Oregon Regional Carbon Sink area managed by the Forestry Department, plus a temporary task force and an advisory board, under an emergency clause.

title: Relating to fire service professional training standards; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Department of Public Safety Standards and Training to study fire service training standards and report findings to interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to retainage in public improvement contracts.
summary: Requires the Department of Administrative Services to study alternative ways to implement retainage in public improvement contracts and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to community water systems.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study community water systems and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to veterans' recognition registration plates.
summary: Allows additional forms of identification to prove veteran status when applying for a veterans' recognition registration plate.

title: Relating to the selection of directors for the school district in which the State Capitol is located.
summary: Requires Salem-Keizer School District board directors to be nominated and elected by zone rather than at large.

title: Relating to correctional facility staffing plans.
summary: Creates staffing committees at each Department of Corrections facility to develop, implement and periodically revise a written facility-wide staffing plan.

title: Relating to the Emergency Board.
summary: Adds more members to the Legislative Emergency Board, operative after adjournment sine die of the 2027 session.

title: Relating to the State Department of Energy; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the State Department of Energy to study energy incentive laws and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to academic credits at public institutions of higher education.
summary: Requires public colleges to award credit for certain high school communications, public speaking or argumentation programs and bars requiring those students to take intro courses as prerequisites.

title: Relating to the Oregon Safety Assessment Program.
summary: Appropriates money to the State Fire Marshal for personnel costs of the Oregon Safety Assessment Program (OrSAP).

title: Relating to youth career-training opportunities.
summary: Creates criteria for recognizing student internships, makes them eligible for career tech grants, and removes the youth apprenticeship participation cap.

title: Relating to tuition at post-secondary institutions of education.
summary: Requires public universities and community colleges to charge active-duty service members, spouses and dependent children resident tuition and fees.

title: Relating to airport infrastructure resilience.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Aviation to study airport infrastructure resilience and report to the Legislature by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to military spouses.
summary: Directs the Oregon Military Department to study military spouses and report findings to veterans-related interim committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to public safety.
summary: Directs the Oregon Criminal Justice Commission to study how sentencing types affect recidivism and report to judiciary committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to professional licensing during emergencies.
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Lets the Oregon Department of Emergency Management issue temporary professional licenses during emergencies to people formerly licensed by certain boards.

title: Relating to rural medical training facilities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study nurse and medical technician shortages in rural areas, including Douglas County, and sunsets December 31, 2026.

title: Relating to veterans.
summary: Requires the Oregon Military Department to study veterans and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to the restructuring of the Oregon Health Authority.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to hire a third party to study restructuring for efficiency and report findings to legislative health committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to animal sanctuaries.
summary: Requires the Department of Fish and Wildlife to study animal sanctuaries and report findings to wildlife committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to aquaculture products; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs Fish and Wildlife to create a program buying trophy trout from private aquaculture facilities, sunsetting January 2, 2031.

title: Relating to long-term recovery groups; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Long-Term Recovery Group Fund and directs ODEM to grant money to recovery groups helping areas affected by emergencies.

title: Relating to community organizations active in disaster; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the state emergency management agency to create a county liaison to help build local disaster community organizations; sunsets in 2028.

title: Relating to property tax exemption for disabled veterans; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands property tax exemptions for veterans with disabilities and surviving spouses who remain unmarried, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to unemployment insurance taxes.
summary: Directs the Employment Department to study allowing employers to pay quarterly unemployment insurance taxes over an extended period and report by September 2026.

title: Relating to post-custodial workforce development.
summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to study post-custodial workforce development and report findings to judiciary interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to alcohol delivery.
summary: Requires the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission to study alcohol delivery and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the military.
summary: Directs the Oregon Military Department to study the military and report findings to veterans and emergency management committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to seaport transportation infrastructure resilience.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Emergency Management to study seaport transportation infrastructure resilience and report findings to interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to seaport transportation infrastructure resilience.
summary: Directs the Department of Emergency Management to study seaport transportation infrastructure resilience and report findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to staffing plans for health care provider entities; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires hospitals to comply with unit nurse staffing plans or statutory ratios, creates violations for noncompliance, and shields hospitals from penalties if they made good-faith efforts.

title: Relating to improvements to Powell Boulevard.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Transportation to improve a portion of Southeast Powell Boulevard.

title: Relating to transportation infrastructure resilience.
summary: Directs ODOT to study transportation infrastructure resilience and report to the Legislature by September 15, 2026; the bill sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to employment.
summary: Requires the Bureau of Labor and Industries to study employment issues and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to education.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to study the adequacy of Oregon public schools and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to a special bridge district; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Salem-area bridge district in four counties with authority to levy property taxes for Willamette River bridges, sunsetting in 2030.

title: Relating to desalination; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Creates a Task Force on Desalination to study a statewide desalination program and report to a legislative water committee by December 15, 2026.

title: Relating to ground transportation infrastructure resilience.
summary: Directs ODOT to study ground transportation infrastructure resilience and report to the Legislature by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to a public corporation for establishing secure cash storage facilities in this state; declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Creates a public corporation to securely hold cash for people who do business in cash, with its own fund, audits, and statewide facilities.

title: Relating to infrastructure financing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Business Development Department to study infrastructure financing tools for lowering infrastructure and housing costs and report to the Legislature.

title: Relating to employment benefits of education workers.
summary: Directs the Oregon Educators Benefit Board to study education workers' benefits and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to desalination; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates the Oregon Desalination Authority and directs it to study desalination facility development and maintenance.

title: Relating to taxable income exemption for military taxpayers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts up to $17,500 of military retirement or pension pay from state income tax for taxpayers 62 or younger, starting tax year 2025.

title: Relating to emergency volunteers; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs ODEM to create a grant program, with the OregonServes Commission, to support and expand community emergency volunteer programs.

title: Relating to fuel.
summary: Requires strategic government facilities to keep a three-week fuel supply from 2031 and all government facilities to use renewable diesel from 2028.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Creates the Oregon Public Assistance Grant Account and continuously appropriates its funds to state agencies, local governments, tribes and nonprofits for emergency response.

title: Relating to regional foodstuff supplies.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Creates the Oregon Strategic Resilience Sustainability Commission, which must run a grant program to increase and secure regional foodstuff supplies.

title: Relating to degrees offered by certain public universities.
summary: Removes the statutory limit on the types of degrees that Western Oregon, Southern Oregon and Eastern Oregon universities may offer.

title: Relating to school meals; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires schools and districts to provide lunch and, where applicable, breakfast to students at no charge, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the eligibility to use electricity generated from waste for renewable energy certificates.
summary: Makes electricity from direct combustion of municipal solid waste eligible for renewable energy certificates, for pre-1995 facilities and capped biogenic combustion.

title: Relating to harmful algal blooms; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through DAS to the Human Access Project for harmful algal bloom mitigation.

title: Relating to the website of the Oregon Business Development Department; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to update and redesign its public website, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to video recordings of certain labor negotiations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires public bodies to video record labor negotiations they conduct or conduct on their behalf; the bill takes effect on signing and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to political expenditures by publicly traded corporations; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Requires publicly traded corporations to get shareholder approval for political expenditures over $100 and to disclose those expenditures and directors' economic interests.

title: Relating to civil penalties for violation of environmental laws.
summary: Lets the Environmental Quality Commission adopt by rule enhanced civil penalties for cargo tank vehicles that violate certain environmental laws.

title: Relating to the authority of the State Accident Insurance Fund Corporation to set premium rates.
summary: Lets the State Accident Insurance Fund set lower workers' comp premiums for employers who reduce risk or meet agreement terms, including new owners on probation.

title: Relating to emergency management volunteers.
summary: Requires the Legislative Revenue Officer to study granting a tax benefit to emergency management volunteers, sunsetting January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to primary prevention of substance use.
summary: Directs the Alcohol and Drug Policy Commission to develop a youth substance use prevention strategy, report by September 2026, and provide provider technical assistance.

title: Relating to parenting time.
summary: Lets minors 14 or older ask courts to suspend or terminate parenting time of a parent whom DHS substantiated for abuse.

title: Relating to traffic offenses; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets drivers 18 and younger with no prior traffic convictions take a driver improvement course instead of being convicted, and directs ODOT to set course standards.

title: Relating to product liability civil actions.
summary: Exempts health care facilities from product liability suits unless they were involved in designing or manufacturing the product.

title: Relating to transient lodging taxes; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets taxing districts in high-tourist counties spend a set percentage of net lodging tax revenue on essential services benefiting residents and tourists.

title: Relating to dental care for seniors; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Seniors Emergency Dental Program at OHA providing no-cost emergency dental services to eligible low-income seniors; also directs a study of senior dental access.

title: Relating to legislation affecting local governments.
summary: Requires the Legislative Policy and Research Director to study laws affecting local governments and report findings to interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to expending county road fund moneys for patrolling.
summary: Adds Grant County to the list of counties allowed to use federal forest reserve road fund money for road patrolling, effective on passage.

title: Relating to incentives for film production; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises the total cap on film production tax credits for contributions to the Oregon Production Investment Fund, starting fiscal years on or after July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to participation in medical procedures.
summary: Expands conscience-based refusal protections for health workers and facilities on abortion, assisted suicide, and gender-affirming procedures, with a private damages action.

title: Relating to catastrophic disaster.
summary: Redirects a percentage of State Accident Insurance Fund dividends into a catastrophic disaster preparedness fund and creates an advisory board to recommend its use.

title: Relating to horse racing.
summary: Redirects certain racing-hub wagering moneys to a horse and jockey safety fund, with expenditure reporting and clawback enforcement.

title: Relating to an income tax subtraction for teachers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a new Oregon personal income tax subtraction for teachers for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to a tax credit for educator classroom expenses; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income tax credit for unreimbursed classroom expenses of certain public school teachers and adjunct instructors for tax years 2025 through 2030.

title: Relating to land use siting of renewable energy facilities that are solar photovoltaic power generating facilities.
summary: Directs the Department of Land Conservation and Development to study land use siting of solar photovoltaic facilities and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to electric transmission systems; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires electric companies to file cost-effective grid-enhancing technology plans with the PUC and streamlines local review of certain GET applications in existing rights-of-way.

title: Relating to photo radar in highway work zones.
summary: Changes Oregon's highway worker photo radar laws in work zones; the text does not say which way.

title: Relating to gender-affirming treatment; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Health Evidence Review Commission to evaluate gender-affirming treatment, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to a psychology licensure compact; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Joins Oregon to a psychology licensure compact, letting compact-authorized psychologists practice without an Oregon license and allowing the board to share information and pay compact obligations.

title: Relating to foreign interest in resources lands; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars listed foreign adversaries from acquiring farm or forest land, voids unauthorized conveyances, and requires an annual Department of Agriculture report on foreign agricultural land ownership.

title: Relating to water; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Oregon Watershed Enhancement Board for a drinking water source protection fund; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to water; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Modifies Oregon water rights regulation and administration; the text gives no specifics, and the change takes effect 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to natural resources.
summary: Directs the Department of Fish and Wildlife to study natural resources and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the total return distribution method for endowment care cemeteries.
summary: Lets cemetery authorities elect the total return distribution method to fund endowment care of their cemeteries.

title: Relating to vehicle registration plates.
summary: Requires taxis and rideshare vehicles to display cherry red rideshare plates and creates a misdemeanor-style offense, with a maximum $250 fine, for failing to do so.

title: Relating to siting of energy facilities in designated critical ground water areas.
summary: Directs DLCD to study land-use siting of energy facilities in designated critical groundwater areas east of the Cascades and report findings by November 30, 2026.

title: Relating to family support payments.
summary: Starting January 2027, DOJ must pass assigned child support payments to certain families, and DHS must disregard certain support income paid to families.

title: Relating to child support.
summary: Makes unspecified changes to the state child support program, including how it is administered.

title: Relating to fire protection; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Rangeland Protection Association Fund, appropriates money to it, and expands State Forester authority to assist fire-protection associations.

title: Relating to fire protection; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the State Forestry Department for the Rangeland Protection Association Fund, which supports rural fire protection groups.

title: Relating to a counseling licensure compact; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Joins the interstate Counseling Compact so licensed counselors from other member states can practice in Oregon without an Oregon license.

title: Relating to the creation of credits for the restoration of salmon habitat; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a voluntary salmon habitat credit pilot in the Coquille and Coos basins, a trust fund, and a programmatic Army Corps permit for restoration work.

title: Relating to the impacts of wildfire on water quality.
summary: Directs Fish and Wildlife and DEQ to study wildfire impacts on stream water quality and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to county sales of lands.
summary: Lets counties keep proceeds from county real property sales by directing the remaining balance to the county general fund.

title: Relating to fish.
summary: Requires the Department of Fish and Wildlife to study fish stocking protocols and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to state financial administration; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through DAS to a nonprofit to provide meal services for elderly individuals.

title: Relating to the reporting of education workplace safety incidents.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to create a method for school districts and ESDs to record workplace injuries and safety incidents.

title: Relating to county property tax collection; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Authorizes counties at high risk of financial distress to withhold 3% of property tax distributions to fund the county assessor's office.

title: Relating to the definition of a totaled vehicle.
summary: Changes the definition of 'totaled vehicle' in the Oregon Vehicle Code; the text gives no other detail.

title: Relating to capital funding for schools; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs corporate kicker revenue to school construction, maintenance and infrastructure in certain districts, contingent on a constitutional amendment.

title: Relating to funding for summer learning programs; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Education to fund a Summer Learning Grant program, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to a tax on sales of tires; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget; Transportation
summary: Creates an excise tax on tire retail sales to fund rail transit, tire pollution prevention and wildlife crossings, with new funds and a DOT program.

title: Relating to the application of overtime under the Oregon Public Service Retirement Plan.
summary: Changes how the overtime cap is calculated when determining final average salary for OPSRP pension members.

title: Relating to water; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Water Resources Department to report to the Legislature and Water Resources Commission on certain water funding programs every eight years, and makes changes to a water supply grant program.

title: Relating to climate change instruction in public schools.
summary: Requires future revisions of core-subject academic content standards to include climate change causes, effects, and mitigation or adaptation strategies.

title: Relating to firefighting funding.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through DAS to the Rogue Siskiyou Regional Training Center for firefighting training.

title: Relating to agricultural labor housing.
summary: Narrows the definition of farmworker camp so related housing statutes apply specifically to camps housing seasonal or temporary workers.

title: Relating to district attorneys; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Makes the state pay counties for one district attorney's salary and half of other DDA and deputy DA salaries, per the state salary plan.

title: Relating to courthouses.
summary: Authorizes the State Treasurer to issue general obligation bonds to finance courthouse expansion.

title: Relating to financial institutions.
summary: Adjusts credit union and bank procedures: deceased-member information timelines, director delegation of reinstatement duties, and supervisory committee requirements.

title: Relating to lienholders of a residential tenant's abandoned property.
summary: Requires landlords to notify lienholders of a tenant's abandoned vehicle and treat them like lienholders of abandoned RVs, manufactured dwellings, or floating homes.

title: Relating to exempt uses of water.
summary: Limits the lawn and garden groundwater exemption: excludes cannabis, keeps hemp, and for two years bars it for commercial gardens in the Lower Umatilla Basin.

title: Relating to education audit reports.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to compile school district, ESD and charter school audit findings into a single distributed report.

title: Relating to medical services for injured workers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets the State Accident Insurance Fund form subsidiaries and provide managed care to injured workers, with required annual audits of that care.

title: Relating to youth substance abuse.
summary: Directs the Alcohol and Drug Policy Commission to study youth substance use prevention and treatment programs and report findings and recommendations to the Legislature.

title: Relating to public defense; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates district defender offices in each judicial district and changes which entities the Public Defense Commission may contract with for public defense services.

title: Relating to the James Beard Public Market; declaring an emergency.
summary: Authorizes state lottery bonds to fund construction of the James Beard Public Market in Portland, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to tenant dwelling access to dwelling unit.
summary: Requires residential landlords to offer a non-app method of entry, such as a physical key, for a dwelling to be considered habitable.

title: Relating to medical assistance reimbursement of emergency medical services.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study Medicaid supplemental reimbursement for ground emergency medical transportation, reporting findings by September 15, 2026, with the study sunsetting January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to emergency medical services providers.
summary: Raises the tax credit for rural volunteer EMS providers from $250 to $1,000 per year, extends it to 2030, and requires an annual report.

title: Relating to public safety.
summary: Directs the Department of Public Safety Standards and Training to study public safety and report findings to judiciary interim committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to administrative rules.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to maintain an online rulemaking information system and requires agencies to make rule information accessible online.

title: Relating to fees charged by county clerks.
summary: Raises certain fees charged by county clerks, increasing costs for people who pay those fees.

title: Relating to filing petitions for initiatives and referenda.
summary: Lets local elections officials decline to act on initiative or referendum petitions filed in a window around May and November elections.

title: Relating to public record fees.
summary: Exempts public records filed with a county clerk from the fee schedule and amends the statute governing those fees.

title: Relating to solemnization of marriage.
summary: Allows a deputy of a county clerk to perform and solemnize marriages.

title: Relating to precinct committeepersons counting ballots.
summary: Lets precinct committeepersons who are on the ballot volunteer to help county clerks count ballots.

title: Relating to recalls of public officials.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to study recalls of public officials and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to elections.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to study elections and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to elections; declaring an emergency.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Sets a method for a joint legislative committee to write ballot titles and explanatory statements for 2025 measures, and requires a Secretary of State elections study.

title: Relating to ranked choice voting.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to study ranked choice voting and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to campaign finance.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to study campaign finance and report findings to interim election committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to measures on the ballot.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to study ballot measures and report findings to legislative election committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to public meetings.
