summary: Requires the Department of Justice to study public meetings and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to government ethics.
summary: Requires the Oregon Government Ethics Commission to study government ethics and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to public records.
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to study public records and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to compensation for public service.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study public service compensation, report to interim committees by September 15, 2026, and sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to state administration.
summary: Requires the Department of Administrative Services to study state administration and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to state administration.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study state administration and report findings to interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to state finance.
summary: Requires the Department of Administrative Services to study state finance and report to ways and means committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to state finance.
summary: Requires the Department of Administrative Services to study state finance and report findings to interim ways and means committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to transportation; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget; Transportation
summary: Omnibus transportation bill raising road, vehicle and fee taxes with set revenue uses, requiring ODOT performance audits, and shifting director appointment to the Governor.

title: Relating to education.
summary: Directs five state education and workforce agencies to create and maintain a statewide educator workforce data system, consolidating existing educator data sources.

title: Relating to education.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study the adequacy of Oregon public schools and report findings to interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to child care.
summary: Requires the Department of Early Learning and Care to study child care and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to higher education.
summary: Directs the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to study higher education and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to health care; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets insurers and pharmacy benefit managers require claims for 340B drugs to carry a modifier identifying them, unless listed conditions are met.

title: Relating to health care; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Amends Oregon's medical corporate-practice and noncompete laws, makes the noncompete ban retroactive, and takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.

title: Relating to behavioral health.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study behavioral health and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the climate.
summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Quality to study the climate and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to natural resources.
summary: Requires the Department of Fish and Wildlife to study natural resources and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Emergency Management to study emergency management and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to wildfires.
summary: Directs the State Forestry Department to study wildfires and report to natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to revenue.
summary: Directs the Legislative Revenue Officer to study the personal income tax system and report findings to interim committees by December 1, 2026.

title: Relating to public safety.
summary: Requires the Criminal Justice Commission to study how different sentence types affect recidivism, reporting to judiciary committees by September 2026, then sunsetting.

title: Relating to economic development.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study economic development and report to the Legislative Assembly by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to water.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study water rules and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to funding for talented and gifted educational programs; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Talented and Gifted Education Account funded by transferring one percent of State School Fund general purpose grant money for TAG programs.

title: Relating to biomarker testing coverage.
summary: Requires certain health insurance policies and Oregon Health Plan managed care plans to cover biomarker testing under specified rules.

title: Relating to energy facility compliance with statewide planning goals; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds a new criterion EFSC must find before granting a planning-goal exception for energy facilities, applying to exceptions taken after the effective date.

title: Relating to information permitted for insurer's decisions concerning motor vehicle liability insurance; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Restricts insurers to specified information for car insurance rates and eligibility, and bars use of credit history for motor vehicle liability insurance.

title: Relating to crime victim rights.
summary: Directs the Department of Justice to study crime victim rights notification procedures and report findings to legislative judiciary committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to grooming.
summary: Creates a new crime of grooming, a sex crime punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a $125,000 fine, with sex offender reporting upon conviction.

title: Relating to unmanned aircraft systems.
summary: Makes it an offense to use a drone to interfere with firefighting or search and rescue, and modifies penalties for drone interference with emergency responders.

title: Relating to an income tax subtraction for a taxpayer having three or more children; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an Oregon personal income tax subtraction for taxpayers with three or more dependent children under 18, for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to exclusions from estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds a $1 million estate tax exclusion, plus an additional $1 million exclusion, with inflation adjustments, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to the Governor's emergency powers authority; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits Governor-declared states of emergency to 60 days unless the Legislature extends them by joint resolution, in increments of no more than 60 days.

title: Relating to an income tax credit for independent physicians; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income tax credit for independent physicians for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to public notices.
summary: Lets certain legally required public notices be published in online news publications instead of only in newspapers.

title: Relating to the redemption of beverage containers at wineries.
summary: Lets wineries refuse to accept and pay refund value for beverage containers not sold at the winery.

title: Relating to beverage containers for wine; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds wine bottles to Oregon's Bottle Bill deposit-and-redemption system, operative July 1, 2026, and modifies its provisions for wine containers.

title: Relating to unemployment insurance benefits for employees unemployed due to a labor dispute; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals the disqualification that denies unemployment benefits to workers out of work due to an active labor dispute at their workplace; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to school meals; declaring an emergency.
summary: Makes school meals free to all students, phases in universal no-cost lunch and breakfast, sets nutrition standards, and appropriates General Fund money for implementation.

title: Relating to costs associated with trees on public property; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars cities from requiring property owners to pay for removing trees on public property or repairing sidewalks damaged by those trees.

title: Relating to public health; declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Bans sale of flavored tobacco and inhalant delivery products, requires licensed premises for sales, and lets localities adopt stricter tobacco rules.

title: Relating to golf courses on exclusive farm use lands in Coos County.
summary: Lets Coos County approve golf courses on exclusive farm use zoned land under new criteria, expiring January 1, 2028.

title: Relating to naturopathic physicians.
summary: Requires insurers and public employee benefit plans to reimburse naturopathic physicians' services and pay them the same as MDs, PAs and NPs.

title: Relating to student proficiency in language arts.
summary: Bars third-graders who lack language arts proficiency from advancing to fourth grade, with exceptions, and bars districts from promoting them.

title: Relating to a state commission for public charter schools.
summary: Creates a State Commission on Public Charter Schools to sponsor and oversee public charter schools statewide.

title: Relating to payment facilitation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts certain payment facilitators from money transmission licensing if they don't engage in money transmission and payment satisfies the payor's obligation.

title: Relating to felon in possession of a firearm.
summary: Makes each firearm possessed by a felon a separately punishable offense, so one incident can carry multiple charges.

title: Relating to public charter school funding; declaring an emergency.
summary: Increases public funding for charter schools by changing district payment percentages, removing Student Investment Account eligibility limits, and equalizing fund transfers.

title: Relating to truancy; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates new truancy violations for students who miss school or fail compulsory attendance rules, with fines up to $500, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to funding to support career and technical education.
summary: Changes how money from the Connecting Education to Careers Account is distributed to schools for career and technical education activities.

title: Relating to nitrous oxide.
summary: Requires retailers selling nitrous oxide canisters to verify buyers are 18 or older, and bars online sellers from delivering without that verification.

title: Relating to school calendars; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires schools to operate 175 days a year on a year-round schedule and directs an advisory group to help districts transition.

title: Relating to a pilot program to provide support to foster child students; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies a foster child student support pilot program, letting grant money fund other schools in the district; declares emergency.

title: Relating to energy storage transition planning; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Department of Energy to develop an energy storage transition plan for bulk oil and liquid fuels terminals in the critical energy infrastructure hub.

title: Relating to the Superintendent of Public Instruction.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Makes the Oregon Department of Education head an elected nonpartisan statewide office and requires the superintendent to convene a parents advisory group.

title: Relating to ballot titles.
summary: Shifts responsibility for drafting state ballot titles from the Attorney General to the Legislative Counsel.

title: Relating to commuter rail; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates the Westside Express Service Authority, transfers the commuter rail line's operation from TriMet to it, and appropriates state funds to support it.

title: Relating to the provision of adoption information to students.
summary: Requires public education programs to give students adoption information whenever they receive contraceptive or STI information.

title: Relating to state forest lands.
summary: Directs the State Board of Forestry to convey certain state forest lands to counties that request them and find conveyance most valuable.

title: Relating to Internet safety policies for minors.
summary: Requires school boards and public library boards to adopt internet safety policies for students and minors, with prescribed requirements.

title: Relating to the use of the E-Verify employment verification system in employment.
summary: Requires all employers to use the federal E-Verify system to verify new hires' employment eligibility.

title: Relating to school policies regarding student use of personal electronic devices.
summary: Requires every school district board to adopt a student cell phone and personal device policy that meets at least the state's least restrictive model.

title: Relating to human development education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires school districts to teach human biology and in-womb development, including related videos, adding this subject matter to instruction.

title: Relating to hyperbaric oxygen therapy; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an Oregon Health Authority program to reimburse hyperbaric oxygen therapy for low-income veterans with traumatic brain injury or PTSD who are ineligible for medical assistance.

title: Relating to machine-powered pesticide application devices; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts certain employees from pesticide licensing when they apply pesticides using a battery-powered device, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to camping on public property.
summary: Bans camping on public property except school lands and state forests, with a maximum $100 fine for violations.

title: Relating to water banks.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study water banks and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to pretrial release for felony sex crimes; declaring an emergency.
summary: Restricts pretrial release for people charged with a new felony sex crime while already on pretrial release for one, requiring a hearing and full security deposit.

title: Relating to fire protection.
summary: Directs the State Forestry Department to try to contract with the U.S. Forest Service for fire protection in certain counties.

title: Relating to tolling on Interstate 205.
summary: Prohibits the Oregon Transportation Commission from tolling Interstate 205.

title: Relating to ballots; declaring an emergency.
summary: Prohibits individuals from collecting and returning another person's ballot, with specified exceptions, and takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.

title: Relating to updating voter registration information; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars county clerks from using ODOT and OHA data to update already-registered voters' information, and lets voters update their own registration by submitting a card.

title: Relating to energy; declaring an emergency.
summary: Counts hydroelectric power toward renewable portfolio standard compliance and repeals the requirement that electric companies phase out coal-fired resources.

title: Relating to verification of voter registration information.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to verify citizenship before passing ODOT and OHA voter registration data to county clerks.

title: Relating to performance audits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Division of Audits to conduct a performance audit of state agencies' emergency-related actions; the bill takes effect 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to vehicles; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs ODOT to study electric-assisted bicycles and motor-assisted scooters and report results to the Joint Committee on Transportation.

title: Relating to registering to vote by voter registration card; declaring an emergency.
summary: Ends automatic transfers of voter registration data from ODOT and OHA to the Secretary of State, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to the Secretary of State conducting a study of changes to the U.S. Postal Service.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to study how possible U.S. Postal Service changes would affect Oregon's vote-by-mail system and report to the Legislature.

title: Relating to teacher licensing requirements.
summary: Directs the Teacher Standards and Practices Commission to study whether teaching license requirements relate to instructional qualifications, reporting findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through DAS to the City of Prineville for improvements to its 3rd Street corridor, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to climate change; declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes Oregon's greenhouse gas reduction goals and replaces 'global warming' with 'climate change' in some laws, including Climate Action Commission provisions.

title: Relating to dispensing nonretail fuel; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Removes fuel-volume requirements for cardlock dispensing eligibility and extends cardlock facility licenses from one year to three.

title: Relating to insurance for unmanned aircraft systems; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Requires commercial drone operators to carry liability insurance, taxes those premiums, and directs the revenue to an advanced air mobility program.

title: Relating to transportation.
summary: Directs ODOT to study uniform standards for speed bump height and markings, with the study requirement sunsetting January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to transportation.
summary: Directs ODOT to study developing uniform standards for speed bump height and markings; the study requirement sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to transportation.
summary: Requires ODOT to study developing uniform standards for speed bump height and markings; the study sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to established camping sites; declaring an emergency.
summary: Clarifies that a homeless camp counts as established only after 72 hours of continuous occupancy before removal notice can be posted; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to water; declaring an emergency.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Appropriates added funds to the Water Resources Department for water right transaction staff, and directs a study of water rules reported to interim committees.

title: Relating to abuse of students.
summary: Changes when DHS may substantiate child abuse findings arising from restraint or seclusion of students.

title: Relating to marine research; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires a University of Oregon scientist on the Research Vessel Council and appropriates funds to HECC and UO for marine biology research programs.

title: Relating to funding grasshopper suppression efforts; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets counties spend up to eight percent of past state grasshopper-suppression funds on administrative costs, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to moving the Oregon-Idaho border; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force to study and report on moving the Oregon-Idaho border to include certain Oregon counties in Idaho.

title: Relating to forestry; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority; providing that this Act shall be referred to the people for their approval or rejection.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a new timber severance tax, repeals existing forest harvest taxes, abolishes the Emergency Fire Cost Committee and Forest Land Protection Fund, and refers the Act to voters.

title: Relating to chiropractic physicians.
summary: Removes limits on the duration of care, number of visits, and areas of practice for chiropractors serving as attending physicians in workers' comp claims.

title: Relating to the family and medical leave insurance program.
summary: Requires the Employment Department to study the family and medical leave insurance program and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to seismic hazards; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs DOGAMI to study earthquake-induced toxic inhalation risks and report to the State Resilience Officer by December 2027; the study is confidential pending review.

title: Relating to political activities in residential tenant facilities; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars landlords of manufactured dwelling parks and marinas from banning political canvassing or solicitation on their property.

title: Relating to medical assistance reimbursement of behavioral health services; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to set minimum Medicaid reimbursement rates for behavioral health services.

title: Relating to merit-based compensation.
summary: Directs the Teacher Standards and Practices Commission to study merit-based compensation for education workers and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to child care facilities; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Land Conservation and Development department to write and publish guidance for local governments on siting child care facilities by end of 2026.

title: Relating to Oregon's growing aging population; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates the Shared Future Oregon Task Force to develop a state plan on aging and requires agencies to consider effects on older adults; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to abuse of students; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Removes certain restraint and seclusion of students from the definition of child abuse, and takes effect 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to urban renewal.
summary: Requires voter approval for new urban renewal plans and substantial amendments to existing plans.

title: Relating to city councillors seeking reelection before the expiration of their current term; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Bars city councillors from seeking reelection before the last election of their current term, except when moving between districts.

title: Relating to water rights.
summary: Bars state consideration of whether certain water right changes would impair or harm the public interest, removing that review criterion.

title: Relating to water right examiner certification.
summary: Removes the sunset so existing water right examiner certification provisions become permanent.

title: Relating to Clackamas County community land trust housing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates money through OHCS to Community LendingWorks to fund community land trust purchases of Clackamas County homes for first-time buyers.

title: Relating to the Teacher Standards and Practices Commission; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates funding for nine new Teacher Standards and Practices Commission staff positions to support student safety and adult accountability, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Bars local governments from imposing or raising system development charges for NFPA 13D home fire sprinklers and for larger water meter capacity; orders a housing study.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Transfers money from the senior property tax deferral account to the Healthy Homes Repair Fund and to DOR for tax deferral outreach.

title: Relating to Housing and Community Services Department home ownership programs; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the state housing department to amend down payment assistance and home ownership programs to expand eligibility, including to moderate-income households, by January 2026.

title: Relating to study of active forest management; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the State Forestry Department to study improving active forest management, report to legislative committees by September 2027, and receives appropriated funds.

title: Relating to coordinated care organization reserves.
summary: Creates a State Treasury escrow fund for CCO restricted reserves and lets CCOs request payments for costs outside their global budgets.

title: Relating to regulating sales of admission tickets to entertainment events.
summary: Bans ticket-buying software that evades sale limits and requires resellers to possess tickets and disclose terms, enforced under the Unlawful Trade Practices Act.

title: Relating to betel nuts; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a betel nut health awareness campaign funded through OHA grants, requires provider training and curriculum content, and mandates an OHA report by December 2026.

title: Relating to PFAS.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Bans sale and distribution of certain consumer products containing intentionally added PFAS, requires manufacturer compliance certificates, and authorizes Attorney General enforcement starting 2027.

title: Relating to solid waste incinerators.
summary: Directs DEQ to study solid waste incinerators and report findings to interim environment committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to publication of certain election information.
summary: Requires county clerks to publish a county voters' pamphlet and at least two unofficial vote tallies on election day for primary and general elections.

title: Relating to training of armed public safety officers.
summary: Requires certification training for firearm-armed public safety officers to include two hours of nonlethal technique training for each hour of lethal training.

title: Relating to the Attorney General.
summary: Directs the Attorney General to study state laws on workplace safety and health and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to obesity treatments.
summary: Requires certain health insurers, OHP, PEBB and OEBB plans to cover specified treatments for an obesity diagnosis, under set conditions.

title: Relating to funding county assessment functions; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Raises and inflation-indexes the county recording fee and diverts a share of non-bond property tax money to the county assessment fund.

title: Relating to a cultural exchange program; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a student cultural exchange program overseen by the Department of Education, funded by transferring money from the Statewide Education Initiatives Account.

title: Relating to notification requirements for structures located within 1,000 feet of an interstate pipeline; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires notice to the Oregon Utility Notification Center before building near interstate pipelines, and bars building permits until pipeline owners' replies are received.

title: Relating to residential tenancy hold deposits.
summary: Requires landlords who revoke a rental offer after taking a hold deposit to pay minimum damages unless the deposit is returned within five business days.

title: Relating to evictions of squatters.
summary: Allows an owner or landlord to evict a squatter, making it easier to remove people occupying property without permission.

title: Relating to housing discrimination based on minor status; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Prohibits discrimination in real property transactions based on minor status, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to the administration of medications for adults in custody.
summary: Directs the Department of Corrections to study when medications can and should be given involuntarily to adults in custody and report by September 2026.

title: Relating to exempt wells that supply ground water for domestic purposes.
summary: Requires landlords renting dwellings with exempt wells in ground water quality management areas to test drinking water for arsenic, coliform, lead and nitrates.

title: Relating to exempt wells that supply water for domestic purposes.
summary: Requires sellers to give buyers well test results and copy them to DEQ, lets buyers sue if results are withheld, and changes the seller disclosure form.

title: Relating to water utility ratepayer assistance; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a state fund, administered through HCSD grants, to help low-income households pay water, stormwater and sewer bills.

title: Relating to state financial administration; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through HECC to the University of Oregon and Portland State University for water-related research and grants.

title: Relating to tribal relations training for the legislative branch; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires quarterly tribal relations training by the Commission on Indian Services and annual attendance by legislators and legislative staff.

title: Relating to highway names.
summary: Requires removal of the term "squaw" from Oregon highway names and directs public bodies to rename affected highways.

title: Relating to the Commission on Indian Services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a natural resources tribal liaison position at the Commission on Indian Services and appropriates money to fund it, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to offensive names; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Oregon Geographic Names Board to list offensive geographic names, recommend replacements to the federal board, and report to the Legislature; sunsets 2029.

title: Relating to required disclosures of fees during certain transactions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires sellers of consumer goods or services to show all mandatory fees in advertised or quoted prices, except government taxes and actual shipping charges.

title: Relating to tuition waivers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands Oregon's veterans tuition waiver to community colleges and partnered apprenticeships, and bars reducing the waiver by certain student aid.

title: Relating to pregnancy resources.
summary: Requires pregnant persons to consult a state pregnancy resources hotline at least 48 hours before an abortion, with $5,000 penalties for violations.

title: Relating to treatment for minors; declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets procedures for parental consent to a minor's inpatient substance use treatment and expands parental access to the minor's related health information.

title: Relating to redistricting; providing that this Act shall be referred to the people for their approval or rejection.
summary: Refers to voters a measure requiring redistricting to seek partisan registration parity within five points in at least 40 House and 20 Senate districts.

title: Relating to civics; declaring an emergency.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Education; Government and administration
summary: Creates a Secretary of State civics division and a task force, requires civics teaching, and sets up a commission that can require warnings on candidates' false statements.

title: Relating to greenhouse gas emissions reporting; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Environmental Quality Commission to hire a third party to set a greenhouse gas reporting emissions factor for unspecified electricity and update rules by 2027.

title: Relating to the costs of compliance with electric energy standards for electric utilities.
summary: Sets a single cost limit on utility compliance with both the renewable portfolio standard and state clean energy targets.

title: Relating to drive-through restaurants.
summary: Requires drive-through restaurants to provide a garbage can within 15 feet of the service window for customers to dispose of trash.

title: Relating to motorcycles.
summary: Allows motorcycles to travel between lanes under certain conditions and raises the fine for unlawful passing by motorcycles or mopeds to a maximum of $2,000.

title: Relating to aquatic invasive species; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to DEQ for activities preventing aquatic invasive species from entering through ballast water, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to water.
summary: Creates uniform procedures for hearing contested cases about water use, without changing substantive water rules.

title: Relating to acquisitions of real property by foreclosure for delinquent taxes; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Sets when HOA and condo assessments begin accruing on tax-foreclosed property deeded to a county, creates a lien, and specifies liability and satisfaction dates.

title: Relating to large energy use facilities; and declaring an emergency.
topics: AI and technology; Environment and energy
summary: Directs the PUC to create a rate class for large energy use facilities, allocating their costs to them, requiring contracts, and reporting to the Legislature; sunsets 2035.

title: Relating to certificates of need; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts institutions for mental diseases from the Oregon Health Authority's certificate of need requirement.

title: Relating to nuclear-fueled thermal power plants; providing that this Act shall be referred to the people for their approval or rejection.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Repeals requirements that nuclear plants have a waste repository and voter approval before siting, and refers the repeal to voters.

title: Relating to fluorescent lamps; declaring an emergency.
summary: Exempts fluorescent lamps used for animal care from the state's ban on fluorescent lamps and from the prohibition on their sale and distribution.

title: Relating to an exemption for certain minor league baseball players from certain laws governing employment conditions.
summary: Exempts minor league baseball players covered by a collective bargaining agreement from certain state employment-condition laws.

title: Relating to the enforcement of federal immigration laws with respect to individuals who are convicted of a crime.
summary: Requires public bodies and law enforcement to help enforce federal immigration laws against people convicted of violent felonies or certain sexual offenses.

title: Relating to regional career centers.
summary: Lets education service districts create regional career centers for career and technical education and appropriates General Fund money to support them.

title: Relating to controlled substance crimes; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a new crime of possessing, buying, making, delivering or selling pill presses, punishable by up to five years and a $125,000 fine.

title: Relating to support for health care providers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates primary care loan repayment and practice incentive programs, low-interest EHR loans, a quality-measure reporting portal, and a credentialing study.

title: Relating to name changes.
summary: Allows people entering marriage or a registered domestic partnership to change their middle name, including back to their birth middle name.

title: Relating to the use of local transient tax revenue; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets cities and counties spend net hotel tax revenue on public safety and certain community infrastructure costs.

title: Relating to standard charges established by a hospital.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Requires hospitals to publish and update standard charge lists, report them to the Oregon Health Authority, and face complaints, corrective action, civil penalties, and private suits over collections.

title: Relating to substance use.
summary: Modifies the definition of 'recovery' in the Drug Addiction Treatment and Recovery Act; the text gives no operative details.

title: Relating to nicotine; declaring an emergency.
summary: Limits nicotine vaping product sales to AG-listed, FDA-authorized products, bans unauthorized flavored versions, and adds age verification and seizure powers.

title: Relating to the siting of child care facilities.
summary: Expands the areas where child care facilities may be sited and requires local governments to update land use laws within one year.

title: Relating to financial assistance for the cost of health care services.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study hospital financial assistance and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to school safety; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires schools to prepare maps for use by local and state first responders and public safety agencies, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to interpersonal boundary invasions affecting youth.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study state laws and reporting requirements on abuse and sexual conduct in public schools, reporting findings by September 2026.

title: Relating to published defamatory statements.
summary: Modifies the procedure for demanding correction or retraction of defamatory statements published in electronic newspapers, magazines or periodicals.

title: Relating to small modular reactor energy facilities.
summary: Allows siting of small modular reactor power plants without a high-level waste repository or statewide voter approval of site certificates.

title: Relating to towing.
summary: Requires towers to accept cash exact change and itemized receipts, allows card payment and retrieval of personal property, and lets people recover damages from unlawful towing.

title: Relating to the culturally responsive organization down payment assistance program.
summary: Appropriates state funds to the Housing and Community Services Department to continue down payment assistance delivered through culturally responsive organizations.

title: Relating to the promotion of seafood products in the public schools of this state; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money to promote seafood in Oregon public schools through the Oregon Coast Visitors Association and the Department of Agriculture.

title: Relating to rules advisory committees.
summary: Requires agencies and the Small Business Rules Advisory Committee to invite certain legislators to join rulemaking advisory committees as nonvoting members.

title: Relating to community infrastructure inventory; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to Business Oregon to update the inventory of infrastructure needed for new housing and to prepare related water infrastructure reports.

title: Relating to water research institutes.
summary: Appropriates money through HECC to Oregon State University for its Institute for Water and Watersheds.

title: Relating to emergency medical services; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Government and administration; Health care; Labor and employment
summary: Directs an EMS strategic plan, provides loan repayment and license-cost subsidies, lets the Governor deploy EMS resources in emergencies, and eases some EMS licensing requirements.

title: Relating to water resources; declaring an emergency.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Water Resources Department for water data collection and monitoring for 2025-27, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to certificate of need laws.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study certificate of need laws and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the transfer of federal public lands.
summary: Directs the Department of State Lands to petition Congress for transfer of federal public lands, then sell them or transfer them to tribes or hold them in trust for counties.

title: Relating to funding for deflection programs; declaring an emergency.
summary: Tasks the Oregon Criminal Justice Commission with creating a formula for distributing grant funds to counties for deflection programs.

title: Relating to wastewater treatment; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates state money through DAS as a grant to Adair Village to build a wastewater treatment facility.

title: Relating to wildfire.
summary: Creates a new Department of Wildfire to oversee wildfire prevention, intervention and recovery in Oregon.

title: Relating to tolling.
summary: Requires voter approval before the Oregon Transportation Commission can impose a toll on a highway.

title: Relating to eelgrass resources in state waters; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Task Force on Eelgrass Resources to study eelgrass in state waters and report to the Legislature by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to sex crime statutes of limitation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Removes the statute of limitations for most felony sex crimes, allowing prosecution later, and takes effect 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to statutes of limitation; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Eliminates the statute of limitations for civil claims based on child sexual abuse or sexual assault, applying prospectively, and takes effect on passage.

title: Relating to domestic violence survivor defendants; prescribing an effective date; providing for criminal sentence reduction that requires approval by a two-thirds majority.
summary: Lets courts treat ongoing domestic violence against a defendant as mitigation, allowing downward departures and lesser sentences even under mandatory minimums.

title: Relating to prostitution; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires prostitution offenders to be 18 or older and authorizes protective custody for children who engaged in or are at risk of commercial sex acts.

title: Relating to strangulation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Increases the penalty for felony strangulation to up to 10 years' imprisonment and a $250,000 fine, placing it in sentencing grid crime category 8.

title: Relating to sexual battery; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a civil cause of action allowing a person to sue someone who removes a condom without their consent.

title: Relating to rocky habitat management; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs DLCD to act on rocky habitat management and authorizes Ocean Science Trust grants for nonregulatory programs, with an appropriation and emergency clause.

title: Relating to business registrations; and declaring an emergency.
topics: AI and technology; Consumer protection and business
summary: Lets the Secretary of State accept commercial mail receiving agency addresses for business filings and shields a business's physical address from public disclosure on request.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Directs Oregon Housing and Community Services to create a senior housing initiative funded by transfers from the senior property tax deferral account.

title: Relating to pediatric care; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Bars out-of-network pediatric providers from balance billing and requires insurers and state benefit boards to pay them like in-network providers in certain cases.

title: Relating to pediatric care; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires health plans, including PEBB and OEBB plans, to reimburse out-of-network pediatric providers at in-network rates and bars extra out-of-pocket costs for pediatric care.

title: Relating to artificial intelligence.
summary: Creates a Senator Aaron Woods AI Commission within DOJ to monitor state AI use, report annually, and hire a Chief AI Officer.

title: Relating to the lower Deschutes River.
summary: Requires the Department of Energy to study the lower Deschutes River and report findings to energy committees by September 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to residency requirements under the wildlife laws.
summary: Lets out-of-state full-time college students buy Oregon wildlife licenses, tags and permits at resident rates.

title: Relating to the Lunar New Year.
summary: Designates the Lunar New Year as a legal state holiday.

title: Relating to wildlife management; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs Fish and Wildlife to study Steens Mountain mule deer, reporting by September 2028, and appropriates General Fund money for the study.

title: Relating to electric vehicles; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets DEQ cut zero-emission vehicle rebates, widens Charge Ahead rebate eligibility, and directs fund money to education and outreach.

title: Relating to electric vehicles.
summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Quality to study electric vehicles and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to Public Records Advisory Council.
summary: Directs the Public Records Advisory Council to study public records and report findings to judiciary interim committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to mental health.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study mental health and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to Oregon's land use system.
summary: Requires the Department of Land Conservation and Development to study Oregon's land use system and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to criminal justice.
summary: Requires the Judicial Department to study how to improve the efficiency of the conviction set-aside process and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to animal rescue entities; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a defense to theft prosecution and civil immunity for animal rescue entities that take, keep, or dispose of cats as the Act provides.

title: Relating to unlawful practices in home solicitation sales; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets consumers sue home solicitation sellers that violate the law and makes such violations unlawful trade practices.

title: Relating to homelessness.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study homelessness and report findings to housing-related interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to health care benefits for part-time faculty.
summary: Directs the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to study health care benefits for part-time faculty and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to decedents' estates.
summary: Directs the Judicial Department to study ways to make decedents' estate administration more efficient and report to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to distributed power plants; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires electric companies to create distributed power plant programs that pay customers and third parties for grid services from distributed energy resources, with annual reporting.

title: Relating to child welfare; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires DHS to study demographics of families in the child welfare system and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to assessments.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to study the adequacy of public school assessments and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to access to resources for development in Curry County.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to study access to development resources in Curry County and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to pharmaceutical purchasing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates the Office of Pharmaceutical Purchasing to coordinate multistate drug buying and run the Oregon Prescription Drug Program, requiring some agencies and CCOs to participate.

title: Relating to tariffs.
summary: Directs OBDD to create a program reimbursing companies that relocate headquarters to Oregon for tariffs paid on goods imported through Coos Bay.

title: Relating to funding for veterans' services.
summary: Directs the Department of Veterans' Affairs to study funding sources for veterans' services and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to an appropriation for the Western Lane Fire and EMS Authority; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates state money to the Western Lane Fire and EMS Authority to remodel one of its fire and rescue stations.

title: Relating to an appropriation for the Mapleton Water District; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates state money to the Mapleton Water District to replace its water distribution lines, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to state financial administration; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through HECC to Southwestern Oregon Community College to repair elevators in Tioga Hall.

title: Relating to domestic relations.
summary: Requires custody orders to be written within five days, limits parenting coordinator appointments to parent agreement after cost discussion, and bars the original judge from hearing remanded custody matters.

title: Relating to the public purpose charge.
summary: Repeals the electricity public purpose charge, its expenditure standard, and the Housing and Community Services electricity fund.

title: Relating to prerequisites to performing abortions.
summary: Requires an ultrasound before abortions, with a three-day waiting period and civil penalties; penalty revenue funds foster children's scholarships.

title: Relating to human trafficking; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires school district boards to teach about child human trafficking and adopt a prevention curriculum addressing it, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to documents issued by the Department of Transportation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires proof of lawful U.S. status before DOT issues noncommercial driver licenses, permits, or ID cards.

title: Relating to examinations administered to homeschooled children.
summary: Requires education service districts to pay for examinations that homeschooled children must take, shifting the cost from parents to ESDs.

title: Relating to public safety.
summary: Lets public safety agencies charge fees to entities that overuse services, after notice and a chance to cure, with annual reporting; sunsets in 2031.

title: Relating to vehicles.
summary: Sets uniform helmet rules for kids under 16 on bikes and e-scooters, and adds age limits for e-bike classes. ODOT must run a public information campaign.

title: Relating to funding for disabled veterans; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Disabled Veterans Assistance Fund and requires grants to disabled veterans for accessibility resources at homes they or their family own.

title: Relating to the Oregon Electric Transmission Authority; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Creates the Oregon Electric Transmission Authority to finance, build and own transmission, funded by bonds, user payments and a capped charge on large industrial customers.

title: Relating to emergency preparedness.
summary: Creates the Oregon Partnership for Resilience, a public corporation to pursue innovative emergency preparedness, with governance, powers, and annual reporting.

title: Relating to estate tax treatment of natural resource property; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends the estate tax exemption for farm, forestry and fishing property to interests held through trusts and business entities, with replacement property allowed.

title: Relating to youth behavioral health services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a sunsetting OHA pilot providing youth substance use prevention and mental or behavioral health services in 20 counties, with outcome and feasibility reports.

title: Relating to restrictions on expression in certain housing communities.
summary: Prohibits continuing care retirement communities from banning certain free expression in common areas, with civil penalties enforced by the Department of Human Services.

title: Relating to pretrial release; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits pretrial release for certain defendants, sets a minimum security amount for Ballot Measure 11 charges, and bars release for new crimes committed while on release.

title: Relating to the water workforce; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Water Workforce Program in the Higher Education Coordinating Commission, funded through grants to local workforce boards, with an emergency clause.

title: Relating to bonding; declaring an emergency.
summary: Raises the cap on XI-G general obligation bonds that a single community college may issue for projects, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to personal injury protection benefits.
summary: Requires insurers offering car insurance to also offer personal injury protection benefits, while letting drivers choose whether to accept them.

title: Relating to the Commission on Statewide Law Enforcement Standards of Conduct and Discipline.
summary: Directs the police standards commission to study law enforcement conduct and discipline standards and report findings to legislative judiciary committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to executive sessions.
summary: Extends the deadline for people to file written grievances alleging public bodies violated executive session rules.

title: Relating to collection of system development charges.
summary: Bars local governments from collecting system development charges for new urban homes before construction is finished or a certificate of occupancy is issued.

title: Relating to farmworker camp registration.
summary: Requires Oregon farmworker camp registration rules to match federal farmworker housing health and safety standards, and directs registration of compliant camps starting in 2028.

title: Relating to ballots.
summary: Prohibits individuals from collecting and returning other people's ballots, with exceptions, and sets fines per ballot for violations.

title: Relating to residential tenancies.
summary: Lets landlords end month-to-month tenancies without cause and raise rents without limit by repealing rent increase limits.

title: Relating to Oregon Youth Suicide Awareness Day; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Designates October 9 each year as Oregon Youth Suicide Awareness Day to raise awareness, with no policy changes.

title: Relating to a statewide shelter program; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a statewide shelter program at the Housing and Community Services Department, selecting regional coordinators to distribute funding to shelter providers; sunsets in 2034.

title: Relating to wildfire.
summary: Requires the State Forestry Department to study wildfires and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to contract preferences in public procurement for employee-owned businesses; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets state agencies give procurement preference to employee-owned businesses, adding them to the permitted preference sources for public contracts.

title: Relating to price displays required for retail fuel dispensing stations.
summary: Requires fuel retailers to post prices for all fuel grades on signs visible from the street and at each dispensing device.

title: Relating to incineration; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the State Police to study locations where controlled substances can be incinerated and report to interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to regional housing coordination; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a one-time grant to a nonprofit for regional housing coordination subgrants, appropriates General Fund money, requires a 2027 report, and sunsets in 2028.

title: Relating to the Latino Health System Task Force; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Latino Health System Task Force with membership and duties, requiring a report by December 15, 2026, then sunsetting.

title: Relating to agricultural seed.
summary: Requires growers planting turf-type perennial ryegrass or tall fescue for agricultural seed sale to register their fields with Oregon State University and file annual reports.

title: Relating to mandatory subjects of collective bargaining for school districts; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds class size and caseload to the mandatory subjects school districts must bargain with unions over.

title: Relating to energy performance contracts; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets state agencies sign energy performance contracts without competitive procurement, using Attorney General rules and a prequalified energy service company.

title: Relating to matching grants for cities; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Caps the local matching-fund share required for state grants to small cities for capital construction and municipal infrastructure.

title: Relating to lagoon wastewater treatment systems.
summary: Directs DEQ to create a program to examine and certify operators of lagoon wastewater treatment systems.

title: Relating to election dates for local option tax measures; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Requires local option tax measures to be decided only at even-year general elections, with an exception for certain extension measures.

title: Relating to damage caused by wildlife; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Creates a pilot program and fund, administered by the Department of Agriculture, for preventing and compensating wildlife damage, sunsetting in 2030 with a 2028 report.

title: Relating to court-appointed counsel.
summary: Limits court-appointed lawyers for parents and children in dependency and contested adoption cases to specified circumstances, such as possible criminal implications or alleged abuse.

title: Relating to revenue estimates; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Prescribes methods for General Fund revenue estimates and requires the Department of Revenue to transfer surplus-refund differences for various purposes.

title: Relating to housing development.
summary: Directs the Department of Land Conservation and Development to study housing development and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to electrical transmission.
summary: Directs the Department of Energy to study electrical transmission and report findings to energy interim committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to clean energy project requests for proposals.
summary: Requires the Oregon Department of Energy to study clean energy and report findings to interim energy committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to rental housing.
summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to study rental housing and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to transportation.
summary: Requires ODOT to study developing uniform standards for speed bump height and markings, sunsetting January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to education.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study the adequacy of Oregon public schools and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to utility wildfire safety practices.
summary: Creates a PUC wildfire safety certification for utilities with a wildfire plan, presuming certified utilities act reasonably on wildfire safety; valid 12 months.

title: Relating to education.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to study the adequacy of Oregon's public schools and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to education.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to study the adequacy of public school education and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to workforce development.
summary: Expands Prosperity 10,000 program goals and shifts administration to grants to local workforce boards, which then distribute funds using specified factors.

title: Relating to high-value farmland.
summary: Requires any company or state agency diverting a water body within 15 miles of high-value farmland to first study the diversion's impacts on that farmland.

title: Relating to senior centers.
summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study ways to fund senior centers and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to public improvement contract preferences for construction materials sourced in this state; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets state agencies and contracting bodies give bid preferences to in-state material makers and in-state benefit companies on public construction contracts, within a cost-increase cap.

title: Relating to the timeline for reviewing land use applications.
summary: Shortens to 90 days the deadline for cities and counties to decide land use applications for housing and mental health or addiction facilities.

title: Relating to fish; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a chum subaccount funded by a new chum fee, with money distributed for chum-related purposes, and changes Oregon Hatchery Research Center board and activities.

title: Relating to staffing plans for hospitals.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study hospital staffing plans and report findings to health interim committees by September 2026, sunsetting January 2027.

title: Relating to a grant program for community water infrastructure.
summary: Creates a grant program, run by OHA with DEQ, to repair or replace small community drinking water and wastewater facilities, funded through a new Small Community Water Infrastructure Fund.

title: Relating to criminal acts committed against certain employees; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands assault and aggravated harassment crimes to cover public employees and requires school expulsion policies for student assaults on school employees.

title: Relating to all-terrain vehicles; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets all-terrain vehicles use county roads where the county approves, expanding ATV highway access routes; effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to the use of crossbows for hunting; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires Oregon's Department of Fish and Wildlife to allow qualifying persons to hunt game mammals with a crossbow.

title: Relating to livestock brands.
summary: Raises some fees related to livestock brands; the text is brief and gives no other details.

title: Relating to energy facilities.
summary: Speeds energy facility siting by setting appeal and decision deadlines, easing site certificate changes and construction extensions, and allowing some transmission lines in farm zones.

title: Relating to the state budget.
summary: Directs the Legislative Policy and Research Director to study changing the budget-passage timeline and report to ways and means committees by June 1, 2026.

title: Relating to interstate bridges.
summary: Treats a local commission formed to replace a Columbia River bridge as a public body under the Oregon Tort Claims Act.

title: Relating to the security of state information technology assets; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets state agencies and their contractors apply for limited waivers from prohibitions on covered products used on state IT assets.

title: Relating to local option tax measures.
summary: Requires ballot title statements for proposed local option tax measures to include information about the measures' effects.

title: Relating to a special election; declaring an emergency.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Sets a November 4, 2025 special election for voters to approve or reject a constitutional amendment requiring a three-fifths vote for future amendments, and appropriates election funds.

title: Relating to majority vote thresholds for local charters; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires simple-majority votes on county and city charter questions and bans supermajority thresholds for them.

title: Relating to a deceased spousal unused exclusion amount for Oregon estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets a surviving spouse claim the unused portion of a deceased spouse's Oregon estate tax exclusion for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to removal proceedings.
summary: Lets the Governor commute prison sentences for removal and requires the Department of Corrections to work with ICE to identify and transfer people subject to removal.

title: Relating to assistance for unauthorized noncitizens.
summary: Bars Oregon Housing and Community Services funds from being spent on people unlawfully present in the US.

title: Relating to requiring the use of a Social Security number to claim an earned income tax credit; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires a Social Security number to claim the Oregon earned income tax credit, bars claims using an individual taxpayer identification number, and extends the credit's sunset.

title: Relating to gender-affirming care.
summary: Ends the requirement that certain health insurers and the Oregon Health Plan cover gender-affirming health care services.

title: Relating to firearms.
summary: Repeals 2021 gun safety laws on safe storage, loss reporting and minor supervision, lifts concealed-carry limits in the Capitol, airports and schools, and cuts CHL fees.

title: Relating to student athletes; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies Oregon law on compensation for student athletes at post-secondary institutions and declares an emergency, effective on passage.

title: Relating to excusal for religious instruction.
summary: Requires school districts to adopt a policy allowing students to be excused for released-time religious instruction courses, under prescribed requirements.

title: Relating to the use of software applications by minors.
topics: AI and technology; Children and families; Consumer protection and business
summary: Requires app stores to verify user ages, obtain parental consent for minors' app downloads and purchases, and enforces violations as unlawful trade practices.

title: Relating to crime; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Makes theft of controlled substances or prescription medication first-degree theft and certain pharmacy burglaries first-degree burglary, with higher maximum penalties.

title: Relating to data centers.
topics: AI and technology; Environment and energy
summary: Requires data centers to report water and electricity use quarterly, and directs the EQC to set emissions standards for their standby generators.

title: Relating to recovery schools.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study statutory requirements for approved recovery schools and report findings to education interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to certification of operators of certain water facilities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs EQC and OHA to adopt rules certifying out-of-state operators of sewage, potable water and distribution facilities from nonreciprocal jurisdictions, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to water management in the Harney Basin; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study Harney Basin water management and report to legislative natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to critical ground water areas; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study critical ground water areas and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to ground water management.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study voluntary agreements for groundwater management and report to legislative natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to water conservation.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study water-related rules and report to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to water management.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study water management issues and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the welfare of young people; declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes child welfare rules on restraint, abuse investigations, agency licensing and out-of-state placements, sets minor inpatient behavioral health admission procedures, and creates a youth institute.

title: Relating to school capital construction.
summary: Requires new school construction in certain districts to meet resiliency standards to qualify for OSCIM matching grants, and creates an advisory committee on emergency shelter rooms.

title: Relating to modifications to an urban growth boundary.
summary: Lets cities of 20,000 or fewer expand their urban growth boundaries through a temporary program, with lower affordable housing percentage requirements.

title: Relating to modifications to an urban growth boundary.
summary: Lets cities of 20,000 or fewer bring exchanged lands into their urban growth boundary through a temporary program, regardless of land designation.

title: Relating to the Ten Commandments.
summary: Directs the State Parks and Recreation Department to place a Ten Commandments monument in the State Capitol State Park.

title: Relating to juvenile offenders.
summary: Requires certain youths under 18 charged with specified crimes to be tried as adults, and repeals second-look, life-sentence bans, and release hearings for them.

title: Relating to the homestead property tax deferral program.
summary: Changes market value and income limits to expand eligibility for the homestead property tax deferral program, and requires an LRO report on equity-based eligibility.

title: Relating to tax treatment of net losses; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Removes the 15-year limit on corporate net operating loss carryforwards and caps the NOL deduction at 95 percent of taxable income.

title: Relating to elections; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to counties for elections infrastructure and to the Secretary of State for a civic engagement toolkit, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to persons with mental illness; declaring an emergency.
summary: Revises civil commitment definitions and evidence rules, sets state hospital bed minimums, modifies psychiatric advance directives, and bars commitment of certain unfit defendants.

title: Relating to electric vehicle rebates.
summary: Modifies Oregon's zero-emission and EV rebate programs: limits eligibility to individuals, caps rebates at one per household every four years, and increases Charge Ahead funding.

title: Relating to maintaining emergency contact information in the records of the Department of Transportation; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to ODOT to create a voluntary emergency contact form for driver records that police can use to reach listed contacts.

title: Relating to police body camera recordings.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Bars officers involved in deadly force incidents from viewing body camera footage before their interview, creates a court appeal path for denied footage requests, and directs storage standards.

title: Relating to housing for individuals with substance use disorders.
summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing for people with substance use disorders and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to open meetings on certain matters; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires labor negotiations conducted by or on behalf of public bodies to be held in open meetings, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to dams; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires a Water Resources Department study of Klamath River dam removal impacts and bars removing certain dams until the report is submitted.

title: Relating to medical assistance for children; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Renames Cover All People to Cover All Children and removes state coverage eligibility for immigrant adults who would otherwise qualify for medical assistance.

title: Relating to registering to vote by voter registration card; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals automatic voter registration data transfers from ODOT and OHA to the Secretary of State and ends pre-registration for those 16 and older; takes effect on passage.

title: Relating to cannabis; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Prohibits marijuana advertising, packaging and labeling likely to cause minors to unlawfully possess or consume marijuana.

title: Relating to health care; declaring an emergency.
summary: Adds insurer reporting and provider-notice duties for behavioral health claims and utilization review, creates a Mental Health Parity Ombudsman with an appropriation, and adds a HIEAC member.

title: Relating to hiring retired corrections officers.
summary: Authorizes the Department of Corrections to hire retired corrections officers under specified conditions, sunsetting January 1, 2032.

title: Relating to telemedicine.
summary: Allows Oregon physicians and physician associates to use telemedicine to treat patients located out of state under specified circumstances, subject to that jurisdiction's laws.

title: Relating to dams.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study topics related to the Winchester Dam and report to legislative natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to crematory incinerators; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars state and regional air regulators from requiring crematory incinerators to operate above 1,600 degrees Fahrenheit.

title: Relating to low-proof spirit beverages; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets wine licensees, distilleries and spirit importers sell and distribute low-proof spirit beverages, and imposes a new tax on manufacturers and importing distributors of them.

title: Relating to reporting by institutions of higher education; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Adds data fields to higher education institutions' annual reports on campus sexual misconduct and violence allegations, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to state financial administration; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Transportation for safety improvements at a specified Gladstone intersection.

title: Relating to state financial administration; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through DAS to the Clackamas County Children's Commission for a Head Start facility.

title: Relating to state financial administration of Housing and Community Services Department programs; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to the Housing and Community Services Department to distribute to named organizations to continue housing and homelessness services, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to health equity.
summary: Directs the Oregon Advocacy Commissions Office to hire permanent staff to convene task forces developing recommendations on health inequities.

title: Relating to translation services.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study cheaper ways for state agencies to procure translation services and report by September 2026.

title: Relating to exclusions from estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds a $4 million estate tax exclusion plus an additional $4 million exclusion, indexed for inflation.

title: Relating to an income tax subtraction for amounts received from retirement plans; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an Oregon personal income tax subtraction for amounts received from retirement plans, for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to dams; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Prohibits removing dams, directs the Water Resources Department to encourage building 10 new dams by 2030, and to compile dam lists and report.

title: Relating to participation in athletic competitions according to biological sex.
summary: Requires schools to designate sports teams by biological sex, bars biological males from female-designated sports, and creates causes of action for enforcement.

title: Relating to legislative staff; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets legislators-elect hire office staff and legislative assistants starting the month they take the oath of office.

title: Relating to the possession of firearms in the Capitol.
summary: Lets legislators and legislative staff with concealed handgun licenses carry firearms in the Capitol, with an affirmative defense against possession charges.

title: Relating to emergency backup power for radio towers.
summary: Requires radio towers to have an emergency backup power system able to provide 14 days of power.

title: Relating to school district investigations of misconduct.
summary: Creates a task force to evaluate how school districts respond to reports of school employee misconduct; it changes no rules.

title: Relating to statutes of limitations for tax debt; prescribing an effective date.
