summary: Cancels uncollected tax debt, penalties and interest after 10 years, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to real property.
summary: Shortens the time to sue for construction defects in condos and HOA homes, adds pre-suit notice rules, and requires moisture inspections.

title: Relating to an income tax credit for solar energy systems; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a refundable income tax credit for buying battery storage and solar photovoltaic systems for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to credentialing of health care practitioners.
summary: Directs OHA to create a common electronic credentialing program and database for health care practitioners, with a General Fund appropriation and a 2028 start.

title: Relating to community solar projects.
summary: Lets community solar projects join the program regardless of size or location and bars the PUC from capping program size below 25% of load.

title: Relating to funding the operations of the Bureau of Labor and Industries; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows the Workers' Benefit Fund to pay the Labor Commissioner's expenses for carrying out statutory duties; declares an emergency, effective on passage.

title: Relating to compensation for services performed in connection with a claim for a veteran's benefit; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars people from taking compensation for helping others get veterans' benefits, unless federal or state law allows it, with violations treated as unlawful trade practices.

title: Relating to provider reimbursement in the state's medical assistance program.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study Medicaid provider reimbursement rates and report findings to legislative health committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to increases of the personal income tax standard deduction; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Increases the Oregon personal income tax standard deduction for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to emergency volunteers.
summary: Directs ODEM to create a registry of emergency volunteers and a statewide training program, and declares a policy that lawmakers should dedicate unexpended funds to volunteers.

title: Relating to a property tax exemption for the homesteads of certain seniors; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a property tax exemption for owner-occupied homes of seniors aged 65+, with 10+ years' residence and household income up to $150,000, increasing annually.

title: Relating to electromagnetic weapons.
summary: Creates a task force to study electromagnetic weapons use in Oregon and report gaps in law by December 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to division of rural lands for dwellings.
summary: Allows owners of rural land with a dwelling to divide it into up to five lots and add up to four more dwellings, if built by 2028; sunsets 2029.

title: Relating to urban growth boundary expansion.
summary: Allows cities to expand their urban growth boundaries to offset unbuildable lands in their buildable lands inventory.

title: Relating to costs of developing housing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to give grants to moderate-income housing developers to offset permitting fees, with an appropriation.

title: Relating to art therapy; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets the Health Licensing Office issue provisional art therapist licenses and requires two years of supervised mental health practice for full licensure.

title: Relating to art therapy; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a provisional art therapist license and requires Medicaid and CCOs to reimburse behavioral health services by licensed art therapists.

title: Relating to the salary threshold for determining overtime exemption status.
summary: Directs the Bureau of Labor and Industries to study the minimum salary threshold for overtime exemptions and report by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the Task Force on Law Libraries; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Establishes a Task Force on Law Libraries that must report to an interim legislative committee by December 15, 2026.

title: Relating to funding for substance use services.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study Measure 110's substance use services funding formula and report to legislative health committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to investments.
summary: Requires the State Treasurer and Oregon Investment Council to run an ESG analysis system, assign oversight staff, report annually, and avoid entities found to violate international law.

title: Relating to claims for transmission of intimate images.
summary: Lets a person sue anyone who sends them an intimate image to their device without consent, in certain circumstances.

title: Relating to local rent control; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals the state ban on local rent control, letting cities and counties impose rent control.

title: Relating to Nowruz Day; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Designates March 21 each year as Nowruz Day in Oregon and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to housing; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Requires DCBS to register all rented or rentable dwelling units, allows civil penalties for non-registration, and adds a fee on large dwelling-unit owners.

title: Relating to unlawful adoption activity.
summary: Creates a new crime of unlawful adoption activity, punishable by up to 30 days' imprisonment, a $1,250 fine, or both.

title: Relating to the regulation of artificial intelligence.
summary: Requires the State Chief Information Officer to study artificial intelligence and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to protected labor relations activities.
summary: Directs the Bureau of Labor and Industries to study safeguarding protected labor relations activities and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to veterans.
summary: Adds veteran-focused personal health navigators as a new traditional health worker category, with OHA setting qualification criteria by rule.

title: Relating to homelessness; declaring an emergency.
summary: Restores the pre-2021 law on removing homeless camps by repealing HB 3124 (2021) and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through DAS to the City of Salem for a plaza and memorial at the former Fairview Training Center site.

title: Relating to agency offices.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study consolidating and selling or leasing unused state office space, reporting by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to conduct of elections.
topics: Elections and voting; Labor and employment
summary: Makes Election Day a paid holiday, makes in-person voting the default, requires photo ID, and requires ballots to arrive by Election Day.

title: Relating to the withdrawal of the federally approved state plan concerning workplace safety; declaring an emergency.
summary: Withdraws Oregon's federally approved workplace safety plan, repeals implementing statutes, and bars state OSHA rules stricter than federal standards.

title: Relating to debt resolution services; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires debt resolution service providers to register with the Department of Consumer and Business Services and regulates their activities with consumers.

title: Relating to producer responsibility; declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes newspaper from Oregon's producer responsibility recycling laws for packaging, printing and writing paper, and food serviceware, effective on passage.

title: Relating to a presumption against liability for claims that result from criminal activity in multifamily residential property; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a rebuttable presumption that apartment owners and operators are not negligent or liable for crime-related injuries or damage if they implement specified security measures and training.

title: Relating to the climate.
summary: Directs the Department of Environmental Quality to study the climate and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to energy.
summary: Requires the State Department of Energy to study energy and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026; the provision sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to the environment.
summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Quality to study the environment and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 2026, sunsetting January 2027.

title: Relating to voting by adults in custody.
summary: Allows people convicted of a felony to register, update registration, and vote while incarcerated, and sets their residence as their pre-incarceration address.

title: Relating to coastal research; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to the Department of State Lands for the Oregon Ocean Science Fund to make competitive coastal research grants; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to checkout bags.
summary: Prohibits restaurants and retailers from providing reusable plastic checkout bags to consumers.

title: Relating to public safety; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates an Oregon Business Development Department grant program for hospitals near tsunami zones to store fuel and water for emergencies.

title: Relating to union misrepresentation.
summary: Makes it unlawful to falsely impersonate a union representative and gives unions sole authority to designate their own representatives.

title: Relating to cannabis health care technicians; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the OLCC to certify cannabis health care technicians and create financial incentives for marijuana retailers that employ them.

title: Relating to the maritime workforce.
summary: Directs the Employment Department to study the state's maritime workforce and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to consumer protection for utility ratepayers.
summary: Doubles the minimum low-income electric bill assistance charge on utility customers to $40 million and raises the per-site customer cap to $1,000 monthly.

title: Relating to public records requests.
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to study public records requests and report findings to judiciary interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to municipal solid waste; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a temporary task force on municipal solid waste in the Willamette Valley, which reports to legislative committees by December 2026 and then sunsets.

title: Relating to human services.
summary: Requires DHS to submit an annual legislative report on a tax preparation assistance grant program and modifies when DHS must appoint Critical Incident Review Teams.

title: Relating to early childhood.
summary: Requires the Department of Early Learning and Care to study early childhood and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to children.
summary: Directs the Department of Human Services to study Oregon's child demographics and report findings by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to electric vehicle fire training for emergency responders.
summary: Directs DPSST, with the State Fire Marshal, to train emergency responders on fires from lithium-ion batteries and electric vehicles.

title: Relating to medical treatments with investigational products.
summary: Lets health care practitioners offer terminal or severe chronic disease patients non-FDA-approved investigational products, with liability protections for those who comply.

title: Relating to the use of ground water in the Harney Basin.
summary: Renames the Greater Harney Valley Groundwater Area of Concern as the Harney Basin Groundwater Management Area and sets Water Resources Department authorities and duties there.

title: Relating to voluntary agreements among ground water users.
summary: Makes unspecified changes to the law allowing voluntary agreements among groundwater users; the summary gives no detail on the changes.

title: Relating to preschool children with disabilities.
summary: Requires the Oregon Department of Education to pay state funds to early intervention and early childhood special education providers in monthly installments.

title: Relating to government efficiency; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs DAS to create workforce plans and uniform agency definitions, requires public-fund recipients to report on spending, and creates KPM and SOS audit teams.

title: Relating to a study concerning disparate homeownership access; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the DLCD to commission and report on a study of policies contributing to disparate access to homeownership; sunsets January 2, 2028.

title: Relating to homicide.
summary: Expands second-degree murder to cover intentionally or knowingly causing the death of an unborn child through unlawful conduct.

title: Relating to water banks.
summary: Authorizes a Deschutes River water bank pilot program through January 2, 2034, and increases Water Resources Department spending authority to fund it.

title: Relating to interscholastic activities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires OSAA and similar interscholastic activity organizations to implement measures addressing discriminatory harassment or bullying by teams and coaches.

title: Relating to interveners for deafblind students.
summary: Requires TSPC to set certification rules for deafblind interveners and directs ODE to fund a program to hire and retain certified interveners in schools.

title: Relating to individual development accounts; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money and establishes quarterly lottery allocations to HCSD for the individual development account program.

title: Relating to a tax credit for employment of agricultural workers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a 2026–2031 income or corporate excise tax credit for taxpayers who employ agricultural workers.

title: Relating to a tax credit for overtime wages paid to agricultural workers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Increases the agricultural overtime wage tax credit, allows advance payment during the wage year, and removes the annual cap, starting tax year 2026.

title: Relating to school nursing.
summary: Requires school districts to adopt and annually update health services plans, changes school nursing categories and staffing ratios, and lets administrators count related professional development toward license renewal.

title: Relating to grants for school nursing services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Authorizes state grants to school districts and ESDs to improve school nursing services, develop health services plans, and run a regional nursing pilot.

title: Relating to seafood processors; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets environmental regulators allow seafood processors' permits to use a mixing zone to meet bacteria water quality criteria.

title: Relating to public safety.
summary: Directs the Criminal Justice Commission to study how different sentence types affect recidivism, reporting by September 15, 2026, and sunsetting January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to victims.
summary: Redirects half of insurance-carrier restitution to DOJ victim services and lets carriers tell DAs not to seek restitution.

title: Relating to ibogaine.
summary: Directs OHA and the Department of Veterans' Affairs to study ibogaine use for certain disorders, reporting to the Legislature by 2029; sunsets 2030.

title: Relating to discipline of children in early childhood care.
summary: Directs the Department of Early Learning and Care to study child suspension and expulsion policies in early childhood care and report findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the State Board of Massage Therapists; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Children and families; Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Lets the massage therapist board post placards on violating facilities, raises civil penalties to $5,000, and increases punishment for repeat unlicensed operation.

title: Relating to the Climate Protection Program.
summary: Requires DEQ to study the Climate Protection Program and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to small business security.
summary: Requires the Oregon Business Development Department to study small business security upgrade needs and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to cybersecurity.
summary: Directs the Office of Enterprise Information Services to study state cybersecurity of cyber assets and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to property taxes; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Exempts from property tax business and residential personal property used to generate or store energy for on-site use, excluding utilities.

title: Relating to physical therapy; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands physical therapist scope to include dry needling, prescribing equipment, administering vaccines, and signing parking permit certificates, and adds claim reporting to the board.

title: Relating to monetary obligations in criminal cases; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Makes court collection remedies for certain under-one-ounce marijuana possession convictions expire, treating those sentence portions as complied with for expungement.

title: Relating to workforce development in the trucking industry; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Higher Education Coordinating Commission program to promote trucking industry workforce development, with grants to local workforce boards.

title: Relating to Columbia River fisheries.
summary: Prohibits gillnet salmon landing in the Columbia River main stem and limits permit renewal to holders who landed salmon in recent years.

title: Relating to privacy protection for personal data.
summary: Requires the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study regulating sensitive personal data and report to interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the expungement of traffic offenses; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Allows certain traffic offense convictions to be set aside, with specified ineligibility criteria, taking effect 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to immigration status.
summary: Bars denying professional licenses or state and local public benefits based solely on immigration or citizenship status, and limits licensing boards' disclosure of SSNs and taxpayer IDs.

title: Relating to public health impacts of land use.
summary: Directs the Department of Land Conservation and Development to study public health impacts of land use and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the creation of a collaborative center; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to grant a nonprofit funds to establish a collaborative center in Harney County.

title: Relating to the decline of ground water levels.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study groundwater level declines and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to compensation for damage caused by wildlife; declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to create a state reinsurance program for insurers covering wildlife damage, funded by a new appropriation to a dedicated fund.

title: Relating to the welfare of young people; declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies rules on restraint, seclusion, abuse investigations, child-caring agency licensing, and out-of-state placements for children in care; requires implementation reports.

title: Relating to firearm transfers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Removes Oregon State Police as the state point of contact for NICS, so gun dealers would seek transfer authorization directly from the federal system.

title: Relating to poverty reduction; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to Oregon Business Development Department grants for cities and tribes with high poverty rates to develop local poverty reduction plans; sunsets 2030.

title: Relating to the Home and Community-Based Services Workforce Standards Board.
summary: Creates a board to set minimum working standards for home and community-based services workers, with standards gated on appropriations and federal approval.

title: Relating to sex offender information.
summary: Directs State Police to make level one and two sex offender information available to school districts and school visitor management services.

title: Relating to economic development.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study economic development and report to the Legislative Assembly by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to a streetcar system in the City of Salem; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs Cherriots to study the feasibility of a Salem streetcar system, reporting by January 2027, and appropriates General Fund money for the study.

title: Relating to the education of migratory children; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money to the Department of Education to distribute to school districts for services to migrant children, following the Migrant Education Program.

title: Relating to state financial administration.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study state financial administration and report findings to legislative ways and means committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to exemptions from estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds an inflation-adjusted exemption against Oregon estate tax and lets estates seek refunds for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2020.

title: Relating to medical assistance reimbursement of emergency medical services.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study Medicaid reimbursement for ground emergency medical transportation and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the Ochoco National Forest.
summary: Lets the State Forestry Department lease management authority and responsibility for the Ochoco National Forest for at least 15 years.

title: Relating to middle housing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates DLCD grants for middle housing infrastructure, appropriates money for them, and exempts local governments from middle housing requirements while grants are pending.

title: Relating to vacation occupancies in historic properties.
summary: Bans short-term vacation rentals of assessed historic properties unless the property is the owner's primary residence or a home share.

title: Relating to veterans.
summary: Requires the Department of Veterans' Affairs to study veterans and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026; the requirement sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to human services.
summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study human services and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to termination of residential tenancies; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets landlords selling to an owner-occupant give 59 days' notice to end a tenancy, after a 31-day pre-listing notice to tenants.

title: Relating to senior citizens.
summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study senior services and report to interim committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to jobs.
summary: Requires the Employment Department to study Oregon job market issues and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to liability.
summary: Bars utilities from recovering from customers certain costs caused by their negligence, and requires utilities to report wildfire-related power line incidents.

title: Relating to agriculture.
summary: Directs the State Department of Agriculture to study agricultural regulation and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to funding the State Department of Fish and Wildlife; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Creates a new personal income tax to fund the Department of Fish and Wildlife, with a credit for fishing and hunting license purchases.

title: Relating to sports economic development in Oregon; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs Business Oregon to study making Portland and Oregon the Pacific Northwest's sports hub and report to lawmakers by September 2026.

title: Relating to lawfully established units of land.
summary: Makes remainder lands created by lawful recorded carve-outs into lawful units of land.

title: Relating to education governance bodies; declaring an emergency.
summary: Abolishes the Educator Advancement Council, changes board memberships for several education bodies, and moves the beginning teacher mentorship program to the Department of Education.

title: Relating to construction contractors; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits major residential contractors to collecting 50 percent of large contracts before completion, and requires Construction Contractors Board certification for spray-on fireproofing installers.

title: Relating to conservation districts.
summary: Changes qualifications for directors of soil and water conservation districts; the text does not specify the changes.

title: Relating to land use.
summary: Requires the Department of Land Conservation and Development to study land use and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to qualifying facilities under the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the PUC to set the eligibility cap for standard PURPA qualifying-facility rates and contracts at no less than 10 megawatts.

title: Relating to electrical infrastructure.
summary: Directs the Public Utility Commission to study electrical infrastructure and report findings to energy interim committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to telephone solicitations.
summary: Restricts telemarketing calls and texts by limiting call hours and frequency, and bans misrepresenting caller identity or purpose under the Unlawful Trade Practices Act.

title: Relating to recreation; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to study wildfire and smoke impacts on recreation, fitness, and related insurance costs, reporting by September 2026.

title: Relating to roads; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs ODOT to study road issues and report the results to the interim Joint Committee on Transportation. No rule changes.

title: Relating to costs for acquiring renewable energy.
summary: Directs the Department of Energy to study PURPA avoided costs versus investor-owned utility costs for renewable generation, reporting by September 2026.

title: Relating to energy procurement.
summary: Directs the State Department of Energy, with the Public Utility Commission, to study central energy procurement and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to public safety; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Business Development Department to distribute to local governments and others for public safety projects.

title: Relating to an animal welfare trust.
summary: Creates an Animal Welfare Trust and fund to give grants for veterinary services to low-income and underserved households, with biennial reporting to the Legislature.

title: Relating to conduct of elections; providing that this Act shall be referred to the people for their approval or rejection.
summary: Makes in-person voting the default, requires photo ID, limits mail ballots, requires return by Election Day, ends state-paid return postage, and refers the Act to voters.

title: Relating to sex offenders; declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes sex offender risk assessment to include victim input, lets victims seek reclassification, and requires residence limits near child-occupied locations.

title: Relating to the jurisdiction of the Energy Facility Siting Council over wind energy facilities.
summary: Raises the threshold for state Energy Facility Siting Council review of wind projects from 50 to 100 MW and requires decommissioning plans for county-permitted 50-100 MW wind facilities.

title: Relating to personal data obtained from a consumer's use of a motor vehicle; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires motor vehicle manufacturers and their affiliates to follow state privacy laws when handling personal data from vehicle use, regardless of consumer count.

title: Relating to the regulation of public property with respect to persons experiencing homelessness; declaring an emergency.
summary: Shields city and county camping restrictions on public property from legal challenges over whether they are objectively reasonable, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to licensing of dwelling units.
summary: Creates an annual DCBS licensing program for rental and vacation dwelling units, with fees, penalties, and eviction dismissal for unlicensed units.

title: Relating to public funding for painful research.
summary: Bars research facilities from using public funds for medically unnecessary painful laboratory research on dogs or cats.

title: Relating to state financial administration; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Changes state budget process by requiring outcomes-based budgeting, zero-based budgeting, vacancy reports, and a biennial budget stress test.

title: Relating to utility infrastructure.
summary: Requires the Public Utility Commission to study utility infrastructure and report findings to energy interim committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to workforce requirements for public improvements constructed by educational institutions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends public-works apprenticeship requirements to school districts, ESDs and charter schools that receive Department of Education matching grants for construction projects.

title: Relating to revenue; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs ODOT to study transportation funding issues and report the results to the Joint Committee on Transportation.

title: Relating to public meetings.
summary: Requires public bodies to include a public comment period at the start of each public meeting.

title: Relating to firearm hold agreements.
summary: Directs the State Police to study whether firearm hold agreements reduce firearm risks and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to highways; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs ODOT to study highway issues and report results to the Joint Committee on Transportation; no change to existing rules.

title: Relating to employment classification of certain strike-prohibited employees.
summary: Redefines "supervisory employee" under public employee bargaining law and limits the permissible makeup of certain public bargaining units.

title: Relating to public meetings.
summary: Requires public bodies to include public comment at meetings where they will vote, give notice of that comment period, and defines "work session."

title: Relating to solar power generation facilities; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Land Conservation and Development Commission to adopt rules by June 30, 2026, allowing temporary housing for solar facility construction workers.

title: Relating to mental health.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study mental health and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to residential tenancies.
summary: Requires law enforcement to notify landlords after responding to incidents at rental units and to give landlords copies of police reports.

title: Relating to behavioral health.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study behavioral health and report findings to legislative health committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the Task Force on Community College Adult Reconnect; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study and recommend ways to help adult learners overcome barriers to community college degrees, sunsetting December 31, 2026.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study health care and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to wind energy; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Allows the State Forester to lease forestlands for siting wind energy facilities; takes effect 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to utilities.
summary: Requires the Public Utility Commission to study utilities and report findings to energy interim committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to public safety.
summary: Requires DPSST to study public safety and report findings to judiciary interim committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to education.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study the adequacy of Oregon's public schools and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to commercial driving privileges.
summary: Requires the Department of Transportation to offer the written commercial driver examination in English and Spanish.

title: Relating to requirements that apply to persons that process consumer personal data.
summary: Lowers thresholds for controller regulation under Oregon's consumer privacy law and bans processing sensitive data for targeted advertising or significant profiling, and any sale of sensitive data.

title: Relating to tax treatment of mortgage interest; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits the mortgage interest deduction to principal residences, phases it out by income, and funds a new housing account with the revenue gain.

title: Relating to water.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study water rules and report to natural resources committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to nursing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Nursing Board to convene advisory committees studying nursing educator and workforce shortages, with reports due in 2026 and a 2027 sunset.

title: Relating to parking minimums for residential development.
summary: Requires local governments in urban areas to mandate at least one parking space per multiunit residential unit, with limited exceptions.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to education funding.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to study the adequacy of state K-12 funding and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to land use applications by entities with the right of eminent domain.
summary: Allows entities with eminent domain power to apply for land use approval for lands subject to their condemnation authority.

title: Relating to vacancies in the United States Senate.
summary: Requires the Governor to appoint a U.S. Senator from the same party after a vacancy and to call a special election.

title: Relating to party membership registration requirements; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Raises the share of registered voters a party must have to qualify as a major political party from 5% to 10%, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to school choice; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands school choice by raising the virtual charter enrollment cap, requiring district open enrollment, and creating an education savings account policy.

title: Relating to domestic water supply district authority; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets domestic water supply districts exercise sanitary district powers in more cases, after a public hearing and written consent from existing providers.

title: Relating to wastewater treatment; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates money to DAS to grant the City of Lakeside funds to build a wastewater treatment facility.

title: Relating to use of the title "doctor"
summary: Requires people using the title "doctor" in a health care context to state their doctoral profession on specified materials, including social media and name badges.

title: Relating to corrections.
summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to reimburse counties for housing defendants sentenced to felonies who receive credit for local jail time.

title: Relating to an income tax subtraction for tips received; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an Oregon personal income tax subtraction for tips received, for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to low-impact pesticides; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Agriculture to develop and maintain a model list of low-impact pesticides for school integrated pest management plans.

title: Relating to funding for local health workforce development activities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to award grants for local health workforce development activities and takes effect on signing as an emergency.

title: Relating to a catastrophic wildfire fund; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Catastrophic Wildfire Fund for utility-ignited wildfire property claims, with utility contributions, caps on damages, and possible cost recovery against imprudent utilities.

title: Relating to permits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires state agencies to set public permit processing deadlines, refund fees when missed where possible, and publish a catalog of permits issued.

title: Relating to academic content standards for social studies.
summary: Requires social studies standards for genocide and Holocaust courses to include current acts of genocide and mass violence.

title: Relating to waiver of tuition for certain qualified students; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands eligibility for tuition waivers for qualified students, including master's degree waivers, and removes the 12-month application deadline.

title: Relating to urban growth boundaries; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Approves Roseburg and Douglas County 2024 ordinances amending the city's urban growth boundary, city limits, and comprehensive plan, and directs a conforming order.

title: Relating to controlled substance crimes; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a new crime of possessing, buying, making, selling or delivering pill presses, punishable by up to five years' prison and a $125,000 fine.

title: Relating to transfers of members from one care organization to another; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the state to allow Medicaid members to transfer between coordinated or dental care organizations when patient care is not lessened, with OHA approval for large transfers.

title: Relating to acquisition of federal lands.
summary: Requires the Department of State Lands to create a program fostering county acquisition of federal lands, with counties and agencies notified by January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to the Sunrise Corridor; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to grant lottery funds to Clackamas County for Sunrise Corridor infrastructure improvements.

title: Relating to missing persons.
topics: AI and technology; Government and administration; Health care
summary: Creates a voluntary OHA program letting parents or guardians message missing family members aged 18 to 30, with provider intake checks and data destruction.

title: Relating to electric transmission infrastructure.
summary: Directs ODOE to study electric transmission needs, build two transmission projects by 2036, and fund them through a new expansion fund.

title: Relating to rural housing development.
summary: Lets counties zone certain rural lands for housing outside statewide land use planning laws and exempts them from certain additional property tax repayment.

title: Relating to the wellness of public safety workers.
summary: Creates or modifies a testimonial privilege protecting public safety workers' confidential communications with peer supporters from being disclosed in court.

title: Relating to the establishment of specific purpose accounts by public officials.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Lets public officials create special accounts to accept donations for emergency expenses, requiring public notices and reports to the Secretary of State.

title: Relating to efficient operations for interactions between residents of this state and government agencies; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates the E-Oregon Task Force to evaluate a single online portal for residents to apply for licenses, IDs and permits.

title: Relating to protecting beavers.
summary: Prohibits taking beavers from certain waters and from public land in designated watersheds or near waterways, with exceptions for land management agency employees.

title: Relating to funding for relief nurseries; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Early Learning and Care to fund Relief Nursery programs, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to a deceased spousal unused exclusion amount for Oregon estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets a surviving spouse claim a deceased spouse's unused Oregon estate tax exclusion, for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to initiating false reports; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates first- and second-degree crimes of initiating a false report with prison terms and fines, and renames the existing offense as third-degree.

title: Relating to the security of state assets.
summary: Bars state agencies from installing, using or accessing AI hardware, software or services developed or owned by a covered vendor, with exceptions.

title: Relating to homeless camps; declaring an emergency.
summary: Shortens the notice period before homeless people can be removed from established camps in cities of 50,000 or fewer, and sets rules for disposing of left-behind property.

title: Relating to applications for a residential tenancy; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars residential landlords from considering the credit scores of rental applicants who qualify for the Oregon Health Plan.

title: Relating to infrastructure projects; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money to OBDD to grant cities for housing infrastructure, extending a residential infrastructure grant program by two years.

title: Relating to wildfire; prescribing an effective date; and providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Raises and redirects revenue, including new taxes on oral nicotine and beverage containers and budget transfers, to fund wildfire prevention and response.

title: Relating to community schools; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a state grant program for community schools administered by the Department of Education, funded with lottery dollars, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to an expedited licensure process for health care facilities.
summary: Directs OHA to create an expedited licensure process letting facilities reopen at a prior closed site's location within 60 months, with provisional licenses.

title: Relating to agency support for housing production; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires all state agencies to report on how their rules affect housing construction and land, and extends housing impact statements to all agencies.

title: Relating to wildfire; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals wildfire building code standards, defensible space requirements, outside-district fire protection rules, and the wildfire hazard map, effective on passage.

title: Relating to the Oregon Government Ethics Commission.
summary: Changes Oregon Government Ethics Commission duties and membership, narrows quorum-violation enforcement to intentional acts, and loosens some official-vote and financial-gain rules while adding serial-communication meeting coverage.

title: Relating to drug crimes occurring near schools; declaring an emergency.
summary: Extends drug-crime penalty zones within 1,000 feet of schools to include preschools, and takes effect on signing as an emergency measure.

title: Relating to use of surplus revenues for wildfire funding; declaring an emergency; providing for revenue estimate modification that requires approval by a two-thirds majority.
summary: Redirects surplus revenue that would otherwise be refunded to taxpayers under the kicker toward wildfire prevention and response, and raises the revenue estimate.

title: Relating to unmanned aircraft systems; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Increases penalties for flying drones over correctional and youth correction facilities, with mandatory forfeiture of the drone upon conviction.

title: Relating to publisher contracts.
summary: Changes terms of State Board of Education contracts with textbook publishers and sets requirements for those contracts.

title: Relating to stored water; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets a spring-property owner store water from the spring for fire prevention and suppression, with a permit, extending existing landowner storage authority.

title: Relating to animal rescue entities.
summary: Changes oversight and recordkeeping for animal rescue entities, exempts veterinary facilities, and removes impoundment as a civil penalty.

title: Relating to sex offender risk assessments.
summary: Appropriates money to the Parole Board to eliminate the backlog of sex offenders awaiting risk-level assessments.

title: Relating to public charter school sponsorship.
summary: Lets Indian tribes ask the State Board of Education to sponsor charter schools, and lets tribal applicants apply to the Board directly.

title: Relating to the Oregon National Guard.
summary: Limits when the Adjutant General may allow federal calls of Oregon National Guard members or units into active service, protecting state emergency response capacity.

title: Relating to research funding at Oregon Health and Science University; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a time-limited matching fund for research at Oregon Health and Science University, appropriating state money that requires matching private funding, sunsetting in 2028.

title: Relating to public health.
summary: Requires syringe service programs to register with local public health authorities and removes local power to waive methadone clinic siting restrictions near schools.

title: Relating to construction labor contractors; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Transfers regulatory authority over construction labor contractors from BOLI to the Construction Contractors Board, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to the application of the state building code.
summary: Requires the state building code to exclusively govern office-to-housing conversions, overriding conflicting city and county ordinances until January 1, 2031.

title: Relating to automatic voter registration.
summary: Changes automatic voter registration by removing the 21-day decline window, letting ACP participants be excluded, and requiring DOT and OHA record-accuracy procedures.

title: Relating to continuing education for health care providers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets health regulators count suicide prevention and lethal means training toward cultural competency CE, and requires such CE to address care for military members and veterans.

title: Relating to family coach teams; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Family Coach Program within the Department of Human Services and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to local taxation; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets local lodging tax revenue fund city or county services through special districts and shifts the split from 70/30 toward local services to 40/60.

title: Relating to offshore wind energy development; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends the deadline for DLCD's report on state enforceable policies for federal consistency review of offshore wind leasing to January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to health insurance contract negotiations.
summary: Creates a voluntary mediation and arbitration process for health insurers and providers in contract disputes, with a binding Governor determination and penalties for noncompliance.

title: Relating to Crater Lake-Klamath Regional Airport; declaring an emergency.
summary: Gives Klamath Falls a $2 million state grant for commercial air service at Crater Lake-Klamath Regional Airport, repayable if service isn't secured by June 30, 2027.

title: Relating to solar energy systems.
summary: Requires disclosures and specified contract terms for solar system sales and leases, requires installer licensing, and makes violations unlawful trade practices.

title: Relating to judges.
summary: Lets the Chief Justice withhold funds and eliminate judges' benefits that are not constitutionally guaranteed compensation.

title: Relating to the military.
summary: Adds Space Force to the list of components of the Armed Forces of the United States.

title: Relating to initiating false reports; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates first and second degree false report crimes with prison terms and large fines, and renames the existing offense as third degree.

title: Relating to youth homelessness; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Expands who can receive Emergency Housing Account homelessness services, creates grants for youth homelessness, and directs agencies to develop funding recommendations.

title: Relating to solid waste disposal in the Willamette Valley; declaring an emergency.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Requires Willamette Valley counties to approve land use applications for landfills and mixed-waste facilities on certain lands, and takes effect immediately.

title: Relating to solid waste.
summary: Gives Benton, Linn and Polk counties solid waste powers like Marion County and lets four counties jointly manage solid waste through an intergovernmental agreement.

title: Relating to paint; declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes paint from the packaging and paper producer responsibility law, so architectural paint no longer needs stewardship collection to be excluded. Declares an emergency.

title: Relating to residential applicant screening charges.
summary: Caps residential landlords' applicant screening charges at $20, extends screening requirements to landlords not charging fees, and allows third-party screening reports.

title: Relating to a tax credit for de novo banks; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a corporate excise tax credit for new banks in each of their first three years of business, for banks starting 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to public records exemptions.
summary: Exempts certain OLCC data and electronic records on sales of non-distilled-liquor items from public records disclosure.

title: Relating to transportation; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Repeals the vehicle emissions inspection program and creates a new transportation infrastructure and congestion fee, deposited into a new State Highway Fund account.

title: Relating to animals; declaring an emergency.
summary: Limits public funding for some dog and cat lab research, bans nonhuman primate research at Oregon's primate center, and creates a planning task force.

title: Relating to labor disputes involving public employees.
summary: Bans public employee strikes and requires that labor disputes be resolved through final and binding arbitration.

title: Relating to levee projects; declaring an emergency.
summary: Makes municipalities eligible for loans and grants for certain levee projects, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to delayed implementation of responsible end market requirements; declaring an emergency.
summary: Delays until July 2026 the requirement that producer responsibility organizations transfer recycled materials to responsible end markets, and bars DEQ from imposing related recycling facility requirements.

title: Relating to transportation.
summary: Redirects bicycle, wage and vehicle privilege tax revenue to the highway fund, taxes diesel like gasoline, revises weight-mile tax rules, and creates refunds.

title: Relating to the possession of firearms by certain persons; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires courts to bar firearm possession for people charged with misdemeanor drug possession, sets penalties, and requires deflection program participants to transfer their guns.

title: Relating to wildfires; declaring an emergency.
summary: Makes utilities liable for plaintiffs' federal income taxes on wildfire damage awards, requires wildfire safety certification, and orders PUC studies.

title: Relating to staffing plans for health care provider entities.
summary: Changes the minimum standards for hospital emergency department staffing plans for direct care registered nurses, without stating the direction of change.

title: Relating to siting of renewable energy facilities by counties on farmland; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets counties approve renewable energy facility siting on farmland for pre-June 2025 applications without the agricultural land use goal or a Goal-3 exception, until 2028.

title: Relating to transportation; prescribing an effective date; and providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Raises road, vehicle, diesel and truck taxes and fees, makes a per-mile usage charge mandatory over time, and adds ODOT audits.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Makes budget changes for state agencies, modifying Emergency Board and agency expenditure limits and appropriating General Fund moneys, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to immigration.
summary: Directs the Department of Justice to study state responses to unlawful immigration enforcement and report to a legislative judiciary committee by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to legislative measures; declaring an emergency.
summary: Caps the number of bills legislators, committees, the Governor, agencies, and other officials can request from Legislative Counsel for odd-year sessions, with exceptions.

title: Relating to medical assistance; declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes the prioritized list for Medicaid coverage decisions and requires OHA to define medical necessity, with Health Evidence Review Commission coverage policies to follow.

title: Relating to natural resources; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Waives forestland special assessment additional taxes for insect or disease losses and lets Water Resources Department extend certain water permit deadlines.

title: Relating to Water Professionals Appreciation Week; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Designates the first weekend of October each year as Water Professionals Appreciation Week to celebrate state water workers.

title: Relating to water rights with points of diversion between river miles 252 and 303 on the Columbia River.
summary: Lets certain Columbia River water rights change diversion points or use off appurtenant land, exempts some from change applications, and requires a 10-year report.

title: Relating to transportation; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lowers e-bike and scooter age limits, sets uniform helmet rules for kids under 16, creates vehicle sale offenses, starts a five-year milk truck weight pilot, and delays a cost allocation review.

title: Relating to a transit funding task force; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Transit Funding Task Force and requires it to report to a transportation interim committee by December 1, 2026.

title: Relating to transportation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Phases in a mandatory per-mile road charge for EV, hybrid and e-commerce delivery vehicles, pauses an EV rebate, and limits another to one per household.

title: Relating to required payments for changes to the scope of work on construction contracts; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires state agencies, contractors and owners to issue change orders for extra construction work on time or pay interest, extending the duty to subcontracts and private contracts.

title: Relating to mandatory subjects of collective bargaining for school districts.
summary: Expands school district collective bargaining so class size and caseload become mandatory subjects of bargaining.

title: Relating to labor contractors; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires studies of labor contractor laws and a construction job-site assessment of unlicensed contractors, with reports due in 2027.

title: Relating to labor standards.
summary: Specifies which federal rules the Bureau of Labor and Industries must use when setting minors' work-hour limits, clarifying its rulemaking scope.

title: Relating to state finance; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study whether Oregon's income tax treatment of international income could be improved or simplified, reporting by December 2026.

title: Relating to connection to federal tax law; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Updates Oregon's tie date to the federal Internal Revenue Code and other federal tax laws, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to tax compliance; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires public contractors to certify and maintain tax compliance as a contract condition starting 2027; orders a Secretary of State study.

title: Relating to use of campaign contributions; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Lets candidates and officeholders use campaign funds for security costs and convert security items to personal use after leaving office, exempt from gift rules.

title: Relating to elections; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets corporations and labor unions set up segregated political funds, lets violations be cured, and changes campaign finance timelines, filings, and carryforward rules.

title: Relating to permits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires certain agencies to decide new permit applications under the rules in effect when the application is deemed complete.

title: Relating to permits; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires certain agencies to state the legal basis for permit denials, provide a contest guide, and set a permit-timeliness performance measure.

title: Relating to administrative rules; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Changes effective dates and notice for some agency rules and requires certain agencies to post rule contact information on their websites.

title: Relating to children's literacy.
summary: Creates the Oregon Imagination Library Program, providing a free monthly book to eligible children, administered by the Department of Early Learning and Care with its own funding account.

title: Relating to mass transit districts initiated by resolution; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Restores restrictions on how certain mass transit districts may finance themselves, and the change takes effect 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to speculative ticket sales; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars ticket resellers from offering or reselling admission tickets they do not possess or lack written authorization to obtain.

title: Relating to the residential rates of public utilities; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets non-power, non-gas public utilities raise residential rates year-round instead of only in a set window, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to consumer protection.
summary: Requires the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study consumer protection and report findings to legislative committees by September 2027.

title: Relating to the Bureau of Labor and Industries; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs DCBS to set an assessment funding a new BOLI Expenses Fund, raises the prevailing wage contract fee cap, and requires biennial reporting and a study.

title: Relating to behavioral health.
summary: Limits insurer and CCO audits of behavioral health provider claims and requires certain carriers to report annually on behavioral health parity compliance to DCBS.

title: Relating to solar energy systems; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires solar sale and lease disclosures and specified contract terms, mandates contractor licensing, and makes violations unlawful trade practices.

title: Relating to packaging subject to producer responsibility requirements; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts certain berry and meat, poultry, fish and seafood packaging from Oregon's producer responsibility requirements for packaging, paper and food serviceware.

title: Relating to the siting of renewable energy facilities; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts certain federally tax-credit-eligible renewable energy facilities from the EFSC site certificate if they are placed in service by 2030 and meet local land use and construction deadlines.

title: Relating to fuel storage sites.
summary: Directs the Department of Energy to study, prioritize and report on geographically dispersed emergency fuel storage sites to interim legislative committees.

title: Relating to emergency volunteers; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Transfers responsibility for the ORVID emergency volunteer database from the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to the Oregon Department of Emergency Management, which must adapt and maintain it.

title: Relating to animal rescue entities.
summary: Narrows the animal rescue entity definition to exclude veterinary facilities, shifts oversight to the Department of Agriculture, changes recordkeeping and licensing, and drops animal impoundment as a civil penalty.

title: Relating to land use; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Expands which cities and Metro can amend urban growth boundaries under a temporary program, adds a Woodburn pathway, and authorizes LCDC grants.

title: Relating to affordable housing; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a housing fund backed by $100 million in state bonds to preserve at-risk affordable housing, and requires a report on barriers to production.

title: Relating to housing; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Streamlines housing approvals and building permit review, adjusts affordable housing loan and grant terms, and limits commercial land use for affordable housing.

title: Relating to health care cost growth; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars the Oregon Health Authority from enforcing the Health Care Cost Growth Target program against providers or payers until 2036.

title: Relating to medical assistance; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires OHA to revise CCO rate-setting and add review steps before rulemaking, bars costly new rules or programs until 2028, and pauses CCO health-disparity spending requirements for three years.

title: Relating to health care; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Omnibus health bill: requires insurers to cover medically necessary anesthesia, lets out-of-state dental students practice under supervision, and lets incarcerated people receive prerelease Medicaid.

title: Relating to public safety; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes penalties for several offenses, sets new deadlines and procedures for re-incarcerating people released in error, and adjusts property-crime dollar thresholds.

title: Relating to the welfare of young people.
summary: Modifies child-caring agency regulation, expands DHS licensing enforcement options, changes youth restraint rules, and creates exceptions to certain placement limits.

title: Relating to courts.
summary: Authorizes state general obligation bonds to fund courthouse renovation and expansion, and requires notifying the court when unfit defendants miss restoration services.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Creates an emergency management office within DHS and two assistance grant programs for emergency-related public and individual needs, with appropriated funding.

title: Relating to search warrant response time limits; and declaring an emergency.
topics: AI and technology; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Requires social media platforms to respond to search warrants within 72 hours, and other communications providers within five business days, in stalking or domestic violence investigations.

title: Relating to nuclear energy; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the state energy department, subject to available funding, to study nuclear energy, including advanced reactors, and report to the legislature.

title: Relating to rural emergency hospitals; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to create rules letting hospitals apply for a rural emergency hospital license.

title: Relating to rural health care tax credits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends the rural health care income tax credit to pharmacist services in rural communities and directs the Office of Rural Health to set certification criteria.

title: Relating to Harney Basin water; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Authorizes the Water Resources Commission to encourage and approve voluntary agreements among Harney Valley groundwater users to limit water use.

title: Relating to funding for education; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Legislative Policy and Research Director to study aligning education funding with costs and report by November 15, 2026.

title: Relating to first-time homeownership; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a three-year program offering first-time homebuyers deferred loans for closing costs, repayable on sale, move-out, or mobile home relocation out of state.

title: Relating to a tax credit for de novo banks; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a three-year corporate excise tax credit for newly commenced Oregon-chartered de novo banks opening between 2027 and 2033.

title: Relating to emergency medical services; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an EMS Program Fund, requires OHA to set minimum EMS provider education rules, restricts EMS titles to matching licensure levels, and creates a long-term care advisory subcommittee.

title: Relating to downcoding.
summary: Requires certain health insurers to notify providers when AI or automated tools downcode a claim and to offer an appeals process for those downcoded claims.

title: Relating to information security; declaring an emergency.
topics: AI and technology; Government and administration
summary: Requires local public bodies to report information security and ransomware incidents to the state within 48 hours, creates a reporting system, and exempts those reports from public records disclosure.

title: Relating to fire protection costs; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money to the Forestry Department to offset landowners' costs of fire protection it provides; takes effect on passage.

title: Relating to the development of children; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires DELC to give subsidy applicants and waitlisted families standardized information on publicly funded early learning programs; orders background check review.

title: Relating to human services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets DHS place certain children, including Indian children, in out-of-state placements without the usual licensing or contract requirements if specified standards are met.

title: Relating to child abuse; declaring an emergency.
summary: Narrows the child abuse definition and DHS investigative jurisdiction, bars certain findings against minors, raises the proof standard for central registry reporting, and requires monitoring.

title: Relating to fluorescent lamps; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Delays the ban on certain fluorescent lamp sales to large-building buyers until 2030 and exempts some care facilities from light fixture plan review.

title: Relating to a unified trade strategy for Oregon; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Business Oregon grant program for small businesses facing tariff costs, updates the state trade strategy, and sets up a business retention task force.

title: Relating to evaluating Business Oregon programs; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Business Oregon director to evaluate the department's programs and recommend ways to streamline them, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to Kei trucks.
summary: Allows Kei trucks to be titled, registered and operated on Oregon highways, and creates a fine of up to $1,000 for unlawful operation.

title: Relating to acquisitions of real property by foreclosure for delinquent taxes; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Sets when HOA and condo assessments accrue on tax-foreclosed property deeded to the county, creates a lien for them, and sets liability and satisfaction dates.

title: Relating to seed contract payments; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies late-payment rules for agricultural seed production and purchase contracts and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to education; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Omnibus education bill changing OHSU board student participation, ESD and school board stipends, ODE rulemaking, a farmworker study, and ESD lamp rules, with an emergency clause.

title: Relating to education.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to study public school adequacy and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2027, then sunsets.

title: Relating to residential treatment homes for transition aged youth; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Expands the age range for transition-aged youth residential treatment homes run by OHA to include young adults aged 17 to 25.

title: Relating to the safety of behavioral health workers; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires behavioral health employers to implement a written safety policy or plan protecting the physical safety of their workers.

title: Relating to health care; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires Medicaid behavioral health access comparable to medical care, limits no stricter than for medical services, and changes which providers may be reimbursed for telemedicine.

title: Relating to recreation; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets recreation operators require adult participants to waive claims for ordinary negligence, and directs OBDD to study recreation commerce and report by December 2026.

title: Relating to arraignment; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Changes the deadline for arraigning released persons and excludes specified periods from that deadline; takes effect 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to administrative law.
summary: Relocates provisions on fiscal impact statements for agency rules affecting businesses and small businesses, with no change in substance described.

title: Relating to hospital staffing.
summary: Raises the med-surg nurse-to-patient ratio from four to five, lets type C hospitals vary from ratios, caps civil penalties, and bars penalties before 2030.

title: Relating to hospital finance; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the State Treasurer to use up to $44 million from unclaimed property funds to guarantee a loan to a rural hospital for financial stabilization.

title: Relating to energy; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets energy facilities using existing surplus or unused interconnection capacity justify exceptions to statewide land use goals, including agricultural land for renewable facilities.

title: Relating to the securitization of a public utility's insurance program; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets public utilities, with Public Utility Commission approval, securitize debt through bonds to fund self-insurance or captive insurance program costs.

title: Relating to an income tax subtraction allowed for plaintiffs in wildfire litigation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts wildfire lawsuit awards and related legal fees paid by plaintiffs from Oregon corporate excise and income tax, with retroactive refund eligibility.

title: Relating to policies for when federal immigration authorities enter public education property; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires school districts and public colleges to adopt policies on how they will respond when federal immigration authorities enter school or campus property.

title: Relating to portable solar photovoltaic energy devices; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets Oregon retail electricity consumers install plug-in solar devices up to 1,200 watts after filing a declaration, and limits landlord and HOA restrictions on them.

title: Relating to photo radar in highway work zones.
summary: Changes Oregon's highway worker photo radar laws in work zones; the summary does not say how.

title: Relating to housing for older persons; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets cities and Metro add urban growth boundary sites for manufactured dwellings, parks, or affordable senior housing through a temporary program ending 2033.

title: Relating to behavioral health care providers; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires OHA to select an electronic credentialing system for behavioral health providers, bars CCOs from extra credentialing, and lets some providers supervise across license types.

title: Relating to economic development; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: AI and technology; Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a Joint Permitting Council for fast-track permits, restricts enterprise zone use for data centers, and modifies the new-jobs tax credit.

title: Relating to autonomous vehicles.
summary: Allows driverless vehicles to operate without a license or permit, including for hire, and preempts local regulation of them and on-demand networks.

title: Relating to economic development; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs Business Oregon to create an industrial symbiosis roadmap and aid four pilot communities, funds a coast fish project, and lets sewer and water districts finance facilities with service charges.

title: Relating to infants born alive.
summary: Requires health care practitioners to give born-alive children the same life-saving care, even after induced abortions, and allows private lawsuits for violations.

title: Relating to health; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Bars Oregon cooperation with out-of-state and federal enforcement over protected reproductive and gender-affirming care, makes related records confidential, and shields licensed midwives from discipline.

title: Relating to criminal offenses related to work.
summary: Expands theft of services to cover partial payments and raises criminal penalties for unlicensed contracting and misuse of contractor license numbers.

title: Relating to county vehicle registration fees; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets large counties reduce or eliminate vehicle registration fees in low-income zones and allocate fee revenue to projects in regional sub-areas.

title: Relating to the Oregon National Guard; declaring an emergency.
summary: Restricts state help with federal Guard mobilizations for law enforcement or immigration duties, bars out-of-state militia entry without consent, and declares emergency.

title: Relating to child safety systems.
summary: Bars selling child safety systems that don't meet federal or Department of Transportation standards, requires compliance disclosures, and creates a private right of action.

title: Relating to protections for persons with disabilities.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Labor and employment
summary: Expands disability protections by barring employers from limiting support persons in accommodation talks and from unrelated physical requirements in job postings, and extends anti-discrimination rules to local governments.

title: Relating to compensation for certain unused paid time off upon termination of employment; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires employers with written policies or contracts promising unused paid time off payouts at termination to pay them under final-wage rules.

title: Relating to semi-independent state agencies.
summary: Makes certain semi-independent state agencies subject to state budget process and fiscal law provisions.

title: Relating to felon in possession of a firearm.
summary: Creates a new crime for convicted felons who possess three or more firearms or have certain prior convictions, with up to 10 years' imprisonment and a $250,000 fine.

title: Relating to the Oregon Ocean Science Trust.
summary: Authorizes the Oregon Ocean Science Trust to create and maintain a nonprofit organization.

title: Relating to violations of the Insurance Code as unlawful trade practices.
summary: Brings insurance practices under the Unlawful Trade Practices Act, removes some insurance exemptions, and adds equitable relief, with prosecutors needing agency request first.

title: Relating to a task force on veterans in crisis; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Task Force on Responding to Veterans in Crisis that reports to a legislative interim committee by September 15, 2026, and sunsets December 31, 2027.

title: Relating to bulk fuel terminals; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Requires bulk oil and fuel terminal owners to obtain a DEQ certificate of financial responsibility for spill costs, and preempts local financial assurance requirements.
