title: Relating to the offense of fleeing or attempting to elude a police officer; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises crime seriousness and sentencing guidelines for felony fleeing or attempting to elude a police officer, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to Department of Environmental Quality regulatory processes; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands DEQ's authority to sign agreements with regulated entities to speed up or improve regulatory processes.

title: Relating to artificial intelligence.
summary: Creates a commission on AI to monitor state AI use and report, and requires DAS to hire an official for privacy and AI strategy.

title: Relating to economic development; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets Oregon CHIPS Fund grants and loans go to firms eligible for federal semiconductor aid that haven't applied, broadens eligible businesses, and renames the fund.

title: Relating to reliable forest management outcomes; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the State Forester to inventory state forestland, set sustainable timber harvest levels, and manage that land, with court-ordered enforcement.

title: Relating to transportation of persons subject to involuntary treatment; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Grants peace officers immunity from criminal and civil liability for restraint or physical force used while transporting people subject to involuntary treatment, if criteria are met.

title: Relating to urgent care centers.
summary: Requires urgent care centers to publish specified information, offer certain services, and keep a licensed provider on site during operating hours.

title: Relating to annexation of land noncontiguous to a city.
summary: Allows the City of Eugene to annex noncontiguous land when all landowners petition and four eligibility criteria are met.

title: Relating to unemployment insurance benefits.
summary: Repeals the law allowing unemployment insurance benefits for workers unemployed due to an active strike, and repeals SB 916 (2025).

title: Relating to ibogaine; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Allows attending physicians to provide ibogaine to patients for certain disorders and exempts it from the controlled substance definition.

title: Relating to immigration-related practices; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice; Immigration
summary: Bars use of immigration status as evidence in civil cases, bars employer retaliation for updating work authorization documents, and adds immigration status to profiling definition.

title: Relating to outdoor school; declaring an emergency.
summary: Increases the biennial lottery fund allocation for the Oregon outdoor school program and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to housing development opportunities conditioned upon land conservation.
summary: Directs the Department of Land Conservation and Development to study housing development conditioned on land conservation and report to legislative committees by September 2027.

title: Relating to law enforcement operations; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates civil suits against federal and out-of-state agents who enter property without a warrant, requires notice and identification, and bars local coordination with noncompliant agencies.

title: Relating to health care providers; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits how often caregivers and behavioral health providers must repeat background checks and credentialing, and requires CCOs to reimburse providers retroactively to enrollment.

title: Relating to consumer finance loans; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Opts Oregon out of a federal DIDMCA rate-preemption provision for consumer finance loans and sets license application requirements for lenders.

title: Relating to universal representation; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Administrative Services for deposit in a Universal Representation Fund; no program rules stated.

title: Relating to food; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires replacement SNAP benefits for stolen benefits and directs reports and studies on food waste, food deserts, and underused assistance programs.

title: Relating to workers' compensation.
summary: Expands which providers can serve as attending physicians for injured workers and requires managed care plans to not discriminate against willing providers.

title: Relating to smoking policies in residential tenancies.
summary: Lets landlords of multifamily housing convert premises to nonsmoking, including for existing tenants, on 180 days' written notice.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Omnibus emergency management bill creating coordination authority, grant programs, and emergency flexibilities, including county waivers of food-service civil penalties during emergencies.

title: Relating to student government at public universities.
summary: Defines student government at public universities, sets its powers and duties, names each school's government, and renames and modifies mandatory student fees.

title: Relating to landlord disclosure of confidential information; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits when landlords may share tenants' confidential information and allows statutory damages for individuals harmed by knowing violations.

title: Relating to the state post-secondary education system; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to study Oregon's post-secondary system and report preliminary and final recommendations to the Legislature in 2026 and 2027.

title: Relating to revenue estimates; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Sets revenue estimate methodology for budgeting and surplus refunds, requires transfers for those differences, and creates a One-Time Emergencies and Finance Fund.

title: Relating to road usage charges; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs ODOT to biennially recommend a per-mile road usage charge rate that would sustainably fund highway maintenance; the bill itself changes no rates.

title: Relating to Medicaid payments to reproductive health care providers; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires OHA to create a state-funded Medicaid payment mechanism for nonprofit reproductive health providers ineligible for federal Medicaid funds.

title: Relating to sale of single-family residences.
summary: Bars large investment entities from buying single-family homes until listed for 90 days, and requires notarized disclosure forms with AG enforcement.

title: Relating to fuel; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Caps low carbon fuel standard emission reductions at 10% below 2010 levels and bars local limits on fossil fuel terminal storage capacity.

title: Relating to farm use.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Extends the farm-use property tax special assessment to land under processing facilities and clarifies what preparing farm products means.

title: Relating to mobile pharmacies; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the State Board of Pharmacy to license qualified applicants to operate mobile pharmacies and sets requirements for them.

title: Relating to veterans; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Makes veterans' law changes, including a suicide prevention and workforce grant program, a higher grant cap, a study of veterans' treatment court access, and funding goals.

title: Relating to alignment with federal education law; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires state participation in a federal scholarship tax-credit program and directs agencies to align with federal Workforce Pell requirements.

title: Relating to funding for natural resource matters; prescribing an effective date; and providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Increases the state transient lodging tax, distributes the new revenue to a renamed wildlife conservation subaccount, and applies to charges from January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to HPV Awareness Day; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Designates March 4th of each year as HPV Awareness Day, a commemorative observance with no policy effect.

title: Relating to tax treatment of mortgage interest; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Ends the personal income tax deduction for mortgage interest on second homes and creates an account for down payment assistance funded by the resulting revenue.

title: Relating to the transfer of interest in motor vehicles.
summary: Lets a previous vehicle owner notify the court of a transfer in lieu of appearing, and avoid liability for a later traffic citation.

title: Relating to limitations on the actions of public employees; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires visible officer identification, bans most police facial coverings, and restricts public employees from cooperating with federal and out-of-state law enforcement.

title: Relating to cannabis; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice; Taxes and budget
summary: Raises illegal marijuana market enforcement grant funding to $3 million quarterly, expands the medical marijuana qualifying-condition definition, adds hemp product sales tax, and tightens cannabis inspections and license suspensions.

title: Relating to metal property.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Creates a crime for selling scrap metal without state seller registration, and adds new ownership-check and theft-alert duties for scrap metal businesses.

title: Relating to debt resolution services; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires debt resolution service providers to register with the Department of Consumer and Business Services and regulates what they may do when negotiating with creditors.

title: Relating to marijuana for medical use; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands qualifying conditions for medical marijuana, requires facility cardholder status for use, mandates staff policies and training, and shields nurses from board discipline for discussing it.

title: Relating to payments to the federal government; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets the Governor direct state agencies to withhold money owed to the federal government when federal funds are unlawfully withheld from Oregon, and indemnifies officials who comply.

title: Relating to batteries.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Requires battery producers to join a responsibility organization and run collection and recycling programs, enforced by DEQ with civil penalties and a new fund.

title: Relating to firearms; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Delays Measure 114 permit requirements for firearm transfers and large-capacity magazine rules until 2028, raises permit fees, and adds an eligibility requirement.

title: Relating to alcohol; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Allows craft low-proof spirit distilleries and larger off-premises sellers to sell low-proof spirits, imposes a tax on them, and creates a craft industry grant fund.

title: Relating to medical assistance; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires an annual report on employers with 500 or more employees whose workers or dependents receive Medicaid.

title: Relating to local taxation; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets local lodging tax revenue fund small restaurant and lodging business grants and special district services, and shifts the tourism-to-local-services split to 50/50.

title: Relating to homeless students.
summary: Requires school districts to adopt policies for immediate enrollment, placement and services for homeless students, and directs ODE to designate a state coordinator.

title: Relating to recipients of public funds; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires state contractors and grant recipients to attest they will not transport detained people for federal deportation, with disqualification or repayment if false.

title: Relating to initiating a false report.
summary: Increases penalties for initiating a false report that intentionally causes an enhanced police response resulting in serious injury or death, up to five years and a $125,000 fine.

title: Relating to remote marriage solemnization of deployed persons.
summary: Lets deployed service members be married remotely, without being physically present, if specified criteria are met.

title: Relating to farm stores.
summary: Allows farm stores on farmlands and lets counties approve them as nonfarm uses on farm-zoned land, replacing the farm stand option.

title: Relating to student attendance data; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Makes student attendance data collected by schools public and requires compiling data on regular attenders and chronically absent students.

title: Relating to infertility.
summary: Requires certain health insurers and public employee plans to cover fertility treatments, exempts some insurers, and creates a reimbursement program and Family Building Fund.

title: Relating to medical assistance reimbursement of emergency medical services; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies requirements for Medicaid supplemental reimbursements paid to emergency medical services providers, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to hearsay; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Allows certain hearsay statements about some sex crimes into evidence even when the speaker is available to testify.

title: Relating to wage requirements for individuals performing companionship services.
summary: Clarifies the definition of companionship services for minimum wage and overtime requirements for certain domestic workers.

title: Relating to the Oregon Government Ethics Commission.
summary: Requires one Ethics Commission member to have local government experience and preserves attorney-client privilege for communications made to the commission about ethics or public meetings complaints.

title: Relating to procedures for medical emergencies in schools; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires schools to adopt cardiac emergency response plans that include automated external defibrillators (AEDs), effective July 1, 2027.

title: Relating to use of official position or office; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates exceptions to the ban on officials using their position for financial gain, allowing public bodies to give officials food, beverages and merchandise.

title: Relating to cannabis worker unionization.
summary: Repeals Ballot Measure 119 (2024), removing the requirement that certain cannabis licensees enter labor peace agreements with unions.

title: Relating to automatic voter registration.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to study automatic voter registration and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 2027.

title: Relating to campaign finance.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to study campaign finance and report findings to interim election committees by September 15, 2027, then sunsets.

title: Relating to campaign finance.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to study campaign finance and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to community safety.
summary: Directs the Criminal Justice Commission to study how different sentence types affect community safety and report to legislative judiciary committees by September 2027.

title: Relating to environmental regulation.
summary: Directs the Department of Environmental Quality to study environmental regulation and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to food assistance.
summary: Requires DHS to study food assistance and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2027, then sunsets.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study health care and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2027, then sunsets.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to immigration.
summary: Directs the Department of Human Services to study immigration and report findings to human services interim committees by September 15, 2027; sunsets January 2, 2028.

title: Relating to government ethics.
summary: Requires the Oregon Government Ethics Commission to study government ethics and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to public meetings.
summary: Directs the Oregon Government Ethics Commission to study public meetings and report to legislative interim committees by September 2027, then sunsets.

title: Relating to public records.
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to study public records and report findings to judiciary interim committees by September 2027, sunsetting in 2028.

title: Relating to transportation.
summary: Directs ODOT to study uniform standards for speed bump height and markings, sunsetting January 2, 2028.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study health care and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to public meetings; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Revises Oregon public meetings law: adds complainant documentation rules, changes training and cure options, and clarifies serial-communication exclusions and penalties.

title: Relating to rounding procedures in transactions; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows businesses and public bodies to round in-person cash transactions to the nearest five cents with posted notice, exempt from unlawful trade practice liability.

title: Relating to entities created by the Oregon Health and Science University.
summary: Lets OHSU create nonprofit corporations it must join, makes them public employers for bargaining, and exempts them from certain professional corporation rules.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Board of Accountancy; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets a biennial expenditure limit on fee and other revenues collected by the Oregon Board of Accountancy, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Department of Administrative Services; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund moneys to the Department of Administrative Services for the biennium and limits its expenditures from various fund sources.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Commission for the Blind; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Commission for the Blind's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting its spending from other revenues and federal funds.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Corrections; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Department of Corrections' 2025-27 budget by appropriating General Fund money and limiting biennial spending from fees and federal funds.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Criminal Justice Commission; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Oregon Criminal Justice Commission's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund and limiting spending from lottery, fee, and federal funds, with an emergency clause.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Adjusts General Fund appropriations and expenditure limits for specified state agencies and the Emergency Board, effective on passage, with an emergency clause.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Employment Department; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Employment Department's biennial budget limits and appropriates money from its federal and special administrative funds for specified purposes.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Employment Relations Board; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Employment Relations Board for the biennium and limits its spending from fees and assessments, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Department of Fish and Wildlife; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Sets the State Department of Fish and Wildlife's biennial budget, appropriating General Fund moneys and limiting expenditures from its various fund sources.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Department of Geology and Mineral Industries; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money and sets biennial expenditure limits for the State Department of Geology and Mineral Industries, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Housing and Community Services Department; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Housing and Community Services Department's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting spending from various fee, federal and lottery revenues.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Judicial Department; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates the Judicial Department's biennial budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting certain fee, federal and other revenue expenditures, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Commission on Judicial Fitness and Disability; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund moneys to the Commission on Judicial Fitness and Disability for its biennial expenses and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Justice; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Department of Justice's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting its spending from other revenues and federal funds.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Bureau of Labor and Industries; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Sets the Bureau of Labor and Industries' 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting expenditures from various fund sources.

title: Relating to the financial administration of legislative branch agencies; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Sets biennial budgets and General Fund appropriations for legislative branch agencies, limits their non-lottery, non-federal revenue spending, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Library; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund moneys to the State Library for the biennium and limits its spending from various revenue sources, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Board of Licensed Social Workers; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the State Board of Licensed Social Workers and caps its biennial spending from fees and other revenues.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets biennial expenditure limits on fees and revenues collected by the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission, with specified nonlimited exceptions, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Long Term Care Ombudsman; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Long Term Care Ombudsman for the biennium and limits its biennial spending from fees and other revenues.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Marine Board; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the State Marine Board's 2025-27 biennial expenditure limits for fee, other, and federal funds, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Medical Board; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Sets a biennial expenditure limit on Oregon Medical Board spending from fees and other revenues, excluding lottery and federal funds, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon State Board of Nursing; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Oregon State Board of Nursing's biennial expenditure limit on its fees and other non-lottery, non-federal revenues, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Business Development Department; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Oregon Business Development Department's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting how its various funds may be spent.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Health Authority; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Oregon Health Authority's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund moneys and limiting biennial spending from various fund sources.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Parks and Recreation Department; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Sets the State Parks and Recreation Department's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting expenditures from fees, lottery and federal funds.

title: Relating to removal of personal property on highway right of way.

title: Relating to vaccine clinics in residential care facilities.

title: Relating to income information provided to students in higher education.
summary: Requires colleges to give students specified information about realistic expected income for jobs related to their degree.

title: Relating to standards of time.
summary: Conditionally ends the twice-yearly clock change in Oregon's Pacific Time portion if California and Washington follow, with fallback restoration if they do not.

title: Relating to the Oregon Perinatal Collaborative; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates the Oregon Perinatal Collaborative at OHSU to work toward better maternal and child health outcomes.

title: Relating to property tax exemption for nonprofit corporation low income housing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends the sunset date of the property tax exemption for low-income housing owned by nonprofit corporations.

title: Relating to pretrial incarceration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Limits pretrial release to security release for people charged with delivering a substantial quantity of a controlled substance, and funds county reimbursement for their pretrial incarceration.

title: Relating to persons arrested for fentanyl crimes; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires officers arresting someone for fentanyl delivery or manufacture to notify federal immigration authorities, and limits pretrial release until notification occurs.

title: Relating to traffic offenses.
summary: Repeals the ban on police stopping drivers solely for specified vehicle lighting violations, expanding officers' stop authority.

title: Relating to the crime of interfering with a peace officer or parole and probation officer.
summary: Restores the pre-2021 interfering-with-officer crime, adding refusal to obey a lawful order and removing the bar on charging when another offense applies.

title: Relating to employment; declaring an emergency.
summary: Clarifies that meal periods are not work time, sets penalties for meal-period rule violations, and defines when a shortened meal period is not a violation.

title: Relating to Oregon Promise program eligibility for career school students.
summary: Allows students enrolled at state-licensed career schools to be eligible for Oregon Promise grants.

title: Relating to voter registration through the State Department of Fish and Wildlife.
summary: Requires the State Department of Fish and Wildlife to give the Secretary of State records so qualified nonregistered persons can be automatically registered to vote, operative June 1, 2027.

title: Relating to access to resources for development in Curry County; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires Curry County and the Water Resources Department to expedite permit reviews for specified lands and appropriates money to Curry County for that work.

title: Relating to elections; declaring an emergency.
summary: Adds proof-of-citizenship for voter registration, limits ballot collection and drop sites, sets an 8 p.m. election-day receipt deadline, and bars certain nonprofit political contributions.

title: Relating to cannabis.
summary: Requires the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission to study interstate cannabis commerce and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to tax compliance required for public contracts; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires public contractors to show and maintain compliance with state, city and county tax laws as a condition of signing public contracts.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through DAS to Southern Coos Hospital and Health Center to expand primary, specialty and pharmacy services in Bandon.

title: Relating to the State Forester; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Moves authority to appoint the State Forester from the State Board of Forestry to the Governor, subject to Senate confirmation, effective on passage.

title: Relating to employment; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Relieves worker leasing companies of paid leave contribution duties for small clients under 25 employees and requires the Employment Department to reimburse certain refunds.

title: Relating to persons authorized to observe vote tallying.
summary: Requires county clerks to let authorized observers watch vote receiving and counting, including signature verification.

title: Relating to video feeds of ballot tallying.
summary: Requires county clerks to live-stream ballot tallying rooms and drop sites online and keep recordings public for two years.

title: Relating to community solar projects.
summary: Lets community solar projects join the program regardless of size or location and bars the PUC from capping program capacity below 25 percent of load.

title: Relating to law enforcement.
summary: Directs State Police to create a drug enforcement and human trafficking section with at least 10 officers, and DOJ to hire two prosecutors for it.

title: Relating to military civil rights.
summary: Declares military members and families have military civil rights and directs the Attorney General to develop guidelines for public bodies on those rights.

title: Relating to a habitat conservation plan.
summary: Directs the Forestry Department to update a habitat conservation plan to increase timber harvest on western Oregon state forests and exempts that work from the Administrative Procedures Act.

title: Relating to workforce housing.
summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study building code exemptions for workforce housing and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the interdependence of the state and local tax systems in Oregon; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Legislative Revenue Officer to study how Oregon's state and local tax systems interact and report recommendations by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to standard charges established by a hospital.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Requires hospitals to publish and update standard charge lists, report them to the Oregon Health Authority, and face complaints, corrective action and penalties.

title: Relating to a lumber grading training program.
summary: Creates a sunsetting OSU Extension lumber grading training pilot and a DCBS process for obtaining lumber from certified graduates.

title: Relating to local authority over regulated utilities.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Lets the cities of Bandon, North Bend and Reedsport set water and wastewater charges by majority vote, and requires a Secretary of State study.

title: Relating to victims of child sex abuse.
summary: Requires DHS to study options for a grant program for child sex abuse victims and report to lawmakers by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to water.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to consider the water basins affected by permitted activity when issuing certain water permits.

title: Relating to supported decision-making.
summary: Creates a Center for Decision-Making Supports to teach people about options for getting help with life decisions.

title: Relating to safety requirements for residential facilities; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Extends and makes permanent an exception letting certain residential training homes and adult foster homes skip the building code's automatic sprinkler requirement.

title: Relating to solid waste in Marion County.
summary: Lets cities in Marion County control or direct the disposal, transfer and recovery of solid waste generated within them.

title: Relating to sex offender classification.
summary: Directs the parole board to classify sex offenders into the same risk level they received in another jurisdiction.

title: Relating to the regulation of human services providers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds new application requirements for ODHS provider licenses and bars new applications for one year after a revocation or denial, plus a cost-reporting requirement.

title: Relating to transportation revenue; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Legislative Revenue Officer to study Oregon transportation taxes and report recommendations to the Legislature by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to incentives for hydrogen production.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Directs the Legislative Revenue Officer to study hydrogen production incentives and report findings to interim committees by December 1, 2026.

title: Relating to the urban growth boundary for the City of Coos Bay; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Land Conservation and Development Commission to approve Coos Bay's submitted urban growth boundary amendments, allowing urban land expansion.

title: Relating to political party affiliation.
summary: Requires county clerks to verify that a voter's party affiliation is not changed when they update their address with ODOT, unless they request the change.

title: Relating to family home health aides; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Health Authority program certifying family caregivers as home health aides to serve eligible relatives in Medicaid, with biennial outcome reports.

title: Relating to funding for services for vulnerable individuals.
summary: Directs DHS to produce caseload forecasts and workload projections for older adults and people with disabilities, and to report mid-biennium changes to the Legislature.

title: Relating to providing proof of United States citizenship when registering to vote; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires proof of U.S. citizenship for voter registration in Oregon and takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.

title: Relating to animals; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Agriculture Department to license animal rescues and breeders, set license fees, inspect breeders, penalize violations, and receives General Fund money.

title: Relating to public records.
summary: Directs the Public Records Advisory Council to study public records and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to official misconduct.
summary: Makes a public servant's failure to make a mandatory child abuse report a second-degree official misconduct crime and extends the prosecution deadline for it.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Adds money to a housing fund and appropriates funds to the Housing Project Revolving Loan Fund.

title: Relating to tax credits for crop donation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises the percentage of crop value allowed as an income and corporate excise tax credit for crop donations and extends its sunset.

title: Relating to regulation of energy use in buildings.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration; Housing
summary: Bars state agencies and local governments from banning natural gas or other energy options in new or existing residential and commercial buildings.

title: Relating to exempting taxpayers with certain incomes from personal income tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts Oregon taxpayers with adjusted gross income at or below 120 percent of the median from personal income tax for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to sex offenders; declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes what information appears on the sex offender website, directing State Police to release information about level two offenders.

title: Relating to sexually violent dangerous offenders; declaring an emergency.
summary: Adds more crimes to the sexually violent dangerous offender law, requiring lifetime post-prison supervision when the court makes certain findings, effective on the Governor's signature.

title: Relating to a tax imposed on university endowments; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Imposes an excise tax on public universities' net investment income and directs the revenue to the Fund for Student Success.

title: Relating to minimum lot sizes for resource lands; declaring an emergency.
summary: Cuts minimum lot sizes for farm, forest and rangeland, and allows smaller lots without water rights if subdivided for at least four dwellings.

title: Relating to an apprenticeship program for building inspectors; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs DCBS to help the Oregon Building Officials Association develop a proposal for a building inspector apprenticeship program, sunsetting January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to public employee retirement.
summary: Directs PERB to study how chaplain salaries are treated under PERS and classifies certain system members as police officers.

title: Relating to information technology; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires state agencies to buy common off-the-shelf software through an approved online IT marketplace portal, exempt from certain public contracting rules.

title: Relating to information technology; declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Requires state agencies to buy common software through an IT marketplace portal and creates a grant and loan program with a Technology Modernization Fund to replace outdated IT.

title: Relating to connection to federal tax law; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Updates the date Oregon ties its tax law to the federal Internal Revenue Code and other federal tax laws, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to information technology; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a state IT modernization fund and grant-and-loan program, and sets a priority process for state agency IT budget and project requests.

title: Relating to transportation protection agreements; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Defines transportation protection agreements for human remains and states they are not funeral merchandise, services, or prearrangement sales contracts.

title: Relating to procedures for conducting cooperative procurements for public contracts; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Streamlines procedures for government agencies to buy goods and services by joining contracts other agencies have signed, effective 91 days after session.

title: Relating to funding for recreation activities.
summary: Directs the Legislative Revenue Officer to study dedicated revenue options for recreation activities and report to interim committees by December 1, 2026.

title: Relating to property tax credits for service members; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates property tax credits for homes of active-duty service members and disabled veterans, and phases out existing partial exemption programs.

title: Relating to vacant home fees; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets cities and counties charge a fee on noncommercial homes vacant more than 180 days in a calendar year.

title: Relating to the protection of domestic violence victims.
summary: Requires GPS tracking devices with real-time victim and law enforcement alerts for domestic violence defendants on pretrial release and for the first 90 days of probation or post-prison supervision.

title: Relating to subsidizing child care; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a two-year child care subsidy pilot run by a nongovernmental organization, funded through a new Tri-Share Child Care Subsidy Fund.

title: Relating to access to materials in schools; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Bars excluding school books based on topic or author, prohibits discriminatory selection or curriculum decisions, sets removal requirements, and directs the Education Department to offer library technical assistance.

title: Relating to use of real property for education; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires cities and counties to allow preschools on church properties and on lands where worship is allowed; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the possession of firearms by noncitizens.
summary: Requires police to ask arrested persons possessing firearms about citizenship and notify federal immigration authorities if they are not citizens.

title: Relating to revenue.
summary: Raises the cap on incremental baseball tax revenues DAS may grant for an MLB stadium, and raises the stadium's minimum cost and salary threshold.

title: Relating to education; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Education; Health care
summary: Makes many school law changes, including a ban on state-required immunizations for school attendance, a private and home school tax credit, and sex-based sports eligibility.

title: Relating to cancellation of voter registration.
summary: Requires county clerks to cancel voter registrations in accordance with the federal National Voter Registration Act of 1993.

title: Relating to energy.
summary: Requires the State Department of Energy to study energy and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to infrastructure development to support housing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Business Oregon loan program for cities and tribes to build infrastructure, such as water, sewer and roads, supporting housing in climate-friendly areas.

title: Relating to accountability for child welfare employees.
summary: Raises the evidence standard for keeping children in protective custody and makes DHS employees who fail to return a child as ordered guilty of second-degree kidnapping.

title: Relating to a child support debit card.
summary: Requires child support awards to be distributed on a monitored debit card with spending limited and tracked by obligor and obligee.

title: Relating to mental health therapy for children in family law proceedings.
summary: Requires courts in parenting time proceedings to order therapy for children aged 5 to 17 who are the subject of the case.

title: Relating to parenting time in family law proceedings.
summary: Creates a rebuttable presumption that equal parenting time is in a child's best interests, rebuttable only by clear and convincing evidence.

title: Relating to paid time off for employees to donate blood.
summary: Allows employees to use earned sick time for blood donations made through approved or accredited voluntary programs.

title: Relating to education; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires education boards to video record their governing meetings, allows audio posting where broadband is lacking, and orders a kindergarten assessment audit.

title: Relating to the pass-through business alternative income tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends the sunsets for the pass-through business alternative income tax and its related personal income tax credit, and lets overpayments carry to later years.

title: Relating to the funding of a business hub.
summary: Authorizes lottery bonds with proceeds going to Williams & Russell CDC to develop a business hub in Portland's Albina neighborhood.

title: Relating to cannabis.
summary: Replaces the word "marijuana" with "cannabis" throughout Oregon statutes and agency rules, with no change to substantive cannabis law.

title: Relating to Department of Human Services admissions of children for treatment; declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets conditions under which DHS may admit children in its care to inpatient or residential treatment instead of congregate care placement.

title: Relating to the welfare of young people.
summary: Modifies rules on restraints and seclusion, abuse investigations, child-caring agency licensing, and out-of-state placements for youth in care.

title: Relating to guilty except for insanity.
summary: Caps commitment and conditional release for certain guilty-except-for-insanity defendants at the sentence they would have received, and lets some petition for post-conviction relief.

title: Relating to social media.
summary: Requires the Department of Administrative Services to study social media and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the Family Preservation Project.
summary: Directs the Criminal Justice Commission to study a parents-in-custody pilot program at Coffee Creek and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to a performance audit of the Department of Transportation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Division of Audits to conduct a performance audit of the Department of Transportation, with no change to policy.

title: Relating to tolling highways; declaring an emergency.
summary: Bars the Oregon Transportation Commission from tolling I-205 and I-5, except the I-5 bridge replacement, and repeals the requirement to assess those tolls.

title: Relating to immigration-related employment activities.
summary: Prohibits employers from engaging in unfair immigration-related employment practices.

title: Relating to tax credits for pension income.
summary: Extends the sunset date for the existing tax credit for pension income, keeping the credit available longer.

title: Relating to adults in custody.
summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to adopt policies for adults in custody, including gender-responsive, trauma-informed practices at Coffee Creek.

title: Relating to the disclosure of private information; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a new misdemeanor for unlawfully disclosing private information and extends a cure period for certain public broadcast stations under the consumer privacy law.

title: Relating to sex offender risk assessments; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Limits sex offender risk assessments to reoffending risk at release, sentencing or discharge, and lets classifiers reassess after new sex crimes.

title: Relating to court visitors.
summary: Grants court visitors immunity from liability for acts taken in good faith within the scope of their court-assigned duties.

title: Relating to public transit vehicle operators.
summary: Adds transit vehicle operators performing official duties to the assault in the third degree and aggravated harassment crimes, with up to five years' imprisonment and a $125,000 fine.

title: Relating to unmanned aircraft systems.
summary: Raises penalties for using drones to interfere with law enforcement, firefighting, search and rescue, or emergency response, and expands the related felony.

title: Relating to physical activity in schools.
summary: Requires recess for students, requires it daily for public elementary students, and bars withholding recess or using physical activity as discipline.

title: Relating to grants for educational activities during noninstructional time; declaring an emergency.
summary: Authorizes ODE grants from the Statewide Education Initiatives Account for educational activities during recess, lunch or after school at Title I schools.

title: Relating to disability under the Public Employees Retirement System.
summary: Defines police officers and firefighters in PERS as disabled if they cannot perform the job they held when disabled.

title: Relating to urban reserves; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Land Conservation and Development Commission to amend its urban reserve rules and declares an emergency, effective on passage.

title: Relating to public accountancy.
summary: Clarifies how out-of-state certified public accountants can obtain an Oregon CPA certificate.

title: Relating to parenting time.
summary: Caps court-awarded parenting time for noncustodial parents at 50 percent and changes remedies when parenting time is not followed.

title: Relating to the Chintimini Wildlife Center; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to award a grant to the Chintimini Wildlife Center, effective July 1, 2025 as an emergency measure.

title: Relating to the disposition of the proceeds of impositions made upon foreign insurers.
summary: Directs insurance-related tax, fee and penalty proceeds collected from out-of-state insurers to the State Forestry Department to fund wildfire prevention and suppression.

title: Relating to accessory dwelling units.
summary: Lets counties approve altering, restoring or replacing certain nonresidential rural structures for use as accessory dwelling units.

title: Relating to an income tax subtraction for insurance expenses of personal income taxpayers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a personal income tax subtraction for premiums paid for a child dependent's medical, dental or vision insurance, for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to county taxes on marijuana production sites; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Lets qualifying counties adopt ordinances imposing a tax on adult-use and medical marijuana production within the county.

title: Relating to land use planning model ordinances; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the land commission to adopt model ordinances letting small non-Metro cities add land to their urban growth boundaries, and limits appeal grounds for housing-related ordinances.

title: Relating to autologous breast reconstruction.
summary: Requires health benefit plans to cover autologous breast reconstruction and related services, with rules on cost-sharing, utilization review, reimbursement and network adequacy.

title: Relating to the Home and Community-Based Services Workforce Standards Board.
summary: Creates a board to set minimum working standards for home and community-based services workers, subject to legislative ratification, with biennial reviews and reports.

title: Relating to noncompetition agreements.
summary: Extends noncompete agreement requirements to employee and customer solicitation agreements and creates an administrative remedy for employees alleging violations.

title: Relating to the property tax system in Oregon.
summary: Requires the Legislative Revenue Officer to study Oregon's property tax system and report to interim revenue committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to English-only policies in the workplace.
summary: Prohibits employers from English-only workplace rules unless justified by business necessity and limited in scope, and requires employers to notify employees.

title: Relating to vacation occupancies on resource lands.
summary: Allows dwellings on farm and forest land to be used for vacation rentals, but limits resuming short-term rentals that were previously nonconforming uses.

title: Relating to the family and medical leave insurance program.
summary: Directs the Employment Department to study family and medical leave insurance benefit issues and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to thermal energy networks; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Labor and employment
summary: Creates a PUC pilot program letting gas companies propose utility-scale thermal energy network projects, and sets labor standards and reporting for certain projects.

title: Relating to cannabis.
summary: Requires the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission to study how much marijuana retailers may sell and report to interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to energy.
summary: Directs the State Department of Energy to study energy and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to water.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study water rules and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to permanent restraining orders for crime victims; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets crime victims request permanent no-contact restraining orders against convicted defendants, at sentencing or later, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to disability income insurance policies.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Prohibits disability income insurers from requiring applicants to use or apply for other available benefits before receiving the insurer's disability benefits.

title: Relating to insurance for rural electric cooperatives.
summary: Requires the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study insurance for rural electric cooperatives and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to revenue.
summary: Requires the Legislative Revenue Officer to study state revenue and report to interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to insurance.
summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study insurance and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to investor-owned utilities.
summary: Requires the Public Utility Commission to study investor-owned utilities and report findings to energy interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the Public Utility Commission.
summary: Requires the Public Utility Commission to study energy and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to water.
summary: Requires Oregon's water agency to weigh in-stream habitat, water quality and public interest impacts before approving certain water right transfers, with tribal review and optional permit conditions.

title: Relating to ground water.
summary: Modifies ground water quality concern and management area declarations and directs state agencies, including DEQ and Agriculture, to take actions in those areas.

title: Relating to affordable housing.
summary: Directs Oregon Housing and Community Services to create a pilot program helping pregnant people and their families obtain stable housing, sunsetting January 2, 2028.

title: Relating to marijuana.
summary: Requires the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission to study marijuana and report findings to health care committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to school safety.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study methods for improving public school safety and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to specie legal tender; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Makes gold and silver legal tender and exempts their purchase, sale and exchange from certain taxes.

title: Relating to the Children's Advocate; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Children and families; Government and administration
summary: Moves the Children's Advocate office from DHS to the Long Term Care Ombudsman, creates an advisory board to nominate candidates, and shifts CIRT oversight to the Advocate.

title: Relating to state finance.
summary: Directs the Legislative Revenue Officer to study the state financial system and report revenue findings to interim committees by December 1, 2026.

title: Relating to the deployment of renewable energy projects; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Department of Energy to study developing certain renewable energy projects in Oregon and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 30, 2026.

title: Relating to organ transport vehicles; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets the Oregon Health Authority license organ procurement organizations to operate organ transport vehicles, with driver requirements, insurance minimums, and lights and sirens allowed.

title: Relating to certificates of need for hospice programs; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires hospice programs to obtain a certificate of need from the Oregon Health Authority before establishing, expanding, or relocating into a new service area.

title: Relating to a right to repair agricultural equipment.
summary: Requires farm equipment makers to provide owners and public bodies repair tools, parts, software and documentation, with AG investigations and civil penalties up to $1,000 daily.

title: Relating to documents issued by the Department of Transportation.
summary: Lets people ask ODOT to note on their license or ID that they have a disability affecting police communication, with health professional verification.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to the Oregon Public Defense Commission to raise hourly pay rates for defense investigators, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to transportation network companies; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires rideshare companies to pay drivers minimum rates, provide paid sick time, allow appeals, and face just-cause limits on account deactivation.

title: Relating to funding to develop successful children; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Early Learning and Care for distribution to seven entities supporting child development.

title: Relating to per-visit compensation for home health care entities.
summary: Bans paying home health care and home hospice staff on a per-visit basis, requiring other compensation methods.

title: Relating to conditional discharge.
summary: Expands pre-plea conditional discharge to most offenses, removes specialty court and DA consent requirements, and allows more than one discharge and dismissal.

title: Relating to property tax exemption for vertical housing development projects; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends the sunset date for the partial property tax exemption for vertical housing development projects, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to access to justice.
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to study access to justice and report findings to judiciary interim committees by September 15, 2026; the bill sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to punitive damages in cases related to wildfires.
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to study punitive damages in wildfire-related civil actions and report findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to firearm prohibitions based on certain convictions.
summary: Removes harassment as a qualifying misdemeanor that triggers the state firearm and ammunition possession prohibition.

title: Relating to product liability civil actions; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Shields certain entities that provide products as part of health care services from product liability suits, unless they were involved in designing or manufacturing the product.

title: Relating to the Board of Licensed Dietitians and Nutritionists; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a licensed nutritionist credential, bars unlicensed medical nutrition therapy and restricted titles, and lets licensed dietitians and nutritionists provide telehealth.

title: Relating to a task force on removing barriers to jury service; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force to study barriers to jury service and report to the Chief Justice, Governor and legislative committees by December 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to education efforts concerning the obligation of places of public accommodation to accept cash as payment; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Bureau of Labor and Industries to publicize and explain the existing duty of public accommodations to accept cash, continuing until compliance is high.

title: Relating to use of surplus revenues for wildfire funding; declaring an emergency; providing for revenue estimate modification that requires approval by a two-thirds majority.
summary: Diverts the 2023 kicker surplus above the revenue estimate into a new wildfire mitigation and adaptation fund.

title: Relating to small-scale renewable energy; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires 10 percent of electricity sold by large electric companies to come from small-scale renewable or certain biomass facilities.

title: Relating to domestic violence survivor defendants; prescribing an effective date; providing for criminal sentence reduction that requires approval by a two-thirds majority.
summary: Lets courts treat ongoing domestic abuse as mitigation, allowing downward departures and lesser sentences despite mandatory minimums, with resentencing for current prisoners and a survivors task force.

title: Relating to property tax exemption for multiunit rental housing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends the sunset date for the property tax exemption for multiunit rental housing, keeping the tax break in place longer.

title: Relating to ballot measures.
summary: Requires the Legislative Policy and Research Director to report prospective initiative petitions to the Legislature and lets leadership request analyses and hearings on them.

title: Relating to Medicare supplement insurance.
summary: Bars Medicare supplement insurers from raising costs or denying coverage over preexisting conditions and sets open enrollment standards.

title: Relating to disposition of surplus real property of the Interstate 5 Rose Quarter Project.
summary: Allows ODOT to lease or sell surplus Rose Quarter Project land to Albina Vision Trust, Inc., and extends the sunset from 2030 to 2040.

title: Relating to firefighting services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through the State Fire Marshal to Central Douglas Fire & Rescue for an apprenticeship program, effective on passage.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Legislative Assembly to fund a year-round legislative assistant for each member, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to requests for information about immigrant status.
summary: Requires DOJ to dedicate an attorney and investigator to federal requests for immigrant status information, and requires state agencies to forward those requests to that attorney.

title: Relating to unmanned aircraft systems.
summary: Modifies provisions on law enforcement agencies' use of unmanned aircraft systems; the summary gives no specific change.

title: Relating to greenhouse gas emissions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Climate Superfund cost recovery program in which DEQ would issue demand notices to entities deemed responsible for climate change costs.

title: Relating to decision-making supports for individuals with complex health care needs; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates two grant programs, funded by General Fund appropriations, to expand guardianship services for people with complex health care needs facing hospital discharge delays.

title: Relating to treatment works within the North Santiam Basin; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a limited exception letting a treatment works in the North Santiam Basin be built without a water quality permit.

title: Relating to a property tax credit for the homestead of residents on active military duty; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a property tax credit for homesteads of residents on active military duty and phases out their existing partial exemption.

title: Relating to mandatory overtime.
summary: Lets residential training home employees refuse an additional mandatory overtime shift after one in a month, and bars retaliation or forced unpaid leave for refusing.

title: Relating to informing others of their rights.
summary: Exempts informing another person of their civil or constitutional rights from certain criminal laws.

title: Relating to hydroelectric water rights.
summary: Bars the Water Resources Director from forcibly converting a hydroelectric water right when FERC has directed the holder to stop generating and other criteria are met.

title: Relating to compensation to student athletes.
summary: Allows public colleges to pay student athletes for NIL use and bars athletic associations from prohibiting such compensation.

title: Relating to water quality permits for wastewater treatment facilities.
summary: Bars state environmental regulators from requiring municipal wastewater treatment plants to meet certain pollutant and temperature criteria for surface water discharges.

title: Relating to residential behavioral health services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs OHA to study and adopt rules on residential mental health treatment facilities and homes, report findings to the Legislature, and sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to recreation.
summary: Directs the Legislative Revenue Officer to study ways to raise dedicated revenue for recreation and report to interim committees by December 1, 2026.

title: Relating to respite care; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires Medicaid to cover respite care for caregivers of children and youth under 26 with complex behavioral health needs or intellectual or developmental disabilities, pending federal approval.

title: Relating to inhalant delivery systems.
summary: Makes it unlawful to sell or distribute vapes packaged inconsistently with Oregon Health Authority rules meant to protect minors.

title: Relating to the development of housing in rural counties.
summary: Lets sparsely populated rural counties rezone up to 50 acres for dense housing and funds infrastructure grants; sunsets in 2034.

title: Relating to designation of incumbent for certain judicial candidates.
summary: Bars the Secretary of State from designating appointed judicial candidates as incumbents on ballots in their first election after appointment.

title: Relating to tax expenditures.
summary: Requires the Legislative Revenue Officer to study tax expenditures and report findings to interim committees by December 1, 2026.

title: Relating to construction labor contractors; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Moves regulatory authority over construction labor contractors from the Bureau of Labor and Industries to the Construction Contractors Board, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to constructing bridges across the Columbia River that are west of the Interstate 5 bridges; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs ODOT to study the feasibility and usefulness of Columbia River bridges west of the I-5 bridges and report by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to transportation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates the Oregon Rail and Transit Department and State Rail and Transit Board, transferring ODOT's rail and public transit duties to them.

title: Relating to development of housing on lands used as golf courses; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows dividing golf course tracts on exclusive farm use land to site single-unit or middle housing, sunsetting January 2, 2036.

title: Relating to the creation of credits for the restoration of salmon habitat; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a voluntary salmon habitat credit pilot in Coquille and Coos basins, a trust fund, and federal Army Corps authorization efforts.

title: Relating to tax subtractions for amounts received in wildfire litigation.
summary: Extends the sunset date for the personal income tax subtraction for amounts received from wildfire-related civil lawsuits.

title: Relating to funding to improve access to health care.
summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study funding to improve health care access and report findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to an appropriation for a community cultural hub.
summary: Appropriates state funds to Soul District Business Association to buy and redevelop property as a Black community cultural hub in Portland.

title: Relating to plastics.
summary: Designates March each year as Plastics Appreciation Month, a ceremonial declaration with no policy effect.

title: Relating to special motions to strike.
summary: Bars defendants from filing special motions to strike (anti-SLAPP motions) against claims brought by public bodies.

title: Relating to earned income tax credits.
summary: Extends the sunset date for the Oregon earned income tax credit, keeping the credit in effect longer.

title: Relating to the Department of Transportation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Department of Transportation to forgive certain debts; the bill's text does not specify which debts or the amounts.

title: Relating to the possession of firearms by certain persons; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires courts to bar people charged with misdemeanor drug possession from having firearms, sets surrender rules, and adds penalties for violations.

title: Relating to student use of personal electronic devices.
summary: Requires school districts to adopt a policy prohibiting student use of cell phones and other personal electronic devices.

title: Relating to Kei trucks.
summary: Allows Kei trucks to be titled and registered in Oregon and operated on highways, and creates a fine-based offense for unlawful operation.

title: Relating to Medicaid reimbursement rates for rural hospitals; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires OHA and CCOs to reimburse certain rural hospitals at no less than 150 percent of current Medicaid rates, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to tax credits for closure of manufactured dwelling park.
summary: Extends the sunset date for the tax credit available for tenants of manufactured dwelling parks that close.

title: Relating to the corporate activity tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends the CAT prescription-drug pharmacy exemption to critical access pharmacies, makes the subcontracting exclusion permanent, and orders a revenue study.

title: Relating to estate tax thresholds; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds an additional, inflation-indexed Oregon estate tax exemption for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to exemption of health care receipts from corporate activity tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Phases in an exemption from the corporate activity tax for health care service reimbursements and clinical-setting medication receipts, starting tax years on or after 2026.

title: Relating to corporation taxes.
summary: Directs the Legislative Revenue Officer to study Oregon's corporate excise and income tax system and report findings by December 1, 2026.

title: Relating to the funding of programs concerning wildfire.
summary: Directs the State Forestry Department to study wildfire program funding and report to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the transmission of electric power.
summary: Requires the Public Utility Commission to study electric power and report findings to interim energy committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to individuals with intellectual disabilities; declaring an emergency.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Health care
summary: Repeals laws allowing involuntary commitment based on intellectual disability and bars public bodies from denying mental illness services due to intellectual disability.

title: Relating to educational requirements of professional licensing boards; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires professional licensing boards to consider work experience in place of a high school diploma or equivalent for licensure.

title: Relating to the long term care workforce; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study recruiting and retaining long-term care workers, including case managers and adult protective services workers.

title: Relating to compensation of service providers.
summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study rate and wage recommendations for service providers and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to children.
summary: Directs DHS to study the demographics of Oregon children and report findings to interim human services committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to developmental disabilities services.
summary: Requires DHS to annually adjust for inflation the payments under contracts with provider agencies that serve people with I/DD through direct support professionals.

title: Relating to electronic monitoring devices in long term care facilities; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a right for long-term care, residential care and adult foster home residents to use electronic monitoring devices in their rooms, subject to conditions and civil penalties.

title: Relating to court appointed special advocates.
summary: Requires representatives of local CASA volunteer programs to serve on specified review teams and advisory bodies.

title: Relating to developmental disabilities services providers.
summary: Lets DHS revoke, suspend, or impose conditions on licenses of intellectual and developmental disability service providers under specified circumstances.

title: Relating to staffing in state-regulated programs.
summary: Directs the Department of Human Services to study regulatory responses to staffing violations in long-term care and other state-regulated programs, reporting by September 2026.

title: Relating to the centralized child abuse reporting system; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows, but does not require, DHS to add a website for electronic reports of suspected child abuse, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to infectious waste.
summary: Allows sharps and waste pharmaceuticals to be consolidated in one container if specified conditions are met.

title: Relating to indecent exposure.
summary: Creates a new crime of indecent exposure, punishable by up to six months' imprisonment, a $2,500 fine, or both.

title: Relating to behavioral health services.
summary: Requires OHA and coordinated care organizations to raise Medicaid reimbursement rates for inpatient psychiatric hospital services and develop discharge care plans for civilly committed patients.

title: Relating to education; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates student outcome measurement and growth targets for school entities, requires interim assessments, authorizes state-directed instructional materials, and orders reporting and administrative reviews.

title: Relating to behavioral health workforce; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates scholarships, grants and loan-forgiveness programs to recruit and retain behavioral health workers, with annual reporting to the legislature.

title: Relating to administration of public funds; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Redirects a larger share of unemployment insurance employer tax into the Supplemental Employment Department Administration Fund and changes the excess-transfer formula; also requires a Treasurer study.

title: Relating to information technology.
summary: Requires the State Treasurer to study information technology and report findings to interim ways and means committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to State Treasury savings programs.
summary: Directs the State Treasurer to study state treasury savings programs and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to trust property.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Modifies unclaimed and escheated property procedures, imposes duties on holders of unclaimed digital assets, and requires a Treasurer study of trust property.

title: Relating to the Elliott State Forest.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Renames the Elliott State Forest a research forest, moves its management to the State Land Board, restricts land sales, and authorizes certificate-of-participation financing.

title: Relating to the State Treasurer.
summary: Directs the State Treasurer to study the office's operations and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to immigration.
summary: Requires DHS to contract with eligible entities for support services and immigration assistance for refugees, and directs a study on immigration.

title: Relating to simple estates.
summary: Expands which estates can use the simple estate process and changes how asset values, including manufactured homes, count toward the limits.

title: Relating to compensation for services performed in connection with a claim for a veteran's benefit; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Bars compensation for helping veterans with benefit claims beyond what law allows, prohibits unreasonable fees, and requires DVA outreach on free assistance.

title: Relating to the Moda Center; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Authorizes DAS to own and operate the Portland Moda Center and creates an Oregon Arena Fund receiving diverted tax revenue for its costs.

title: Relating to proposed legislative measures to be filed by the Secretary of State; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to file a pre-session bill recommending changes to campaign finance limits for the 2027 session.

title: Relating to the administration of epinephrine.
summary: Allows schools to administer and provide epinephrine by methods other than injections and broadens related training requirements.

title: Relating to the Home and Community-Based Services Workforce Standards Board.
