summary: Creates a board to set minimum working standards for home and community-based services workers, conditioned on appropriated funding and federal approval.

title: Relating to the Bureau of Labor and Industries; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a BOLI Expenses Fund funded by a Workers' Benefit Fund assessment, raises the prevailing wage contract fee cap, and requires a biennial BOLI staffing report.

title: Relating to revenue; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Updates federal tax conformity, raises the earned income tax credit, decouples from certain federal deductions, and creates a new-jobs tax credit.

title: Relating to elections.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to study elections and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2027, then sunsets.

title: Relating to electors of President and Vice President of the United States; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires presidential electors to vote as pledged, lets unfaithful electors be replaced, sets elector qualifications, and pays mileage to attending electors.

title: Relating to wage theft.
summary: Directs the Bureau of Labor and Industries to study wage theft and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to taxation; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Omnibus tax bill: expands film contribution credit to commercials, extends pass-through alternative tax and cargo container property tax exemption, and makes other technical changes.

title: Relating to the estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Converts the estate tax exclusion to a $2.5 million deduction, adjusts rates and filing threshold for inflation, and directs an LRO estate tax study.

title: Relating to workforce development.
summary: Expands the goals of the Prosperity 10,000 workforce program and requires HECC to award grants to local workforce boards to administer it.

title: Relating to real estate professionals; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Delays until July 1, 2027, the deadline for real estate teams to change terms used in their team names.

title: Relating to the regulation of public property with respect to persons experiencing homelessness; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals the 2021 statewide standard that limited city and county rules on public property use by people experiencing homelessness, along with its legal challenge and defense provisions.

title: Relating to wrongful convictions; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a time-limited post-conviction relief petition process for convictions based on discredited forensic science and modifies wrongful-conviction compensation petitions.

title: Relating to public safety; and declaring an emergency.
topics: AI and technology; Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Restricts police use of license plate readers, limits data retention and vendor access, lets people sue vendors, and expands aggravated harassment to threats against public officials.

title: Relating to civil litigation; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets sports, fitness and recreation operators require participants to waive ordinary negligence claims, except certain non-waivable claims, and makes inherent risk a legal question.

title: Relating to worker protections.
summary: Clarifies the meaning of "companionship services" for minimum wage and overtime rules for certain domestic workers, and directs BOLI to study worker protections.

title: Relating to total disability.
summary: Changes the formula for setting temporary and permanent total disability workers' compensation benefits, tied to the state average weekly wage.

title: Relating to emergency management.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Emergency Management to study emergency management and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the administration of moneys within the Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance Fund; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets the Employment Department director adopt rules creating an accounting system for handling Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance Fund moneys.

title: Relating to local requirements to develop affordable housing.
summary: Bars Portland-area cities and counties from requiring affordable units in multiunit housing unless they first calculate and offset developers' expected losses.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to electronic access to residential tenancies; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets tenants and applicants opt out of landlord tenant portals and electronic payments, requires landlord alternatives, and allows certain card processing fees.

title: Relating to horse racing.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a continuing allocation of lottery revenues to support specified horse racing events and facilities, operative July 1, 2027.

title: Relating to organizations relevant to Oregon's coastal resources; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Blue Economy Task Force to study Oregon's blue economy and report by September 2027, and lets the Ocean Science Trust form a nonprofit.

title: Relating to the facilitation of projects.
summary: Directs ODOE to seek grant money to form a nonprofit entity that will finance clean energy and resilience projects, reporting annually to the Legislature.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Bars cost-sharing for certain health plans, including OEBB and PEBB, on cervical cancer screenings and follow-up exams.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Expands drug manufacturers' annual reporting to cover all patient assistance programs that aided Oregon consumers, operative January 1, 2028.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study health care and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2027, then sunsets.

title: Relating to veterans.
summary: Directs the Department of Veterans' Affairs to study veterans and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to crime; declaring an emergency.
summary: Expands aggravated harassment to cover threats against public officials, with up to five years' imprisonment and a fine up to $125,000; takes effect on signing.

title: Relating to funding for emergency medical services.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study funding emergency medical services through a universal health care model, reporting by September 2027, then sunsetting.

title: Relating to services for vulnerable persons; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies long-term care and I/DD service rules, child placement and restraint limits, facility license conditions, and directs a differentiated rate model for agencies employing direct support professionals.

title: Relating to the rights of children in care; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies foster children's rights laws, exempts parents from abuse-of-child-in-care provisions, and requires DHS to disclose it cannot give parents legal advice.

title: Relating to the welfare of young people; declaring an emergency.
summary: Modifies laws on abuse of children in care, child-caring agency licensing, and out-of-state placements, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to child care; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets the Early Learning Council change child care subsidy priority for TANF families and creates a liability insurance study work group reporting by 2027.

title: Relating to educational assessments.
summary: Directs the Department of Education to study the adequacy of public school assessments and report to interim education committees by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to boards of education of community college districts; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires community college board members to have public email addresses, adds a nonvoting student board member, requires a compliance report, and changes vacancy rules.

title: Relating to conduct of public education; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires school districts to admit all students regardless of immigration status, bars immigration-based discrimination in education, and adds AG model policies on immigration enforcement at schools.

title: Relating to providing animal health care.
summary: Lets individuals verify whether cattle are pregnant without a veterinary license in certain circumstances, with board rules and a 2031 sunset.

title: Relating to universal health care.
summary: Directs the Universal Health Plan Governance Board to study universal health care and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to property insurance; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires insurers to disclose wildfire risk scoring models to the state, credit property mitigation actions in pricing, and let policyholders appeal classifications and discounts.

title: Relating to greenhouse gas emissions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a climate change cost recovery program that directs DEQ to issue demand notices to entities deemed responsible for climate costs, funded through a new account.

title: Relating to transportation.
summary: Directs the Oregon Transportation Commission to create a 10-year capital investment plan with a project scoring method, and requires an ODOT highway condition report.

title: Relating to transportation; declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget; Transportation
summary: Requires ODOT to get Oregon Transportation Commission review before requesting state bonds, and directs the commission to adopt a highway debt financing policy.

title: Relating to transportation; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs ODOT to report on audits and progress, centralizes project delivery, eliminates the Joint Committee on Transportation, and expands who qualifies for transit funds.

title: Relating to corner crossing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows corner crossing between public land parcels without trespass liability, grants landowners immunity from negligence claims, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to artificial intelligence companions.
topics: AI and technology; Children and families; Health care
summary: Requires AI companion operators to disclose non-human status, prevent suicide-related output, run suicide and self-harm protocols with crisis referrals, add minor protections, and report annually.

title: Relating to licensed behavioral health and wellness practitioners; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a new state license for behavioral health and wellness practitioners under the Board of Psychology, restricts the title to licensees, and requires them to report certain abuse.

title: Relating to marijuana; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice; Government and administration
summary: Requires individually packaged cannabis edibles capped at 10 mg each, lets localities set wider buffer zones, and requires risk labels on hemp-derived cannabinoid products.

title: Relating to a tax credit for political contributions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises the maximum personal income tax credit for political contributions for tax years 2026 and 2027.

title: Relating to the military.
summary: Requires the Oregon Military Department to study the military and report findings to veterans and emergency management committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to scrutinizing death.
summary: Requires investigators to review abuse evidence and interview family in certain suspicious deaths, mandates further post-mortem exams for suspected domestic violence homicides, and expands family notice and evidence access.

title: Relating to fire hardening of residential properties; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Voids HOA and deed restrictions that bar owners from replacing materials with fire-hardened ones, and limits HOA enforcement against such upgrades.

title: Relating to the transfer of real property; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires county clerks to notify property owners when a title-affecting document is recorded, except when filed by financial institutions, insurers, attorneys or their agents.

title: Relating to wildfires resulting from the fault of an electric company; declaring an emergency.
summary: Bars electric utilities from passing wildfire litigation costs to ratepayers after fault findings, requires escrow funds for victims, and creates a Wildfire Recovery Fund from punitive damages.

title: Relating to infants born alive.
summary: Requires practitioners to provide life-preserving care to any child born alive, including after an induced abortion, and lets specified persons sue for violations.

title: Relating to the constitutional requirements for public education appropriations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes how state education funding needs are calculated, revises quality goals, and abolishes the Quality Education Commission and a joint appropriations committee.

title: Relating to representation of persons in the magistrate division of the Oregon Tax Court; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Consolidates statutes on who may represent parties before the Oregon Tax Court magistrate division, effective for proceedings starting in 2027.

title: Relating to courts; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Modifies contempt of court procedures and the confidentiality provisions for surrogacy agreements; the text gives no detail on either change.

title: Relating to hospital staffing.
summary: Raises the medical-surgical nurse-to-patient ratio from four to five, lets type C hospitals vary from ratios, and adds notification duties and capped civil penalties.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study health care and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2027, then sunsets.

title: Relating to international affairs.
summary: Requires the Legislative Policy and Research Officer to study international affairs and report findings to interim committees by September 15, 2026, sunsetting January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to allowable uses of place of worship.
summary: Limits county rules that would restrict a church's use of its property and limits counties' power to regulate activities inside places of worship.

title: Relating to restoration of dwellings damaged by involuntary causes.
summary: Lets owners restore or replace homes made uninhabitable by involuntary causes through an alternative approval process that local governments must follow.

title: Relating to local taxation; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets local lodging tax revenue fund city or county services through special districts, shifts the use split to 40-60 percent, and requires biennial reporting.

title: Relating to civil rights; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a state civil cause of action for damages and injunctive relief against persons acting under color of law who violate Oregon rights, with attorney fees.

title: Relating to the City of Woodburn's urban growth boundary; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds specified lands to Woodburn's urban growth boundary and requires the city to designate them for certain development.

title: Relating to snowmobiles; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises snowmobile registration fees, with the change taking effect 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to the prevailing rate of wage; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts certain affordable-housing public works projects from the prevailing wage requirement, so public agencies need not set those wage levels.

title: Relating to mixed income housing; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a mixed-income housing loan program and fund at HCSD, financed by transferring money from the Housing Project Revolving Loan Fund.

title: Relating to perinatal services; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires Medicaid, coordinated care organizations and pregnancy-covering health plans to cover doula and lactation counselor services, creates a voluntary lactation counselor registry, and creates a perinatal collaborative.

title: Relating to public employee retirement.
summary: Reclassifies certain Public Employees Retirement System members as police officers for retirement purposes.

title: Relating to federal affairs.
summary: Requires the Legislative Policy and Research Officer to study federal affairs and report findings to interim committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to protections in health care facilities; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires hospitals to have law enforcement response policies and bars disclosing immigration status or birth country to police, and protects employees who distribute immigration rights materials.

title: Relating to consumer products for adults; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands tobacco and nicotine definitions, bans giving these products away free, requires in-person sales at licensed premises, and shifts under-21 sales enforcement from criminal to civil.

title: Relating to education; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adds teacher removal and return rules for disruptive students, requires proficiency for diplomas, sets science-based language arts standards, and bars advancing third graders who lack reading proficiency.

title: Relating to syringe service programs.
summary: Bars syringe service programs from operating mobile or temporary sites within 2,000 feet of schools or licensed child care facilities, and allows private lawsuits for violations.

title: Relating to voting at primary elections.
summary: Lets 17-year-olds who will turn 18 by the general election vote in their party's primary, and appropriates General Fund money for extra ballots.

title: Relating to hospice licensure; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Tightens hospice licensing with new initial license requirements, bars excluded or fraudulent individuals from hospice ownership, and pauses new licenses pending rulemaking.

title: Relating to accessibility standards for housing; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs building code rules to conform to federal housing accessibility standards and bars state funding for new subsidized rental housing that fails specified accessibility standards.

title: Relating to the labeling of alternative protein food products.
summary: Requires alternative protein foods that imply meat or egg content to carry text disclosing they are not made from meat or eggs.

title: Relating to rural residential development.
summary: Lets rural counties with low population density rezone up to 50 acres for dense homes and expands rural accessory dwelling units, until 2034.

title: Relating to false reports of child abuse; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Increases penalties for making a false report of child abuse, with fines and jail terms rising for second and third offenses.

title: Relating to charges in lieu of security deposit.
summary: Allows landlords and tenants to agree to a recurring charge in place of a security deposit, with set agreement requirements.

title: Relating to compensation for journalism.
topics: AI and technology; Government and administration
summary: Requires platforms to get agreements before using Oregon news content, creates a private right to sue and arbitration, and establishes a civic information grant consortium.

title: Relating to school meals; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires school districts to offer free breakfast and lunch to all students regardless of income, with state-paid nutrition standards, effective July 1, 2026.

title: Relating to energy; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires electric companies to create distributed power plant programs that pay customers' distributed energy resources for grid services, with cost recovery, PUC targets and annual reports.

title: Relating to substance use.
summary: Creates a Behavioral Health and Deflection Committee within the Criminal Justice Commission to run grants for resource networks and deflection programs, taking over OAC duties.

title: Relating to the creation of credits for the restoration of salmon habitat; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a voluntary salmon habitat credit pilot in the Coquille and Coos basins, establishes a trust fund, and seeks federal approval for a bank instrument.

title: Relating to matching grants for cities; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Caps the local matching share required for state grants to small cities for capital construction and municipal infrastructure projects.

title: Relating to economic development; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Environment and energy; Housing; Taxes and budget
summary: Omnibus economic development bill changing tax credits and breaks, setting permit processing deadlines and permit lists, and adding rural reserve land to Metro for industrial use.

title: Relating to data brokers; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars public bodies from disclosing personal information to data brokers unless the broker attests it won't be used to enforce federal immigration law.

title: Relating to inclusive utility investment programs.
summary: Requires electric companies to create programs financing customer energy efficiency and renewable projects, with savings reflected in lower utility costs, under PUC standards.

title: Relating to lobbying; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires lobbyists to file notices with the Oregon Government Ethics Commission on client representation, compensation, and changed positions on legislative or administrative action.

title: Relating to veterans' recognition plates.
summary: Lets qualifying owners of motorcycles and mopeds obtain veterans' recognition registration plates from the Department of Transportation.

title: Relating to public lands; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Prohibits state public bodies from assisting federal privatization of certain federally owned public lands, sunsetting in 2032, effective immediately.

title: Relating to an inland port; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs OBDD to study establishing an inland port for infrastructure, trade and economic development, reporting findings by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to primary elections.
summary: Creates a top-two primary open to all electors, lets parties opt out, changes vacancy filling, and repeals party committee provisions.

title: Relating to recreation; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets recreation operators require participants to release them from ordinary negligence claims, and directs OBDD to study the recreation industry.

title: Relating to immigration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Justice Department to consult the Office of Immigrant and Refugee Advancement when developing model policies limiting immigration enforcement at public facilities; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to professional workforce; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires professional licensing boards to publish licensure guidance and ensure staff receive culturally responsive training by January 1, 2028.

title: Relating to play-based learning.
summary: Lets play-based learning count toward required instructional time for kindergarten through grade five students.

title: Relating to energy generation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires electric utilities and energy facility developers to disclose to customers and the public the costs of storing nuclear waste from electricity generation.

title: Relating to access to health services; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires certain health plans to cover federal preventive services as of June 2025 and future vaccines the Public Health Officer recommends, and authorizes standing prescription orders.

title: Relating to a special election date for Referendum Petition 2026-302; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Moves the statewide vote on a referred transportation measure to the May 19, 2026 primary election and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to records of state agencies.
summary: Requires executive agencies that testify on bills to disclose all related public records, overriding exemptions, including attorney-client privilege.

title: Relating to transportation taxes; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Repeals the state payroll tax on wages that finances transportation investments and public transit services, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to Legislative Equity Office operations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes what records of legislative personnel rule-violation investigations can be made public, and eliminates the offsite process counselor role.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Makes miscellaneous budget and finance changes, including fund transfers to the General Fund and Transportation, lottery transfer cap removal, and an emergency clause.

title: Relating to funding for local health workforce development activities; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to award grants to recipients for local health workforce development activities, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to cannabis; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Lets cannabis regulators destroy hoop houses during searches, allows five-year license terms, repeals the school-proximity buffer for retailers, and permits hemp biomass inspections.

title: Relating to fiscal impact statements from school districts.
summary: Directs a study of the accuracy of school district fiscal impact statements submitted to the Legislative Fiscal Office, with findings due September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to kindergarten through grade 12 education.
summary: Requires the Department of Education to study K-12 public education adequacy and report findings to interim education committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the disposition of animals after veterinary treatment.
summary: Prohibits veterinarians from requiring owners to surrender treated animals because the owners have not paid the bill.

title: Relating to the destruction of animals by animal shelters.
summary: Prohibits animal shelters from killing dogs or cats for lack of space, except for terminal illness or severe injury, and requires annual reporting.

title: Relating to reusable beverage containers.
summary: Requires a beverage distributor cooperative to run a reusable container system meeting return targets, and requires certain dealers to stock reusable containers.

title: Relating to human services.
summary: Directs DHS to study how it delivers services to children and families and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the placement of utility lines.
summary: Directs the Public Utility Commission to adopt standards requiring electric power lines to be placed underground, with exceptions.

title: Relating to native fish.
summary: Directs ODFW to manage hatchery and naturally produced salmon and steelhead in a watershed as a single population.

title: Relating to the recovery of game fish carcasses.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife to develop a project to recover game fish carcasses.

title: Relating to a principal Act for predator damage control districts; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets landowners form predator damage control districts that fund county predator control, including lethal methods, through per-acre or flat charges.

title: Relating to damages incurred as a result of wildfire.
summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study financial impacts of wildfire damages and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to animal processing waste products.
summary: Directs the State Department of Agriculture to study uses for animal processing waste and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to meat rendering plants; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Agriculture to develop a grant program funding construction of meat rendering plants.

title: Relating to parcel sizes of resource lands.
summary: Lets counties authorize subdividing farm- and forest-zoned land into smaller parcels, based on the average size of existing county lots.

title: Relating to legislative confirmation of national marine sanctuaries.
summary: Requires the Governor to certify to the federal Commerce Secretary that a national marine sanctuary designation in Oregon waters is unacceptable unless the Legislature confirms it.

title: Relating to Sudden Oak Death; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the State Forestry Department to address the plant disease Sudden Oak Death, including a task force, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to long term care; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires ODHS to study long-term care facility ownership disclosure and an online portal, and requires state approval and resident notice before owner or operator changes.

title: Relating to fire insurance that covers properties at particular risk of wildfires; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars insurers from canceling wildfire-area fire policies or raising premiums over 3% a year for properties in wildland-urban interface or farming and resource-extraction insureds.

title: Relating to a natural resource credit against estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lowers the acreage and estate-value thresholds for forestland and forestland homesites to qualify for the natural resource estate tax credit.

title: Relating to small forestland owners.
summary: Lets small forestland owners harvest trees they planted under reforestation rules, with reforestation duties applying after harvest; the State Board of Forestry may adopt rules.

title: Relating to forest management; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the State Forestry Department to study forest management and report recommendations to an interim legislative committee, with a 2027 sunset.

title: Relating to wildfire.
summary: Directs DEQ to notify the Attorney General when smoke from federal-land wildfires stays severe for seven days, and directs suits over negligent forest management.

title: Relating to fire.
summary: Requires a joint underwriting association for small forestland fire insurance and lets plaintiffs recover replanting costs from the federal government or contractors for fires from federal forests.

title: Relating to wildfire; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a state forestry wildfire-risk pilot grant program, funded by a General Fund appropriation and sunsetting June 30, 2027.

title: Relating to farm use land used for illegal growing of marijuana; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Ends farm-use special tax assessment for land where the owner or controller is penalized or convicted for illegal marijuana growing, with exceptions for lack of knowledge or prompt reporting.

title: Relating to hunting.
summary: Directs the Fish and Wildlife Commission to set fees for multiyear hunting licenses and fixes agent issuance fees, operative January 1, 2027.

title: Relating to cougars.
summary: Lets county voters approve dog-assisted cougar hunting, and state wildlife officials may issue special cougar tags to residents of those counties.

title: Relating to medical assistance.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study medical assistance and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to decreasing the barred owl population to conserve the spotted owl population; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Fish and Wildlife Commission to authorize barred owl takings, create a reward program, and appropriates money to fund it.

title: Relating to the capture of pikeminnow; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates Fish and Wildlife funds for a $5-per-fish bounty on pikeminnow taken in compliance with wildlife laws, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to a grant program that facilitates the eradication of gorse for wildfire mitigation in southwest Oregon; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a State Department of Agriculture grant program and fund to eradicate gorse for wildfire mitigation in southwest Oregon, sunsetting in 2030.

title: Relating to wolf predation of livestock; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to a wolf compensation trust fund and requires it be used to relocate livestock-killing wolves to specified counties.

title: Relating to relocating beavers.
summary: Expands a voluntary beaver relocation program to include moving beavers from western Oregon to central and eastern Oregon.

title: Relating to air curtains; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a State Forestry pilot grant program promoting air curtains for wildfire risk management, funded by a General Fund appropriation and sunsetting June 30, 2027.

title: Relating to the Invasive Species Council; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Invasive Species Council for specified purposes and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to ports.
summary: Lets ports assess public bodies for a portion of the costs of removing sediment from port waters.

title: Relating to the Ocean Beach Fund; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates the Ocean Beach Fund from 1% of lodging tax collected at ocean shore state recreation areas, to pay for managing those areas.

title: Relating to the environmental impact of camping sites used by homeless individuals on the waters of the state; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets any person complain to DEQ about homeless campsites discharging waste into state waters, and directs DEQ to remove campers and clean the sites.

title: Relating to patient billing.
summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study patient billing and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to machine-powered pesticide application devices; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts certain employees from pesticide licensing when they apply pesticides using battery-powered machine devices.

title: Relating to port dredging; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Oregon Business Development Department to distribute to specified ports for dredging projects.

title: Relating to water.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study water-related rules and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to meat processing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Extends and funds a General Fund grant program for meat processing and sales establishments through the Department of Agriculture; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to marine ecosystem data.
summary: Directs DEQ to study marine ecosystem data and report findings to interim environment committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to wildfire.
summary: Directs the Attorney General to help wine grape growers recover damages from the federal government for wildfire smoke harm.

title: Relating to the sale of eggs to restaurants.
summary: Allows egg producers to sell and deliver their eggs directly to restaurants without an egg handler's license.

title: Relating to prohibitions on business closures mandated by the executive branch; declaring an emergency.
summary: Bars the Governor and state agencies from ordering lawful businesses to close or suspend operations during declared emergencies, and takes effect on passage.

title: Relating to declarations of emergency; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits governor-declared states of emergency to 30 days, with the Legislature able to extend them in 30-day increments. Takes effect 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to greenhouse gas regulation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars the Governor and specified state agencies from taking measures to reduce Oregon greenhouse gas emissions unless the Legislature authorizes them by later law.

title: Relating to pharmacy.
summary: Directs the State Board of Pharmacy to study pharmacy and report findings to legislative health committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to administrative rules.
summary: Requires the Legislative Policy and Research Director to send interim committees summaries of recently adopted administrative rules relevant to each committee's subject.

title: Relating to transfer of federal public lands.
summary: Directs the Department of State Lands to petition Congress to transfer certain federal public lands to the state, to be managed as trustee for counties.

title: Relating to Willamette Valley brassica production.
summary: Repeals restrictions on canola and other brassica production in the Willamette Valley.

title: Relating to the Department of Justice.
summary: Bars DOJ from billing state agencies for legal work, requires DOJ to pay those costs from appropriated funds, and limits union contracts tied to attorney billable hours.

title: Relating to the Good Neighbor Authority Agreement.
summary: Sets limits on projects under the Good Neighbor Authority Agreement, per a thin summary with no detail on the limits.

title: Relating to the Good Neighbor Authority Agreement.
summary: Establishes additional requirements for projects under Oregon's Good Neighbor Authority Agreement; the text is too thin to determine specifics.

title: Relating to health care provider incentives.
summary: Defines 'rural' for the rural health care provider incentive program, without stating any funding amount.

title: Relating to exemption of health care receipts from corporate activity tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts health care service receipts, including Medicaid and Medicare reimbursements and certain clinical medication receipts, from the corporate activity tax starting tax year 2026.

title: Relating to charges for senior citizens to use areas under the jurisdiction of the State Parks and Recreation Department.
summary: Directs State Parks to let Oregon residents aged 65 and older use state parks, campsites and day-use areas without charge.

title: Relating to an exemption for pharmacy receipts under the corporate activity tax.
summary: Exempts certain pharmacy drug sale receipts from the corporate activity tax permanently by removing the exemption's sunset.

title: Relating to prescription drugs.
summary: Directs the State Board of Pharmacy to study prescription drugs and report findings to interim legislative health committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to exemptions from estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an additional Oregon estate tax exemption that phases out as estate size grows, for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to exempt amount under corporate activity tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises the exempt amount and filing threshold for Oregon's corporate activity tax, effective for tax years starting January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to exemption of prescription drug sales; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts receipts from prescription drug sales by licensed retail pharmacies from the corporate activity tax, starting tax years on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to medical interventions; declaring an emergency.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Government and administration; Health care
summary: Bars public bodies and private entities from requiring vaccines or immunity passports, or discriminating against people who decline them, and limits pandemic-based rights restrictions.

title: Relating to abortion.
summary: Requires providers to give born-alive infants medical care after abortion attempts, mandates hospital transport, and creates criminal and civil penalties for violations.

title: Relating to false reports of child abuse; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Increases penalties for making a false report of child abuse, with escalating fines and jail terms for repeat offenses.

title: Relating to the crime of patronizing a trafficked child.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Creates a new crime of patronizing a trafficked child with prison and fine penalties, repeals the purchasing-sex-with-minor crime, and authorizes wiretap orders for it.

title: Relating to property tax exemption for disabled veterans; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises property tax exemptions for disabled veterans and extends exemptions to their unmarried surviving spouses, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to the Oregon Health Policy Board.
summary: Restructures the Oregon Health Policy Board, adds oversight of the Oregon Health Authority, places the Health Evidence Review Commission under the board, and requires a 2026 coordinated care report.

title: Relating to harassment protective orders.
summary: Lets a person petition a court for a harassment protective order restraining a respondent from harassing the petitioner.

title: Relating to primary care.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study primary care in Oregon and report findings to interim legislative health committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to transfer of certain receipts by the University of Oregon to Oregon State University; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the University of Oregon to transfer its athletic conference receipts to Oregon State University, and bars HECC distributions to UO until it does.

title: Relating to title fraud; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force to study ways to prevent real property title fraud and report back, sunsetting December 31, 2026.

title: Relating to the date of elections during presidential election years.
summary: Moves certain elections in presidential years from the third Tuesday in May to the first Tuesday in March.

title: Relating to solar events.
summary: Directs the Oregon Department of Emergency Management to study solar events and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to corporate activity tax revenues.
topics: Education; Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Redirects corporate activity tax revenue for ten years from the Fund for Student Success to pay the PERS unfunded liability.

title: Relating to hydrogen.
summary: Directs the Oregon Business Development Department to report on promoting hydrogen fuels to energy interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to applying to public universities.
summary: Requires public universities to create a common undergraduate application for admission across public colleges in the state.

title: Relating to employer time-rounding policies.
summary: Exempts employer time-clock rounding policies that comply with federal standards from state unpaid-wage recovery laws and penalties.

title: Relating to greenhouse gas emissions; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires fees and charges from greenhouse gas reduction programs to be deposited in the State Highway Fund instead of elsewhere.

title: Relating to payment of surplus revenue refunds in form of check; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Department of Revenue to issue kicker surplus refunds as paper checks for biennia beginning on or after July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to Internet service providers.
summary: Requires Internet service providers to issue prorated bill credits for outages over one hour and keep outage and credit records for three years.

title: Relating to public health.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study public health and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to removal-fill permits; declaring an emergency.
summary: Exempts removal-fill projects from state Department of State Lands permits when a federal Army Corps of Engineers permit is obtained; declares emergency.

title: Relating to State School Fund adjustments for children in poverty; declaring an emergency.
summary: Increases the State School Fund weight for children in poverty, sending more money to schools serving those students.

title: Relating to patrol trooper staffing levels for the Department of State Police.
summary: Requires the State Police to maintain at least 20 patrol troopers per 100,000 residents starting January 1, 2036.

title: Relating to ballot return date.
summary: Requires mail-returned ballots to be received by election day, ending the postmark-based return window.

title: Relating to state forest lands.
summary: Directs the State Board of Forestry to convey certain state forest lands to counties that request them and show greater permanent value.

title: Relating to conforming estate tax to federal basic exclusion amount; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises Oregon's estate tax exemption to match the federal basic exclusion amount, $13.61 million, for decedents dying from 2026.

title: Relating to zero-based budgeting.
summary: Requires state agencies to justify proposed expenditures in budget requests and declares zero-based budgeting as state policy, starting with the 2027 biennium.

title: Relating to decreases in capital gains tax rates; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Reduces tax rates on capital gains for personal income and corporate excise taxpayers, applying to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025.

title: Relating to estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Repeals the Oregon estate tax, limiting its imposition to estates of decedents dying on or before January 1, 2025.

title: Relating to carbon sequestration.
summary: Requires counting carbon sequestered by state lands and waters when calculating progress toward greenhouse gas emissions reduction goals.

title: Relating to substance use disorder.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to study substance use disorder and report findings to health interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to transportation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Repeals the weight-mile tax, taxes diesel like gasoline, and increases fees for specified vehicles; effective 91 days after adjournment.

title: Relating to legislative approval of administrative rules; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires legislative approval before newly adopted state agency rules take effect, contingent on voters approving a constitutional amendment.

title: Relating to cougars.
summary: Requires Fish and Wildlife to offer special cougar tags allowing dogs to hunt or pursue cougars, and lets certain license holders get one free.

title: Relating to limitations on nonresident student enrollment at public universities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires public universities to cap nonresident student enrollment at 35% of total students and takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.

title: Relating to the unlawful dissemination of intimate images; declaring an emergency.
summary: Expands the crime of unlawful dissemination of an intimate image to cover computer-generated explicit likenesses, and takes effect on passage as an emergency.

title: Relating to zero-emission vehicle incentives.
summary: Directs the DEQ to study zero-emission vehicle incentives and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to electronic credentials issued by the Department of Transportation.
summary: Directs ODOT to offer optional mobile driver licenses, permits and ID cards for a fee, and lets it contract with private vendors.

title: Relating to outdoor advertising signs.
summary: Modifies rules for relocating or reconstructing billboards and specifies documents accepted as proof of landowner consent for sign permits.

title: Relating to TriMet.
summary: Requires TriMet to remove a specified territory from its district boundaries by ordinance, with no voter referral allowed.

title: Relating to taxation of multinational corporations; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Children and families; Taxes and budget
summary: Changes corporate excise tax unitary reporting to include foreign corporations and directs estimated new revenue to a new perinatal, child and maternal health fund.

title: Relating to vaccine financing.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Oregon Health Authority for a Vaccine Access Program and requires a vaccine financing study reported by September 2026.

title: Relating to Healthy Families Oregon home visiting services.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Early Learning and Care to expand or sustain Healthy Families Oregon home visiting services.

title: Relating to the youth behavioral health workforce.
summary: Requires the System of Care Advisory Council to study the youth behavioral health workforce and report findings by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to developmental disabilities services; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs DHS to run a pilot stabilization program to reduce placement disruptions and find long-term solutions for people with IDDs.

title: Relating to penalties for violation of requirement to accept cash as payment in places of public accommodation.
summary: Requires BOLI to study penalties for violating cash-acceptance requirements in public accommodations and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Oregon Health Authority for an electronic filing system tied to the Death with Dignity Act.

title: Relating to fees charged for use of a payment card.
summary: Prohibits merchants that do not accept cash from charging customers a fee for paying by credit or debit card.

title: Relating to wages.
summary: Makes owners and direct contractors jointly liable for construction workers' unpaid wages, presumes workers are employees, and exempts small residential and commercial projects.

title: Relating to water transfers.
summary: Prohibits proposed water appropriation or use changes that would diminish streamflow, tightening limits on water transfers.

title: Relating to sales of units of land not lawfully established for conservation purposes.
summary: Exempts sellers and nonprofit conservation buyers from civil or criminal liability for selling land units not lawfully established.

title: Relating to firearms; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires gun dealers to wait 72 hours after a background check request before transferring a firearm or unfinished frame or receiver, with civil immunity for compliant dealers.

title: Relating to waste management.
summary: Requires DEQ to study waste management and report findings to interim environment committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to disclosures required in connection with online transactions.
summary: Requires online sellers to display prices that include all mandatory fees, except government taxes and reasonable shipping costs, and enforces violations under the Unlawful Trade Practices Act.

title: Relating to state offices.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to study state offices and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to addressing wildfire originating on federal lands.
summary: Directs the state forester and contracted forest protective associations to take specified actions when fires starting on federal lands threaten their protection areas.

title: Relating to a self-service storage facility's sales of personal property subject to a lien.
summary: Raises from $300 to $1,000 the threshold above which storage owners must advertise lien sales, and lets owners dispose of smaller items any way they choose.

title: Relating to the Ocean Beach Fund; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates the Ocean Beach Fund, directing one percent of lodging tax collected at ocean shore state recreation areas to park management.

title: Relating to the Housing Accountability and Production Office.
summary: Requires DLCD to study the Housing Accountability and Production Office and report findings to housing-related interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to constructing child care facilities within projects for affordable housing; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Children and families; Labor and employment
summary: Lets nonprofit child care facilities be built within affordable housing projects without subjecting the whole project to prevailing wage, while the child care construction itself stays covered.

title: Relating to public notices.
summary: Allows certain legally required public notices to be published in online news publications, not only newspapers.

title: Relating to family dwelling units; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Allows owners of rural property outside urban growth boundaries to site an additional dwelling for a relative.

title: Relating to constructing child care facilities within projects for affordable housing; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Children and families; Labor and employment
summary: Exempts affordable housing projects with a qualifying on-site child care facility from prevailing wage, while requiring prevailing wage for the child care facility's construction.

title: Relating to elections.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to study elections and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to a homebuilding contract exemption under corporate activity tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises the corporate activity tax exempt amount and filing threshold for homebuilding contracts, starting tax years on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to biological products.
summary: Removes pharmacist requirements to notify of biological product substitutions and to retain related records.

title: Relating to services for COFA citizens; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a COFA Shared Services Office to help COFA citizens apply for and access benefits and services.

title: Relating to family medicine residency training programs.
summary: Appropriates state money through HECC to OHSU's Area Health Education Center to support family medicine residency training.

title: Relating to accessibility standards for housing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires state building code conformance to housing accessibility standards and conditions state funding of new subsidized rental housing on meeting accessibility standards.

title: Relating to medical services for injured workers; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets the State Accident Insurance Fund form subsidiaries and provide managed care to injured workers, with an annual audit of that care.

title: Relating to benefits packages for school employees; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs DAS to study and develop standardized job profiles for unlicensed school jobs, convene an advisory committee, and report to legislative committees.

title: Relating to patient assistance programs; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires pharmacies to notify patients receiving prescription drugs that the manufacturer may offer a patient assistance program.

title: Relating to medication-induced movement disorders; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study medication-induced movement disorders and report to legislative committees by December 31, 2025.

title: Relating to the Task Force on Health Care Training Partnerships; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a task force on health care training partnerships that must report to an interim legislative committee by December 15, 2026.

title: Relating to elections.
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to study elections and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to Ruby Bridges Walk to School Day; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Designates November 14 each year as Ruby Bridges Walk to School Day and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to health care.
summary: Requires health insurance coverage of cervical cancer screenings and follow-up exams to be provided without cost-sharing for patients.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through DAS to Marion-Polk Food Share for a capital expansion project, effective July 1, 2025, with an emergency declaration.

title: Relating to local transient lodging taxes.
summary: Requires the Legislative Revenue Officer to study the 70-30 split on uses of local transient lodging tax revenue and report by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the revenue of rural fire protection districts; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a Legislative Revenue Officer study and a State Fire Marshal advisory committee on rural fire district funding, with reports due in 2026 and a 2027 sunset.

title: Relating to forest trust land counties.
summary: Directs the State Forestry Department to study the economic effects of a habitat conservation plan and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to grants to improve school attendance; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to the Department of Education for grants to address chronic absenteeism and improve school attendance.

title: Relating to transient lodging taxes.
summary: Requires the Legislative Revenue Officer to study allowing transient lodging tax money for public safety, reporting by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to U.S. Highway 30; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires ODOT to study a section of U.S. Highway 30 and report findings to the Joint Committee on Transportation by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the Oregon Board of Maritime Pilots.
summary: Changes residency rules for Oregon Board of Maritime Pilots members: public members must be Oregon residents, at least one licensee must be, and other licensee residency is removed.

title: Relating to government ethics.
summary: Requires the Oregon Government Ethics Commission to study government ethics and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to an exemption of pre-apprenticeship participants from the application of the prevailing rate of wage; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts pre-apprenticeship participants working on public works from Oregon's prevailing wage requirements, taking effect 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to documents issued under the wildlife laws.
summary: Requires paper copies of wildlife licenses on request, bars mandatory electronic licensing systems, and raises the fee share certain license agents keep.

title: Relating to continuing education course for planners.
summary: Requires Business Oregon to create a land use planner education course, which planners must complete at least every two years.

title: Relating to reporting on the soundness of the state's Insurance Fund; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Department of Administrative Services to report to the Legislature every even-numbered year on the soundness of the state's Insurance Fund.

title: Relating to Housing
summary: Creates an alternative approval path for owners altering, restoring or replacing dwellings, which local governments must approve outside land use review.

title: Relating to individual development accounts.
summary: Removes the annual cap on IDA matching funds and sets a cap on total matching funds an account holder can accrue.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through DAS to the Tsuga Community Commission for the Oregon Summer Star program, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to tax credits for child care workers; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Children and families; Labor and employment; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a refundable income tax credit for certain child care workers starting in 2026, with an option to deposit the refund in the Oregon Retirement Savings Plan.

title: Relating to employment agreements for health professionals.
summary: Makes noncompetition agreements void and unenforceable when the employee is a health professional.

title: Relating to the State Board of Parole and Post-Prison Supervision.
summary: Directs the parole board to study Oregon parole law and report findings to interim judiciary committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to obsolete activities of public entities.
summary: Eliminates obsolete public entities and modifies laws about obsolete activities of public entities.

title: Relating to recordings of occupants of transient lodging; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Consumer protection and business
summary: Bars hotels, short-term rental hosts and their intermediaries from recording guests in private spaces, and lets guests sue for invasion of privacy.

title: Relating to Class 3 electric assisted bicycles.
summary: Prohibits riding Class 3 electric-assisted bicycles on sidewalks, bicycle lanes and bicycle paths.

title: Relating to actual conflicts of interest among members of a district school board.
summary: Lets education service district boards decide alleged school board member conflict-of-interest violations, with an option to appeal to the State Board of Education.

title: Relating to crime; declaring an emergency.
summary: Bars firearm possession by people convicted of menacing a public official and creates a new crime of threatening a public official with penalties.

title: Relating to the Criminal Defense Clinical Legal Education Program; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a criminal defense clinical legal education program within HECC and funds it, effective July 1, 2025, with an emergency declaration.

title: Relating to the application of overtime under the Oregon Public Service Retirement Plan.
summary: Changes how the overtime cap is calculated when determining final average salary for OPSRP pension members.

title: Relating to professional workforce; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows the Oregon Medical Board to issue provisional licenses to qualified internationally trained physicians, who must practice under supervision for four years before full licensure.

title: Relating to state financial administration.
summary: Appropriates money to the Criminal Justice Commission for the Justice Reinvestment Equity Program, with no program details stated.

title: Relating to duties of boards of education of community college districts; declaring an emergency.
summary: Revises community college board duties: requires association membership approval, allows member stipends, posts member emails publicly, adds a student voting member, and requires compliance reporting.

title: Relating to sewage disposal system permits; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars DEQ from deeming a community sewer system available for a sewage permit unless it is within 200 feet of the property, sunsetting in 2031.

title: Relating to housing; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets cities and counties repay state housing loans from non-developer-fee sources and make loans and grants, limits developers' use of older land-use rules inside UGBs, and amends the temporary UGB expansion program.

title: Relating to contract terms for point of sale systems.
summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study point of sale system contract terms and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to earned income access services; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires a state license to provide earned income access services, sets application criteria, licensee requirements, prohibitions, and civil penalties up to $2,500 per violation.

title: Relating to administrative rules.
summary: Bars state agencies from adopting administrative rules unless statutory authority exists for them.

title: Relating to administrative rules.
summary: Requires the Legislative Policy and Research Director to study methods for legislative oversight of administrative rules and report findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to small claims.
summary: Raises the small claims court filing limit from $10,000 to $20,000.

title: Relating to estate tax; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Limits the estate tax exemption for natural resource forestland to small owners and ties it to active forest management, for estates of decedents dying from 2026.

title: Relating to immigration enforcement.
summary: Repeals Oregon's limits on state and local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, including service denials, citizenship inquiries, and reporting requirements.

title: Relating to the repeal of the corporate activity tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Repeals Oregon's corporate activity tax for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to the repeal of provisions related to requirements for agricultural overtime.
topics: Labor and employment; Taxes and budget
summary: Repeals Oregon's overtime pay requirement for agricultural workers and the related tax credit for employers paying that overtime.

title: Relating to the Oregon Legislative Information System; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs legislative administrators to let amendments and informational material be posted to bills on OLIS regardless of hearing scheduling; sunsets 2030.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Adds two members, representing two professions, to the Building Codes Structures Board and requires a housing study report by September 2026.

title: Relating to exempt amount under corporate activity tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises the corporate activity tax exempt amount and filing threshold, starting tax years on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to persons arrested for drug crimes.
summary: Requires arresting officers to notify federal immigration authorities for certain drug delivery or manufacturing arrests, and limits pretrial release for those arrests.

title: Relating to the Department of State Police.
summary: Creates a State Police division to enforce laws against illegal marijuana cultivation.

title: Relating to short-acting opioid antagonists; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets EMRs and EMTs draw up and give doses of naloxone from multi-dose containers, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to employment of forestry workers; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study pay and classification for state forestry and wildfire positions and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to residential rent increase limits.
summary: Exempts residential tenancies within 25 miles of the coastline from state maximum limits on rent increases.

title: Relating to rent increase limits.
summary: Repeals statutory limits on how much landlords may raise residential rent.

title: Relating to construction standards for energy efficiency; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bars cities and counties from adopting building energy standards, such as the Reach Code, that are stricter than the state's building code.

title: Relating to accessory dwelling units.
summary: Allows owners of pre-1974 historic homes on rural residential land to build an accessory dwelling unit.

title: Relating to manufactured dwellings.
summary: Appropriates money to the Housing and Community Services Department to replace old manufactured dwellings in specified southwest Oregon counties.

title: Relating to faculty qualifications for public universities.
summary: Requires public university governing boards to adopt faculty personnel standards mandating at least a master's degree, with exceptions.

title: Relating to housing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets the housing department use set-aside LIFT fund money to buy apartments for conversion to affordable housing, sunsetting June 30, 2027.

title: Relating to tax incentives for affordable housing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income or corporate excise tax credit for part of the costs of building affordable single-family homes sold to households at or below 120% of area median income.

title: Relating to standing in land use appeal.
summary: Limits who may appeal land use decisions to people who live or run a business within 25 miles and attended a hearing in person.

title: Relating to attorney fees for appeal of quasi-judicial land use decisions.
summary: Makes unsuccessful intervenors in quasi-judicial land use appeals pay the winning party's attorney fees.

title: Relating to security on farms.
summary: Allows recreational vehicles to be temporarily sited on exclusive farm use zoned land to provide farm security.

title: Relating to bioengineering for the protection of coastal resources.
summary: Directs the Land Conservation and Development Commission to adopt guidance rules on nature-based, nonstructural shoreline stabilization by 2028, with General Fund money for that work.

title: Relating to county emergency management.
summary: Creates a grant program through ODEM to fund county emergency preparedness coordinators, and a council committee to study county emergency management capacity.

title: Relating to prohibiting gender-affirming care at correctional facilities.
summary: Bars the Department of Corrections, Oregon Youth Authority and Oregon Health Authority from paying for or providing gender-affirming care to people in custody.

title: Relating to fentanyl; declaring an emergency.
summary: Separates fentanyl possession, delivery and manufacture into their own statutes, raises some sentences, and adds mandatory minimums and limits on probation for repeat offenders.

title: Relating to prohibiting geographic tracking in connection with motor vehicle liability insurance policies; prescribing an effective date.
topics: AI and technology; Consumer protection and business
summary: Prohibits auto insurers from using devices or technology that track or reveal an insured's geographic location while driving a covered vehicle.

title: Relating to motor vehicle emission standards.
summary: Bars Oregon's environmental commission from adopting California zero-emission truck sales rules and bars enforcing earlier ones.

title: Relating to housing; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the housing department to fund affordable housing property management and create a program to preserve low-income homes, including manufactured dwelling parks.

title: Relating to utility rate impacts.
summary: Requires the Public Utility Commission to study rate impacts of HB 2021's greenhouse gas reductions and report findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the creation of credits for the restoration of salmon habitat; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a voluntary salmon habitat restoration credit pilot in the Coquille and Coos basins, with a trust fund and a programmatic federal-state permit pathway.

title: Relating to the Rock Creek Hatchery; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the state fish and wildlife department to study Rock Creek Hatchery impacts, report by September 2026, and appropriates General Fund money for the study.

title: Relating to fish.
summary: Requires the state fish and wildlife department to study salmon and fish stocking protocols and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the impacts of wildfire on water quality.
summary: Requires Fish and Wildlife and Environmental Quality to study wildfire impacts on stream water quality and report findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the impacts of sediment on the Rogue River; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money through DAS to the Umpqua Fishery Enhancement Derby for salmonid habitat restoration on the Rogue River.

title: Relating to a program of state inspection by the State Department of Agriculture; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates money to the State Department of Agriculture for a state meat inspection program covering nonamenable species, effective immediately as an emergency.

title: Relating to county sales of lands.
summary: Directs leftover proceeds from county real property sales into the county general fund.

title: Relating to county property tax collection; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets counties at high financial risk withhold three percent of property tax distributions to fund the county assessor's office.

title: Relating to a taxable income exemption for taxpayers who are a veteran.
summary: Exempts veterans' retirement pay and pensions for Armed Forces service from state income tax, starting tax years on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to housing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Legislative Policy and Research Director to study affordable housing and report to interim committees by August 15, 2026.

title: Relating to veterans.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to Administrative Services to provide veterans in Coos and Curry Counties transportation to the Roseburg VA medical center.

title: Relating to urban reserves.
summary: Requires more cities to create urban reserves and allows certain development in those reserves and expanded urban growth boundaries.

title: Relating to clustered resource dwellings.
summary: Lets counties allow clustered nonresource homes and bonus dwellings on farm and forest lands, with siting and subdivision requirements.

title: Relating to the transition from an abbreviated school day program; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets students removed from an abbreviated school day program use transitional services, including students with disabilities whose parents revoke consent or object to placement.

title: Relating to exemptions of abbreviated school day program requirements; declaring an emergency.
summary: Exempts certain students from abbreviated school day program requirements and laws, effective July 1, 2025, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to residential land use.
summary: Amends criteria and processes for expedited land division to allow residential lot splitting in cities; the direction of the change is not stated.

title: Relating to microfibers.
summary: Bans sale of new clothes washers lacking a microfiber filtration system, starting January 1, 2030, to reduce microfiber pollution.

title: Relating to behavioral health workforce training for students; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to award grants to local workforce boards for high school behavioral health training programs, sunsetting in 2029.

title: Relating to regional health equity coalitions; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money to fund regional health equity coalitions and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to community health; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets OHA contract directly with community health workers, nurses and community organizations to serve Medicaid recipients, and sets their billing codes and supervision rules.

title: Relating to housing.
summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to study housing and report to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to regional health equity coalitions; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to inflation-adjust grant amounts awarded to regional health equity coalitions, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to a wellness program for Oregon health care professionals; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs DAS to distribute money to the Oregon Wellness Program, which supports wellness for health care professionals.

title: Relating to dental insurers.
summary: Requires dental insurers to follow specified rules for paying and denying claims.

title: Relating to restrictions on 340B covered entities.
summary: Bars drug manufacturers from interfering with 340B covered entities' drug acquisition, delivery or dispensing, with civil penalties for violations.

title: Relating to allowable claims of equity in a property that is subject to a reverse mortgage; declaring an emergency.
summary: Limits a reverse mortgage lender's claim on home equity to the share matching the lump sum provided, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to infertility; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires certain health insurers to cover fertility treatments, exempts some insurers, and creates a DCBS reimbursement program funded by a new Market Equity Fund.

title: Relating to medical examiners.
summary: Lets licensed physician associates and nurse practitioners serve as medical examiners, and adds a licensure requirement for physicians who serve.

title: Relating to violence in health care settings.
summary: Requires certain health care employers and home care settings to adopt workplace violence prevention measures, excludes Oregon State Hospital, and requires a DCBS incident report.

title: Relating to in-home care for minor children with disabilities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires ODHS to pay parents for in-home attendant care of children with developmental disabilities and to pursue federal matching funds.

title: Relating to fees charged for services provided in hospital-based facilities.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Limits hospitals' facility fees to campus or emergency-department sites, bans fees for certain services, requires patient notice and reporting, and allows OHA civil penalties.

title: Relating to cooling for residential tenancies.
summary: Requires landlords to provide indoor cooling in residential units, with cooling spaces in buildings of 10+ units, and makes cooling an essential service.

title: Relating to drug labeling requirements; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires manufacturers or wholesalers to list gluten-containing grain ingredients on labels of orally administered drugs, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to computer science education; declaring an emergency.
