summary: Requires school district boards to ensure all schools offer computer science education in all grades, adding it to required content areas.

title: Relating to gluten.
summary: Requires gluten-containing foods to carry labels, restricts when foods may be labeled gluten free, and allows civil penalties for violations.

title: Relating to traffic safety education.
summary: Requires ODOT to translate driver education student and instructor curricula into Spanish, post them online, and offer printed copies for a fee.

title: Relating to the installation of vaporizing detection devices in high schools.
summary: Requires vaping detection devices in certain areas of high schools with 1,000 or more enrolled students.

title: Relating to an income tax credit for volunteer firefighters; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income tax credit for volunteer firefighters for tax years 2026 through 2031, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to signature collection for charitable checkoff participation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets Oregon voters sign electronically to support charities seeking income tax checkoff contributions, with the Department of Revenue setting the electronic collection method.

title: Relating to Oregon Native Plant Appreciation Month; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Designates April of each year as Oregon Native Plant Appreciation Month and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to marriage.
summary: Raises Oregon's minimum legal marriage age to 18, eliminating marriage of minors under 18.

title: Relating to complex rehabilitation technology.
summary: Requires OHA and coordinated care organizations to decide prior authorization requests for complex rehabilitation technology repair within 72 hours.

title: Relating to farm cafes.
summary: Allows certain farm cafes on Lane County exclusive farm use land under new standards, with Oregon Health Authority licensing tied to land use compliance.

title: Relating to a right to repair consumer equipment.
summary: Expands Oregon's right-to-repair law to cover electric wheelchairs and complex rehabilitation technology, requiring manufacturers to make repair tools and parts available.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Advocacy Commissions Office; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Oregon Advocacy Commissions Office for the biennium and caps its spending from other revenues; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Department of Agriculture; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Department of Agriculture's biennial budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting expenditures from fees, lottery and federal funds.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Approves certain new or increased fees adopted by the State Department of Agriculture and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Department of Aviation; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Oregon Department of Aviation's biennial expenditure limits for fees, miscellaneous receipts and federal funds, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets bonding authorization amounts for the 2025-27 biennium, adds conditions on certain bonds and community college bonding, and authorizes future Interstate 5 bridge bonding.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets six-year capital construction spending limits for state agencies and higher education bond proceeds, and extends expiration dates on prior approvals.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the biennial expenditure limit for the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners' fee and other revenues, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Columbia River Gorge Commission; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Columbia River Gorge Commission for its biennial expenses and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Construction Contractors Board; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets a biennial expenditure limit on revenues collected by the Construction Contractors Board and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to plastic waste.
summary: Bans single-use checkout bags at restaurants and retailers and restricts single-use plastic utensils, condiment packaging and small lodging toiletry containers unless requested.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Approves a fee increase adopted by the Construction Contractors Board and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Consumer and Business Services; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Department of Consumer and Business Services' 2025-27 budget by appropriating General Fund moneys and limiting its biennial expenditures, and takes effect immediately.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Board of Dentistry; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Oregon Board of Dentistry's biennial expenditure limit on its fees and other revenues, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Justice; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund moneys to the Department of Justice for biennial district attorney expenses and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Early Learning and Care; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates the Department of Early Learning and Care's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting certain agency expenditures, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Education; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Department of Education's 2025-27 biennial budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting spending from lottery, fee, federal and other accounts.

title: Relating to the state financial administration of the Department of Education; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Education for the State School Fund and limits spending from lottery and other revenue sources; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Department of Emergency Management; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Oregon Department of Emergency Management's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund moneys and limiting certain agency expenditures, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Department of Energy; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the State Department of Energy's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting its biennial spending from various fund sources.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Approves certain new or increased fees adopted by the State Department of Energy and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to public defense.
summary: Directs the Oregon Public Defense Commission to study public defense best practices and report to interim legislative committees by December 31, 2026.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Environmental Quality; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Department of Environmental Quality's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting spending from fees, bonds, federal funds and lottery moneys.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Forestry Department; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the State Forestry Department's biennial budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting spending from fees, lottery and federal funds, with an emergency clause.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Government Ethics Commission; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Sets a biennial expenditure limit on the Oregon Government Ethics Commission's fees, miscellaneous receipts and federal reimbursements, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Office of the Governor; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates the Office of the Governor's biennial budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting spending from lottery, fee and other revenues.

title: Relating to the financial administration of specified boards; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Caps the biennial spending of fees and other revenues collected by six licensing boards, and takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Higher Education Coordinating Commission; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Higher Education Coordinating Commission's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting spending from lottery, federal, timber tax and other funds.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Human Services; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Department of Human Services' biennial budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting expenditures from certain fees and federal funds.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Approves certain new or increased fees adopted by the Department of Human Services and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Land Conservation and Development; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Department of Land Conservation and Development's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting its spending from other revenues and federal funds.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Land Use Board of Appeals; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Land Use Board of Appeals for the biennium and caps its biennial spending from certain fees and revenues.

title: Relating to data center power usage.
summary: Directs the State Department of Energy to study data center power usage and report findings to legislative interim committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Budgets and allocates lottery, veterans', criminal fine, marijuana, student success and tobacco settlement account moneys for the 2025-27 biennium.

title: Relating to lottery bonds; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Authorizes and modifies state lottery bond issuance and purposes for specified agencies, creates funds, and appropriates money for financed projects.

title: Relating to the financial administration of specified boards; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund moneys to two licensing boards for the biennium and caps their spending from fees and other revenues.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Oregon Military Department; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Budget bill appropriating General Fund moneys to the Oregon Military Department and limiting its biennial expenditures from fees, federal funds and other revenues.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Public Employees Retirement System; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Sets biennial expenditure limits for the Public Employees Retirement System and modifies certain limits for the 2023-25 biennium, effective on passage.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Public Records Advocate; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Limits the Public Records Advocate's biennial spending from fees and other non-lottery, non-federal revenues, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Revenue; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates the Department of Revenue's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting certain biennial expenditures from department revenues.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Secretary of State; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Secretary of State and limits its biennial spending from fees, other revenues and federal funds, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of the State Fire Marshal; and declaring an emergency.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Sets the State Fire Marshal's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting biennial expenditures from fees, other revenues, and federal funds.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of State Lands; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of State Lands for its biennial budget and limits how certain department revenues may be spent.

title: Relating to reusable packaging systems.
summary: Directs the Department of Environmental Quality to study reusable packaging systems and report findings by September 15, 2026, then sunsets.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Board of Tax Practitioners; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets a biennial expenditure limit on fees and revenues collected by the State Board of Tax Practitioners, with an emergency clause effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Department of Transportation; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the Department of Transportation's biennial budget, appropriating General Fund moneys and limiting expenditures from various fund sources.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the State Treasurer; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Sets the State Treasurer's biennial expenditure limits for certain fee and other revenues, excluding lottery and federal funds, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the financial administration of the Water Resources Department; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates the Water Resources Department's 2025-27 budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting spending from lottery, fee, and federal funds.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Approves new or increased fees adopted by the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Approves certain fees adopted by the Department of Consumer and Business Services and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Authorizes state agencies without an enacted budget to spend on obligations incurred after July 1, 2025, and appropriates moneys, sunsetting September 15, 2025.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund moneys to DHS and OHA for the 2023-25 biennium and limits certain expenditures from specified funds, declaring an emergency.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates an agency budget by appropriating General Fund moneys and limiting biennial expenditures; the recipient agency and amounts are left blank.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates an agency budget by appropriating General Fund moneys for biennial expenses and limiting biennial expenditures from fees, other revenues, and federal funds.

title: Relating to Legislative Policy and Research Office confidentiality.
summary: Makes research requested, collected, maintained or used by the Legislative Policy and Research Office confidential unless release is specifically authorized.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Adjusts state agency budgets and General Fund appropriations for the 2023-25 biennium and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a state agency budget, appropriating General Fund money and limiting biennial expenditures from fees, other revenues and federal funds, with an emergency clause.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates an agency budget, appropriating General Fund moneys to an unnamed agency and limiting its biennial expenditures, with amounts left blank.

title: Relating to state financial administration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a biennial agency budget with a blank-named agency, appropriating General Fund moneys and limiting expenditures from fees and federal funds, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to cannabis; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Lets licensed marijuana businesses use motion cameras and digital manifests, drops plant tagging, adds a hemp endorsement, and allows interstate commerce if federal law permits.

title: Relating to membership requirements of the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission.
summary: Requires at least one Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission member to hold a marijuana processor, producer, retailer or wholesaler license.

title: Relating to cannabis market growth; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands cannabis licensees' ability to share samples at temporary events, sell wholesale at events, and transfer usable marijuana between producers.

title: Relating to early medical release; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Parole Board to study changes to early medical release procedures for incarcerated adults and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to cardiac computerized tomography coronary calcium score scans.
summary: Requires Oregon Health Plan and private health insurance to cover coronary calcium score CT scans for people 40 and older.

title: Relating to an income tax subtraction for tips received; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a personal income tax subtraction for tips received in tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to income tax subtractions for child care expenses; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Children and families; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a personal income tax subtraction for child care expenses for tax years 2025 through 2030.

title: Relating to enrollment in virtual public charter schools; declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes the enrollment cap for virtual public charter schools and drops resident district approval and related information requirements.

title: Relating to tax incentives for financial institution lending in rural areas; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates temporary Oregon tax subtractions and CAT exemptions for banks' interest on rural farm, home and fishing-boat loans, for tax years 2026 through 2031.

title: Relating to U.S. Highway 20; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs ODOT to study and report on increasing motor vehicle capacity on a portion of U.S. Highway 20; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to state parks; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Transfers management of Capitol grounds from State Parks to DAS and requires a state parks study and report by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to standards of time.
summary: Keeps the Pacific Time Zone portion of Oregon on standard time year-round if California and Washington do the same within 10 years.

title: Relating to child care provider incentive program; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a child care provider incentive program run by the Department of Early Learning and Care, funded through a new Child Care Provider Incentive Fund.

title: Relating to a specially assessed value for the homesteads of seniors; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a six-year property tax special assessed value for homesteads of people 70 or older, with existing enrollees keeping it after sunset.

title: Relating to organizations that assist with COBID certification.
summary: Creates a grant program for nonprofits that help minority-owned businesses get COBID certification to compete for public contracts.

title: Relating to a tax credit for expenses related to journalism; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates an income tax credit for subscriptions to news outlets and donations to journalism organizations, bans false advertising of the credit, and sets civil penalties.

title: Relating to local marijuana taxes; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Raises the maximum local tax cities and counties may impose on marijuana sales and sends part of new revenue to eligible counties.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Authorizes new state lottery bonds and bond or certificate issuance for projects including Moda Center and an OSU Cascades health center, with conditions.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Changes budgets and timelines for state capital construction projects, modifies spending limits, and extends expiration dates for certain project approvals and expenditure limits.

title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Budget bill changing allocations from several state funds, including the Oregon Marijuana Account and Fund for Student Success; declares emergency.

title: Relating to road infrastructure; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study road infrastructure as it relates to housing and report findings to housing interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the Oregon Racial Justice Act.
summary: Creates a court process letting people challenge charges, convictions or sentences as race-based, applying retroactively to specified cases from 2027.

title: Relating to surplus revenue disposition; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Repeals the personal income tax kicker, ending refunds of surplus revenue to taxpayers, starting with biennia ending June 30, 2027, if SJR 15 is approved.

title: Relating to the death penalty; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Removes Oregon's statutory death penalty provisions, effective only if voters approve Senate Joint Resolution 16 (2025) in November 2026.

title: Relating to references to individuals.
summary: Replaces "men and women" with gender-neutral terms like "people" in certain statutes and encourages that wording in laws, rules and orders.

title: Relating to Japanese beetle grubs; declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Agriculture to eradicate Japanese beetle grubs, effective on passage as an emergency.

title: Relating to energy generation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires electric utilities to recover waste storage costs from energy facilities and requires developers to disclose those storage costs.

title: Relating to filing deadlines for county voters' pamphlets; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Sets filing deadlines for candidates to submit a portrait and statement for inclusion in county voters' pamphlets, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to funding for fire stations; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money through the State Fire Marshal to Central Douglas Fire and Rescue for fire station purposes, effective on passage.

title: Relating to expanding the supply of affordable housing; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates grant programs for homeowners and counties to build rentable auxiliary dwellings, and bars reassessment of those units for property tax.

title: Relating to election documents posted on county or city websites; and prescribing an effective date.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Requires county and city filing officers to post certain filed election documents online within two business days, and permits fees in some cases.

title: Relating to mental health care provider incentives; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a state psychology provider incentive program offering financial incentives and loan repayment to psychology students and licensed psychologists, funded by a new fund.

title: Relating to police body camera recordings; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Bars officers in deadly force incidents from viewing body camera footage before interviews, creates a court route for denied footage access, and directs storage standards.

title: Relating to a public bank task force; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a State Public Bank Task Force to study and recommend on a state public bank, reporting by September 1, 2026.

title: Relating to Oregon Truffle Month; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Designates February each year as Oregon Truffle Month, a commemorative declaration with no policy effect.

title: Relating to public employee retirement.
summary: Requires the Public Employees Retirement Board to study retirement and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to termination of tenancy due to sale of dwelling unit; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets landlords pay tenants one month's rent to shorten the move-out notice for sales to owner-occupant buyers from 90 to 60 days.

title: Relating to an income tax subtraction for amounts received in wildfire litigation; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates corporate excise and income tax subtractions for wildfire lawsuit awards and related legal fees paid by plaintiffs, with refunds for earlier years.

title: Relating to disability benefits under the Public Employees Retirement System; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets police officers and firefighters receive PERS disability benefits more easily, including for on-duty PTSD, and requires hearings on denied claims to be referred promptly.

title: Relating to adult foster homes.
summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study adult foster homes and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to producing food in planned communities.
summary: Allows HOA members and their tenants in planned communities to grow gardens and raise hens or bees.

title: Relating to long term care.
summary: Directs the Department of Human Services to study long-term care and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026; sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to the long term care facility assessment.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study the long term care facility assessment, report to interim committees by September 15, 2026, and sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to the Stafford triangle area in Clackamas County.
summary: Directs DLCD to study forming a new city in the Stafford triangle and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to the regulation of public property with respect to persons experiencing homelessness; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals HB 3115 (2021), removing the statewide objective-reasonableness standard, cause of action, and affirmative defense for local laws on homeless persons' use of public property.

title: Relating to terminations of residential tenancies without tenant cause.
summary: Prohibits landlords from ending residential tenancies for no-fault reasons during the school year when the tenant is a grade school student or teacher.

title: Relating to Department of Human Services contracts.
summary: Requires DHS multiyear contracts with health or social service providers to include annual cost-of-living adjustments.

title: Relating to veterans' recognition registration plates.
summary: Lets veterans with a disability qualify for a veterans' recognition plate and request a surcharge waiver, funded by a DOT appropriation.

title: Relating to oral health care coordination.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to create a grant program funding certified dental sealant programs' oral health care coordination activities.

title: Relating to step therapy for nonopioids.
summary: Requires certain health insurers and the state Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee to give nonopioid drugs equal coverage and utilization rules as opioid alternatives.

title: Relating to immigration status discrimination in real estate transactions; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Bans landlords and property sellers from discriminating against tenants or applicants based on immigration or citizenship status, with statutory penalties.

title: Relating to a deadline within which to act upon an application for a building permit.
summary: Sets firm deadlines for building permit decisions, deems permits approved if agencies miss them, and makes agencies liable for fees and costs.

title: Relating to the Oregon Tort Claims Act.
summary: Exempts child abuse claims against government entities from Oregon Tort Claims Act notice requirements, revives certain barred claims, and requires filing within two years.

title: Relating to affordable housing.
summary: Requires the Housing and Community Services Department to study affordable housing and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to affordable housing.
summary: Requires the housing department to study affordable housing and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to state agency relations with nonprofit organizations.
summary: Creates an advisory council to consult on and recommend improvements to state grant and contracting processes with nonprofits, and to evaluate a grants database.

title: Relating to standards for state agencies that award grants to nonprofit organizations; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires state agencies to follow DAS budgeting guidelines for grant programs and sets prevailing wages and benefits for nonprofit grant-funded workers through BOLI.

title: Relating to the Strong Start Program; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates the Strong Start Program in HECC to support first-year and underrepresented students at public universities, and declares an emergency effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to medical debt reporting.
summary: Bars medical providers and consumer reporting agencies from reporting or including medical debt in credit reports, with private lawsuits and Unlawful Trade Practices Act enforcement.

title: Relating to occupational disease.
summary: Adds certain health care employees to the workers whose stress disorders are presumed compensable workers' compensation occupational disease claims.

title: Relating to behavioral health services provided by federally qualified health centers.
summary: Directs the Oregon Health Authority to study alternative payment methods for behavioral health care at federally qualified health centers and report by September 30, 2026.

title: Relating to services for medically complex Oregonians.
summary: Directs DHS to create a home care worker certification program and orders several studies on services for people with complex medical and behavioral health needs.

title: Relating to equitable access to health care services.
summary: Sets minimum Medicaid reimbursement rates for primary care, optometry, dental and behavioral health services, directing OHA and CCOs.

title: Relating to medical assistance provider audits; declaring an emergency.
summary: Limits OHA's ability to claw back Medicaid provider payments, barring recovery when services are verified and sampling-based recoveries absent a 15% error rate.

title: Relating to funding for substance use services.
summary: Moves Behavioral Health Resource Network grant administration to OHA, repeals the statewide hotline requirement, and orders a study of Measure 110 funding.

title: Relating to public assistance; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a state-funded nutrition assistance program for children aged six and under who would qualify for SNAP but for immigration status, with outreach and an advisory group on customer treatment.

title: Relating to undocumented individuals.
summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to create and update a list of undocumented individuals charged with or convicted of crimes, and the crimes involved.

title: Relating to the repeal of certain provisions related to pay equity; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals certain pay equity provisions, removing some employer pay equity obligations, rights and remedies, and takes effect immediately.

title: Relating to inherently dangerous sporting activities; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows operators of inherently dangerous sporting activities to require patrons to sign anticipatory releases of liability, including for the operator's negligence, and deems them not unconscionable.

title: Relating to permanent physical injury.
summary: Creates an aggravated assault and attempted murder charge for causing permanent injury, with a mandatory 300-month sentence unless a lesser sentence applies.

title: Relating to preservation of trees for housing development.
summary: Bars local governments from conditioning needed-housing development or use on retaining trees, with exceptions, through January 1, 2036.

title: Relating to crime.
summary: Amends crime provisions: enhances sentences for some child-related crimes, changes GEI rules and DV merger treatment, and raises invasion of privacy in the first degree to grid category 8 when the victim is a minor.

title: Relating to participation in athletic competitions according to biological sex; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires school districts to designate sports by biological sex and bars biological males from female athletic competitions, with private causes of action.

title: Relating to executive clemency.
summary: Requires all gubernatorial clemency actions to be initiated by application and follow specified procedures.

title: Relating to consumer engagement in the behavioral health care system; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates an Oregon Health Authority consumer engagement program for behavioral health, funded by $1 per member monthly from CCOs, plus an eastern Oregon early psychosis residential pilot.

title: Relating to settlement agreements entered into by the Department of Justice.
summary: Requires the Attorney General to report annually to legislative judiciary committees on DOJ settlements requiring state payments over $4 million.

title: Relating to approval of state agency fees by Legislative Assembly; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires that new or increased state agency fees take effect only if the Legislative Assembly approves them by law; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to employment subject to unemployment insurance taxes; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Labor and employment; Taxes and budget
summary: Exempts employers from unemployment insurance taxes on wages paid to H-2A visa workers and other noncitizen agricultural workers not eligible for benefits.

title: Relating to the offense of attempting to elude a police officer.
summary: Increases sentencing guidelines and penalty seriousness for felony attempting to elude a police officer.

title: Relating to recipients of public moneys; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Requires recipients of certain state grants and loans to file annual spending and political contribution reports, with agencies notifying them of the requirements.

title: Relating to the repeal of provisions related to requirements for agricultural overtime; prescribing an effective date.
topics: Labor and employment; Taxes and budget
summary: Repeals Oregon's overtime pay requirement for agricultural workers and the related tax credit for employers' overtime wages, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to encouraging child sexual abuse; declaring an emergency.
summary: Expands three child sexual abuse encouragement crimes to cover computer-generated depictions, and takes effect on signature.

title: Relating to vehicle registration.
summary: Switches most vehicles to one-time ownership registration fees instead of biennial fees and eliminates offenses for failing to renew registration.

title: Relating to informed consent.
summary: Requires physicians and physician associates to attempt to obtain patient informed consent before dismissing a patient for emergency care or transferring care.

title: Relating to the Oregon Medical Board.
summary: Requires the Oregon Medical Board to consider a reasonable person standard when defining unprofessional conduct.

title: Relating to personal income tax rates; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Imposes a flat-rate personal income tax on taxpayers below an adjusted gross income threshold, starting with tax years beginning in 2026.

title: Relating to scholarships for use at participating nonpublic schools.
summary: Creates an Educational Scholarship Program giving eligible students state money to pay costs at participating nonpublic schools.

title: Relating to instruction on the prevention of sex trafficking of children; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires school districts to add sex trafficking of children to their child sexual abuse prevention instruction, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to public charter school eligibility for grants from the Student Investment Account; declaring an emergency.
summary: Makes virtual public charter schools eligible to receive Student Investment Account grants and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to enrollment in virtual public charter schools; declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes the enrollment cap on virtual public charter schools and the resident district approval requirement for non-district-sponsored virtual charters.

title: Relating to the use of hydroelectric energy to comply with a renewable portfolio standard; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows electricity from hydroelectric facilities to count toward compliance with Oregon's renewable portfolio standard, and declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to a study on the feasibility of developing nuclear energy generation in this state; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs Oregon State University to conduct a feasibility study on developing nuclear energy generation in Oregon, and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to payment for use of the roads by electric motor vehicles.
summary: Directs ODOT to study a road usage charge for electric and hybrid vehicles and report to legislative transportation committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to the transfer to the State Highway Fund of charges imposed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the use of motor vehicle fuel.
summary: Directs fees from motor fuel greenhouse gas programs to the State Highway Fund and requires the Governor to budget estimated transfers.

title: Relating to small forestland owners.
summary: Lets small forestland owners harvest trees they planted under reforestation requirements, with reforestation duties applying after harvest; the Board of Forestry may adopt rules.

title: Relating to low forest fuel load levels on state forestland.
summary: Directs the State Forester to actively manage state forestlands to achieve and maintain low forest fuel load levels.

title: Relating to payment of dependent care tax credits in installments; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs ODHS to seek a federal SNAP waiver so recipients can receive dependent care tax credits in advance installments; sunsets 2031.

title: Relating to crime victims who are under 18 years of age.
summary: Expands the criminal offenses and penalties for sex crimes and assault against minors, including family-relationship and victim-age provisions.

title: Relating to land rights of People's Republic of China in this state.
summary: Bans China and entities under Chinese jurisdiction from buying or leasing farmland in Oregon.

title: Relating to state financial administration.
summary: Appropriates state funds to the State Police to reduce the backlog of untested sexual assault forensic evidence kits.

title: Relating to residential tenancies.
summary: Lets landlords end month-to-month tenancies without cause and repeals limits on rent increases.

title: Relating to auditing the Oregon Food Bank; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a joint legislative committee to audit Oregon Food Bank financial transactions for political campaign or issue activity, reporting by November 2025, sunsetting January 2027.

title: Relating to the regulation of public property with respect to persons experiencing homelessness; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals HB 3115 (2021), which set a statewide reasonableness standard for local laws on homeless persons' use of public property, along with its cause of action and affirmative defense.

title: Relating to school access.
summary: Lets resident students attend any public school, requires board consent for nonresidents with limited exceptions, bars tuition, and removes the virtual charter enrollment cap.

title: Relating to virtual public charter school enrollment.
summary: Raises from to five percent the share of a district's students who may attend certain virtual charter schools without district approval.

title: Relating to conforming estate tax to federal basic exclusion amount; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises Oregon's estate tax exemption to match the federal $13.61 million threshold and raises the estate tax return filing threshold to the same level.

title: Relating to estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Repeals Oregon's estate tax, applying it only to decedents dying on or before January 1, 2025, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to civil rights.
summary: Creates a state-law civil action for damages and equitable relief against persons acting under color of law who violate Oregon rights, with fee-shifting for prevailing parties.

title: Relating to a specially assessed value for the residences of seniors; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a specially assessed property tax value for owner-occupied primary residences of people aged 65 or older.

title: Relating to the Secretary of State's business registry functions.
summary: Directs the Secretary of State to study ways to reduce business paperwork filing burdens and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to reading instruction; declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows school districts, education service districts and public charter schools to employ unlicensed people to teach reading, effective on passage.

title: Relating to the abolishment of the Department of Education.
summary: Creates a task force to study and recommend on abolishing the Department of Education, sunsetting January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to the development of student vocational skills.
summary: Lets school boards adopt policies encouraging students to build vocational skills by doing maintenance work for their districts.

title: Relating to ballot security.
summary: Creates a public, searchable database of scanned ballot copies, adds secret unique ballot IDs, and lets voters inspect their ballots and observers watch printing.

title: Relating to energy; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an Oregon income tax credit for energy production and a task force to review how energy production is regulated.

title: Relating to school district budget expenditures; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires school district boards to direct at least half of district budgets to pay teachers of core academic subjects and manual skills.

title: Relating to employment preference for veterans.
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Government and administration
summary: Expands veterans' hiring preference enforcement for public employers, adding interview and notice duties, jury trials, noneconomic damages, a DVA arbitration program, and a training defense.

title: Relating to waiver of tuition.
summary: Prohibits reducing a qualified student's tuition waiver by the amount of certain other student aid they receive.

title: Relating to economic development; declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets Business Oregon survey state economic development loan and grant programs; declares an emergency effective on passage.

title: Relating to the expenditure of state moneys based on the amount that is attributable to a student; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires school districts, education service districts and public charter schools to use state money received for each student to educate that same student.

title: Relating to social studies standards; declaring an emergency.
summary: Stops the State Board of Education's review of social studies standards and repeals the directive requiring that review, effective on passage.

title: Relating to a tax credit for political contributions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Increases the maximum personal income tax credit allowed for political contributions for tax years 2025 through 2027.

title: Relating to fees.
summary: Prohibits state agencies from charging fees.

title: Relating to gravity separation mines.
summary: Defines gravity separation mines to include those using air, water or froth flotation, and deems mines solely using gravity separation to be gravity separation mines.

title: Relating to monetary penalties.
summary: Requires public bodies to send certain fine and civil penalty revenue to the state General Fund instead of keeping it.

title: Relating to abortion restrictions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Bans abortion at 15 or more weeks gestational age with limited exceptions, adds facility rules, private lawsuits, and state reporting.

title: Relating to the militia of the state.
summary: Bars the Governor from ordering the state militia into armed conflict or war unless Congress declares war or calls the militia forth under the U.S. Constitution.

title: Relating to tuition benefits connected to disabled veterans; declaring an emergency.
summary: Expands tuition waivers for Oregon 80%-disabled veterans and their spouses and children to cover more programs and bars reducing waivers by other aid.

title: Relating to procedures for the reduction of educator staff; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires school districts making educator staff reductions to prioritize seniority when deciding which teachers to retain.

title: Relating to the family and medical leave insurance program.
summary: Requires the Employment Department to study the family and medical leave insurance program and report findings to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to possession of controlled substances; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Reinstates criminal penalties for drug possession, reversing Measure 110's decriminalization, with jail time and fines set by drug schedule.

title: Relating to duties of the Oregon Government Ethics Commission.
summary: Ends the Oregon Government Ethics Commission by July 2027 and orders studies and plans for shifting its duties to other officials and local governments.

title: Relating to prohibiting gender-affirming care at correctional facilities.
summary: Bars the Department of Corrections, Oregon Youth Authority and Oregon Health Authority from paying for or providing gender-affirming care to people in custody.

title: Relating to the Columbia River.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Commission and state agencies to allow water appropriation from the Columbia River mainstem for eastern Oregon, including granting easements.

title: Relating to the Columbia River.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Commission to allow Columbia River mainstem water appropriation at two percent of average annual flow and requires easements to facilitate it.

title: Relating to interest on unpaid property taxes; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lowers the interest rate on unpaid property taxes to one-half of one percent per month, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to veterans' loans for acquisition of real property.
summary: Caps interest on Oregon veterans' home and farm loans at prime plus one percent and appropriates General Fund money to the War Veterans' Fund for those loans.

title: Relating to the provision of menstrual products in schools; declaring an emergency.
summary: Removes requirements that menstrual products be provided in male bathrooms and in public charter schools.

title: Relating to wildfire; declaring an emergency.
summary: Repeals the wildfire risk-classification and wildfire protection changes Oregon adopted in SB 762 (2021) and declares an emergency.

title: Relating to harms associated with climate change; declaring an emergency.
summary: Makes large greenhouse gas emitters strictly liable to harmed parties for damages from climate-driven extreme weather and climate disasters.

title: Relating to job-protected leave that is unpaid.
summary: Directs BOLI to study unpaid, job-protected leave laws and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to greenwashing; declaring an emergency.
summary: Prohibits false or misleading environmental, net zero, and reputational advertising claims, making violations unlawful trade practices with $200 statutory damages.

title: Relating to a moratorium on private investments by the State Treasurer in fossil fuel dominant funds.
summary: For five years, bars the State Treasurer from new or renewed investments in private market funds whose managers intend to invest in fossil fuels.

title: Relating to greenhouse gas emissions; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Climate Superfund Cost Recovery Program at DEQ and an account for it, and requires a Treasurer assessment of emissions costs.

title: Relating to primary care physicians; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to count practicing primary care physicians every two years, report to the Legislature, and publish the report.

title: Relating to housing; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Expands housing authorities' authority over mixed income housing and requires OHCS reports and long-term financing rules; loan program and fund language is unclear.

title: Relating to hydrogen; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires gas utilities to notify customers and the PUC before exceeding 2.5% hydrogen blending, and requires utilities to get PUC authorization for hydrogen projects.

title: Relating to civic information.
topics: AI and technology; Government and administration
summary: Requires platforms to have agreements before accessing news content, creates a private right of action and arbitration, and establishes a civic information consortium that awards grants.

title: Relating to transportation.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets certain cities, counties and local governments enact fuel taxes or vehicle registration fees without first submitting them to voters.

title: Relating to performance-based regulation of electric utilities.
summary: Lets the Public Utility Commission adopt performance-based regulation for electric companies, using incentives and penalties, and appropriates funds to implement it.

title: Relating to rail; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates the Oregon Rail Department and State Rail Board, transferring ODOT's rail duties to the new agency.

title: Relating to laws concerning job-protected leave from work; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Adjusts Oregon paid family and medical leave rules, including BOLI oversight, statute tolling, return-to-work certification, and a flight crew eligibility exemption, and orders an Employment Department study.

title: Relating to perinatal public health; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Delays residential nonpayment eviction trials for tenants who seek OHP health-related housing supports, and prioritizes housing funding for infants under 12 months.

title: Relating to health care; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires OHA and coordinated care organizations to reimburse peer delivered services in any setting and cover certain inpatient hospital services, and funds an OHSU maternal-neonatal entity.

title: Relating to perinatal services.
summary: Creates a community perinatal services access program and expands medical assistance and insurance coverage for doulas and lactation providers, with Health Licensing Office rules for lactation practitioners.

title: Relating to the perinatal workforce; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Task Force on the Perinatal Workforce to evaluate the workforce and report recommendations to legislative health committees by December 2026.

title: Relating to children; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Increases the maximum child tax credit and raises its income limits, starting with tax years beginning January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to coordinated care organizations; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs OHA and CCOs to build a whole-person maternal health model for Medicaid members and adds maternal and early childhood provisions to CCO contracts and metrics.

title: Relating to rapid fire activators; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates new crimes for transporting, manufacturing, transferring or possessing rapid fire activators, with prison terms and fines.

title: Relating to firearms.
summary: Bars people under 21 from possessing firearms and bars transferring certain firearms to them, with criminal penalties and exceptions.

title: Relating to the possession of firearms in certain public areas.
topics: Government and administration; Guns and weapons
summary: Lets public building governing bodies limit the CHL affirmative defense for firearm possession, making it a Class A misdemeanor where such a policy applies.

title: Relating to medical devices.
summary: Requires health insurers to cover prosthetic and orthotic devices for more patients, exempting state employee benefit boards unless they give notice.

title: Relating to strikes by transit workers.
summary: Repeals the state law prohibiting transit workers from striking, so they may strike.

title: Relating to the Bureau of Labor and Industries.
summary: Directs the Bureau of Labor and Industries to study matters tied to its enforcement laws and report findings to interim committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to water safety; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires children under 16 to wear a properly fitted life jacket on boats and when using floating items outside swimming areas, with fines up to $250.

title: Relating to telehealth services for K-12 students; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a 2025-2026 pilot for telehealth services in K-12 schools, requires a report by September 2026, appropriates funds, and takes effect on passage.

title: Relating to public health; declaring an emergency.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Bans sales of flavored tobacco and inhalant products except through certain licensed premises, restricts free distribution, and lets local governments adopt stricter rules.

title: Relating to immigration; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates state-funded grants to nonprofits helping noncitizens change immigration status or obtain permanent residency, with reporting and referral requirements.

title: Relating to worker classification.
summary: Creates a rebuttable presumption that anyone paid to perform work for a hiring entity is an employee, and directs agencies to use common criteria.

title: Relating to temporary total disability.
summary: Sets a weekly minimum workers' compensation benefit floor for temporary total disability that workers must receive.

title: Relating to wages; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study methods for detecting paycheck errors and report findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to exemption of prescription drug sales; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Exempts prescription drug sale receipts from the corporate activity tax, extending the exemption to critical access pharmacies starting tax year 2026.

title: Relating to public safety.
summary: Directs the Criminal Justice Commission to study how different sentence types affect recidivism and report to legislative committees by September 2026.

title: Relating to a tax credit for apprenticeships; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an income tax credit for taxpayers that provide apprenticeship opportunities, applying to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to employment.
summary: Directs the Employment Department to study employment issues and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026; the bill sunsets January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to judicial training.
summary: Lets the Chief Justice set continuing education requirements for state judges, directs the court administrator to offer that training, and requires reports and a domestic violence training study.

title: Relating to photo radar in highway work zones.
summary: Changes Oregon's highway worker photo radar laws in work zones; the summary gives no detail on the changes.

title: Relating to maximum assessed value; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Raises the maximum assessed value of property by three percent each tax year, starting the 91st day after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to levees; declaring an emergency.
summary: Authorizes lottery bonds to fund a Levee Project Grant Fund for levee projects, with an emergency clause effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to the Columbia corridor flood safety project.
summary: Authorizes lottery bond sales to fund Columbia corridor flood safety projects in Multnomah County.

title: Relating to the Cascadia High Speed Rail Task Force; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Cascadia High Speed Rail Task Force to study high speed rail in Oregon and report on progress and findings.

title: Relating to urgent care centers.
summary: Requires insurers and state health plans to pay 20% more for services at registered urgent care centers until January 2033, and sets OHA registration rules.

title: Relating to stipends for student teachers.
summary: Creates a HECC pilot program providing stipends to student teachers and their mentor educators, sunsetting January 2, 2028.

title: Relating to Parkinson's disease registry; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a Parkinson's disease registry, with the act taking effect 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to graffiti courts.
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to study graffiti courts and report findings to legislative judiciary committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to property insurance.
summary: Requires the Department of Consumer and Business Services to study property insurance and report findings to interim legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to funding for a cultural workforce center; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates state money through DAS to Portland Opportunities Industrialization Center to build and operate a cultural workforce center.

title: Relating to the suppression of evidence.
summary: Repeals the statutory bar on courts excluding evidence obtained in violation of a statute, except in specified circumstances.

title: Relating to residential tenancies.
summary: Bans landlords from using certain software to set rents or occupancy, adds tenant damages, and shortens the new-unit rent cap exemption from 15 to seven years.

title: Relating to two-person crew member requirements on trains.
summary: Requires trains to have at least two crew members, with federal-exception carve-outs, and sets civil penalties for violations.

title: Relating to the Corrections Ombudsman.
summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to study the Corrections Ombudsman and report findings to interim judiciary committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to case management services for individuals with developmental disabilities; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs ODHS to adopt a rule requiring a minimum 30-to-1 staffing ratio for developmental disability case managers, sunsetting January 2, 2027.

title: Relating to landfill emissions monitoring; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires operators of Benton County municipal solid waste landfills to monitor surface methane emissions and report the data.

title: Relating to the definition of "health care provider" for purposes of certain job-protected leave laws; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Modifies the definition of "health care provider" used in Oregon job-protected leave laws; the text does not say whether eligibility widens or narrows.

title: Relating to abuse of vulnerable persons.
summary: Expands who can sue for abuse of vulnerable persons, adds under-18s to that definition, and applies child-abuse limitation periods to those claims.

title: Relating to mental health services for individuals with disabilities; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends the ban on denying mental health services to people with intellectual or developmental disabilities to all public bodies and all such individuals.

title: Relating to redesignating resource lands for nonresource use.
summary: Limits how farm, forest, and mixed-use resource lands may be rezoned for nonresource uses.

title: Relating to rights of recipients of child welfare services.
summary: Gives certain foster and adopted children rights to sibling contact and life-history records, and lets DHS redirect subsidy payments when direct support ends.

title: Relating to public employer policies regarding language pay differentials.
summary: Requires public employers' pay policies to give sign language skills the same extra-pay differential already offered for other bilingual or multilingual skills.

title: Relating to executive appointments.
summary: Requires the Governor to appoint a new agency head within three months after the Senate fails to confirm a reappointment.

title: Relating to dogs harming livestock.
summary: Expands the definition of 'potentially dangerous dog' for dog control to include dogs that seriously injure or kill livestock.

title: Relating to the use of mechanical restraints on certain young people; declaring an emergency.
summary: Prohibits certain mechanical restraints on youth, adjudicated youth and young persons in detention and youth correction facilities; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the application of abbreviated school day program requirements to students who are enrolled in a public charter school; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Exempts students in public charter schools from abbreviated school day program requirements when certain conditions are met, effective on passage.

title: Relating to investigations of child abuse involving the child's parent; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Exempts parents from abuse-of-a-child-in-care provisions and requires DHS to tell parents its employees are not attorneys.

title: Relating to middle housing land division; declaring an emergency.
summary: Expands the notice radius for proposed middle housing land divisions and requires additional content in those notices.

title: Relating to waiver of tuition for qualified students.
summary: Changes the age limit and required time in foster care for foster children to qualify for state college tuition waivers.

title: Relating to long term care oversight.
summary: Tightens oversight of residential care facilities and adult foster homes, adding licensing requirements and notice duties, while allowing two-year licenses for consistently compliant adult foster homes.

title: Relating to determinations of navigability on Oregon waterways.
summary: Lets the Department of State Lands claim state interest in submerged lands of navigable waterways, negotiate with owners, convey mineral rights, and apply accretion and avulsion principles.

title: Relating to persons from whom assets were seized by the state when the persons were under 21 years of age; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates a DHS grant program to repay former foster youth whose benefits were seized by the state while in its care.

title: Relating to foster parent compensation.
summary: Requires DHS to report every even-numbered year to legislative committees on compensation for foster home providers and proctor foster homes.

title: Relating to electronic meetings to discuss an abbreviated school day program placement; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Allows parents or foster parents to hold and consent to initial meetings about abbreviated school day placements by phone or electronically.

title: Relating to records of interviews in child abuse investigations.
summary: Requires DHS and law enforcement to electronically record certain interviews with suspected child abusers during child abuse investigations.

title: Relating to intestate estates.
summary: Requires petitioners in intestate estates to make reasonable efforts to locate higher-priority persons before a personal representative is appointed.

title: Relating to the frequency of meetings regarding abbreviated school day programs for students who are terminally ill; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Lets parents or foster parents of seriously ill students request annual, not more frequent, reviews of abbreviated school day programs; declares an emergency.

title: Relating to the use of outside counsel by the Department of Justice; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to report annually to legislative committees on its use of outside counsel to defend state agencies.

title: Relating to the application of fertilizer.
summary: Requires owners of 200+ irrigated agricultural acres to report annual fertilizer application data to the state, with civil penalties for violations.

title: Relating to unemployment insurance.
summary: Allows drug testing for certain unemployment claimants, disqualifies those who fail until they pass a retest, and has the Employment Department pay for tests.

title: Relating to participatory budgeting when preparing a school district budget; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a sunsetting pilot program letting students participate in preparing a school district budget, administered by the Department of Education.

title: Relating to wildfire hazard requirements for nonurban dwellings.
summary: Removes wildfire hazard requirements for building accessory dwelling units on rural residential land and replacement dwellings on resource land.

title: Relating to the payment schedule for state employees; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Directs DAS to pilot biweekly pay for State Police employees and report to an interim committee by September 15, 2027.

title: Relating to retirement of public safety workers; declaring an emergency.
summary: Creates a task force studying health insurance for retired police and firefighters, and directs PERB to define those job titles for benefits.

title: Relating to statewide economic development plans.
summary: Directs Business Oregon to review other states' economic development plans and report recommendations for an Oregon statewide economic development plan.

title: Relating to rail.
summary: Directs ODOT to plan rail operation and funding with Washington and British Columbia, and report biennially to the Joint Committee on Transportation.

title: Relating to penalties for failure to comply with certain requirements under the laws governing public employee collective bargaining.
summary: Creates penalties for public employers that violate collective bargaining rules and lets unions sue for late employee information.

title: Relating to security in schools.
summary: Directs DPSST to study placing police officers or security guards in schools and report findings by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to blood pressure cuffs for medical assistance recipients.
summary: Requires OHA and coordinated care organizations to reimburse the cost of clinically validated blood pressure cuffs prescribed to Medicaid recipients.

title: Relating to the salary of chaplains under the Public Employees Retirement System.
summary: Requires a housing allowance for OHSU chaplains to be counted as taxable income when calculating OPSRP pension salary, and orders a PERS study.

title: Relating to the application of a prevailing rate of wage to offsite custom work for use in public works; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Extends the prevailing wage requirement to certain off-site custom work made to specifications for a particular public works project.

title: Relating to the funding of infrastructure projects.
summary: Directs Business Oregon to study using a loan loss reserve fund for infrastructure projects in underserved communities and report to the legislature by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to groundwater permit requirements for small agricultural parcels.
summary: Directs the Water Resources Department to study groundwater permit requirements for small agricultural parcels and report to legislative committees by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to fire safety systems in public buildings; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Requires public building owners to test and inspect fire and smoke dampers and smoke control systems, imposes civil penalties, and mandates worker benefits on related repair contracts funded by public money.

title: Relating to the Walla Walla basin.
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Allows the Water Resources Department to approve temporary leases of Walla Walla basin water rights for instream use and appropriates General Fund money for basin projects; sunsets 2030.

title: Relating to the repeal of the corporate activity tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Repeals Oregon's corporate activity tax for tax years beginning January 1, 2026, effective 91 days after sine die adjournment.

title: Relating to the unlawful disclosure of information about crime victims.
summary: Creates a crime for health care providers who unlawfully disclose information about sexual assault or sex trafficking victims, with escalating fines and jail terms.

title: Relating to estate tax treatment of family-owned business; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Excludes interests in family-owned businesses from the taxable estate for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Relating to the use of meat.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Allows people who take nuisance game mammals to keep, give away, donate, or otherwise dispose of the meat as permitted by rule.

title: Relating to minimum wage.
summary: Caps the percentage by which the state minimum wage can be adjusted for inflation.

title: Relating to instruction on the prevention of sex trafficking of children; declaring an emergency.
summary: Requires every school district board to teach and adopt a curriculum on preventing child sex trafficking, effective July 1, 2025.

title: Relating to agricultural research.
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Requires the state to match donations of $10,000 or more to the OSU Foundation for cereal grain agricultural research, subject to available funds, and appropriates money for it.

title: Relating to county elections concerning methods of taking wildlife; providing for criminal sentence reduction that requires approval by a two-thirds majority.
summary: Allows counties to permit hunting cougars with dogs if county voters approve, exempting them from the state ban.

title: Relating to home occupations on resource lands.
summary: Describes which home occupations are allowed on forest- and farm-zoned lands, which appears to permit work from homes on resource lands.

title: Relating to estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Repeals the Oregon estate tax, while also limiting it to decedents dying on or before January 1, 2025, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to funding for rodeo repairs.
summary: Creates a grant program through the Oregon Business Development Department for capital repairs at rodeos in communities of 12,000 or fewer.

title: Relating to tribal health.
summary: Creates a tuition-and-fees scholarship for Indian health students tied to tribal service commitments and appropriates funds to OHSU to administer it.

title: Relating to assaults committed against corrections officers.
summary: Creates a mandatory minimum 48-month prison sentence for inmates who assault corrections officers.

title: Relating to the release of booking photos.
summary: Lets law enforcement release a person's booking photo after a second arrest within 12 months, or when the person is a missing person.

title: Relating to ground water data accountability.
summary: Requires that ground water data used or generated by four state agencies undergo peer review.

title: Relating to predator management in drought-stricken regions; declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs Fish and Wildlife to conduct predator control in drought-affected wildlife management units and herd ranges, funded by a General Fund appropriation.

title: Relating to the depredation of livestock.
summary: Caps wolf depredation livestock and working-dog payments at $25,000 per animal, removes missing-livestock compensation, and adds county and agency reporting.

title: Relating to reimbursement rates for air ambulance services.
summary: Requires OHA and coordinated care organizations to reimburse air ambulance services for Medicaid recipients using the national Ambulance Inflation Factor.

title: Relating to providing for the mental health needs of the agricultural workforce; declaring an emergency.
summary: Appropriates General Fund money to support operation of the AgriStress Helpline for Oregon's agricultural workforce's mental health needs.

title: Relating to replacement dwellings.
summary: Caps the size of replacement dwellings allowed on forest and farm zoned land.

title: Relating to allocations to the County Fair Account.
summary: Removes the annual inflation-adjusted $1.53 million cap on allocations from the Economic Development Fund to the County Fair Account.

title: Relating to the acquisition of bank assets by a credit union.
summary: Keeps receipts from a bank business portfolio acquired by a credit union subject to Oregon's corporate excise and activity taxes.

title: Relating to behavioral health deflection programs.
summary: Raises the grant funding counties may receive for behavioral health deflection programs, including the minimum grant amount.

title: Relating to deputy district attorneys.
summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to study state funding of deputy district attorney salaries and report by September 15, 2026.

title: Relating to dual credit programs.
summary: Adds agriculture, forestry and natural resources programs to the statewide standards for dual credit programs.

title: Relating to an agriculture education scholarship.
summary: Creates an Agriculture Education Scholarship Program giving grants to students training to become high school agriculture teachers, and appropriates funds to HECC.

title: Relating to academic credits at public institutions of higher education.
summary: Requires public colleges to award credit for certain high school courses and programs, and bars requiring some students to take intro communications courses as prerequisites.

title: Relating to participation in athletic competitions according to biological sex.
summary: Requires school sports to be designated by biological sex and bars biological males from female-designated athletic competitions and extracurricular sports, with private causes of action.

title: Relating to events on lands zoned for exclusive farm use in eastern Oregon.
summary: Allows farm-zoned (EFU) land east of the Cascades to host weddings and other events.

title: Relating to the Oregon Board of Psychology; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Lets the Oregon Board of Psychology charge costs of disciplinary action to the person disciplined, effective 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to the regulation of dwellings on resource lands.
summary: Bans homes not used for farm or forest purposes in sensitive or unsuitable areas of farm and forest-zoned resource lands.

title: Relating to the Oregon Advocacy Commissions Office.
summary: Renames the head of the Oregon Advocacy Commissions Office from Administrator to executive director, with no other change.

title: Relating to insurance for unmanned aircraft systems; prescribing an effective date; providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
summary: Requires commercial drone operators to carry liability insurance and taxes those premiums, with revenue going to an advanced air mobility program.

title: Relating to aviation.
summary: Lets the Oregon Department of Aviation set airport and aircraft fees by rule, with inflation adjustments.

title: Relating to easements on state land; and declaring an emergency.
summary: Directs the Department of State Lands to set application fees and compensation rates for easements on state land within the territorial sea.

title: Relating to the Oregon Public Guardian and Conservator; prescribing an effective date.
summary: Modifies the Oregon Public Guardian and Conservator's duties and powers to provide services and supports to certain persons; takes effect 91 days after sine die.

title: Relating to marine cleanup; and prescribing an effective date.
summary: Creates an abandoned-vessel offense with a $2,000 maximum fine, expands derelict-vessel possession offense, and lets agencies remove marine debris without notice.

title: Relating to Oregon Board of Accountancy scholarships; and declaring an emergency.
