summary: Expands access to academic reengagement opportunities for eligible students, though the bill text is brief and lacks detail.

title: Military families/education
summary: Aims to promote educational stability for children of military families, but the text gives no specific provisions.

title: Homes for heroes program
summary: Creates a Homes for Heroes pilot offering no-interest down payment and closing cost loans, up to $15 million, to eligible workers and veterans.

title: Cosmetology compact
summary: Establishes the Cosmetology Licensure Compact, letting licensed cosmetologists practice across state lines with a multistate license, and creates a multistate commission.

title: St. Edward state park
summary: Extends the maximum lease term at Saint Edward State Park from 62 to 80 years and removes the limit confining leases to specific buildings and nearby property.

title: LTSS trust exemptions
summary: Reopens the window for employees who bought long-term care insurance to be exempt from the state long-term services and supports trust program.

title: LTSS trust spousal benefits
summary: Allows spouses to share benefits under the long-term services and supports trust program.

title: Housing of inmates
summary: Concerns how inmates are housed in state correctional facilities; the title gives no specific change.

title: Child exposure to violence
topics: Children and families; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Updates definitions for child forensic interviews and children's advocacy centers, and allows confidential peer review of recordings of closed child abuse cases.

title: 3D-printed buildings
summary: Concerns 3D-printed building construction, but the provided text gives no specific requirements or changes.

title: Counted ballot audits
summary: Ends several existing election audits and lets counties choose between a limited hand-count audit or a risk-limiting audit.

title: School facility temperatures
summary: Aims to mitigate rising temperatures in school facilities caused by climate change; the summary gives no specific mechanism.

title: School district elections
summary: If voters approve a constitutional amendment, school districts could issue capital bonds, levy taxes to repay them, and exceed debt limits by simple majority.

title: Child care local licensing
topics: Children and families; Government and administration
summary: Lets counties adopt ordinances to license and regulate child care centers and family homes instead of DCYF, effective no sooner than July 2026, with reporting requirements.

title: Nonopioid drugs for pain
summary: Concerns nonopioid drugs for treating pain; the summary gives no detail on what the bill changes.

title: Higher ed. traumatic stress
summary: Requires public colleges and universities to publish secondary traumatic stress resources and adopt model workplace mental health policies with workforce committees.

title: Labor trustees/colleges
summary: Requires college boards of trustees to include labor and business members, and restricts who may serve on university and Evergreen boards.

title: PFD formation
summary: Lets cities and counties form public facilities districts by interlocal agreement, with a governing board and an ex officio treasurer.

title: Gender/health providers
summary: Prohibits puberty-blocking medications, cross-sex hormones, and gender transition surgeries for minors.

title: Gov. services/tribal lands
summary: Lets a federally recognized tribe and an adjoining city agree, through 2028, to extend urban governmental services to abutting tribal property outside city limits.

title: Rental income/property tax
summary: Lets seniors and disabled homeowners deduct up to $6,000 in primary-residence rental income from the property tax exemption income test, makes the preference permanent, and excludes short-term rentals.

title: Replacement tires
summary: Aims to improve consumer choices of replacement tires, but the text gives no specific rule changes.

title: County treasurer costs
summary: Authorizes county treasurers to charge taxing districts a capped cost recovery fee for property tax billing, collection, and distribution, credited to a county account.

title: Commute trip reduction
summary: Reduces the per-employer cap on the Commute Trip Reduction tax credit available to businesses.

title: County REET admin. fees
summary: Raises the county fee on real estate excise tax affidavits from $5 to $20, with inflation adjustments, and splits the revenue between county assessor and treasurer administrative funds.

title: Uniformed personnel
summary: Adds small-city and small-county law enforcement officers to the definition of uniformed personnel, giving them interest arbitration rights.

title: Motor vehicle damage/rescue
summary: Grants civil immunity to people who forcibly enter a locked vehicle to rescue a vulnerable person or domestic animal in imminent danger.

title: Fire district equip. taxes
summary: Exempts sales and use tax on fire and emergency medical equipment purchased by fire districts in rural counties with population of 10,000 or less.

title: Rangeland fire pilot
summary: Creates a 2026-2029 DNR pilot in Eastern Washington letting rangeland fire protection associations form outside fire district boundaries.

title: Sexual assault nurses
summary: Aims to increase the availability of sexual assault nurse examiners; the text gives no mechanism or funding details.

title: Naval Academy license plates
summary: Creates a Naval Academy special license plate with original and renewal fees, directing proceeds to the Veterans Stewardship Account for veterans and their families.

title: IEP team meetings/recording
topics: AI and technology; Children and families
summary: Lets parents or guardians audio record their student's IEP team meetings and requires other team members to comply with the Washington Privacy Act.

title: Hate crime offense
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Expands the hate crime offense to cover acts committed, in whole or part, because of the perceived protected characteristic of another person.

title: Juvenile access to attorney
summary: Concerns juvenile access to an attorney; the text provided gives no detail on the specific change.

title: County ferry contracts
summary: Allows county ferry maintenance or repair unit-priced contracts to run up to 10 years.

title: Transparency ombuds study
summary: Titled as a study of a transparency ombuds, with a stated goal of enhancing public records access; no operative provisions are given.

title: Law enf. misconduct
summary: Authorizes the Attorney General to investigate and sue local police and corrections agencies for state law violations and requires a model accountability policy.

title: Access to federal funds
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Directs Commerce to help applicants win federal economic development grants, creates a MATCHED account for state matching funds, and requires reporting on the program.

title: Freight railroad infra.
summary: Creates B&O and public utility tax credits for freight railroad construction and maintenance, plus a sales tax exemption for track maintenance materials, with a $8 million annual credit cap.

title: Industrial insurance/duties
summary: Changes duties of industrial insurance self-insured employers and third-party administrators; the summary gives no specific direction.

title: Newspaper tax preference
summary: Requires businesses claiming the newspaper B&O tax exemption to file annual reports, and imposes back tax and interest if they are ineligible or fail to file.

title: Residential parking
summary: Lets cities and counties allow residents to park across their own driveway entrance, if sidewalks, other driveways and the roadway stay unobstructed.

title: Biomarker testing coverage
summary: Requires health coverage for biomarker testing, according to a one-line title; full bill text is not provided.

title: Earned wage access services
summary: Requires earned wage access providers to be licensed and regulated by DFI, with new obligations, prohibited acts, and enforcement duties.

title: System improvement team
summary: Makes the Interagency, Multijurisdictional System Improvement Team permanent and requires a biennial report to the Legislature starting November 1, 2026.

title: Family burial grounds
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration; Housing
summary: Creates private family burial grounds on owner-designated land with setback, consent and recording rules, exempts them from cemetery licensing, and lets cities and counties regulate them.

title: Regulated substance use data
summary: Creates a data dashboard to track use of regulated substances. The text gives no rules, funding, or enforcement details.

title: Cannabis/dept of agriculture
summary: Transfers cannabis production, processing, and testing licensing and regulation from the Liquor and Cannabis Board to the Department of Agriculture, along with records, property, and appropriations.

title: DOC WMS employee arbitration
summary: Grants Washington Management Service employees in the Department of Corrections interest arbitration rights.

title: Supp. retirement bargaining
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Makes DOC employees' supplemental retirement contributions, including medical plans, a mandatory bargaining subject but excludes them from interest arbitration.

title: PTSD/correctional workers
summary: Creates a rebuttable presumption that PTSD is an occupational disease for correctional facility workers, making workers' compensation claims easier to bring.

title: Recycling rates
summary: Requires producers of covered plastic packaging and paper products to register with Ecology starting March 1, 2026, with exemptions for government, nonprofits, and de minimis sellers.

title: Health care services
summary: States an intent to preserve access to protected health care services; the text gives no operative provisions.

title: National guard retention
summary: Directs the Adjutant General to study National Guard retention needs and set bonus criteria, and requires a triennial report to the Legislature.

title: Hit & run/first-time waiver
summary: Makes hit and run resulting in death ineligible for the first-time offender waiver, so those offenders cannot receive that sentencing alternative.

title: Affordable housing financing
summary: Removes the 15%-of-area-median-income rent cap for for-profit-owned PHA-financed housing, instead requiring units be affordable to households at or below 80% AMI.

title: Health technology assessment
summary: Changes Washington's health technology assessment process to prioritize treatments with Medicare access, weigh rare-disease trial evidence, and require published decisions and written explanations.

title: IUD pain control options
summary: Requires providers under the Uniform Disciplinary Act to tell patients seeking IUD placement or removal about available pain control options when scheduling.

title: Pet insurance
summary: Concerns pet insurance, but the provided text does not state any specific change to the rules.

title: Remote testing
summary: Lets online school districts offer remote statewide testing from 2027-28 and requires OSPI to create or update testing security policies and rules.

title: Lodging fee disclosure
summary: Requires hotels and short-term rentals to include all fees and taxes in advertised prices, with civil penalties for violations, capped at $1,000 for small owners.

title: Solicited real estate
summary: Gives owners of off-market property solicited for purchase a right to a licensed appraisal, notice of that right, and penalty-free contract cancellation.

title: Child care provider qualif.
summary: Concerns qualifications for child care providers; the text does not say whether requirements would be added, loosened or changed.

title: Aircraft fuel tax distrib.
summary: Changes how revenue from the aircraft fuel tax is distributed; the text does not specify the new allocation.

title: Unleaded aircraft fuel/tax
summary: Creates state tax exemptions for unleaded aircraft fuel, reducing the tax paid on that fuel.

title: School safety/penalties
summary: Expands assault-type interference offenses to cover school employees, students and officials at extracurricular athletics, raises penalties, and allows student exclusions and required signage.

title: Motor vehicle chop shops
summary: Concerning motor vehicle chop shops; the text gives no detail on what the bill changes.

title: Criminal endangerment
summary: Expands the crime of endangerment with a controlled substance to cover fentanyl and other high-potency synthetic opioids.

title: Residential landlord-tenant
summary: Creates a task force to prepare revisions to the landlord-tenant act and imposes a moratorium on new residential landlord-tenant regulations.

title: Eviction reform
summary: Makes unspecified eviction reforms and tenant safety changes; the text gives no details of what changes.

title: Contraceptive coverage
summary: Extends the existing 12-month contraceptive supply requirement to all contraceptive prescriptions, not just refills.

title: SVP supervision credit
summary: Bars sexually violent predators under concurrent less-restrictive alternative supervision from earning supervision compliance credit on other causes.

title: Children/controlled sub.
summary: Bill on children and controlled substances; the text is too thin to determine what it changes.

title: Massage therapy coverage
summary: Requires Washington's medical assistance plans to cover massage therapy, expanding the publicly funded services available to enrollees.

title: Social services/property tax
summary: Exempts nonsectarian nonprofit-owned property from property tax when leased to a government, tribe, or nonprofit for social services.

title: Law enforcement funding
summary: Lets counties and cities impose a 0.10% sales tax for law enforcement, at least half for commissioned officers, phased in by population from 2026 to 2028.

title: Lot splitting
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration; Housing
summary: Requires cities to allow administrative lot splits creating one new buildable lot, limits local review and density caps, and exempts ordinances from SEPA appeal.

title: Gov. services beyond UGA
summary: Allows urban sewer and other governmental services to extend into rural areas in four specified circumstances, including failing septic systems and nearby existing lines.

title: County local roads
summary: Creates a county local road trust account within the Motor Vehicle Fund, restricting its money to county local road preservation and program administration.

title: Tenant assistance program
summary: Creates a tenant assistance program; the text gives no details on eligibility, funding, or tenant rights.

title: Local sales and use tax
summary: Creates a local sales and use tax; the text is a one-line title with no further details.

title: Vehicular homicide offenses
summary: Designates vehicular homicide as a violent offense in all circumstances and removes reckless-driving vehicular homicide from the most serious offenses list.

title: Veteran support and services
summary: Expands veterans service officer eligibility and prioritization, requires WDVA outreach to discharged veterans, and adds biennial reporting on veterans' services.

title: Unwanted calls & texts
summary: Tightens telemarketing and commercial text rules: broader 'person' definition, narrower business-to-business exemption, and a ban on commercial texts to registered Washington cell numbers.

title: Professional engineers' reg.
summary: Revises Washington professional engineer and land surveyor registration rules, including Board membership, experience credit, application verification, fees, and certificate validity.

title: DOC employee bargaining
summary: Exempts certain Department of Corrections employees with interest arbitration rights from coalition bargaining, letting them negotiate a separate master contract.

title: Disabled veterans/prop. tax
summary: Lowers the service-connected disability rating needed for disabled veterans' property tax exemption from 80 percent to 40 percent, starting in 2027.

title: Fashion environmental impact
summary: Addresses environmental impacts of the fashion industry, but the text does not say what the bill would require or change.

title: Housing cost task force
summary: Directs WSIPP to study the primary cost drivers for homeownership and rental housing and report findings to the Legislature by December 1, 2026.

title: Public facilities districts
summary: Extends the maximum period for two local sales and use taxes that finance public facilities district regional centers and theaters from 40 to 55 years.

title: DUI conviction vacation
summary: Allows people to vacate (set aside) prior driving under the influence convictions.

title: Early release petitions
summary: Changes early release petition rules for people convicted of crimes before 18, adds a 70-petition annual cap through 2035, and authorizes DOC rental vouchers.

title: Judges pro tempore/residency
summary: Removes the requirement that municipal judges pro tempore in cities over 400,000 reside in the city where the court sits.

title: Misdemeanor dismissal
summary: Allows courts to continue certain misdemeanor cases up to 12 months with conditions, then dismiss charges if the defendant substantially complies.

title: Respiratory care compact
summary: Establishes an interstate compact letting licensed respiratory care practitioners practice across member states under a compact privilege, administered by a commission.

title: Recording fees/escrow tax
summary: Excludes escrow-collected county recording fees from retail sales tax and business and occupation tax when separately itemized on closing documents.

title: Election day
summary: Encourages governments and educational and cultural groups to recognize Election Day and hold educational programming.

title: Motor vehicle emissions
summary: Removes state authority to adopt California motor vehicle emissions standards, aiming to cut administrative burden and generate transportation revenue.

title: Firearm rights restoration
summary: Lets certain people with specified felony drug convictions petition superior court to restore firearm rights, and sets filing venue rules.

title: Supervision compliance
summary: Limits supervision compliance credits: people sanctioned for community custody noncompliance lose credit eligibility, and those on conditional commutation or certain sentencing alternatives are excluded.

title: School staff salary alloc.
summary: Determines how the state allocates funding for school staff salaries.

title: Work restrictions/age 16, 17
summary: Requires L&I rules to let 16- and 17-year-old students in career/technical or college programs work school-year hours matching vacation limits.

title: Student mobile device use
summary: Restricts mobile device use by public school students, adding limits on phone use during the school setting.

title: Health carrier reimbursement
summary: Caps and sets floors on hospital reimbursement rates in state employee benefit plan contracts, with tighter caps starting 2029.

title: Prescribing psychologists
summary: Establishes a prescribing psychologist certification in Washington, creating a credential pathway for psychologists to prescribe.

title: Sentence modification
summary: Creates a process letting many felons serving prison terms petition for sentence modification based on age, time served, medical condition, and rehabilitation.

title: Local tax rate changes
summary: Requires local governments to notify the DOR in writing of sales tax rate changes, with ordinance copies, annexation documents, and bond retirement dates.

title: Unclaimed property
summary: Modifies provisions of the revised uniform unclaimed property act, which governs how abandoned property is held and returned.

title: Child care workforce board
summary: Creates a 10-member Child Care Workforce Standards Board to recommend improvements to child care worker employment standards, with reports made public.

title: Fertility-related services
summary: Addresses health plan coverage of fertility-related services; the text does not say whether it adds or removes coverage requirements.

title: Dev. disabilities waiver use
summary: Directs DDA to prioritize specific populations for enrollment in open home and community-based waiver slots and publish related data.

title: Clemency and pardons
summary: Expands the Clemency and Pardons Board to 10 members, adds expedited review and immigration-blind pardon eligibility, and requires DOC supervision of conditionally commuted sentences.

title: Bulk firearm purchases
summary: Prohibits firearm dealers from delivering more than one firearm or set ammunition amounts per purchaser within 30 days, with exceptions; violations risk license forfeiture.

title: Sexually violent predators
summary: Lets prosecutors and the Attorney General compel relevant records, including from public agencies, to decide SVP civil commitment petitions, and bars earning supervision credit on concurrent less-restrictive alternatives.

title: Schools/resource conserv.
summary: Promotes resource conservation practices in public schools; the text gives no details on specific requirements or funding.

title: Local government planning
summary: Requires local governments to amend noncompliant planning provisions before the Growth Management Hearings Board can find them compliant with the GMA.

title: Student navigational support
summary: Replaces the FAFSA/WASFA outreach pilot with a subject-to-appropriation program using specialists to help high schools in low-completion regions file financial aid applications.

title: DOC discipline
summary: Limits DOC administrative segregation, adds notice and oversight requirements, bars losing programming solely due to segregation, and requires annual reporting.

title: Criminal interview practices
summary: Presumes statements obtained through officer deception in interrogations inadmissible, and requires CJTC to offer evidence-based interrogation training starting July 2026.

title: Unlawful firearm possession
summary: Raises penalties for unlawful firearm possession by reranking offenses to higher seriousness levels, increasing offender-score points for prior firearm convictions, and requiring warrantless arrests.

title: K-12 scholarship program
summary: Creates the EmpowerED Scholarship Program, an education savings account system letting parents of K-12 students use state-provided funds for qualifying educational expenses.

title: Ag. cannabis workers
summary: Creates collective bargaining rights for cannabis farm workers, with PERC administering union recognition, elections, and bargaining obligations.

title: In-home care training
summary: Aligns training requirements and certification exemptions for family members providing in-home long-term care across consumer-directed, agency, and WA Cares pathways.

title: College grant award amounts

title: Voting in jails, hospitals
summary: Improves voting access and removes barriers for people held in jails and state hospitals.

title: Civic engage./state custody
summary: Supports civic engagement for incarcerated and institutionalized people in state custody to promote inclusion and rehabilitation.

title: Youth athletics/sales tax
summary: Exempts goods and services provided by youth athletic facilities from state sales and use tax.

title: Cruelty to animals
summary: Modifies enforcement and criminal penalties for violations of Washington animal cruelty laws; the direction of the change is not stated.

title: Solid waste management
summary: Requires paper and packaging producers to join a producer responsibility organization that must develop and finance a statewide recycling program, with fees paid to Ecology.

title: Ninth grade success grants
summary: Creates a ninth grade success grant program; the summary gives no detail on eligibility, amounts, or funding.

title: Firearm storage
summary: Requires locked, concealed, unloaded storage of firearms in vehicles and secure storage in residences, with graded penalties for violations.

title: Urban forest management
summary: Concerns urban forest management ordinances; the short text does not say what changes.

title: Solid waste handling
summary: Requires Ecology to review and approve landfill permits and sets procedures for Ecology to take over enforcement from local health districts.

title: Noncompetition agreements
summary: Makes all noncompetition covenants void and unenforceable, regardless of when the parties entered into them.

title: Volunteer firefighters/DCP
summary: Allows volunteer firefighters whose agencies joined the state deferred compensation program to choose to participate in it.

title: Vital records family access
summary: Adds great-grandchildren to the family members who may qualify to obtain certified birth or death certificates.

title: Community inclusion services
summary: Requires DSHS to contract directly with providers for developmental disability community inclusion services, sets standards, and limits billing and ratio rules.

title: Control. subst. endangerment
summary: Concerns the crime of endangerment involving a controlled substance; the summary gives no details on what changes.

title: Veteran employability
summary: Creates a subject-to-appropriations program at the community and technical college board to give justice-involved veterans job-readiness and transitional training.

title: Health care work violence
summary: Requires health care settings to investigate every workplace violence incident promptly and to review and update their violence prevention plans at least yearly.

title: Firearm purchase
summary: Requires a state permit to purchase firearms before dealer transfers, adds background-check delays and denials for warrants and open charges, and expands record requirements to all transfers.

title: Urban growth area boundaries
summary: Requires cities and counties to expand urban growth area boundaries to include qualifying residential parcels, authorize matching density, and allow urban service connections.

title: Property tax exemptions

title: DOC reentry education
summary: Creates a DOC education act allowing prisoners to own laptops, get Wi-Fi access, take approved distance courses, and qualify for financial aid.

title: Maritime careers task force
summary: Requires a temporary career and technical education task force to recommend pathways into Coast Guard-approved maritime postsecondary programs.

title: Artificial intelligence info
summary: Requires developers to post training-data documentation before releasing generative AI systems publicly, with Attorney General enforcement and daily civil penalties.

title: Fabricated depictions/minors
summary: Creates or revises criminal offenses involving fabricated depictions of minors, likely covering AI-generated or synthetic child sexual imagery.

title: Mandated reporting/higher ed
summary: Makes attorneys employed by higher education institutions, and their supervised staff, mandatory reporters of child abuse and neglect, excluding client-representation information.

title: Fire district civil service
summary: Concerns civil service systems for fire protection districts; the summary gives no detail on what changes.

title: Small businesses/residential
summary: Requires cities to allow neighborhood stores and cafés in residential zones, with local parking, hour and size rules permitted.

title: Health care/minors
summary: Aims for greater consistency in health care services provided to minors under 17; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Child welfare housing assist

title: Property tax value freeze
summary: Provides a property tax valuation freeze for senior citizens and disabled veterans.

title: Sex offender failure to reg.

title: Labor standards
summary: Amends labor standards and the Washington minimum wage act; the text provided does not state the specific changes.

title: Parks & rec./interest arb.

summary: Grants interest arbitration rights to Parks and Recreation Commission employees, excluding confidential employees and internal auditors.

title: Building codes
summary: Requires GMA cities and counties to allow insulated exterior walls to project 8 inches into setbacks, exceed roof height by 8 inches, and measure floor area from interior wall faces.

title: Overtime exemption
summary: Creates a narrow exemption from state overtime requirements for certain nonprofits and small businesses.

title: Correctional industries comm
summary: Adds two governor-appointed voting members with lived experience from underrepresented populations to the Correctional Industries Advisory Committee.

title: Medication dispensing
summary: Allows hospitals and health care entities to dispense more than 48- or 72-hour drug supplies in specified situations and bars separate billing for those supplies.

title: Delayed ambulance bills

title: School volunteers/conviction
summary: Requires schools to let parents with expunged, pardoned, or restored convictions show rehabilitation or innocence documents, barring denial on those convictions, and sets evaluation and notice procedures.

title: UW health sciences library
summary: Grants psychological associates and mental health counselor associates access to the UW health sciences HEAL-WA library.

title: Manufactured home titles
summary: Lets manufactured home owners with an individual interest in their park apply to DOL to remove or waive the home's vehicle title.

title: DOC disciplinary hearings
summary: Lowers the standard of proof for DOC disciplinary hearings on community custody and partial confinement violations to preponderance of the evidence, and requires DOC rulemaking.

title: Child welfare workers
summary: Increases protections for child welfare workers; the text gives no further detail on how.

summary: Requires cities and counties under the GMA to allow STEP housing in residential and commercial zones, review permits administratively, and face Commerce enforcement with revenue withholding.

summary: Narrows voting disqualification for criminal convictions to death-eligible crimes, automatically restores voting rights for most others, and lets more people hold state and local office.

title: Insurance code violations
summary: Lets the insurance commissioner order regulated persons to pay restitution with 8% interest to those owed money, within 30 days.

title: DD parental caregivers
summary: Directs DDA to seek federal approval to let parents of minors with developmental disabilities be paid for extraordinary personal care under DDA waivers.

title: Emergency shelters/pets
summary: Requires local emergency plans to identify pet-friendly shelters and coshelters, set safety procedures for animal sheltering, and post companion animal preparedness information online.

title: State gen. obligation bonds
summary: Authorizes the State Finance Committee to issue up to $4.9 billion in general obligation bonds for capital projects and related debt payments.

title: Tobacco & nicotine products
summary: Bans retail sale, display and advertising of flavored tobacco, nicotine, vapor and entertainment vapor products starting 2026, with required signage and DOH prevention campaign.

title: Senior shared housing
summary: Bars landlords under the MHLTA from prohibiting tenants age 55 or older from having a roommate, including homesharing arrangements, and requires written notice of this right.

title: Forged digital likeness

title: Salmon recovery projects
summary: Makes the habitat recovery pilot permanent as a permit pathway for salmon restoration projects, streamlining permit applications and cultural resource review.

title: Sodium nitrite

summary: Extends the completion deadline for certain clean energy facilities receiving urban tax preferences and adds labor compliance, prevailing wage, and apprenticeship verification requirements.

summary: Requires cities to allow child care centers as outright permitted uses in all zones except industrial, with phased implementation deadlines.

title: Natural death act/pregnancy

title: Capital budget
summary: Makes supplemental capital budget appropriations for the 2023-25 fiscal biennium.

title: Residential tenants
summary: Caps annual rent increases for residential and manufactured-home tenancies at CPI-based limits, bars first-year increases, and exempts several housing types, until 2040.

title: Competency eval. & restor.
summary: Revises competency restoration rules: limits forced restoration for some nonfelony defendants, loosens outpatient eligibility, expands forensic navigator duties, and sets involuntary medication hearing procedures.

title: Interbranch advisory comm.
summary: Extends an interbranch advisory committee to 2031, adds a judicial member, and restores staff support and meeting-schedule provisions previously vetoed.

title: Behavioral health/assaults
summary: Addresses the appropriate response to assaults committed by people in behavioral health crisis; the summary does not specify changes.

title: Gubernatorial proclamations
summary: Increases legislative involvement in the governor's proclamations declaring a state of emergency.

title: Gambling commission/PRA
summary: Exempts proprietary financial and security information submitted to the gambling commission from public inspection and copying.

title: Voter challenges
summary: Modifies forms, processes, and adjudication methods for voter registration challenges to limit frivolous claims.

title: Working families' tax credit
summary: Modifies the working families' tax credit to improve claim collection and raise participation through data-sharing agreements.

title: Budgeting process
summary: Reforms the state budget process by prioritizing essential spending, limiting spending and revenue proposals, and requiring accountability for state dollars.

title: Transportation budget, supp.
summary: Makes supplemental transportation budget appropriations for the 2023-2025 fiscal biennium.

summary: Appropriates $15.2 billion for the 2025-27 biennium to state transportation agencies, including WSDOT, debt service, the State Patrol, and the Department of Licensing.

title: Toxicology testing
summary: Concerns toxicology testing performed by certified or accredited laboratories; the summary gives no details of any change.

title: Persistent offenders
summary: Provides for resentencing of individuals who were sentenced as persistent offenders; the text gives no details on the change.

title: Disability insurer filings
summary: Requires experience-rated group disability insurers to file detailed rating formulas and credibility factors so the insurance commissioner can replicate premiums.

title: Public school starting times
summary: Expresses support for exploring and implementing later start times for public schools.

title: Private detention facilities
summary: Modifies operational standards for certain private detention facilities and lets the Department of Health inspect them and take enforcement action against noncompliant ones.

title: Work programs/incarceration
summary: Makes incarcerated people's work program participation voluntary, bars punishment for refusing, and requires pay for participants in Class I-IV programs.

summary: Lets either an advanced social worker or an independent clinical social worker fill a required seat on the counselors and social workers advisory committee, and limits the office ban to governing roles.

title: GMA housing element
summary: Requires Commerce to review local housing elements and development regulations for GMA compliance before they take effect, with appeals to the GMHB.

title: Littering, penalty increase
summary: Increases penalties for littering violations.

title: Energy facility site eval.

summary: Adds public hearings and approval standards for energy facility siting, requires considering preempting local land use rules, and repeals expedited EFSEC processing.

title: Rare diseases adv. council
summary: Creates an advisory council within the UW School of Medicine to advise the Secretary of Health on rare disease research, diagnosis, treatment, and education.

title: Vehicle impounds
summary: Protects vehicles used as homes from impound sales and charges, extends hearing rights, waives fees for hardship, and makes government pay certain storage costs.

title: Students with disabilities
summary: Aims to improve access to and provision of a free appropriate public education for students with disabilities; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Prof. licensing reporting
summary: Expands reporting requirements for professional licensing; the text gives no further detail.

title: DSHS overpayments
summary: Lets DSHS waive collection of unintentional overpayments in the ABD program and for certain long-term support and developmental disabilities clients, with rules setting the criteria.

summary: Bill text is a title-only placeholder stating it concerns business development, with no specific policy change described.

summary: The bill concerns juvenile justice, but the provided text does not describe any specific change.

title: Advanced nuclear commission
summary: Creates an advisory commission to advise on commercial deployment of energy from advanced nuclear power.

title: Law enf agency accreditation
summary: Facilitates accreditation for law enforcement and corrections agencies; the text gives no details of rule changes.

title: Report of death

summary: Adjusts the funded special education enrollment count used for K-12 special education funding; the text gives no details.

summary: Lets the State Patrol chief mobilize local jurisdictions under the state fire services plan for emergencies or predicted disasters beyond local capacity.

summary: Continues a CTE dual credit pilot program through SBCTC grants, subject to appropriations, and requires joint legislative reports with recommendations.

summary: Addresses organized retail theft; the title alone does not state what changes in current law.

title: Career & tech. ed./6th grade
summary: Addresses career and technical education in sixth grade; the text gives no specifics on what would change.

summary: Makes technical corrections and removes obsolete language from the Revised Code of Washington, with no substantive policy change.

summary: Expands child care provider posting and website disclosure duties, requires DCYF to notify parents of license actions, and sets insurance notice rules and minimum liability limits by agency rule.

summary: Makes electronic vehicle and vessel titles the default, requiring a fee for paper titles, and lets a DOL subagent remove liens on electronic records.

title: Investmnt income B&O deduct.

summary: Requires public high school students to meet state financial education standards to graduate starting with the class of 2031, and requires districts to offer that instruction.

title: Control. subst. endangerment
summary: Amends the crime of endangerment involving a controlled substance; the summary does not say whether penalties rise or fall.

title: Health info./coordination
summary: Allows behavioral health providers to disclose client information under the Uniform Health Care Information Act when the client gives written acknowledgement of a disclosure statement.

title: Climate funding/outdoor rec.
summary: Directs investments in outdoor recreation and climate adaptation as part of environmental leadership; the text gives no details.

summary: Directs educational service districts to create a voluntary parent satisfaction survey, share anonymized results with schools, and publish an annual summary.

title: Plan 1 retiree COLAs
summary: Changes cost-of-living adjustments for Plan 1 retirees of the teachers' and public employees' retirement systems; the text gives no detail.

summary: Raises littering penalties, delays the plastic bag thickness increase to 2028, and requires a 4-cent bag penalty deposited into the waste reduction account.

summary: Extends the Pesticide Application Safety Committee's sunset from 2025 to 2035 and removes the restriction on its in-person meetings.

title: Student athlete insurance
summary: Lets public four-year university governing boards offer and pay for insurance covering current and some former student athletes.

title: Minimum parking requirements
summary: Concerns minimum parking requirements; the text does not say whether it adds, removes, or reduces them.

summary: Repeals six DOL professional accounts, moves their balances and the related professions' fees into the Business and Professions Account.

summary: Requires free phone and tablet communication for people in DOC and DCYF custody, bans facility revenue from these services, and adds contract fee disclosure and reporting.

summary: Lets municipal utilities, by ordinance, waive connection charges for organizations using properties for industrial symbiosis projects that cut resource use or emissions.

summary: Adds environmental justice as a SEPA element, requires Ecology to set standardized mitigation, and lets HEAL Act assessments satisfy SEPA review.

title: Boundary review filings
summary: Changes when a notice of intention filed with a boundary review board takes effect, a procedural timing change.

title: Property owners/projects
summary: Lets water-sewer and street reimbursement contracts run up to 20 years and extends pre-2020 COVID-era contracts if owners request it before March 31, 2026.

title: International med. pathways
summary: Creates preceptorship and hardship pathways that let international medical graduates reach medical practice.

title: Child care product sales tax
summary: Removes state sales and use tax on diapers and essential child care products to ease family costs.

summary: Requires private employers to give employees copies of personnel files and discharge statements within set deadlines, enforceable through a private lawsuit with statutory damages.

title: Burrowing shrimp

summary: Creates a subject-to-appropriation burrowing shrimp research program under WSDA, with a governing board, expiring July 1, 2035.

title: Business & occupation tax

title: Transportation funding/CCA
summary: Directs Climate Commitment Act revenues to fund the state transportation system.

summary: Reclassifies several hunting and hydraulic code offenses as infractions, sets a $500 big game fine, and requires fishing guides and charter operators to register and submit logbooks.

summary: Bill concerning dignity in pregnancy loss; the text provided is only a title and one-line summary, so its specific effects are unclear.

title: Utility meter choice
summary: Protects utility consumers' choice of meter; the text gives no details on what rules change.

title: School operating costs

title: Prepared food sales tax

title: Cannabis industry
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Relaxes cannabis license ownership-disclosure rules for small stakeholders, allows added fees for nonresident investigations, and requires suspension of inactive producer licenses.

title: Cannabis testing labs
summary: Shifts cannabis testing lab oversight from the Liquor and Cannabis Board to WSDA accreditation, ending LCB certification and limiting its enforcement role.

title: Cannabis/employee ownership
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Authorizes employee stock ownership plans to own licensed cannabis businesses and exempts ESOP employees, administrators and trustees from licensing vetting and residency rules.

title: Pension credit for leave
summary: Lets LEOFF Plan 2 members who retire after an ALOA leave purchase up to two years of service credit, with contributions based on leave-time salary.

title: Child care reimburse. rates
summary: Modernizes reimbursement rates for the Working Connections Child Care program; the text does not give specific rate changes.

title: ECEAP age requirements
summary: Lets DCYF enroll some 3-year-olds who turn 3 after August 31 in ECEAP, subject to available space and funding, and aligns statute with current age rules.

title: Educator support/nurses
summary: Extends the beginning educator support team program to provide mentors for novice nurses.

title: ADU self-certification
summary: Lets cities run ADU self-certification programs where only registered architects certify permits, with mandatory audits, penalties, and liability release.

title: Session employees/PEBB
summary: Addresses insurance coverage for legislative session employees through the public employees' benefits board (PEBB).

title: Tax compacts/capital invest.
summary: Lets compacting tribes receive 100 percent of state sales and use tax revenues after completing a qualifying capital investment, for compacts effective on or after 2028.

title: K-12 funding
summary: Raises school district enrichment levy limits and the state Local Effort Assistance threshold starting in 2026, with a fixed per-pupil cap from 2031.

title: Special education funding
summary: Raises special education excess cost multipliers, creates inclusion grants and statewide activities, and shifts general apportionment funds toward special education.

title: Mobile home community sale
summary: Concerns notice requirements when manufactured or mobile home communities are sold or leased.

title: Criminal insanity
summary: Creates a task force to review laws on criminal insanity and competency to stand trial, with no change to current rules.

title: Quantum economic development
topics: AI and technology; Government and administration
summary: Creates a quantum technology advisory committee and a state grant program for quantum projects, requiring five-to-one private matching, and exempts private applicants' financial information from public disclosure.

title: Process service
summary: Updates how legal papers are served on companies, repeals a corporate service section, and revises nonresident motorist service procedures.

title: Gambling diversion court
summary: Creates a gambling treatment diversion court pilot program, letting eligible offenders with gambling disorders receive court-supervised treatment in place of immediate sentencing.

title: Child care licensing
summary: Sets child care staff-to-child ratios and group sizes, requires 34 square feet per child, bars requiring early childhood certification, and repeals the community-based training pathway.

title: Unlicensed bingo, etc.
summary: Raises the annual gambling revenue threshold for charities and nonprofits to run bingo, raffles, and amusement games without a state license, and raises local gambling tax exemption thresholds.

title: Mobile home rental assist.
summary: Creates rental assistance for manufactured and mobile home park tenants.

title: Military surplus vehicles
summary: Authorizes military surplus vehicles to operate on public highways.

title: Right shoulder/motorcycles
summary: Restricts motorcycles riding on right shoulders, including speed limits, single file, reentry requirements, and limited-access exit rules.

title: New special license plates
summary: Creates new special license plates whose fees fund designated organizations and causes, and sets timelines for issuing plates that meet signature requirements.

title: Working forest license plate
summary: Creates a special license plate that supports working forests.

title: Mt. St. Helens license plate
summary: Creates Mount St. Helens special license plates for vehicles.

title: Veteran parking privileges
summary: Extends disability parking eligibility to veterans with a 70%+ service-connected rating who use a service dog, through 2035, with DOL reporting.

title: JLARC studies
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Directs JLARC to weigh two more factors in its work plan, size review resources to budget complexity, and review DNR's 2025-2034 sustainable harvest calculation regardless of litigation.

title: Senior citizens local tax
summary: Authorizes a local sales tax that is fully credited against the state sales tax, with proceeds supporting senior citizen programs.

title: Sales and use tax rate
summary: Reduces the state sales and use tax rate, lowering state sales tax collected on purchases.

title: Estate tax exclusion
summary: Updates the consumer price index reference used to adjust the estate tax exclusion amount each year.

title: Capital gains tax prepayment
summary: Lets taxpayers prepay capital gains tax up to six months early and bars interest on prepaid amounts later found overpaid.

title: Ferry system emergency decl.
summary: Declares the state ferry system in an emergency so officials can take expedited actions.

title: Eluding & resisting arrest
summary: Changes penalties for eluding police vehicles and resisting arrest; the text does not say whether penalties increase or decrease.

title: Health carrier reporting
summary: Lets the insurance commissioner require health carriers to report annual primary care expenditures, and makes those reports public.

title: Public property regulations
summary: Requires local sitting, lying, sleeping, and keeping-warm laws on public property to be objectively reasonable, creates a defense and a lawsuit route, and applies retroactively.

title: Elections/language assist.
summary: Requires counties with large limited-English-proficient language groups to provide election language assistance, backed by a state grant program if funded.

title: All payers claim database
summary: Expands who may receive All Payers Claims Database data, removes proprietary-information restrictions, and changes the OFM reporting cycle from biennial to every five years.

title: Baby products grant program
summary: Creates a grant program to fund purchasing and distributing essential baby products.

title: Winery tax exemption
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Gives wineries selling under 20,000 gallons a year a reduced excise tax rate, exempts them from most other wine and cider excise taxes, and sets a 10-year preference.

title: Background checks
summary: Directs the State Patrol to join the national criminal history compact and authorizes fingerprint-based background checks for employment or volunteering in care roles.

title: Firearms tax
summary: Imposes a new tax on firearms, firearm parts, and ammunition.

title: Prevailing wage/public works
summary: Amends rules on prevailing wages paid on public works projects; the summary gives no specific change.

title: Mobile market programs
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Creates a Department of Health mobile market program giving WIC and senior farmers market benefit participants nutrition access, contingent on USDA funding and rulemaking.

title: Timber purchase reporting
summary: Extends the expiration date of the timber purchase reporting requirement from September 30, 2025 to September 30, 2029.

title: Community protection program
summary: Repeals statute references to DSHS's Community Protection Program effective 2027 and requires a plan to move participants into other services.

title: Court alternatives/youth
summary: Limits juvenile diversion eligibility to offenses before age 18, bars parents from blocking diversion, removes diversions from criminal history, and requires AOC data and reporting.

title: Medicaid access program
summary: Creates an assessment on Medicaid managed care organizations and health carriers and raises Medicaid professional services rates to Medicare-equivalent levels.

title: Commencement/cultural exp.
summary: Requires schools to let graduating students wear culturally significant items with their gowns, subject to decorum rules and disruption limits.

title: Hospital medical records
summary: Requires hospitals to keep all medical records for at least 26 years, in paper, microfilm, electronic, or other media.

title: Home care worker background
summary: Limits when long-term care providers must undergo fingerprint background checks and lets them have unsupervised access to children and vulnerable adults for up to 30 days during a review.

title: Office of corrections ombuds
summary: Increases transparency and accountability requirements for the office of corrections ombuds.

title: Local property tax levies
summary: Deducts veterans' assistance and MHDD levies from the state property tax collection at no county cost and removes levy proration provisions.

title: Adult family home arb.
summary: Sets out factors to be considered in interest arbitration involving adult family home providers; the text gives no specific change.

title: Sheriffs, chiefs, etc.
summary: Standardizes and tightens eligibility rules for police chiefs, marshals and sheriffs, adding background checks, certification deadlines and conviction bars.

title: Officer certification
summary: Defines the terms "certified" and "commissioned" for purposes of the CJTC chapter on officer certification.

title: Nautical NW license plate
summary: Creates a new nautical Northwest special license plate option for vehicle owners.

title: Job posting/driver's license
summary: Bars employers from requiring a driver's license in job postings unless the job requires driving, and allows injured applicants to sue.

title: Condominium construction
summary: Revises condo implied warranties, creates a 2-10 warranty alternative for small ADU condos, and exempts those ADUs from building enclosure design and inspection requirements.

title: Free school meals
summary: Requires public schools starting 2026-27 to provide free breakfast and lunch to any requesting student, with state reimbursement for unfunded meals.

title: Complete streets obligations
summary: Reduces the requirements that transportation projects must meet under complete streets obligations.

title: Associate development orgs
summary: Sets funding allocation rules for associate development organizations, including caps, rural county minimums, in-kind match limits, and removal of some small-business reporting.

title: Graffiti & property damage
summary: Concerns criminal offenses involving graffiti or other property damage; the summary does not say whether penalties rise or fall.

title: Community authority funding
summary: Diverts 30 percent of state sales tax revenue from qualified large stadium facilities into CPDA accounts through 2037, with a JLARC review and reporting.

title: Clean fuels program
summary: Modifies Clean Fuels Program carbon intensity requirements, moves CFP violations out of Clean Air Act civil and criminal penalties into CFP-specific penalties, and requires Ecology to publish credit market analysis.

title: Inactive cannabis producers
summary: Concerns suspending licenses held by inactive cannabis producers; the text does not state the specific change.

title: Assumed revenues
summary: Limits the revenues the state may assume in budgeting to the projections made by the economic and revenue forecast council.

title: Comm'n, M. East & N. Africa
summary: Creates a 12-member Governor-appointed commission on MENA Americans to improve data collection, advise on policy, and support cultural awareness, and designates April as heritage month.

title: Opioid reversal purchasing
summary: Prohibits government purchases of opioid overdose reversal medications from certain unspecified entities.

title: CTE careers work group
summary: Expands a CTE task force, postpones its report to November 2026, and lets agencies begin rule changes on minors' work restrictions.

title: Long-term services trust
summary: Implements recommendations of the long-term services and supports trust commission, which concern the state's long-term care benefit program.

title: Tobacco & vapor products tax
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Raises the state tax on tobacco products and on vapor products.

title: Cigarette carbon tax
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Establishes an embodied carbon tax on cigarettes, adding a new tax burden on tobacco products.

title: PTBA governing body members
summary: Lets transit agency boards add two transit-user voting members, with rules for who qualifies, required training, and transit-accessible meeting times.

title: Interpreter background check
summary: Requires interpreters working for four state agencies to submit FBI fingerprint background checks, with annual Identity History Summary submissions starting July 2026.

title: Textile producers
summary: Requires textile and apparel producers to join or register with a state-approved coordinating organization by 2027 and begins a needs assessment for a future product stewardship program.

title: Smokey Bear license plates
summary: Creates Smokey Bear special license plates for the state Department of Natural Resources.

title: Drug take-back program
summary: Adds reporting, DOH audit and inspection powers, and fee rules for drug take-back programs, plus a one-time fee to fund a JLARC review.

title: Vehicle noise cameras
summary: Creates a 2026-2028 pilot allowing up to three cities to use cameras that record audio and video to enforce vehicle noise limits, with deletion and reporting requirements.

title: Jail system
summary: Addresses transparency, public safety, and independent oversight of city, county, and regional jails; the text gives no specific mechanics.

title: Pharmacogenomic testing
summary: Requires insurance coverage of pharmacogenomic testing used to guide psychotropic medication prescribing.

title: Impaired driving civil order
summary: Creates a new civil Impaired Driving Protection Order that courts can issue against people who pose a significant danger of drunk driving.

title: Peer support specialists
summary: Renames certified peer specialists, funds domestic violence and trafficking training, expands peer support billing and access, and weights MCO peer access in Medicaid procurement.

title: Criminal justice assistance
summary: Raises base state transfers to county and municipal criminal justice accounts to $50 million each and relaxes municipal eligibility requirements.

title: Extended foster care/housing
summary: Creates a rental assistance program for homeless or at-risk youth in extended foster care and requires DCYF to plan transitions before age 21.

title: APRN & PA reimbursement
summary: Requires private health carriers to reimburse APRNs and PAs at least what they pay physicians for the same primary or behavioral health services, and has OIC report on implementation.

title: Rental car agreements
summary: Limits rental car companies to separately stating only government-imposed taxes and surcharges, bars implying Washington imposes cost recovery fees, and requires a disclaimer for voluntary cost descriptions.

title: Mental health services
summary: Expands mental health and substance use coverage requirements for health plans, including limited-duration and student plans, and conforms parity rules to federal MHPAEA standards.

title: Psychedelic substances
summary: Creates a state-regulated program allowing adults 21 and older to use psilocybin in licensed administration sessions at DOH-licensed service centers.

title: Eid al-Fitr & Eid al-Adha
summary: Designates Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha as legislatively recognized days, removing their status as paid state legal holidays.

title: Law enf. hiring grants
summary: Creates a state grant program covering up to 75% of entry-level salaries and benefits for new local and tribal police officers, with annual reporting to the Legislature.

title: Law enf. officers/increase
summary: Creates incentives for cities and counties to increase their employment of commissioned law enforcement officers.

title: Tourism promotion
summary: Requires appointing an advisory group to study and recommend a industry-funded tourism assessment, and lets the tourism marketing account pay its costs through June 2026.

title: Housing permit approval
summary: Sets criteria for residential projects in urban growth areas to gain permit approval unless local governments identify serious health or safety concerns in writing.

title: Vehicle and driver licensing
summary: Modifies vehicle, odometer and driver-record rules, bars diversion for CDL holders' traffic convictions, and repeals certain honorary consul license plate authority.

title: Civil forfeiture proceedings
summary: Creates a uniform civil asset forfeiture chapter with notice, hearing, burden-of-proof, and attorney-fee rules that apply to specified statutes.

title: Broadband/repair and replace
summary: Authorizes repair and replacement of public works broadband projects, according to a short title and one-sentence summary only.

title: Gray wolf management
summary: Directs WDFW to manage gray wolves in counties meeting breeding-pair criteria as if state endangered listing were removed, via a work-group management plan.

title: Mobile dwellings
summary: Requires fully planning cities and counties to allow mobile dwellings on residential lots in urban growth areas with an existing housing unit.

title: Whole genome sequencing
summary: The bill concerns rapid whole genome sequencing, but the provided text does not state what it would do.

title: Washington health trust
summary: Text only names and refers to developing a Washington health trust; no operative provisions are described.

title: George Washington's birthday
summary: Renames the state holiday on the third Monday of February to George Washington's Birthday (observed).

title: Financial aid award amounts
summary: Bill concerns state financial aid award amounts, but the text gives no detail on what changes.

title: Local elections
summary: Lets local jurisdictions adopt ranked choice voting, sets RCV counting and implementation rules, and creates a King County pilot supporting voters with developmental disabilities.

title: Home cultivation of cannabis
summary: Legalizes home cultivation of up to six cannabis plants per housing unit with liability insurance, and creates civil infractions for 6 to 15 plants while keeping felony penalties for 16 or more.

title: Transition to kindergarten
summary: Caps statewide Transition to Kindergarten enrollment at 2023-24 levels, limits approved sites and per-site enrollment, and requires OSPI approval before enrolling children.

title: SVP civil commitment
summary: Concerns civil commitment of sexually violent predators; the short text does not specify what changes it makes.

title: Vehicle & retail theft
summary: Addresses motor vehicle and retail theft offenses; the summary gives no detail on what changes.

title: Scrap metal/stolen copper
summary: Increases penalties for scrap metal businesses that purchase stolen copper from telecommunication cables.

title: Drug task force funding
summary: Provides funding for multijurisdictional drug task forces. It does not change drug laws or enforcement rules.

title: Toxicology lab. funding
summary: Provides funding for state toxicology labs to process drug and alcohol impairment case submissions promptly.

title: Law enforcement personnel
summary: Changes conditions, policies, and programs to support specified law enforcement personnel and aid recruiting and retaining officers.

title: SVP electronic monitoring
summary: Requires electronic monitoring with real-time tracking and exclusion zones before a sexually violent predator may be conditionally released to a less restrictive alternative.

title: Embodied carbon/buildings
summary: Requires the State Building Code Council to adopt embodied carbon reduction standards for large new construction, additions and renovations (50,000+ sq ft) via three compliance paths.

title: Child fatalities
topics: Children and families; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Renames child mortality reviews to child fatality reviews, extends them to age 19, allows retaining case data, and bars public release of identifying information.

title: Protection order hope cards
summary: Expands the Hope Card program for protection order petitioners, removes the fee, adds trauma-informed design, and adds firearm prohibition information to the card.

title: Joint operating agencies
summary: Raises the dollar thresholds that trigger sealed-bid requirements for joint operating agency contracts involving materials, supplies, and construction.

title: Hydrofluorocarbons
summary: Sets declining global warming potential limits on hydrofluorocarbon refrigerants from 2030 and 2033, creates a transition task force, and directs future low-GWP alternative rules.

title: Cash assistance time limits
summary: Adds financial-distress hardship as a circumstance allowing extensions of TANF cash assistance time limits.

title: Home equity sharing
summary: Creates a licensing requirement from July 2026 for home equity sharing agreement originators, with a $30,000 surety bond, background checks, and DFI examination and enforcement powers.

title: Defendant supervision costs
summary: Concerns how counties and local governments share the costs of supervising defendants; the text gives no further detail.

title: Hospital safety net program
summary: Increases the biennial contribution hospitals make in lieu of state funds to the hospital safety net program.

title: Actuarial pension funding
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Stretches pension benefit cost amortization to 15 years and sets revised employer and member contribution rates for state retirement plans.

title: Accounts
summary: Modifies several state accounts, redirects dedicated revenue, extends school district interfund loan terms, and changes how some funds are held and paid.

title: ASAM 4 treatment criteria
summary: Delays the use of ASAM 4 treatment criteria for addictive, substance-related, and co-occurring conditions.

title: DDA no-paid services
summary: Addresses the developmental disabilities administration's no-paid services caseload, with the text describing a reduction but no details.

title: BSA transfers
summary: Concerns transfers from the state budget stabilization account; the title gives no amounts or other details.

title: Yakima & Rainier schools
summary: Requires DSHS to close the Rainier and Yakima Valley residential habilitation centers by 2027, relocating residents, while keeping some respite and crisis beds at Yakima.

title: Wildfire BSA appropriations
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Appropriates $77.7 million from the budget stabilization account to cover Department of Natural Resources wildfire suppression costs from the 2024 season.

title: PERS/TRS 1 benefit increase
summary: Provides a one-time 3 percent benefit increase, capped at $110 monthly, to eligible PERS and TRS Plan 1 retirees starting July 2025.

title: National board bonuses
summary: Suspends the state bonuses that certificated instructional staff receive for National Board for Professional Teaching Standards certification.

title: Nursing home rate rebase
summary: Delays nursing home rate rebasing from 2026 to 2027 and keeps the fiscal year 2025 weighted average payment rate in effect for 2026 and 2027.

title: WA saves trust account
summary: Renames the Washington Saves Administrative Treasury Trust Account to the Washington Saves Administrative Trust Account, with no other changes.

title: Death cert./subst. homicide
summary: Changes the manner of death recorded on a death certificate after a controlled substance homicide conviction.

title: Office of native ed. grants
summary: Establishes a state matching grant program to support American Indian and Alaska Native students, with an Office of Native Education.

title: Affordable housing REET
summary: Lets all counties impose a real estate excise tax to fund affordable housing, subject to voter approval.

title: Nuclear energy study
summary: Directs a study on commercializing advanced nuclear energy; the summary describes no change to existing rules.

title: Health coverage access
summary: States a general goal of assuring equity in health coverage; the text gives no specific mechanism or rule change.

title: Digital electronics/repair
summary: Requires manufacturers to offer parts, tools and documentation for digital electronic products to independent repairers and owners on fair terms, and limits parts pairing.

title: Victim of rape/pregnancy
summary: Adds rape-resulting-in-pregnancy to the aggravating circumstances that allow exceptional sentences above the standard range, regardless of victim age.

title: Services and activities fees
summary: Raises the annual cap on public college services and activities fee increases from 4 to 6 percent.

title: Student member on SBCTC
summary: Adds a student member to the State Board for Community and Technical Colleges, with age, enrollment, term, and recusal requirements.

title: Crime victim services
summary: Addresses funding related to the federal Victims of Crime Act; the text gives no details on amounts or rule changes.

title: Conservation district limits
summary: Caps the annual per-parcel rate for conservation district RACs systems at $25 and adjusts it by CPI every three years starting in 2029.

title: Childhood ed./impl. dates
summary: Delays ECEAP entitlement and Working Connections Child Care income-eligibility expansions to later years, pushing back expanded access.

title: Background checks
summary: Requires fingerprint-based national background checks for more DSHS and DCYF long-term care, child placement, and transitional care workers, and defines related roles.

title: Transit-oriented housing dev
summary: Defines a station area as either a rail or bus station area for transit-oriented housing development; the text gives no operative rules.

title: Students with dependents
summary: Gives students with dependents early registration access at public colleges, a procedural priority with no described cost or policy change.

title: DDA employment services age
summary: Lets DDA clients access employment waiver services from age 19 and sets employment service hours by the assistance needed, not hours worked.

title: Multiple-unit dwellings/tax
summary: Authorizes cities and counties to offer multifamily property tax exemptions for rental and homeownership housing near transit and in urban growth areas.

title: College promise pilot
summary: Creates a college promise pilot program; the short summary gives no details on eligibility or funding amounts.

title: Health care information
summary: Strengthens patients' rights regarding their health care information; the provided text gives no specifics.

title: Waste material management
summary: Requires smaller solid waste collection containers, starting in 2028, to follow color-coding rules for gray, black, blue, green, and brown bins.

title: Domestic viol. co-responders
summary: Adds a $100 marriage license fee, deposited into a dedicated account to fund a new domestic violence co-responder grant program.

title: Legal financial obligations
summary: Eliminates many court costs and fees on criminal defendants, repeals interest on restitution, and voids unpaid debts for those eliminated charges.

title: CIC resale certificates
summary: Modifies condo resale certificate contents, fee limits, purchaser cancellation timelines, and seller disclosure questions; allows owners to sue for noncompliance.

title: CIC unit owner inquiries
summary: Requires common interest community associations to respond to owner inquiries within 30 days, with specified extensions, and awards attorneys' fees to the prevailing party in inquiry disputes.

title: Behavioral health teaching
summary: Creates a behavioral health teaching clinic designation and an enhanced payment rate for those clinics.

title: Digital equity
topics: AI and technology; Government and administration
summary: Shifts digital equity planning, outreach and reporting duties from the broadband office to the Office of Equity, adding broadband adoption goals and a biennial report.

title: Firearm financial resp.
summary: Requires proof of financial responsibility to purchase or possess a firearm or operate a firearm range.

title: Insurance statutes
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration; Health care
summary: Miscellaneous insurance cleanup: exempts certain direct-practice reports from public records, narrows an auto rating rule to personal auto, changes refund and reporting deadlines, and removes several reports.

title: Credit union-bank merger/tax
summary: Credit unions that merge with or acquire a DFI-regulated bank lose their B&O tax exemption and pay a 1.2 percent rate starting October 2025.

title: Health care nondisclosure
summary: Voids provider-patient nondisclosure clauses that bar disclosing possible malpractice, torts, or crimes, with damages and retroactive notice requirements.

title: Ecosystem services
summary: Aims to expand revenue and economic opportunities from natural climate solutions and ecosystem services; specific mechanisms are not stated.

title: Family reconciliation
summary: Requires DCYF, subject to funding, to contract for community-based family reconciliation services and expands eligibility to detained youth and those in the housing stability program.

title: PERS/appeal commissioners
summary: Allows commissioners of the supreme court and court of appeals to participate in the PERS judicial benefit multiplier program.

title: Ferry captains
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Redefines WSF captains' duties, adds international law compliance, and lets captains and mates consolidate bargaining units if a majority votes.

title: Traffic safety
summary: Creates a grant program for nonpunitive responses to nonmoving violations by low-income road users and limits police to stopping drivers for equipment and paperwork violations only as secondary actions.

title: Seashore conservation area
summary: States an aim of safeguarding natural resources in the Washington State Seashore Conservation Area, without specifying any mechanism.

title: Low carbon thermal energy
summary: Brings thermal energy companies under Utilities and Transportation Commission regulation like gas and electric utilities, with exemptions for small and existing systems and an opt-in option.

title: Alcohol service in public
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Allows local governments to request, and the Liquor and Cannabis Board to approve, expanded outdoor and civic-campus alcohol service through 2027.

title: Insurance/affordable units
summary: Directs the Office of the Insurance Commissioner to study insurance options that could reduce condominium construction defect liability costs for affordable homeownership projects.

title: Digital equity/revenue
summary: Imposes a $2 excise tax on smart wireless devices over $250 and directs the revenue to digital equity and learning device programs.

title: Vehicle collision liability
summary: Creates a presumption that larger vehicle operators, and certain operators of smaller vehicles and bicycles, negligently caused collisions with pedestrians, bicyclists, or smaller vehicles, adding damages and fee remedies.

title: Vehicle subagent fees
summary: Raises Washington vehicle and vessel title, registration and transaction fees charged by subagents, with the increases delayed to January 1, 2026.

title: Pharmacist scope of practice
summary: Expands pharmacists' scope of practice to improve access to care and chronic disease management.

title: Complex care serv./children
summary: Supports caregivers who provide complex care services to children with heightened medical needs; specific provisions are not stated.

title: Utility wildfire mitigation
summary: Requires investor-owned utilities to file wildfire mitigation plans for UTC approval, with updates every three years, and repeals the utility wildland fire reporting requirement.

title: Essential worker health care
summary: Establishes an essential worker health care program; the summary gives no details on eligibility, coverage, or funding.

title: Isolated employees
summary: Expands isolated-employee protections for janitors, guards and hotel housekeepers, requiring training records, panic buttons, annual contractor reporting, and civil penalties for willful violations.

title: Vehicle sales tax/tribes
summary: Removes the delivery-to-Indian-country requirement for the sales and use tax exemption on vehicles sold to tribes and tribal members, through 2037, with a JLARC review.

title: Snack bar liquor licenses
summary: Allows snack bar liquor licensees to sell wine by the glass for on-premise consumption, in addition to beer.

title: Health care claims mediation
summary: Bars settlement demands in mandatory-mediation medical malpractice cases from expiring before the parties attend mediation in good faith.

title: Special education IEPs
summary: Seeks to improve individualized education plans for special education; the text gives no specifics on changes.

title: Cities/county road resources
summary: Lets cities use county road crews for street work without contracting out, and exempts such county work from public works dollar limits.

title: Reg. businesses/card fees
summary: Allows tow truck operators to charge a credit card transaction fee capped at 3 percent, if a no-cost payment option is offered and disclosed.

title: Communicable disease
summary: Requires state and local officials to implement and promote evidence-based communicable disease measures, including vaccines, and voids any law barring them.

title: Sales tax sourcing impact
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Allows cities meeting population and industrial-assessment thresholds to add a 0.3% sales tax, conditioned on specified budget public-process requirements.

title: Specialty electricians
summary: Lets employers with journey-level electrical apprenticeship programs use apprentices for specialty electrical work outside the program without changing their program status.

title: Tobacco, nicotine, and vapor
summary: Requires vapor nicotine manufacturers to certify FDA compliance annually with fees, creates an LCB directory, and bans unlisted products from sale.

title: Dental insurance practices
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Requires dental insurers to honor dentist treatment decisions, bars certain claim denials, and mandates refunds when dental loss ratios fall below 85 percent.

title: Juveniles/firearm possession
summary: Concerns offenses involving unlawful juvenile possession of firearms; the short summary gives no detail on specific changes.

title: Roadway safety account use
summary: Expands allowable uses of the roadway safety account to fund WATV-related roads, signage, mapping, and city grants, with conditions on DNR and WDFW transfers.

title: Capital assistance/schools
summary: Creates a supplementary capital grant program for small school districts to modernize or replace aging instructional facilities, with a prioritized grant list.

title: Wildfire protection
summary: Establishes a Wildfire Mitigation and Resiliency Standards Work Group, including insurance, utility, fire, and landowner representatives, to study wildfire mitigation standards.

title: Homelessness/tribal colleges
