summary: Allows accredited tribal colleges in Washington to implement a program for students experiencing homelessness.

title: Veterans affairs adv. comm.
summary: Changes the membership makeup and appointment criteria for the Veterans Affairs Advisory Committee, including the number of appointees from veterans organizations and at-large seats.

title: Senior independent housing
summary: Establishes minimum resident rights for independent senior housing, such as freedom from reprisal and the right to install cameras, enforceable as Consumer Protection Act violations.

title: Clean buildings standard
summary: Adds alternative compliance metrics and more exemptions and extensions to the clean buildings standard, extends utility data duties to Tier 2 buildings, and bars passing penalties to compliant tenants.

title: Child abuse risk assessment
topics: Children and families; Government and administration
summary: Requires DCYF to study and improve its child abuse risk assessment tool, report to the Legislature by 2026, and certify the assessment process every three years.

title: Cardiac and stroke outcomes
summary: Creates a statewide cardiac and stroke registry, requiring hospitals and EMS agencies to submit data, with annual reports and quality-improvement work starting 2027-2028.

title: Radiologic technologists
summary: Lets radiologic technologists perform intravenous contrast procedures under general rather than direct supervision, and allows general supervision to be delivered remotely by telecommunications.

title: Student mental health net.
summary: Establishes a statewide network providing mental and behavioral health services for students.

title: Cannabis retail robberies
summary: Aims to deter robberies at cannabis retail establishments; the summary does not specify the mechanism.

title: Responsible bidder criteria
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Adds responsible bidder criteria for public works contracts, including training and apprentice utilization plan requirements for bidders.

title: Electric vehicle batteries
summary: Requires registration and reporting for propulsion battery providers and handlers, with Ecology approving a plan for batteries lacking a responsible entity.

title: Cannabis social equity prg.
summary: Extends the cannabis social equity licensing program to 2034, requires an evaluation report, and removes a grant eligibility restriction.

title: Real estate broker fee
summary: Extends expiration of real estate broker and managing broker license fees and the Washington Real Estate Research Account to September 30, 2035.

title: Dairy inspection program
summary: Extends the expiration date of the assessment on in-state processed milk from June 30, 2025 to June 30, 2031.

title: College bound scholarship
summary: Expands College Bound Scholarship eligibility to students who have received a high school equivalency certificate.

title: Nursing home payment rates
summary: Concerns nursing home payment rates; the text gives no detail on what changes.

title: HS completers/CTC tuition
summary: Removes the age-19 minimum so community and technical college boards may waive high school diploma or certificate course fees for younger students.

title: Guaranteed admissions prg.
summary: Establishes the Washington Guaranteed Admissions Program, requiring named public colleges to guarantee admission to eligible students and mandating student data sharing from high schools.

title: Broadcasters
summary: Moves the radio and television broadcasting B&O tax into a new section, defines broadcasting, and exempts it from tax preference review and the 10-year expiration.

title: I-5 Columbia river tolls
summary: Concerns tolling on Interstate 5 bridges spanning the Columbia River; the text does not specify the tolling details.

title: Hospital exec. excise tax
summary: Imposes an excise tax on annual compensation paid to certain highly compensated hospital employees, with revenue funding health care access.

title: Domestic workers
summary: Extends state minimum wage, overtime, and sick leave protections to domestic workers such as nannies, house cleaners, and home care workers.

title: Diaper changing stations
summary: Requires public buildings with restrooms to install baby diaper changing stations in new construction and in renovations costing $15,000 or more, with exemptions and warnings before penalties.

title: Prescribed fire claims
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Creates a subject-to-appropriation pilot program to reimburse damage and suppression costs from certified prescribed or cultural burns, expiring in 2033.

title: Child care assist./B&O tax
topics: Children and families; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a business and occupation and public utility tax credit to support employers who provide child care assistance to employees.

title: Dual enrollment scholarship
summary: Expands Running Start dual enrollment scholarship eligibility, replaces textbook vouchers with broader course materials vouchers, removes the GPA requirement, extends the program to 2032, and appropriates $750,000.

title: Prior authorization/health
summary: Restricts insurers' prior authorization practices: limits policy changes to quarterly, requires provider credentials in denials, and bars AI-only denials of care.

title: Health care administrators
summary: Creates state licensing requirements for nonclinical hospital managers, directors and executives who supervise clinical providers, and defines related unprofessional conduct.

title: Financial aid eligibility
summary: Creates a $500 Bridge Grant for maximum Washington College Grant recipients not in the College Bound Scholarship, starting 2025-26, prorated for part-time enrollment.

title: Tax exemptions
summary: Bill aims to increase transparency and accountability for tax exemptions; the text provides no detail on specific mechanisms.

title: Academic employee bargaining
summary: Extends public-employee collective bargaining rights to student employees at four regional universities, with a single systemwide bargaining unit.

title: Occupational disease/heart
summary: Removes exposure and exertion qualifiers so heart problems in covered firefighters and law enforcement officers are presumed occupational diseases.

title: Higher ed. accreditation
summary: Exempts certain nonprofit institutions operating in Washington from the Degree-Granting Institutions Act when specified conditions are met.

title: Oath of office timing/local
summary: Lets newly elected local officials take their oath of office anytime between election certification and the day before their term begins.

title: Substance use/care, services
summary: Bill concerns substance use services and care; the text is too brief to show how it changes current law.

title: Residential property
summary: Concerns the defense of property rights; the text is a one-line title with no operative provisions.

title: Historic landmarks/cities
summary: Limits cities' ability to designate historic landmarks without owner consent, mainly for properties under 125 years old outside historic districts.

title: Palliative care/volunteer
summary: Addresses whether volunteer organizations providing uncompensated hospice care may also provide palliative care services.

title: Long-term care prg. repeal
summary: Repeals Washington's long-term care services and supports trust program, eliminating its public long-term care benefits.

title: Student transportation
summary: The bill's text is a title-level statement about providing adequate and predictable student transportation, with no operative provisions.

title: CTE/alt. learning exp. prgs.
summary: Addresses career and technical education within alternative learning experience programs; the text gives no details of the change.

title: 988 line tax
summary: Increases the statewide excise tax that funds the 988 behavioral health crisis and suicide prevention line.

title: Child care centers/buildings
summary: Requires occupancy load for child care centers in multi-use buildings to count only the areas where child care is provided.

title: Traditional health/medicaid
summary: Requires the state Health Care Authority to seek a federal waiver and cover traditional health care practices for Medicaid patients served at tribal, IHS, or urban Indian facilities.

title: In-person voting
summary: Ends universal vote-by-mail for nonabsentee voters and restores in-person voting at polling places and voting centers.

title: Voter citizenship verif.
summary: Requires verification of citizenship as a condition for voter registration.

title: Rules review committee
summary: Modifies procedural provisions of the joint administrative rules review committee; the title gives no detail on substantive changes.

title: Partner promise scholarships
summary: Lets local governments create Promise Scholarships, administered by WSOS, that cover tuition and fees not met by state aid, with state matching funds capped at $250,000 per year.

title: Organic, etc. agriculture
summary: Directs WSDA to develop an organic action plan and creates a subject-to-appropriation microgrant program and optional fee-reduction authority for organic agriculture.

title: Health carriers & providers
summary: Requires health carriers to give providers advance notice and contract information before contract changes, including 90 days' notice of significant payment modifications, starting in 2027.

title: Self-resiliency skills
summary: Directs instruction in self-resiliency skills to support student success; the text gives no further detail.

title: Defendant survivors
summary: Creates a sentencing alternative letting courts impose reduced or below-minimum sentences for defendants who were verified survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, or trafficking.

title: Public defense services
summary: Shifts funding responsibility for public defense services between the state and local governments, starting FY 2026, based on a five-year expenditure average.

title: Social equity land trust
topics: Children and families; Environment and energy
summary: Creates child care trust lands managed by DNR and a Child Care Trust Account to fund Commerce grants that retain and expand child care in underserved areas.

title: School costs/CCA
summary: Addresses school transportation and operating cost increases caused by the Climate Commitment Act, apparently through school funding relief.

title: Economic development plan
summary: Creates a Commerce advisory committee to guide a five-year statewide economic development plan, with legislative proposals and progress reports due through 2027.

title: Speeding
summary: Requires intelligent speed assistance devices as a license condition for certain drivers, limiting vehicle speed to the posted limit during probation or by court order.

title: Agricultural overtime
summary: Lets agricultural employers choose 12 weeks a year when workers can work up to 50 hours a week before overtime applies.

title: Community solar
summary: Creates a community solar program letting utility customers subscribe to solar projects and receive bill credits, with net-crediting and a valuation methodology.

title: Consumer debt adjusters
summary: Requires debt resolution services providers and debt adjusters to be licensed by DFI starting July 2026, shifts regulatory authority to DFI, and removes debt settling from the debt adjusting definition.

title: Family services support fee
summary: Raises the maximum local marriage license fee that counties may impose for family services from $15 to $30.

title: Crime victims/capital gains
summary: Allows crime victims to deduct certain capital gains, reducing their taxable income.

title: Liquor food service options
summary: Lets breweries and microbreweries subcontract food service requirements for restaurant licenses and host third-party food operators on their premises, with separation and permit conditions.

title: Medicare supp. coverage
summary: Requires insurers to issue Medicare supplement policies on a guaranteed issue basis to people switching from Medicare Advantage to traditional Medicare during open enrollment.

title: Jail searches/gender
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Sets jail search rules for transgender and intersex detainees, limiting cross-gender and genital-status searches and requiring consideration of gender identity.

title: State patrol longevity bonus
summary: Expands the State Patrol longevity bonus to more commissioned employees, paying one-time retention incentives of $3,750 per quarter by June 30, 2025.

title: Journal access/state empl.
summary: Directs the Washington State Institute for Public Policy to study funding and mechanisms for state employee access to peer-reviewed journals, due June 2026.

title: Recycling & waste reduction
summary: Requires beverage container producers to appoint and register recycling refund organizations and fund refund liabilities, or be barred from selling covered containers in Washington.

title: Farmed octopus
summary: Prohibits knowingly selling, possessing, transporting or distributing farmed octopus, with a civil penalty of up to $1,000 for violations.

title: Natural resources board/OSPI
summary: Allows the Superintendent of Public Instruction to send a designee to serve on the Natural Resources board.

title: Critical energy infra./PRA
summary: Exempts critical energy infrastructure information held by any agency from disclosure under the Public Records Act.

title: Unmanned aircrafts/foreign
summary: Prohibits purchasing small unmanned aircraft made or assembled by a covered foreign entity.

title: High school/AP, IB, CIE exam
summary: Concerns advanced placement, International Baccalaureate, and Cambridge international exams; the summary does not state the specific change.

title: Ticket sales
summary: Bill concerning ticket sales; the text provided gives no details of what it would change.

title: Capital gains tax
summary: Revises Washington capital gains tax: repeals the B&O tax credit, adds a capital gains credit for B&O taxes paid, and clarifies definitions and deductions.

title: Water system classifications
summary: Bars using a default people-per-connection number to classify a public water system as Group A when that would move it from Group B.

title: Transit conduct/ferries
summary: Expands the legal definition of transit authority to include Washington State Ferries.

title: UW primate research center
summary: Concerns the Washington National Primate Research Center at the University of Washington; the text states no specific change.

title: College in HS/private school
summary: Expands the college-in-the-high-school program to students attending private schools.

title: Dockworkers/family leave
summary: Extends Washington's paid family and medical leave employer definition to cover representatives of employers of collectively bargained dockworkers, who take on PFML reporting duties.

title: Parenting plan limitations
summary: Reorganizes parenting plan limits; mandates restraints for parents convicted of child sex offenses, raises rebuttal standards, and revises supervised visitation rules.

title: Housing court commissioners
summary: Lets superior courts appoint housing court commissioners to help handle residential unlawful detainer (eviction) actions, with required training and judicial oversight.

title: Collective bargaining/AI use
topics: AI and technology; Labor and employment
summary: Requires public employers covered by PSRA or the collective bargaining act to bargain with employees over adopting or modifying AI, unless a third party implements it; void without funding by June 30, 2026.

title: Tips/credit card fees
summary: Prohibits employers from deducting credit card processing fees from employees' tips or gratuities.

title: Alcohol taxes and fees study
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Directs a study of taxes and fees related to alcohol; it changes no existing tax or rule.

title: Back country search & rescue
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Creates grants for back country search and rescue groups and lets local governments recover unreimbursed search and rescue costs.

title: PFML grants/school districts
summary: Expands eligibility for Paid Family and Medical Leave Program grants to second class school districts, including those with fewer than 2,000 students.

title: Health plans/annual services
summary: Requires health plans issued or renewed after January 1, 2026 to let enrollees get annual and multiyear covered services up to one month early, without added cost-sharing.

title: Fire service policy board
summary: Creates a Washington State Fire Policy Board to advise the fire protection director and recommend budget requests and fire service training strategies.

title: Inmate place./biological sex
summary: Sets restrictions on placing inmates of different biological sexes in correctional facilities; the summary gives no detail on the rules.

title: Livestock methane emissions
summary: Requires dairy farms and feedlots to annually report their methane emissions to Ecology, with Ecology setting rules and a reporting schedule.

title: State marine forest
summary: Designates bull kelp forests as the state marine forest of Washington, a symbolic designation with no regulatory effect.

title: Medical debt
summary: Bill aims to protect consumers by removing barriers created by medical debt; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Public works/bidding
summary: Adjusts public works bidding rules for listing licensed plumbing, electrical and HVAC subcontractors, allows substitution changes, and removes an outdated board report requirement.

title: Behavioral health/schools
summary: Requires OSPI and ESDs to develop a framework of technical assistance and training to support student behavioral health in schools, with a legislative update due in 2027.

title: Consumer cooperative boards
topics: Consumer protection and business; Labor and employment
summary: Requires large consumer cooperatives to reserve two board seats for nonmanagerial employees, chosen by employee vote, with recusal on employee pay matters.

title: Wine & spirit sales limits
summary: Removes the 24-liter per-sale limit on wine and spirits sales from licensed wholesalers and retailers to on-premises retailers.

title: School safety
summary: Proposes nonfirearm measures to increase school safety for students and staff; the summary gives no specifics.

title: Chronic pain/good faith
summary: Enacts the Good Faith Pain Act concerning chronic pain; the summary text is too brief to determine specific changes.

title: Medicare advantage discl.
summary: Requires entities offering Medicare Advantage coverage in Washington to provide certain disclosures to consumers.

title: Med. & PA licensure compacts
summary: Brings Medical and PA Compact licensees under the Uniform Disciplinary Act, with the Commission as disciplining authority for those licenses.

title: Definition of timberland
summary: Expands the timberland real estate excise tax rate of 1.28 percent to certain forestlands sold or transferred to governmental entities that keep managing them as forestland.

title: Pension plan choice
summary: Lets certain public retirement system members choose Plan 2 or Plan 3 for future service, suspended if federal IRS guidance finds a conflict.

title: Utility facility removal
summary: Addresses which parties are responsible for removing or relocating utility facilities during transportation system improvements.

title: Working minors
summary: Extends child labor penalties and citation authority to agricultural employers, raises penalty minimums, and requires worksite consultation before certain minor work variances.

title: Automobile insurance
summary: Requires auto policies with physical damage coverage to include a right to appraisal for disputes over vehicle value and loss, with specified process and cost reimbursement rules.

title: DNR civil enforcement appeal
summary: Lets the Pollution Control Hearings Board hear appeals of DNR civil enforcement decisions under RCW 76.04.205.

title: Surface mine reclamation
summary: Establishes new permit fees for surface mine reclamation, adding a cost to surface mine reclamation permits.

title: Child care qualifications
topics: Children and families; Labor and employment
summary: Lets licensed child care providers meet staff qualifications through alternative pathways, including experience-based competency, until at least 2030, and convenes a stakeholder group to report on improvements.

title: Child care/community pathway
summary: Redesigns the community-based training pathway for licensed child care providers; the summary gives no detail on requirement changes.

title: Airport projects/local REET
summary: Allows local real estate excise tax revenues to fund capital projects at smaller airports, excluding leaded fuel distribution systems.

title: Teacher residency & apprent.
summary: Formalizes teacher residency and apprenticeship preparation models, requiring PESB approval, mentor support, and funding and stipends for residents and mentors.

title: Ocean vessels/environment
summary: Starting 2028, ocean-going vessels within three miles of Washington shorelines must use fuel at or below 0.1 percent sulfur, with recordkeeping, noncompliance fees and penalties.

title: Tow truck payments/indigent
summary: Creates a DOL program that reimburses tow operators for towing and storage of indigent owners' vehicles, which must then be released without the operator's lien or deficiency claim.

title: International fire code
summary: Lets large fire protection districts or authorities take over International Fire Code administration and enforcement from the county fire marshal, with six months' notice and fees allowed.

title: Provider contract comp.
summary: Concerns compensation terms in health care provider contracts; the text does not say what change it makes.

title: Wildfire costs/securitizing
summary: Lets utilities finance disaster-related costs, including wildfire costs, through UTC-approved bonds repaid by customer charges that cannot be avoided.

title: Washington 13 free guarantee
summary: Creates a Washington 13 Free Guarantee covering up to 45 technical college credits tuition-free for eligible students regardless of income, starting in 2027-28.

title: History museum funding
summary: Ensures dedicated state funding for history and heritage museums and county historic preservation programs.

title: Early childhood court prg.
summary: Expands the early childhood court program; the text gives no further detail on scope or funding.

title: Child welfare/racial dispro.
summary: Requires DCYF to submit biennial reports on racial disproportionality in child welfare, with disaggregated data and recommendations to address it.

title: Future fund pilot project
summary: Concerns a Washington future fund pilot project; the text does not describe its purpose or mechanics.

title: Education agencies/OSPI
summary: Makes the State Board of Education, Professional Educator Standards Board, Financial Education partnership, and Charter School Commission operationally independent of OSPI, starting July 2027.

title: Youth mental health/schools
summary: Expands youth mental health training and the school workforce to improve student well-being.

title: Long-term care ombud funding
summary: Provides sufficient funding for Washington's long-term care ombuds program.

title: Capital gains tax repeal
summary: Repeals Washington's capital gains income tax.

title: Estate tax repeal
summary: Repeals Washington's estate tax. The text is a one-line title and summary with no further detail.

title: Cancer education programs
summary: Concerns comprehensive cancer education programs; the text gives no details on what the bill would require or fund.

title: Community custody
summary: Removes offender scoring for escape from community custody convictions and requires behavioral health providers to report supervised persons' treatment compliance to their community corrections officer.

title: Prosthetic limb coverage
summary: The bill concerns insurance coverage requirements for prosthetic limbs and custom orthotic braces, but the text gives no detail on the change.

title: Sewage-containing spills
summary: Directs the Department of Ecology to create a public website with information about sewage spills.

title: Personal data privacy
summary: Creates Washington consumer personal data privacy rights and imposes requirements on businesses that collect or process consumers' personal data.

title: Employer technology use
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Labor and employment
summary: Limits employers' electronic monitoring of employees to specified purposes and requires advance notice, with bans on monitoring off-duty workers and private areas.

title: Electric transmission system
summary: Creates the Washington Electric Transmission Authority, with a board-appointed executive director who serves a three-year term and hires staff.

title: Hepatitis B & C screening
summary: Concerns hepatitis B and hepatitis C screening; the text does not state what the bill would change.

title: Corp. practice of medicine
summary: Concerns the corporate practice of medicine, but the provided text is only a title, so specific changes cannot be determined.

title: Charter school contracts
summary: Lets the Charter School Commission reassign surrendered, revoked, or non-renewed charter contracts, exempts them from the expired 2021 establishment deadline, and sets a 24-school operating cap.

title: Postsecondary/med. abortion
summary: Requires public colleges to offer or refer students to medication abortion, provide telehealth space and devices, and post reproductive health information online.

title: Sewage discharge fee
summary: Creates a sewage discharge fee to fund enhanced wastewater treatment infrastructure for salmon recovery.

title: Nuclear reactor projects
summary: Encourages electric utilities to invest in advanced nuclear reactor projects to help meet Clean Energy Transformation Act compliance.

title: Preventive dental care
summary: Aims to improve access to patient care by increasing preventive dental care; the text does not specify mechanisms.

title: HVAC electrical work
summary: Allows HVAC and refrigeration electricians to perform certain electrical work on ductless mini-split HVAC systems.

title: Unemployment ins./part-time
summary: Modifies unemployment insurance availability rules so part-time workers and certain full-time workers facing qualifying hardships can remain eligible while seeking reduced hours.

title: School director districts
summary: Requires school districts over 2,000 students to elect at least three or four directors from designated districts, with appointment fallbacks and a small-district exemption.

title: Water recreation facilities
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Expands the definition of water recreation facilities, adds aquatic facilities, requires permits and $100,000 liability insurance, and requires cold-water health warnings in operating instructions.

title: Fish and wildlife governance
summary: Makes the Fish and Wildlife Commission advisory, shifts authority to the WDFW Director, and requires the Governor to appoint the Director with Senate confirmation.

title: Health care entity registry
summary: Creates a health care entity registry; the summary gives no details on who must register or what it requires.

title: Social housing authorities
summary: Allows state public bodies to assist social housing public development authorities in planning, building, and operating housing projects.

title: Electric security alarms
summary: Requires localities that do not regulate electric security alarm systems to follow statewide standards for them.

title: Emissions/vessels at berth
summary: Lets Ecology adopt California's at-berth emissions rule for ocean-going vessels, effective no earlier than 2028, with up to three years of extensions.

title: Water and sewer systems
summary: Directs the Departments of Health and Ecology to jointly produce a statewide needs assessment of water and sewer system maintenance and upgrades.

title: Yakima basin water plan
summary: Extends the water supply milestone for the Yakima River basin integrated plan to 2035.

title: Tribes/PRA exemption
summary: Exempts information about American Indians, Alaska Natives, and tribes held by listed state health and social agencies from Public Records Act disclosure.

title: WIC hematological screening
summary: Exempts WIC program staff from certain requirements so they can perform hematological screening tests.

title: City & county REET revenues
summary: Lets cities and counties use REET 2 revenue for homelessness facilities and affordable housing, removing the time limit and allowing interlocal housing projects.

title: Unincorporated villages/GMA
summary: Addresses unincorporated villages under the state Growth Management Act; the text gives no specific change.

title: Covenant homeownership prg.
summary: Raises Covenant Homeownership Program income eligibility to 120% of AMI, allows full loan forgiveness after five years for lower-income participants, and changes oversight committee membership.

title: Newborn screening additions
summary: Requires newborn screening for an expanded panel of conditions, mandates reporting of positive tests, and creates a dedicated newborn screening revenue account.

title: Liquor permits & licensing
summary: Broadens the on-premise licensed facility definition for server permits, drops the video training requirement, and eliminates the military liquor permit and the public house license.

title: Interscholastic sports
summary: Titled as defending equity in interscholastic sports; the text gives no operative provisions, so its effect cannot be determined.

title: Comprehensive plan updates
summary: Delays the next comprehensive plan review and revision deadline for listed eastern and southwest Washington counties and their cities from 2026 to 2036.

title: Liquor licensee premises
summary: Allows liquor licensees and other businesses to operate separate premises in a shared facility, including leasing space and kitchens, with conditions.

title: Public utility tax, counties
summary: Lets counties impose a tax of up to 3 percent on utilities serving unincorporated areas, with a portion set aside for low-income utility assistance.

title: Equine industry
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Authorizes Commission fees to cover federal horseracing compliance costs, creates a B&O tax credit for race meets, and transfers up to $1.5 million yearly from the General Fund.

title: Cannabis revenue/local gov.
summary: Increases the share of cannabis tax revenue distributed to local governments. Does not change cannabis access rules.

title: Large animal veterinarians
summary: Convenes a work group to study and recommend ways to recruit, train, and retain large animal veterinarians.

title: Prior auth. APIs/health
summary: Requires insurers and managed care plans to maintain prior authorization APIs consistent with CMS rules, extends interoperability to other processes, and makes state requirements enforceable in 2027 regardless of federal changes.

title: Noxious weeds list/crops
summary: Requires noxious weed listing guidelines to restrict listing agricultural crops until a work group reports, with allowed exceptions, and removes a required public hearing.

title: Homelessness info. dashboard
summary: Creates a homelessness information dashboard to help local governments report on the impacts of homelessness.

title: Adrenal insufficiency care
summary: Requires school districts to adopt adrenal insufficiency care policies and lets trained parent-designated adults administer emergency corticosteroid injections, with liability protections.

title: Voting rights act compliance
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Elections and voting
summary: Requires jurisdictions with past voting-discrimination findings to obtain Attorney General preclearance before changing election methods, districts, or language access.

title: DCYF/financial stability
summary: Aims to strengthen the financial stability of people in the care of the Department of Children, Youth, and Families; the summary gives no specific mechanism.

title: Qualified biomass facilities
summary: Changes Energy Independence Act rules so qualified biomass electricity counts toward utility renewable targets without serving load, but must be utility-purchased from Pacific Northwest facilities.

title: Automatic voter reg./tribes
summary: Authorizes the Secretary of State to create compacts with federally recognized tribes to automatically register eligible tribal members to vote.

title: Small business risk pooling
summary: Lets small businesses with 20 or fewer employees form joint self-insurance programs for property and liability risks, subject to Risk Manager approval and rules.

title: Energy standard/comply cost
summary: Directs JLARC to study and report on state agencies' costs to comply with the clean buildings energy standard, using a sample of state-owned buildings.

title: Dog breeding
summary: Modifies dog breeding regulations; the title and one-line summary give no detail on the changes.

title: Affordable housing/sales tax
summary: Lets cities and counties create a sales and use tax remittance program that returns sales tax to eligible organizations developing affordable housing.

title: Health care prof. well-being
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Health care
summary: Exempts physician well-being programs from certain reporting duties and makes their participant records confidential, shielded from subpoena and public disclosure.

title: Liquor licensee events
summary: Creates a special liquor permit letting licensed liquor manufacturers and retailers hold up to 12 public tasting and sales events a year, with local approval, plans, and staffing requirements.

title: Community care/Rx assistance
summary: Expands the authority of nonpractitioners in community and in-home care settings to set up diabetic devices and hand injectable medications for self-administration.

title: Zero emissions vehicles/sale
summary: Allows qualified zero-emission vehicle makers to sell directly to consumers, creates a dealer charging and training grant program, and bans subscription fees for built-in vehicle features.

title: Secondary career education
summary: Lets 16-year-olds start certain EMS training through approved programs, requires a fire service training study, and bars L&I from blocking minors in bloodborne-risk jobs when licensed.

title: School construction projects
summary: Requires school districts to mandate project labor agreements with labor organizations on state-funded school construction contracts of $35 million or more, with limited exemptions.

title: POLST orders
summary: Allows verbal confirmation and electronic signatures for POLST forms, requires annual provider reviews, and creates a new statewide DOH registry for POLST forms.

title: Biosimilar medicines
summary: Lets pharmacists substitute biosimilars and interchangeable biologics unless prescribers object, and lets insurers require trying biosimilars or generics before covering brand drugs.

title: WA lumber mills/public works
summary: Requires public works projects over $500,000 in state funds to source lumber from Washington, Oregon, or the U.S., with waivers subject to public notice and comment.

title: School library info and tech
summary: Concerns school library information and technology programs; the text gives no details on what changes.

title: Estate tax/nonfamilial heir
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Extends the farm estate tax deduction to qualified nonfamilial heirs who were farm employees, for estates of decedents dying on or after August 1, 2025.

title: State school levies
summary: Reduces both parts of the state school levies to provide property tax relief.

title: Aircraft fuel tax proceeds
summary: Directs revenue from aircraft fuel taxes to be deposited into the aeronautics account.

title: Unclaimed property/museums
summary: Replaces newspaper notice for unclaimed museum property with alternative notice methods, such as websites, emails, social media, and posted notices, and sets an ownership-establishment process.

title: Home buying by entities
summary: Bars large business and investment entities from buying single-family homes, with exemptions, Consumer Protection Act penalties, and a Commerce report on disincentives.

title: Agency displacement expenses
summary: Sets caps on displacement reestablishment payments for state and other displacing agencies, with a 2% annual inflation adjustment starting in 2025.

title: Outdoor learning grants
summary: Creates a competitive capital grant program in the Recreation and Conservation Office to expand outdoor learning facilities, prioritizing projects that serve public school students.

title: Force-feeding of birds
summary: Bans the sale, possession, transportation, or distribution of products made by force-feeding birds, with civil penalties.

title: Missing persons
summary: Shifts missing-person dental record and statewide missing persons website duties to the Washington State Patrol unit, and requires dentists to release records under specified conditions.

title: Apprenticeships/tribal gov.
summary: Concerns federally approved apprenticeship programs operated by tribal governments; the summary gives no details on specific changes.

title: Veteran benefits access
summary: Adds Public Health Service and NOAA Corps service to the uniformed services counted in public employee pension and retirement benefit rules.

title: Self-service checkout
summary: Regulates the use of self-service checkout stations; the summary gives no details on the specific rules.

title: OII expansion/prosecutions
summary: Expands the Office of Independent Investigations to also prosecute criminal conduct, adding enforcement authority to the office.

title: PANDAS, pediatric treatment
summary: Expands access to treatment for pediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric disorders linked to strep infections and pediatric acute-onset neuropsychiatric syndrome.

title: Urban design/environment
summary: Creates a contingent Department of Ecology center to encourage sustainable, health-promoting urban architectural and landscape design, funded by state or non-state sources.

title: Health providers/carceral
summary: State reimburses community health providers serving local jails for medical malpractice judgments or settlements above $50,000.

title: Gift card criminal conduct
summary: Aims to deter criminal conduct involving gift cards; the text gives no specifics on what changes.

title: Election audits
summary: Requires independent manual hand-count audits of ballots in at least 12 precincts per county after each election, plus a one-time 2024 audit and reports to the Legislature.

title: School local effort assist.
summary: Provides state local effort assistance funding for public school districts; the text gives no amounts or rule changes.

title: Job applicants and employees
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Limits employers from rejecting or disciplining applicants and employees based on criminal records, banning action on arrests and juvenile records and requiring a legitimate business reason for adult convictions.

title: Insurance & credit study
summary: Directs a study of credit history, credit-based insurance scores, and other rate factors used in personal insurance pricing. It changes no rules.

title: SEPA considerations
summary: Requires state environmental policy act reviews to consider climate change, carbon sequestration, environmental health disparities, and treaty-protected and cultural resources.

title: Voting rights act claims
summary: Creates a new standard under the Washington Voting Rights Act: local election policies with a material disparate burden on protected classes violate the law, without proving intent.

title: Course materials sales tax
summary: Creates a sales and use tax exemption for required course materials bought at public higher education institutions.

title: Juvenile misdemeanor jdx
summary: Gives courts of limited jurisdiction concurrent authority over juvenile misdemeanor offenses. The text does not state any change to penalties or rights.

title: Child removal/opioid use
summary: Modifies the child removal standard where another person uses or possesses a high-potency synthetic opioid, addressing threats of harm to children.

title: Medicare suppl./guaranteed
summary: Requires insurers to issue Medicare supplemental policies on a guaranteed issue basis to traditional Medicare enrollees during open enrollment periods.

title: Coronary interventions/CN
summary: Exempts elective coronary interventions performed in state-owned or state-operated hospitals from certificate of need requirements.

title: Lead in cookware
summary: Concerns lead in cookware; the provided text does not specify what the bill would require.

title: Residential use/existing
summary: Lets existing buildings convert to housing in residential zones without change-of-use permits and eases energy code requirements for those conversions.

title: Aquatic land lease inflation
summary: Replaces the All Commodity Producer Price Index with the Seattle-area Consumer Price Index for inflation adjustments to aquatic land leases and log storage rents.

title: Day of the 12s
summary: Designates December 12th as the Day of the 12s, a legislatively recognized day, with no policy effect.

title: Manufactured homes/org. sale
summary: Exempts certain nonprofits, housing authorities, and public entities selling up to 12 manufactured homes per 12 months to low-income buyers from vehicle dealer licensing.

title: Local elected official oaths
summary: Changes the timing of the oath of office for local elected officials. The text is a short title only.

title: Higher ed./residence req.
summary: Bans public and private higher education institutions from requiring students to live on campus.

title: Affordable housing funding
summary: Imposes a 6% statewide excise tax on short-term rental lodging to fund affordable housing and homeless assistance, with density, impact-fee, and unit-size conditions on infrastructure projects.

title: Labor standards
summary: Raises Washington's minimum wage to $25 by 2031 and requires paid vacation and bereavement leave, plus paid leave for rideshare drivers.

title: Subscriber emails/PRA
topics: AI and technology; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Exempts email addresses of people subscribing to local agency newsletters and updates from disclosure under the Public Records Act.

title: Health carrier practices
summary: Bars health carriers acting as third-party administrators for public or school employee self-funded plans from requiring state-owned hospitals to join their commercial plans as a condition of participation.

title: School enrollment/funding
summary: Concerns how school enrollment figures relate to enrichment funding; the text gives no detail on the change.

title: Manuf. housing purchases
summary: Bars large business entities and investment entities from acquiring manufactured housing communities or lots, with exemptions, civil penalties, and forced resale for violations.

title: Abandoned vehicle auctions
summary: Brings abandoned vehicle sales under B&O and sales and use taxes, with wholesale and consumer rates applying and an exemption from review and expiration requirements.

title: Vision benefits
summary: Concerns the administration of vision benefits; the summary does not say what changes.

title: Universal communications
summary: Concerns the state universal communications services program; the text gives no details on changes to rules or funding.

title: Shared streets
summary: Lets cities designate shared streets with a 10 mph speed option, vehicle yield duties to pedestrians and micromobility users, and exemptions from other roadway right-of-way rules.

title: Wage replacement
summary: Creates a state Wage Replacement Program paying weekly benefits to unemployed workers ineligible for UI due to work authorization, funded by a new account.

title: Lease of unused highway land
summary: Lets WSDOT lease unused highway land for community purposes like housing, shelters and parks, counting social benefits as partial rent.

title: Fur products
summary: Requires fur farms to join certified animal welfare and environmental programs, bans producing fur products unless certified, and creates a temporary transition grant program.

title: Firearm check fee refunds
summary: Provides reimbursement of firearm background check fees. The short text does not specify who receives reimbursement or how it is funded.

title: Apprenticeship approval
summary: Requires the apprenticeship council to approve programs meeting standards, limits review of federally approved programs, and allows sanctions against frivolous competitor objections.

title: State sales tax revenues
summary: Shares state sales tax revenues with local governments without raising state or local sales tax rates.

title: Ag. employers/overtime
summary: Lets agricultural employers choose 26 weeks a year to employ workers up to 50 hours a week before overtime applies.

title: Doctor title/health provider
summary: Bill concerns how health care providers may use the title 'doctor' and related credentials, aiming for accurate patient communication. Text is a short summary only.

title: PDC enforcement actions
summary: Concerns enforcement actions by the Washington Public Disclosure Commission; the summary gives no detail on specific changes.

title: Campaign reporting timeline
summary: Moves campaign contribution and expenditure report deadlines one day earlier and shifts the reporting cutoff to two business days before filing.

title: Law enf. officers/colleges
summary: Lets law enforcement officers accept gifts up to $25 from colleges for criminal justice course presentations without violating state ethics rules.

title: Certified medical assistants
summary: Concerns certified medical assistants; the title and one-sentence summary give no details of what changes.

title: Excessive executive comp.
summary: Imposes a surcharge on publicly traded companies that provide excessive executive compensation.

title: Public safety facilities
summary: Adds public safety facilities to the projects that local infrastructure financing revenues may fund.

title: Substance use/commitment
summary: Updates the standards for involuntary treatment commitment of people with substance use disorders.

title: Workers' compensation
summary: Raises total-disability workers' compensation payments to 60-75% of wages based on family size, and adds a 2% payment to custodial guardians of injured workers' children.

title: Photovoltaic modules
summary: Establishes a photovoltaic module stewardship and takeback program for solar panels; the summary gives no operative details.

title: Defined benefit accrual
summary: Increases defined benefit accrual rates for specified years of service in state retirement systems.

title: Local real estate excise tax
summary: Lets local governments use real estate excise tax funds longer and without the $1 million cap for homelessness and affordable housing, and exempts certain affordable housing sales from REET.

title: Nursing assistant regulation
summary: Consolidates state regulatory authority over nursing assistants; the summary gives no detail on changed requirements or funding.

title: Reports of fire losses
summary: Modifies the reporting requirements for fire losses; the text gives no detail on who reports or what changes.

title: OFM, eliminating
summary: Eliminates the Office of Financial Management, the state agency that handles budget and fiscal administration.

title: Student restraint, isolation
summary: Bans mechanical, chemical and breathing-restricting restraints on students, limits planned restraint and isolation, and bars new isolation rooms in schools.

title: School construction debt
summary: Lets school districts borrow and issue bonds without a public vote for school buildings, subject to a debt limit and conditions.

title: DCYF & law enforcement
summary: Addresses cooperation between the department of children, youth, and families and law enforcement; details not stated.

title: Firefighters' pension boards
summary: Lets the county auditor and treasurer send a designee to sit on firefighters' pension boards.

title: Violent firearm offenses
summary: Addresses persons convicted of violent offenses involving a firearm, but the text gives no specific provisions.

title: Homeless housing grants
summary: Establishes accountability requirements for homeless housing grant programs, without changing eligibility, services, or enforcement rules.

title: Sentencing guidelines commn.
summary: Adds legislative members to the voting membership of the sentencing guidelines commission, changing its composition without altering sentencing rules.

title: Obstructing first responder
summary: Creates a prohibition on obstructing law enforcement officers or other first responders.

title: Safety of youth sports
summary: Promotes safety of youth sports; the text gives no specific rules, funding, or mechanism.

title: Community solar projects
summary: Expands the state community solar incentive program by allowing precertification payments, reserving funds for small projects, and adding eligible administrators.

title: Children services/local tax
topics: Children and families; Taxes and budget
summary: Allows counties to impose a 0.1 percent local sales tax, with revenue dedicated to services for children and families.

title: Commercial fishing revenue
summary: Cuts the state General Fund share of enhanced food fish tax revenue by half and redirects that portion to the cities or counties where fish are landed.

title: Catered events with alcohol
summary: Allows caterers to sell alcohol at events open to the public regardless of sponsor type, and requires licensees to give the LCB requested information on the hosting entity.

title: Homeownership revolving loan
summary: Creates a state revolving loan fund in Commerce to finance nonprofit or government-sponsored permanently affordable homeownership for low-income households.

title: Behavioral health response
summary: Creates EMS behavioral health training, an optional endorsement on EMT and paramedic certifications, a co-response training academy, and Medicaid payment for EMS behavioral health services.

title: Seismic hazard risk, reduce
summary: Concerns seismic hazard risk reduction; the bill text gives no specific measures.

title: Crisis co-response
topics: Criminal justice; Health care; Labor and employment
summary: Creates a crisis co-response framework and a crisis responder training academy, bars regional crisis lines from dispatching police, and extends a workers' compensation presumption to co-response teams.

title: Anesthesia services
summary: Requires health plans, public employee plans, HCA, and Medicaid MCOs to cover necessary anesthesia regardless of procedure duration, barring time-based caps and denials.

title: Medical assist reprocurement
summary: Expands behavioral health crisis services by requiring MCO-BHASO crisis delegation, Medicaid rate adjustments for service changes, and coordinated crisis hotline and care coordination standards.

title: SEPA/trails and paths
summary: Exempts small trail or path projects on certain interim railroad rights-of-way in cities of 500,000+ from SEPA review, with tribal notice and consultation requirements.

title: Prison riot offenses
summary: Narrows the prison riot offense to exclude juvenile facilities, vacates related convictions, requires resentencing, and moves riot behavior in DCYF facilities to internal infractions.

title: Civilian crisis resp. teams
summary: Lets cities and counties over 200,000 people optionally create civilian crisis teams to answer non-violent 911 calls instead of police.

title: Schools/sexual assault
summary: Requires OSPI to post trauma-informed sexual abuse response training and create a multilingual student and family guide, and mandates such training for school employees.

title: Administration of plats
summary: Requires administrative approval of most plat applications without public hearings, removes some notice and timing rules, and allows binding site plans for mixed-use residential development.

title: Transmission capacity
summary: Exempts existing powerline upgrades and rebuilds within current rights-of-way from SEPA review and removes a utility's transmission-capacity reporting from Clean Energy Action Plans.

title: Family vlogs/minor children
summary: Would protect the interests of minor children featured in for-profit family vlogs; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Interested party/prev. wage
summary: Expands who counts as an interested party under prevailing wage law and lets them request certified payroll records, limiting committee use to filing wage complaints.

title: Driver course/work zones
summary: Requires new Washington drivers under 26 to pass a free online work zone and first responder safety course, which DOL must contract for and may fund with speed camera revenue.

title: Transp. improvement board
summary: Replaces 'nonmotorized' with 'active transportation' in Transportation Improvement Board statutes and defines the term to cover walking, wheelchairs, bicycles and small personal devices.

title: Accredited birthing centers
summary: Lets the Department of Health accept accrediting-body surveys of birthing centers in place of its own, capping DOH validation surveys at 10 percent of accredited applicants.

title: Grizzly bear management
summary: Repeals state requirements to protect grizzly bears and develop habitat plans, repeals WDFW's duty to negotiate grizzly management, and repeals the ban on importing grizzlies from out of state.

title: Mobility equipment repair
summary: Requires manufacturers of mobility devices to provide repair parts, software, and tools to independent repairers and owners, enforceable by the Attorney General under the Consumer Protection Act.

title: Basic education/juv. justice
summary: Shifts and delays the Superintendent of Public Instruction's institutional education duties to 2028, requires rules, planning, and recommendations on governance options for justice-involved students.

title: Plasma donation/physicians
summary: Authorizes MA-EMTs to practice in source plasma donation centers and perform physician substitute duties there, as federal law allows.

title: Tribal warrants
summary: Expands tribal warrant enforcement and arrest authority, adds officer and jail liability immunity, and limits habeas review for people detained on tribal warrants.

title: Dev. disabilities/rec checks
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Health care
summary: Limits record-check reports to SPI-set access rules, requires notice to employers of applicant disqualifications, and expands database access to contractors serving children or people with developmental disabilities.

title: Wage and salary disclosures
summary: Allows employers to correct wage and salary disclosures. The summary is thin, so the effect on pay-disclosure rules is unclear.

title: Student performance
summary: Creates new per-student allocations for supplemental supports and staff bonuses, repeals National Board bonuses, creates a READ literacy grant program, and requires structured literacy programs in grades K-4.

title: AI grant program
summary: Authorizes Commerce to create the Spark Act grant program to promote innovative AI uses, funded through a new nonappropriated account of federal funds and donations.

title: Online services/minors
topics: AI and technology; Children and families; Consumer protection and business
summary: Bans addictive feeds and late-night or school-hour notifications for minors, requires user controls on addictive services, and makes violations Consumer Protection Act violations.

title: Cannabis licensing/zoning
summary: Aligns the liquor and cannabis board's cannabis licensing decisions with local zoning ordinances.

title: Local news journalism
summary: Expresses support for local news journalism; the text describes no specific policy changes.

title: Intercity passenger rail
summary: Sets intercity rail service targets for Seattle-Portland-Vancouver, requires WSDOT reporting, and orders an independent review of the Amtrak Cascades plan.

title: College grant/cert. programs
summary: Expands Washington College Grant eligibility to students in certificate programs for high-demand fields.

title: Advanced computing surcharge
summary: Amends the advanced computing surcharge to increase investments in the state workforce; the text gives no further detail.

title: Middle housing
summary: Lets counties allow middle housing on single-family parcels, caps LAMIRD density at four units, bars stricter standards, and exempts approvals from GMA and SEPA appeals.

title: Art purchase program
summary: Creates a loan program helping individuals buy art by Washington and indigenous artists, administered by the Arts Commission if funds are available; the state appropriation was removed.

title: Captive insurers/PUDs
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Allows local government entities and public utility districts to form, own, or use captive insurers, and broadens which insurance companies count as eligible captives.

title: Students/unemployment ins.
summary: Repeals the rule that disqualifies otherwise eligible students enrolled in 12 or more weekly instructional hours from receiving unemployment insurance benefits.

title: Alternative jet fuels
summary: States an intent to advance production and use of alternative jet fuels in Washington; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Cash assistance payments
summary: Concerns payment standards for cash assistance programs; the text does not state whether benefits rise or fall.

title: Sounders FC license plate
summary: Directs proceeds from a Seattle Sounders FC special license plate, after administrative expenses, to the team's RAVE foundation charity.

title: Distributed alt. energy dev.
summary: Designates distributed solar, storage, wind and demand programs as energy priorities and directs Ecology to evaluate SEPA streamlining, including possible categorical exemptions.

title: Traumatic brain injuries
summary: Raises the traffic infraction fee for the traumatic brain injury account from $5 to $10 and directs DSHS to fund in-person peer support, community integration, and federal grant-seeking.

title: Rx drug donation program
summary: Expands the list of drugs eligible for the unexpired prescription drug donation program.

title: Glucose monitor replacement
summary: Aims to facilitate prompt replacement of defective continuous glucose monitoring equipment; the summary gives no further detail.

title: Higher ed. property damage
summary: Prohibits public colleges and universities from using state appropriated funds to repair property damaged in disruptive activities.

title: Local gov. property transfer
summary: Bans local governments from transferring real property to nongovernment entities unless they receive fair consideration.

title: Green community schoolyards
summary: Designates school district recreational properties as green community schoolyards and develops a model shared-use agreement to expand public use of playgrounds and playfields.

title: Rural areas/subdivision
summary: Authorizes subdivision of rural land for families, allowing parcels to be divided for household use.

title: Discrimination in schools
summary: Expands anti-discrimination protections for certain students in public schools to promote inclusivity.

title: Municipal gas utilities/CCA
summary: Changes the Climate Commitment Act compliance obligation for certain municipal gas utilities; the summary does not say how.

title: Asbestos building materials
summary: Exempts commercial aggregates with 0.25% or less asbestos from asbestos building material prohibitions, labeling, and manufacturing facility inspection and management requirements.

title: Deed of trust assignment/fee
summary: Removes the recording-fee exemption for assignments and substitutions of deeds of trust from the housing surcharge and the Covenant Homeownership assessment.

title: Housing dev./religious orgs.
summary: Requires cities to create density bonuses for affordable housing built on religious-organization property, conditioned on income-restricted units.

title: Supply chain competitiveness
summary: Creates a supply chain competitiveness grant and loan program for public and tribal ports, funded through a new state account and administered by the Department of Transportation.

title: Smoke impacts/DNR burns
summary: Requires notification of smoke impacts from Department of Natural Resources-initiated or silvicultural burns.

title: Train length
summary: Caps train length at 8,500 feet unless the UTC approves up to 10,000 feet with added crew and equipment, and sets fines for violations.

title: Schools/cardiac emergencies
summary: Promotes cardiac emergency response plans in schools; the title and summary describe no mandate or funding.

title: Ambulances/transport options
summary: Lets ambulances transport patients to non-emergency facilities like urgent care, requires that transport in regional plans, and requires coverage by health carriers, public plans, and Medicaid.

title: Working conn. child care
summary: Expands Working Connections Child Care subsidy access to small business employees and adjusts the program's implementation dates.

title: Grant fund advances pilot
summary: Creates a pilot program to advance grant funds to nonprofits so they can support grant performance.

title: Affordable housing REET
topics: Government and administration; Housing; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets all counties and eligible cities impose a local affordable housing real estate excise tax of up to 0.5 percent, with county credits for city-imposed taxes.

title: Athletic trainers in schools
summary: The bill aims to expand access to athletic trainers in Washington schools, though the summary gives no mechanism or funding details.

title: Transit costs/adjacent state
summary: Prohibits Washington state funds from paying capital costs of transit agencies created under the laws of an adjacent state.

title: Public health clinics/tax
summary: Lets counties levy up to 5 cents per $1,000 assessed value to fund public health clinic operations, maintenance and capital, exempt from certain levy limits.

title: Residential energy storage
summary: Creates a residential battery incentive program run by WSU Energy Program, requiring large electric utilities to offer one-time per-kWh battery incentives and plan for battery use.

title: Firearms
summary: Concerns firearms, but the text gives no detail on what the bill would change.

title: WC child care/grad. students
summary: Expands eligibility for the Working Connections child care program to graduate and professional students.

title: Textured hair training
summary: Requires the Department of Licensing to add textured hair care, styling, and treatment training to cosmetology, barbering, esthetics, and hair design curricula starting March 2026.

title: Sick leave/immigration
summary: Lets employees and rideshare drivers use paid sick leave to attend immigration proceedings, with documentation rules that protect immigration status information.

title: Death with dignity act
summary: Changes the requirements for accessing Washington's death with dignity act; the summary gives no detail on what changes.

title: Public education system
summary: Eliminates public education offices, agencies, programs and services that lack direct daily interaction with students.

title: Young driver safety
summary: Phases in driver training requirements for drivers 18–21 and mandates safe driving courses or license suspension for young new drivers with repeat violations.

title: Hospital worker breaks
summary: Concerns meal and rest breaks for hospital workers; the text does not say whether it adds or relaxes break requirements.

title: Legislature/appropriations
summary: States that the legislature alone determines and makes appropriations; the text specifies no other changes.

title: Health care marketplace
summary: Requires hospitals, provider groups, and insurers in material change transactions to give 90 days' notice to the Health Care Authority and Attorney General, with an emergency fast-track.

title: State tax on lodging
summary: Creates a temporary 2 percent lodging tax for stays from April to September 2026, with revenue going to counties, anti-trafficking programs, and state tourism.

title: Employment training program
summary: Amends provisions of the Washington customized employment training program; the text provided does not state the specific changes.

title: Cannabis regulation
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Directs the Liquor and Cannabis Board to prioritize youth prevention and diversion enforcement, review and trim burdensome cannabis rules, and audit reporting data within existing resources.

title: Legislative privilege/PRA
summary: Removes the legislative privilege exemption from the Public Records Act, expanding public access to legislative records.

title: Firefighter memorial plate
summary: Creates a firefighter memorial license plate with original and renewal fees, with proceeds directed to the Washington State Council of Firefighters.

title: Data broker registry & tax
topics: AI and technology; Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Requires data brokers to register annually with the Department of Licensing and disclose data practices, and imposes a graduated monthly per-resident severance tax starting 2027.

title: Naturopathic physician scope
summary: Concerns naturopathic physician scope of practice; the short text does not say whether scope would expand or narrow.

title: Continuing care oversight
summary: Adopts DSHS report recommendations on a regulatory oversight plan for continuing care retirement communities.

title: Prosecutor liability
summary: Establishes liability standards for prosecutors; the summary gives no detail on what conduct is covered or what consequences apply.

title: Defense counsel liability
summary: Establishes liability standards for criminal defense counsel; the summary gives no detail on what those standards require.

title: State legislator liability
summary: Establishes liability standards for state legislators; the summary gives no detail on what those standards require.

title: Judicial liability
summary: Establishes liability standards for superior, district, and municipal court judges; the text does not specify the standards.

title: Tribes/K-12 instruction
summary: Expresses support for public school instruction on tribal sovereignty and federally recognized Indian tribes; the text does not specify required changes.

title: Educational assist./B&O tax
summary: Creates a business and occupation tax credit for small business employers that provide educational assistance to their employees.

title: Local law enf. officers
summary: Lets counties and cities levy a 0.1% sales tax to hire more commissioned police, and requires the training commission to run at least 27-28 basic academy classes a year.

title: Community safety/liability
summary: Grants good-faith liability immunity to community-based public safety programs and their staff when serving people in behavioral health crisis or with legal system involvement, excluding gross negligence or willful misconduct.

title: Truck and trailer length
summary: Raises the legal maximum length for three-axle truck and trailer combinations to 85 feet when empty or carrying agricultural product.

title: Homelessness point-in-time
summary: Replaces the annual homeless census requirement with a Commerce-set schedule and removes outdated 2005-era program tasks for homelessness services.

title: Financial fraud protections
summary: Requires banks and securities firms to report suspected fraud or financial exploitation to state agencies and to flag affected accounts internally.

title: Mattress producer resp.
summary: Establishes a framework for mattress producer responsibility organizations; the text is too brief to specify the obligations imposed.

title: Transp. project permitting
summary: Directs WSDOT and Ecology to convene a work group that will develop recommendations for streamlining transportation project permitting.

title: Low-income energy assistance
summary: Creates a state-run low-income energy assistance program administered by Commerce through participating utilities, subject to appropriation and not funded by utility surcharges.

title: Declawing cats
summary: Bans veterinarians from declawing cats except for therapeutic purposes, and preempts local ordinances regulating declawing.

title: Invol. treatment counsel
summary: Concerns appointed counsel for individuals detained under the involuntary treatment act; the text gives no details.

title: Water system rates
summary: Adds UTC rate-setting rules and oversight for water companies, bars approval of control changes without customer net benefits and notice, and allows optional multiyear rate plans.

title: Self-service storage/tax
summary: Starting 2026, treats self-storage unit rentals as retail sales subject to B&O and sales/use tax, with revenue intended for affordable and cooperative manufactured housing.

title: Res. habilitation centers
summary: Keeps existing state residential habilitation centers operating for people with developmental disabilities and allows new residents to be admitted.

title: Court unification task force
summary: Creates a task force to study the state court system and identify where more unified or centralized court operations could improve efficiency and consistency.

title: Teacher-librarian funding
summary: Increases state funding for teacher-librarians in Washington schools.

title: Pollinator license plates
summary: Creates pollinator special license plates with original and renewal fees, directing plate proceeds to the Washington State Beekeepers Association.

title: Agricultural fuel/CCA ex.
summary: Extends the Climate Commitment Act fuel exemption for agricultural fuel by two years, broadens covered fuels, and creates a directory and guide for exempt fuel sellers and users.

title: Public utility tax credit
summary: Repeals the public utility tax credit for home energy assistance, ending that tax credit for utilities.

title: Discover pass, day-use cost
summary: Updates the cost of Discover Passes and day-use permits for state recreation lands; the amounts are not specified in the text.

title: Tenant protections
summary: Adds notice and proof requirements for evictions, extends notice for nonpayment in certain federally backed or subsidized units, and creates a defense tied to landlord maintenance failures.

title: Voter registrations
summary: Limits who may challenge voter registrations and on what grounds, raises the burden of proof, and adds penalties for false or baseless challenges.

title: Juvenile rehabilitation
summary: Sets juvenile rehabilitation capacity limits and lets DCYF transfer or release youth, including moving some adult-court youth to DOC custody, when facilities exceed 105 percent of safe capacity.

title: Supreme court districts
summary: Creates judicial districts for the state supreme court, changing how its justices are organized or chosen by district.

title: Working conn. child care
summary: Delays scheduled child care subsidy income expansions four years, while adding eligibility for small-business employees up to 75% of SMI.

title: Juvenile access to attorneys
summary: Addresses juvenile access to attorneys when contacted by law enforcement; the summary gives no detail on the specific change.

title: Transportation revenue
summary: Creates voluntary and mandatory per-mile road usage charges on vehicles, replacing EV and hybrid fees for enrollees and directing revenue to highway maintenance.

title: Hydraulic project mitigation
summary: Changes how hydraulic project approval mitigation applies after natural events; the summary gives no detail on the specific change.

title: Passenger-only ferries
summary: Expands passenger-only ferry district formation, adds governance and construction rules, changes district tax authority, requires whale-avoidance procedures, and adds an enforcement fare surcharge.

title: Manufacturing/sales tax
summary: Creates a sales and use tax exemption for manufacturing facilities and green manufacturing facilities.

title: Natural resources careers
summary: Expands secondary-level training programs for careers in natural resources and conservation; the text gives no details on mechanics or funding.

title: Home care aides
summary: Removes the 200-day home care aide certification deadline, has DOH and DSHS set the timeline by rule, and integrates testing into training programs.

title: Rent payment reporting
summary: Creates a voluntary pilot in which up to 10 landlords report tenant rent payments to credit bureaus, with Commerce running recruitment, rules and optional reimbursement.

title: Supreme court vacancies
summary: Requires Senate confirmation of the governor's appointments to Washington Supreme Court vacancies.

title: Court of appeals vacancies
summary: Requires Senate confirmation of the governor's appointments to Court of Appeals vacancies.

title: Fish and wildlife commission
summary: Restructures the Fish and Wildlife Commission so six regional members are chosen by county legislative authorities and three at-large members by the Governor, with staggered six-year terms.

title: Special license plate funds
summary: Directs proceeds from the Seahawks and Sounders special license plate sales, after administrative costs, to team-affiliated charitable foundations.

title: Cannabis consumption
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Creates a cannabis consumption event organizer license allowing monthly on-site adult cannabis consumption events, with fees directed to cannabis, community, and youth prevention accounts.

title: Overdose information
summary: Provides universal access to overdose information for law enforcement and emergency services providers.

title: Employment investigation/PRA
summary: Expands the redactions required before releasing employment discrimination or harassment investigation records, including complainants' and witnesses' identifying details and altered audio voices.

title: Project permit definition
summary: Excludes building permits from the definition of project permit for purposes of local permit review requirements and deadlines.

title: Schools/postretirement
summary: Extends until 2030 the allowance for retired teachers and public employees to work up to 1,040 hours a year, including in some school administrative roles, while still collecting benefits.

title: Industrial stormwater permit
summary: Gives industrial stormwater permit holders a presumption of water-quality compliance and lets transportation facilities skip stormwater sampling until Ecology finds it safe.

title: State flag redesign
summary: Creates a state committee to redesign the Washington state flag.

title: FIFA world cup/low-income
summary: Aims to promote opportunities for low-income people during the 2026 FIFA World Cup; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Cannabis industry
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice; Taxes and budget
summary: Removes the six-month Washington residency requirement for cannabis licenses, allows extra nonresident investigation fees, and exempts social equity licensees from B&O tax for five years.

title: Agricultural coops/cannabis
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Lets licensed cannabis producers form agricultural associations or cooperatives and treats cannabis as an agricultural product for that purpose, but caps each group at three producer licenses.

title: AI economic development
summary: Stated purpose is promoting economic development of innovative uses of artificial intelligence; operative provisions are not described.

title: Blood donation/school instr.
summary: Encourages public schools to provide instruction raising student awareness of blood donation, without mandating it.

title: Water-sewer district surplus
summary: Concerns how water-sewer districts may sell surplus property; the text gives no details of the change.

title: Crime victims ombuds
summary: Creates a crime victims ombuds office to advocate for and assist crime victims.

title: Local board of health/tribes
summary: Requires local and health district boards of health to allow a tribal representative from each tribe and Urban Indian Organization in the county, selected by that tribe or organization.

title: Group B public water systems
summary: Exempts most new Group B public water systems from mandatory satellite system management agency ownership or operation, unless specified conditions apply.

title: Environment/port districts
summary: Directs port districts to reduce environmental and health disparities and improve residents' health, but the summary gives no specific mechanism.

title: Scholarly communications/PRA
summary: Exempts certain scholarly communications from disclosure under the Public Records Act.

title: Subcontractors, indemnifying
summary: Requires contractors who cause late payments to subcontractors to indemnify certified subcontractors for trust contribution penalties on public works projects.

title: TNCs/large-scale events
summary: Concerns regulation of transportation network companies such as rideshare services during large-scale events; details are not specified in the text.

title: Special license plates
summary: Creates a task force to review special license plate processes and costs, and pauses new special plate applications through June 30, 2029.

title: Unclaimed property/local gov
summary: Lets local governments receive unclaimed property from the Department of Revenue without filing a form, with annual notice of available property.

title: Critical comm infrastructure
summary: Creates criminal and civil penalties for destroying critical communications infrastructure.

title: Fishing & shellfishing/youth
summary: Encourages youth participation in fishing and shellfishing; the summary gives no specific mechanism.

title: Public defense recruitment
summary: Concerns public defense recruitment and retention; the text gives no details on specific changes.

title: Health plan rate approval
summary: Makes the rate approval process for individual and small group health plans more consistent. The text does not change coverage or rate standards.

title: Interstate bridge toll bonds
summary: Authorizes up to $2.5 billion in bonds, backed by tolls, fuel taxes and state credit, for the Interstate Bridge Replacement project.

title: Office of equity repeal
summary: Repeals the Office of Equity, eliminating that state office.

title: Renewable energy
