summary: Directs development of a statewide food security strategy; the text gives no further detail on rules or funding.

title: Assault of transit employee

title: Utility disaster costs

title: Agency email subscribers/PRA

title: Safe system approach strat.
summary: Revises state active transportation, shared-use path, roundabout, and Complete Streets rules, including allowing local facilities to substitute for some Complete Streets requirements.

summary: Clarifies which investment income qualifies for the business and occupation tax deduction; the text gives no details on the change.

summary: Creates enforcement actions for property damage to electric vehicle charging stations.

title: Industrial land banks

title: Competency-based assessments

title: Personal hygiene products

summary: Clarifies how the real estate excise tax is calculated when a controlling interest in an entity holding real property is transferred.

title: Dependency/attorney appt.

title: Partial confinement

summary: Concerns law enforcement officers' use of face coverings; the text does not say whether it allows or restricts them.

title: Accident risk zones
summary: Lets local governments or WSDOT create crash prevention zones with increased enforcement and a fixed $73 penalty for speed and collision infractions, with penalty revenue funding safety work.

title: Free DME providers/tax
summary: Exempts free durable medical equipment providers, which are nonprofits that give equipment to patients at no charge, from retail sales and use tax.

title: Drug therapy agreements/PRA
summary: Makes collaborative drug therapy agreements confidential under the Public Records Act, except when tied to disciplinary orders, and requires redaction of personal information.

title: Definition of fetal death
summary: Modifies the vital statistics definition of fetal death; the summary gives no detail on any effect on access or rules.

title: Court rules and procedures
summary: Reconciles conflicting damage limits for second-degree malicious mischief and moves LFO collection grant administration from the Administrative Office of the Courts to the State Treasurer.

title: Port workers PERS membership
summary: Excludes port district employees enrolled in the Federal Railroad Retirement System from PERS membership starting January 1, 2027, and states legislative intent against dual participation.

title: Coaches of youth sports
summary: Concerns coaches of youth sports organizations; the title alone does not state any specific change.

title: Atmospheric river response
summary: Provides funding for response activities following the December 2025 atmospheric river and winter storm event.

title: Abortion medications
summary: Lets the state distribute abortion medications at no required charge, broadens the covered medications and reproductive care, and limits recipients to providers using them for reproductive care.

title: Heat response plans
summary: Requires counties planning under the GMA to adopt extreme heat response plans by July 1, 2027, developed with local health and emergency management agencies.

title: OT intramuscular needling
summary: Concerns allowing occupational therapists to perform intramuscular needling, which would expand their scope of practice.

title: Homeless youth committee
summary: Adds members with lived experience of youth homelessness or public systems of care to the Homeless Youth Advisory Committee.

title: Federal funds
summary: Requires Commerce to inventory economic development grants, help applicants for federal funds, and award competitive matching funds subject to appropriations.

title: Child care assist./B&O tax
topics: Children and families; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a business and occupation and public utility tax credit to support employers that provide child care assistance to employees.

title: Industrial insurance rates
summary: Promotes transparency in certain industrial insurance (workers' compensation) rate increases; the summary gives no specifics.

title: Workers' comp. settlements
summary: Expands which workers may use voluntary workers' compensation settlements.

title: Language access providers
summary: Makes missed-appointment payments and other pay items bargainable for language access providers, and gives collective bargaining agreements priority over conflicting executive orders, rules, and agency policies.

title: Construction worker wages
summary: Extends wage liability to property owners and contractors, creates personal liability for officers, presumes workers are employees, and bars retaliation.

title: Roadway fatalities
summary: Updates the Washington traffic safety commission's role in identifying risk factors behind roadway fatalities, without changing traffic rules.

title: Mortgage lending fraud acc.
summary: Concerns the mortgage lending fraud prosecution account; the text does not say what changes.

title: Cultural access sales tax
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets counties and cities concurrently impose a cultural access sales tax, with counties crediting city taxes.

title: City initiatives, referenda
summary: Concerns city initiatives and referendums; the text gives no detail on specific changes.

title: PANDAS, pediatric treatment
summary: Expands access to treatment for children with PANDAS and PANS, based on the bill title and short summary.

title: English as state language
summary: Designates English as the official language of the state.

title: Permitting and licensing
summary: Creates a searchable statewide catalog of state-issued credentials, requires annual agency reporting on applications, and sets published decision-time deadlines for cabinet agencies.

title: Derelict vessels
summary: Aims to reduce impacts from derelict vessels; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: DD residential settings data
summary: Requires a JLARC review and recurring DSHS reports on safety and placement stability in developmental disability residential settings, starting 2027-2028.

title: Urban growth area planning
summary: Requires counties to make their plans and regulations in cities' urban growth areas conform to the city's plans and rules, with compliance by the 2027 update cycle.

title: Rainier school dental care
summary: Creates a dental care pilot program at the Rainier School residential habilitation center.

title: Interference with emergency
summary: Makes people convicted of or deferred for reckless interference with emergency operations liable for emergency response costs, capped at $25,000.

title: Health technology assessment
summary: Concerns the health technology assessment program; the text provided does not say what it changes.

title: Regulated sports wagering
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Permits sports wagering on in-state college events, bans wagers on in-state college athletes, and makes threats against sports participants a class C felony.

title: Uniformed & overseas voting
summary: Conforms Washington voting law to the federal military and overseas voter act, expanding who qualifies and adding email and electronic ballot delivery.

title: Warehousing of alcohol
summary: Creates a bonded and nonbonded beer warehouse license allowing off-premises beer storage, with separation, tracking, zoning and monthly reporting requirements.

title: Health continuing ed./tax
summary: Exempts health care continuing education classes from state retail sales and use tax.

title: Stolen property/sentencing
summary: Concerns sentencing enhancements for theft, robbery, possessing stolen property, and trafficking stolen property; the summary does not state the direction of change.

title: Local government elections
summary: Lets local jurisdictions in one or more counties opt into ranked choice voting, with IRV or STV counting, primaries for single-winner races, and voter education requirements.

title: Medically tailored meals
summary: Sets standards for medically tailored meals that state agencies contract for Medicaid enrollees, including nutrition, vendor priority, and local-sourcing requirements.

title: Washing machine microplastic
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Requires commercial and industrial washing machines to have microfiber filters, with sale restrictions from 2028 and retrofits by 2034, and allows later residential rules and penalties.

title: Metal property
summary: Addresses theft and vandalism involving metal property, but the text provided does not specify the changes.

title: Self-insurers/claims
summary: Allows self-insurers to accept certain industrial insurance (workers' compensation) claims, expanding what they may cover.

title: Fuels/climate commitment act
summary: Lowers the emissions threshold for fuel suppliers in the cap-and-invest program, exempts lubricants from compliance, and bars certain fuel suppliers from public procurement contracts.

title: Emergency response
summary: Text is a short statement about protecting emergency responders and emergency response operations, with no specific provisions given.

title: Rehabilitative pathways
summary: Replaces the first-time offender waiver with court-granted pretrial deferral or suspended sentences for eligible first-time offenders, with community custody and revocation terms.

title: Workers' comp. medical care
summary: Expands injured workers' choice of providers and out-of-network care in workers' comp, adds employer notice duties, and sets a 10-day utilization review deadline.

title: Child care providers
summary: Requires zero-tolerance drug rules and immediate license suspension for child care, while allowing more mixed-age group time and waiving some repeat orientation.

title: CJTC oversight
summary: Changes peace officer certification hearings to a six-member panel with a peer officer, and requires law enforcement agencies to report training and decertification data to the CJTC.

title: Ungulate populations
summary: Requires WDFW to designate at-risk ungulate populations and implement predator mitigation, including wolf translocation and targeted predator removal, plus annual deer counts and reporting.

title: Weather modification
summary: Restricts weather modification activities, such as cloud seeding, under Washington law.

title: Irrigation dist. directors
summary: Addresses when irrigation district directors may hold beneficial interests in contracts; the text does not state the specific change.

title: Fire protection districts
summary: Requires cities forming fire districts after July 2026 to cut their levy rate, and excludes a fire district levy portion from the aggregate tax rate limit.

title: AI companion chatbots
topics: AI and technology; Children and families; Consumer protection and business
summary: Requires AI companion chatbot operators to disclose they are not human, protect minors, maintain suicide-prevention protocols, and makes violations Consumer Protection Act violations.

title: PTBA governing bodies
summary: Changes how the governing body of a public transportation benefit area is represented.

title: Affordable housing/REET
summary: Expands the REET exemption for affordable homeownership facilitator sales to drop labor participation requirements, with the exemption expiring January 1, 2030.

title: Scissor stairs
summary: Directs the State Building Code Council to convene a technical group to recommend code amendments allowing scissor stairs in multifamily buildings for the 2027 update.

title: Professional engineers
summary: Revises the Professional Engineers' Registration Act, including board membership, experience and exam requirements, applications, continuing development, and removal of obsolete language.

title: DD res. service providers
summary: Streamlines monitoring and oversight activities for community residential service providers serving people with developmental disabilities.

title: Felonies/postsecondary inst.
summary: Increases criminal penalties for felony offenses committed at postsecondary institutions.

title: Time-sensitive emergencies
summary: Requires the Department of Health to create a statewide data repository by 2031 to collect and analyze time-sensitive emergency data, including stroke, cardiac, and trauma events.

title: Retail bags
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Restricts thin film plastic carryout bags, raises the paper bag pass-through charge to 20 cents, adds manufacturer penalties, and bars charges to WIC and benefit card users.

title: School utility costs
summary: Addresses increased school utility costs caused by the Climate Commitment Act; the summary does not say what action it takes.

title: PRA firearm exemptions
summary: Exempts firearm purchase, transfer and concealed carry permit records and related documents from public disclosure, with limited sharing for law enforcement and court orders.

title: Housing finance commission
summary: Bars the Housing Finance Commission from directly making owner-occupied home mortgage loans, except certain down payment assistance, and repeals its Housing Finance Program and Plan.

title: Deputy state fire marshals
summary: Requires deputy state fire marshal pay to stay competitive with seven local fire agencies, with periodic OFM reviews, and orders a report on separating the State Fire Marshal's Office from the State Patrol.

title: Statewide food security
summary: Directs the Department of Agriculture to monitor food system performance, report on regulatory competitiveness, and recommend a statewide food security strategy.

title: Family burial grounds
summary: Lets private landowners designate family burial grounds with size, setback, and fireproofing limits, plus county recording and seller disclosure requirements.

title: Storage space rentals
summary: Lets self-storage rental agreements be signed electronically and deemed accepted after 30 days, and lengthens the termination notice period to 25 days.

title: Radiation dose standards
summary: Establishes radiation dose standards for operating ionizing radiation screening systems regulated by the Department of Health.

title: Preventive health services
summary: Delays and narrows state preventive-service coverage mandates for health plans, and shifts immunization coverage from ACIP recommendations to Department of Health recommendations.

title: Workers' comp./PTs & OTs
summary: Adds licensed physical and occupational therapists as eligible attending providers within the workers' compensation medical provider network.

title: Public records exemptions
topics: Children and families; Government and administration
summary: Removes or narrows confidentiality exemptions across several agencies, making more public records open to disclosure, including Financial Institutions investigations, blood analyses, and family court files.

title: Consumer-owned utilities
summary: Narrows Clean Energy Transformation Act coverage for some single-customer PUDs and residential self-generators, while broadening affected market customer definitions and requiring UTC compliance reporting.

title: Student firearm violations
summary: Extends firearm-related discipline authority to charter, tribal compact, deaf and blind schools and ESDs, allowing up to one-year suspensions or expulsions and limiting readmission.

title: Veterinarian relationship
summary: Defines the veterinarian-client-patient relationship and expands when veterinarians may provide ongoing and limited care through telehealth instead of in-person exams.

title: Corporate filings
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Revises Secretary of State corporate filing procedures, adds an initial report for some nonprofits and LLPs, and exempts remote workers from foreign entity doing-business rules.

title: Civil service/WaTech
summary: Adds WaTech officers and employees who perform network and systems security duties to the State Civil Service Law.

title: Charity care residency
summary: Limits hospital charity care eligibility to Washington residents, defines residency, and excludes people who enter the state mainly for health care.

title: Climate commit. act accounts
summary: Repeals three Climate Commitment Act accounts, creates operating and capital accounts, renames the transportation account, and expands allowable uses for electric vehicles.

title: State historical records
summary: Concerns preservation and inspection of state historical records; the provided text gives no specific changes.

title: DCYF licensing division
summary: Tightens DCYF foster and child care licensing rules, including attendance tracking, capacity enforcement, and fraud-based disqualification, while relaxing some kinship training requirements.

title: Partnership access line
summary: Allows a third-party administrator's costs for the partnership access line to be included in assessments on health carriers and employers, excluding other HCA administrative costs.

title: Litigation finance
summary: Regulates third-party litigation funding by requiring disclosure of funders and agreements, and voiding agreements that do not comply.

title: Unauthorized UCC filings
summary: Creates a process to terminate Uniform Commercial Code filings that were made without authorization.

title: Tax administration
summary: Removes alternative nicotine products from the list of tobacco products barred from mail or internet ordering or purchase, and makes implementation changes to two 2025 laws.

title: Animal control excise tax
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Authorizes cities and counties to levy a household excise tax to fund animal control and shelter operations, maintenance, and capital needs.

title: Initiatives and referenda
summary: Requires initiative sponsors to file 1,000 voter signatures, has the Secretary verify them, and bans pay-per-signature petition gathering with a private enforcement action.

title: Ballot measure petitions
summary: Adds signature-gatherer declaration requirements under penalty of false swearing and requires residence addresses to match voter registration for petition signatures to count.

title: Health care credentials
summary: Requires credentialed health care providers to wear visible ID badges, disclose credentials in advertising, and restricts use of 'physician surgeon' titles.

title: Signature education
summary: Adds cursive signature and election-signature instruction to high school civics, and requires reports on signature-mismatch ballot rejections by age group.

title: Public counsel
summary: Establishes a public counsel integrity act; the text provided does not describe its specific provisions.

title: Unemployment ins./layoffs
summary: Lets workers who voluntarily take part in an employer layoff plan keep unemployment eligibility, removing the employer 'final action' requirement for claims on or after June 14, 2026.

title: Extreme heat/tenants
summary: Bars landlords from restricting tenants' portable cooling devices, requires cooling facilities and notice, and bars sheriffs from physical evictions during extreme heat.

title: Supportive & emerg. housing
summary: Requires cities and counties to allow transitional, supportive, and indoor emergency shelter housing in urban growth areas, limits industrial siting, and caps local standards.

title: Urban forest management
summary: Directs Commerce to produce a model urban forestry ordinance prioritizing avoiding tree removal, then minimizing impacts, then mitigating, with updates every 10 years.

title: Mortgage escrow accounts
summary: Concerns residential mortgage loan escrow accounts; the summary does not say what changes.

title: Middle housing/uninc. areas
summary: Requires middle housing in rural and nonrural LAMIRDs to be served by public sewer or, in rural counties, a large on-site sewage system.

title: Lodging tax revenue use
summary: Gives small cities more flexibility in how they may spend lodging tax revenue.

title: Plastics/recycled content
summary: Sets higher post-consumer recycled content minimums for many plastic products and packaging, with some exemptions and changes to producer obligations.

title: Ski areas and winter sports
summary: Extends ski lift safety duties, skier conduct rules, and $1 million liability insurance requirements to aerial tramways, tows, and conveyors.

title: Embodied carbon/buildings
summary: Requires the State Building Code Council to adopt embodied carbon reduction standards for new, added-to, or renovated buildings of 100,000 square feet or more.

title: Commercial electronic mail
summary: Narrows the commercial email subject-line test to require knowledge of falsity and lowers statutory damages to $100 or actual damages.

title: Wildfire prevention
summary: Creates a council to oversee and administer a wildfire prevention fund and modifies utility wildfire mitigation plan requirements.

title: Home care rates
summary: Modifies home care rate statutes to improve how they function; the summary does not specify the changes.

title: Wildfire risk models
summary: The bill concerns wildfire risk models and disclosure of their scores, but the text gives no operative details.

title: Tourism promotion areas
summary: Removes the July 1, 2027 expiration date, letting tourism promotion areas keep collecting the $3 per night lodging charge.

title: Agriculture/PFAS chemicals
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Requires WSDA to set criteria by 2026 and review fertilizer and pesticide registrations from 2027, allowing refusal or cancellation of PFAS-containing products.

title: Legislator facility access
summary: Gives legislators access to state-owned facilities and to facilities that contract with or are licensed by state agencies.

title: State-tribal relationship
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Requires state agencies to consult tribes before actions affecting tribal cultural places and bars undue burdens on traditional practices absent a compelling interest.

title: Transition to kindergarten
summary: Supports implementation of transition to kindergarten programs; the text gives no details on rules or funding.

title: Medical loss ratio
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Requires fully insured health plans issued or renewed from 2028 to maintain at least a 90 percent medical loss ratio, and lets the commissioner collect related data in rate filings.

title: Litter reduction
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Cancels the scheduled 2028 thickness increase for plastic carryout bags, makes the 4-cent thick-bag penalty permanent, adds potato starch compostables, and creates a litter task force.

title: Carbon capture
summary: Lets electric utilities count power from certain gas plants with carbon capture toward Clean Energy Transformation Act obligations, treating them like renewables.

title: Social worker licensure
summary: Removes the exam requirement for advanced social workers and lets enhanced supervision count toward the 3,000 hours of required experience for independent clinical social worker licensure.

title: Pupil transp. safety net
summary: Provides state funding as a safety net for pupil transportation costs.

title: Env. programs/fee accounts
summary: Concerns dedicated accounts that hold fees collected to implement environmental programs.

title: Operating budget, supp.
summary: Supplemental operating budget for 2025-27 sets NGF-O appropriations at $79.9 billion and total funds at $156.2 billion.

title: Schools/sales tax
summary: Exempts schools and school districts from paying retail sales and use tax.

title: Kratom
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Creates a licensing regime for kratom retailers and processors, sets an age-21 limit, bans delivery and samples, and requires warning labels.

title: Small business stock gains
summary: Makes long-term capital gains from selling qualified small business stock subject to the capital gains tax, for gains on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Law enf. training/foreign
summary: Bars Washington law enforcement agencies and the Criminal Justice Training Commission from training programs, exchanges, or travel with foreign military, intelligence, or security services.

title: Use restrictions/food, med.
summary: Voids private deed restrictions that bar grocery stores or pharmacies where local land use rules otherwise allow them, and makes enforcing such restrictions unlawful.

title: Capital budget, supplemental
summary: Proposed 2026 supplemental capital budget adds $911 million in new appropriations for capital projects, $397 million financed by general obligation bonds.

title: Distributed energy resources
summary: Lets utilities invest in efficiency upgrades for rental housing, recover costs through tenant bills, and requires owners to give tenants 30 days' notice before work.

title: Grocery store incentives
summary: Exempts grocery store purchases of security and investigative services from sales tax and creates B&O and property tax preferences for grocery stores in underserved zones.

title: Property title protection
summary: Lets counties offer voluntary title fraud protection, letting owners block property transfers and delaying recording or refunds, and exempts related instruments from certain surcharges.

title: Independent living ombuds
summary: Establishes an independent living ombuds to support seniors in independent living facilities and continuing care retirement communities.

title: Worker health care costs
summary: Would assess employers for health care costs the state pays for their workers; the text gives no rates or details.

title: Paint producer resp.
summary: Concerns extended producer responsibility requirements for paint, which would place obligations on paint producers; the text gives no details.

title: Pharmacist prescriptive auth
summary: Expands pharmacists' prescriptive authority, allowing them to prescribe more under state law.

title: Employee microchipping
topics: AI and technology; Labor and employment
summary: Bans employers from requiring, requesting, or coercing employees to implant microchips, and lets employees sue for violations.

title: Condominium warranties
summary: Lets declarants or dealers offer a 2-10 warranty for condo units in small buildings of 12 or fewer units and four or fewer stories.

title: Travel vans
summary: Clarifies that travel vans are not classified as motor homes for vehicle registration purposes.

title: Transportation budget, supp.
summary: Supplemental 2025-27 transportation budget that increases appropriations by $1.08 billion and makes fund transfers.

title: Commute trip reduction/times
summary: Removes the fixed 6:00 to 9:00 a.m. window used to identify major employers, commute trips, and worksites for commute trip reduction.

title: Vehicle financial responsib.
summary: Addresses enforcement of motor vehicle liability insurance and financial responsibility requirements; the text gives no details of changes.

title: Postgrad degree requirements
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Bars the state compensation plan from requiring a postgraduate degree as the only way to show qualifications, unless law requires it for the job.

title: Sexually motivated assault
summary: Changes criminal classification and penalties for fourth-degree sexually motivated assault; the summary does not say whether penalties rise or fall.

title: Workforce board admin.
summary: Adjusts the WEIAO Board's internal administration and reporting, and eliminates its public data dashboard requirement.

title: Shared leave/immigration
summary: Authorizes shared leave for workers who are absent because of immigration enforcement actions.

title: Public grocery stores
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Authorizes cities to create publicly owned grocery stores in underserved areas, with capital grants, food locker systems, TIF, and eminent domain.

title: DD RHC dental care services
summary: Addresses dental care services provided at residential habilitation centers; the title gives no detail on specific changes.

title: Cannabis oversupply
summary: Addresses preventing an oversupply of cannabis; the text gives no details on how.

title: Shrubsteppe/land use
summary: Bars treating shrubsteppe in urban growth areas as protected habitat or critical areas, and bars requiring its mitigation, replacement, or penalties.

title: Early learning licensing
summary: Exempts Early Childhood Education and Assistance Program and Head Start programs from DCYF licensing when they run school-day operations in public school or college buildings.

title: Early achievers awards
summary: Allows Early Achievers providers to count children in ECEAP or Head Start toward the 5 percent threshold needed to qualify for a quality improvement award.

title: DD RHC facilities renaming
summary: Renames four state developmental disability residential habilitation centers and directs DSHS to update rules to reflect the new names.

title: Firearm manufacturing
summary: Bans 3D-printed or CNC-made manufacture of machine guns, undetectable and untraceable firearms, and frames or receivers, and restricts sharing digital gun-making code.

title: 3D printer blocking tech.
summary: Requires three-dimensional printers to be equipped with certain blocking technologies, apparently to prevent printing weapons.

title: Alternative jet fuel
summary: Aims to give certainty for developing low-to-zero carbon alternative jet fuel production in Washington; the text gives no mechanism.

title: Traffic stops/blue envelope
summary: Requires the Department of Licensing to create a Blue Envelope Program, with free envelopes, to help neurodiverse drivers communicate with officers during traffic stops.

title: Child of veteran/tuition
summary: Extends the time a veteran's child has to use a disability-based tuition waiver to eight years from the parent's disability determination if made after age 18.

title: Tourism assessment
summary: Authorizes a Tourism Assessment Program that levies a percentage of business gross revenue, governed by an expanded Authority board and a Ratepayer Oversight Board.

title: Emerg. med. service levies
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets fire protection districts impose an EMS levy on areas not covered by another taxing district's EMS levy, if voters in those areas approve.

title: County forest board lands
summary: Directs an audit of county forest board lands.

title: School maps
summary: Requires schools to create and maintain maps as part of their safe school plans.

title: Midwife supervision
summary: Adds licensed midwives to the list of health care practitioners who may supervise medical assistants.

title: State campus district energy
summary: Directs a committee to create a framework for recommending capital funding for decarbonizing state campus district energy systems.

title: Pediatric care rates
summary: Aims to prevent reductions in access to pediatric primary care and behavioral health services, apparently through rate provisions; details are not in the text.

title: Driver privacy
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Health care; Immigration
summary: Generally bans state and local ALPR use, allowing it only for listed purposes with watch-list limits, retention rules, audits, and bans on immigration and protected health care uses.

title: Political violence
summary: Allows candidates and officials to use campaign and surplus funds for proportional personal security measures, with limits on paying relatives or related entities.

title: Cash transactions/pennies
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Allows in-person cash totals and change to be rounded to the nearest 5 cents, with taxes unchanged and local rules and Consumer Protection Act claims preempted.

title: B&O tax increases repeal
summary: Repeals the business and occupation (B&O) tax increases enacted in 2025.

title: Independent medical exams
summary: Lets workers' compensation independent medical exams be recorded through a state-approved, application-based third-party platform.

title: Individual providers/family
summary: Repeals the requirement that paid family individual providers of long-term care begin continuing education by January 1, 2027.

title: Community weatherization
summary: Allows weatherization grant funds to pay for community-scaled projects across multiple units, exempt from the all-low-income occupancy rule, prioritizing low-income households.

title: Nursing
summary: Updates nursing license rules: drops transcript submission for applicants, allows interim practice permits, clarifies ARNP titles, and continues CRNA controlled-substance authority.

title: Nursing assistants/SUD prg.
summary: Bars online posting of enforcement actions against compliant nursing assistants in substance use monitoring, and extends Board stipends to cover monitoring program costs for them.

title: National voter reg. day
summary: A ceremonial measure celebrating National Voter Registration Day, with no policy effect.

title: Religious liberty commission
summary: Establishes a Washington state religious liberty commission; the summary does not describe its powers or duties.

title: Game farm/water quality
summary: Requires WDFW's publicly owned game farms that meet CAFO thresholds to obtain Ecology water discharge permits, with the strictest standards for large game bird facilities.

title: Safe cookware
summary: Aims to give consumers access to safe cookware and provide trade certainty in regulating lead in cookware; operative provisions are not specified.

title: Paid leave contributions
summary: Reallocates paid leave premium shares between employees and employers, with employees paying the full medical leave share and overall obligations roughly unchanged.

title: Middle housing/perf. codes
summary: Concerns performance-based building codes for middle housing; the summary gives no details on specific requirements.

title: Luxury aircraft tax
summary: Repeals the state luxury aircraft tax in its entirety, eliminating that tax on aircraft purchases.

title: Timber sale process
summary: Adds standards governing sales and transfers of certain state-acquired lands, including the timber sale process.

title: Sexually violent predators
summary: Expands who must receive advance notice before sexually violent predators are released, transferred, or discharged, and sets a seven-day deadline for notice after court-ordered release.

title: DD RHC federal compliance
summary: Requires DSHS to post and share notices when a residential habilitation center is out of federal compliance, including with residents' designees and legislative committees.

title: Emergency response
summary: Bars counties, cities, towns and incident command systems from using resources to help enforce laws that target emergency responders based on protected traits, including immigration status.

title: Conflict of interest
summary: Lowers the ownership threshold for state officers' conflicts of interest to 1 percent and bars them from accepting compensation from certain owners in state transactions.

title: Capital predesign thresholds
summary: Raises the capital construction predesign threshold from $10 million to $15 million and requires annual OFM inflation adjustments starting July 2027.

title: Common interest communities
summary: Exempts small middle-housing common interest communities from most WUCIOA rules and raises the association audit threshold from $50,000 to $100,000.

title: Domestic workers
summary: Establishes labor protections for domestic workers, such as nannies, caregivers, housekeepers, and cooks working four or more hours a month in private homes.

title: PRA/homicide cases
summary: Lets homicide victims' next of kin sue under the Public Records Act to block disclosure of law enforcement records about the homicide.

title: Civil air patrol
summary: Creates a Washington Civil Air Patrol division, sets its membership and leadership rules, and lets the Governor order it into state service.

title: Aquifer recharge areas
summary: Requires local governments to consider critical aquifer recharge areas when revising urban growth area boundaries.

title: Affordable housing funding
summary: Modifies requirements and allowed uses for certain state funding that supports affordable housing and related services.

title: Albuterol access in schools
summary: Lets schools and private schools keep albuterol inhalers on site from 2027-28, with trained staff administering it under a standing order and limited liability protections.

title: Small loans maximum amount
summary: Raises the maximum small loan limit from $700 to $1,200, adjusted biennially for Seattle-area CPI inflation, capped at 30 percent of gross monthly income.

title: Impaired driving
summary: Lowers the blood alcohol limit for impaired driving and related offenses, license sanctions, and probation conditions from 0.08 to 0.05, with a public campaign and WSIPP evaluation.

title: Music therapy exemptions
summary: Lets music therapy license applicants practice under a licensed therapist's supervision for up to six months while exam results are verified, starting in 2028.

title: Poverty reduction task force
summary: Renames and restructures the poverty reduction task force and advisory council, adds state agency members, and redefines their duties around the 10-year poverty plan.

title: Digital opportunities
topics: AI and technology; Government and administration
summary: Expands the Statewide Broadband Office's mission to promote broadband adoption and digital equity, reshapes the Digital Equity Forum, and renames the grant program.

title: School board compensation
summary: Concerns school board member compensation; the text gives no details of what would change.

title: Coal-fired electric plant
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Ends cap-and-invest exemptions and greenhouse gas standard limits for older coal plants after 2025, and repeals sales and use tax exemptions for coal used in power generation.

title: Quantum technology industry
summary: Directs state efforts to develop the quantum technology industry for economic development and workforce; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Local foods/public schools
summary: Creates a voluntary Washington Local Food for Schools Program within OSPI to increase procurement of Washington-grown foods for school districts.

title: Housing assessment & support
summary: Concerns assessment and support requirements for housing; the text is too brief to show specific changes.

title: Imagination library program
summary: Transfers the Imagination Library children's book program from the Department of Children, Youth, and Families to OSPI.

title: Workers' compensation
summary: Requires workers' compensation time-loss recipients to receive 100% of the employer's prior monthly healthcare payment, unless the employer keeps paying for benefits.

title: Electric utility bill assist
summary: Requires electric utilities to offer a monthly low-income bill discount with income tiers, streamlined enrollment, multilingual outreach, and expanded reporting.

title: Electric motorcycle, bicycle
summary: Concerns regulation of electric-assisted bicycles and electric motorcycles; the summary does not state the specific change.

title: Running start allocations
summary: Concerns the Running Start allocations granted to school districts; the summary gives no details on amounts or changes.

title: Property tax
summary: Exempts seniors, disabled people and qualifying veterans in the SPTE program from the consolidated levy and raises its income thresholds and maximum exemption.

title: Pay transparency/applicants
summary: Defines the term "applicant" to clarify pay transparency enforcement, without changing the underlying disclosure requirements.

title: HVAC scope/electricians
summary: Directs L&I to adopt rules clarifying the scope of work for HVAC/refrigeration specialty electricians on ductless mini-split systems.

title: Emergency tolling suspension
summary: Requires WSDOT to suspend tolling on possible evacuation routes during a multi-property level 3 or "go now" evacuation notice, until no longer needed.

title: Financial services apps
summary: Protects consumers' personal information when they use financial services apps on mobile or internet-connected devices.

title: Low-rise res. buildings
summary: Directs the building code council to create a performance-based compliance pathway for low-rise residential buildings, recognize third-party certifications, and allow embodied carbon reductions to offset some energy requirements.

title: Tobacco product excise taxes
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Adds a 10-cent-per-cigarette excise tax, about $2 per pack, on cigarettes starting July 1, 2027.

title: Involuntary treatment act
summary: Bill concerning the involuntary treatment act; the text provided does not state what changes.

title: Continuing care retirement
summary: Requires continuing care retirement communities offering life care contracts to submit actuarial analyses reviewed by the Insurance Commissioner, with registration fees covering review costs.

title: Medicaid access program
summary: Requires the state to seek federal approval and raise Medicaid professional service rates toward Medicare levels, and extends the program's expiration to 2032.

title: Garnishment forms
summary: Replaces statutory garnishment answer forms with a Washington Pattern Forms Committee form or substantially similar form for continuing earnings liens.

title: Elected sheriffs
summary: Bars uncertified elected sheriffs from performing reserved law enforcement actions and lets decertification trigger recall proceedings, with a special election for mandatory decertification.

title: Distributed energy/ag. lands
summary: Lets counties and cities allow distributed energy facilities as an accessory use on agricultural land.

title: Criminal offenses under 18
summary: Expands juvenile alternatives to confinement, making suspended dispositions the default, widening Option B and C eligibility, and allowing appeals of commitment decisions.

title: Fenestration certification
summary: Establishes fenestration (window and door) certification requirements for certain public works contracts.

title: PRA/lists of individuals
summary: Amends the Public Records Act on disclosure of lists of individuals; the text gives no detail on the change.

title: Hazardous facility workforce
summary: Requires building and construction contractors to use a skilled and trained workforce for work at certain hazardous facilities.

title: Correctional fac. liability
summary: Limits correctional facility liability for inmate injuries from voluntary controlled substance use when lawful intake and medical care requirements are met.

title: Insurance crimes
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Expands the insurance fraud crime and program to cover schemes harming consumers and beneficiaries, makes insurance fraud a class B felony, and adds restitution requirements.

title: Private docks and buoys
summary: Authorizes additional use of certain private recreational docks and mooring buoys, according to a one-line description with no further detail.

title: Agency decision direct rev.
summary: Allows direct review of administrative agency decisions in certain circumstances; the text is brief and procedural.

title: Fire services mobilization
summary: Requires the Washington State Patrol to ensure fire mobilization reimbursements reach host districts and agencies within 60 days of receiving complete documentation.

title: Maritime trade ed. assist.
summary: Creates business and occupation and public utility tax credits for small employers that provide maritime trade educational assistance.

title: Prop. insurance assignments
summary: Prohibits and voids assignments of post-loss property insurance benefits from insured persons to contractors or other service providers.

title: Social media content
topics: AI and technology; Children and families; Consumer protection and business
summary: Requires vloggers earning $12,000+ to register with DOR and requires platforms to withhold part of pay from videos featuring minors into trust accounts.

title: Boys and men commission
summary: Creates a nine-member Boys and Men Commission as a standalone agency, contingent on nonstate funding through 2029.

title: Phthalates/medical equipment
summary: Bans DEHP phthalates in IV solution containers from 2030 and IV tubing from 2035, with exemptions, shortage waivers, and a limited delay option.

title: Sex offenders/registration
summary: Lowers the penalty for third-or-later Failure to Register offenses to a class C felony, sets mandatory community custody for repeat violations, and directs DOC reentry planning for sex offenders.

title: Special fuels taxes
summary: Reduces taxes on special fuels, which would lower state fuel excise tax revenue.

title: PTSD treatment and research
summary: Creates a PTSD workers' compensation pilot letting opted-in workers get treatment before claim adjudication, plus workplace behavioral health grants and a 2030 report.

title: LNI communication methods
summary: Lets the Labor and Industries Department send many notices electronically, with paper options, and changes some appeal and rulemaking notice timelines.

title: Wildfire mitigation grants
summary: Creates a wildfire mitigation grant program. The text does not specify funding amounts or eligible uses.

title: Obsolete statutory language
summary: Removes expired and obsolete statutory references, including COVID-era shared leave authority, 2013 wage and award prohibitions, and 1980s salary language.

title: Agricultural employees/PERC
summary: Places agricultural workers' collective bargaining under PERC, setting up union certification, election procedures, and interest arbitration for farmworker bargaining.

title: Commercial truck council
summary: Creates a commercial truck safety council under the Traffic Safety Commission and doubles the commercial vehicle enforcement fee to fund its recommended programs.

title: Shared leave
summary: Authorizes shared leave for employees who are hate crime victims or whose absence results from immigration enforcement actions against them or a relative.

title: Superior court judge/Yakima
summary: Adds a ninth superior court judge position in Yakima County, increasing the number of judges from eight to nine.

title: Electric utilities/adequacy
summary: Aims to give regulatory certainty for utility investments in new energy generation to meet Washington's energy needs under the Clean Energy Transformation Act.

title: Wildland firefighters/LEOFF
summary: Addresses whether wildland and aviation firefighters may be members of the LEOFF law enforcement and firefighters' retirement system.

title: DSHS unexpected fatalities
summary: Requires DSHS to review unexpected deaths of residents in its facilities, report findings to the Legislature, and create corrective action plans.

title: Waste to energy facilities
summary: Gives pre-1992 waste-to-energy facilities free emissions allowances through 2030, with banking and conditions, and requires a 2030 emissions and waste reduction plan.

title: Military code/victim rights
summary: Adds protections for victims of offenses committed while serving in Washington's organized militia to the state code of military justice.

title: Permit review
summary: Sets strict permit review deadlines and fee refunds for residential project permits, and limits completeness checks to procedural review.

title: Address confid./ALJs & OAH
summary: Expands the Address Confidentiality Program to cover administrative law judges and staff at the Office of Administrative Hearings who are threatened or harassed.

title: Small works roster limits
summary: Raises the dollar limits for public works contracts awarded through small works rosters, in stages from 2027 to 2030.

title: Tires/6PPD and substitutes
summary: Starting 2035, bans sale of new vehicle tires containing 6PPD or Ecology-identified regrettable substitutes, with exemptions for certain federal aviation, defense, homeland security and NASA products.

title: Private security guards
summary: Removes security guard license fees for applicants, requires employers to pay employee licensing fees, and bars deducting those costs from wages.

title: Retirement distributions
summary: Protects consumers from unreasonable delays in processing retirement account distributions.

title: Temporary staffing/sales tax
summary: Exempts temporary staffing services from the retail sales tax, reducing state sales tax collection on those services.

title: Nursing delegation
summary: Expands nurses' ability to delegate tasks to nursing assistants and home care aides, including subcutaneous injections, and removes setting-specific and insulin-training requirements.

title: Pollution control appeals
summary: Aims to improve efficiency in appeals to the Pollution Control Hearings Board; the text gives no substantive details.

title: Tattoo artist training
summary: Establishes the Ink of Hope Act concerning tattoo artist training; the text gives no specific requirements or effects.

title: Life insurance policy lapses
summary: Requires insurers to send written lapse-for-nonpayment notices to policyholders and designated third parties, with proof of delivery, for individual life policies issued after the effective date.

title: Youth behavioral health
summary: Extends the Children and Youth Behavioral Health Work Group to 2031, creates a Governor's leadership council, and requires alignment with the Washington Thriving Strategic Plan.

title: Crime victim penalty assess.
summary: Raises crime victim penalty assessments to $1,000 for felonies and $500 for misdemeanors, allows surcharges up to $50,000 for wealthy defendants, and limits waivers to indigent defendants.

title: Nonprofit halls/fundraising
summary: Raises from 15 to 50 days the limit on regularly scheduled fundraising in nonprofit-owned halls that keeps them eligible for property tax exemption, starting with 2027 taxes.

title: Students/surplus technology
summary: Exempts school districts from surplus property public notice rules when selling or granting surplus student technology at depreciated cost, prioritizing students with greatest need.

title: Cannabis excise tax
summary: Concerns the cannabis excise tax; the text gives no details of any change.

title: Rabies medication
summary: Seeks to ensure availability of rabies medication for postexposure prophylaxis; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Leg. Indian affairs office
summary: Creates a legislative branch Office on Indian Affairs to provide tribal-affairs training and resources to legislators and legislative staff.

title: Oil tanker escort
summary: Requires oil tankers of 40,000 to 125,000 deadweight tons entering Puget Sound to have a tug escort meeting specified horsepower standards.

title: Opioid treatment prg. fees
summary: Lets the Department of Health seek federal approval to accredit opioid treatment programs, set accreditation fees in rule, and use opioid settlement funds to cover costs.

title: Early education scholarship
summary: Creates the SEEDS Scholarship, funded at $10 million a year from the GET account, for low-to-moderate income students in early childhood education programs who commit to working in early learning centers.

title: Tobacco product policy
summary: Raises tobacco and vapor license fees to $1,000 and creates a voluntary responsible vendor training program that halves penalties for participants.

title: Education ombuds records
summary: Makes identifying information from education ombuds complainants confidential, limits its disclosure, and gives complainants access to their own records.

title: Survivor insurance/LEOFF
summary: Expands medical premium reimbursement for survivors of LEOFF 2 members killed on duty to cover Medicare Parts A and B and continued employer coverage.

title: Local government fund use
topics: Government and administration; Housing; Taxes and budget
summary: Expands local governments' authority to use housing, real estate and rental car tax revenues, and to extend property tax levy lid lifts.

title: Armed forces reserve grant
summary: Creates a new postsecondary education grant for members of the armed forces reserve.

title: Scholarship contributions
summary: Requires Washington to participate in the federal tax credit for individual contributions to scholarship granting organizations.

title: Probate
summary: Tightens who may serve as estate personal representative, adds petition and bond requirements, and sets venue rules for suitable-person appointments.

title: Quantum technology industry
summary: Requires Commerce to develop a state quantum technology strategy by June 30, 2027, using outside gifts, grants, or contracted help.

title: State shark
summary: Designates the bluntnose sixgill shark as Washington's official state shark.

title: State expenditure limit
summary: Reinstates a state expenditure limit to promote sustainable budgets and provide permanent tax relief for Washingtonians.

title: Zero-based budget reviews
summary: Proposes zero-based budget reviews to reform the state budgeting process; the text gives no details.

title: Food assistance/state prg.
summary: Maintains state food assistance for certain individuals who would otherwise lose federal food benefits due to federal eligibility changes.

title: Local tax increment fin.
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Adds conditions and limits for local tax increment areas, including project analysis, taxing district consultation, and mitigation negotiation or arbitration.

title: Rent increase notice service
summary: Changes how MHLTA rent increase notices must be served, switching from unlawful detainer service rules to the same methods used for other MHLTA notices.

title: Psychiatric pharmacists
summary: Concerning psychiatric pharmacists; the title alone does not state any specific change to law.

title: Infrastructure materials
summary: Reduces regulatory burdens on small producers of infrastructure materials, according to its title; the text gives no specifics.

title: Foster care housing pilot
summary: Creates a two-year, 50-youth rental assistance pilot for homeless or at-risk foster youth and requires transition planning before age 21.

title: Juvenile firearm interv.
summary: Creates an early intervention alternative for juveniles charged with second-degree unlawful firearm possession, available only with prosecutor agreement.

title: Crime victim penalty assess.
summary: Raises crime victim penalty assessments and allows surcharges up to $50,000 for defendants with substantial resources, narrowing waivers for indigent defendants.

title: College grant/credential prg
summary: Extends Washington College Grant eligibility to nondegree credential programs starting 2027-28 and requires a proposed maximum award amount by December 2026.

title: Schools outside UGAs
summary: Allows school districts to site schools serving urban students in rural areas near existing schools, overriding county planning policies and requiring utility extensions.

title: Vacancies in partisan office
summary: Requires an appointee to a vacant partisan office to share the party of the former official when that official declared a party preference.

title: Commission on boys and men
summary: Establishes a Washington state commission on boys and men to study issues affecting them.

title: Unpiloted aircraft systems
summary: Addresses unpiloted aircraft systems (drones) and countering them; the summary does not state specific rules or funding.

title: Farmers/food programs
summary: Expands food donation eligibility to at-risk dairy and directs a new Agriculture grant program for hunger relief groups buying directly from farmers.

title: Private detention/reports
summary: Addresses reporting requirements and law enforcement responses for incidents at private detention facilities; the text gives no specifics.

title: Water recreation facilities
summary: Requires DOH to create a water recreation user safety guide and requires short-term rentals with such facilities to post it.

title: Social workers board
summary: Creates a Washington state board of governors for licensed social workers.

title: Fifth-wheel travel trailers
summary: Allows fifth-wheel recreational trailers up to 46 feet long to be operated on public highways, defining the covered vehicle type.

title: DSHS terminology
summary: Updates outdated references to eliminated DSHS administrations, replacing them with current agency components, and makes technical harmonizing changes.

title: Public bank task force
summary: Creates a task force to study the feasibility of establishing a state-owned public bank. It does not create the bank itself.

title: On-base school construction
summary: Increases state school construction assistance by 15 percentage points for projects on military bases and excludes on-base space from district inventory calculations.

title: Collective bargaining
summary: Conditionally establishes private-sector collective bargaining if federal preemption ends or the NLRB declines jurisdiction, and gives PERC authority to administer it.

title: Fire sprinkler work
summary: Adds enforcement tools for fire sprinkler contractor and fitter licensing, including stop-work orders, infraction penalties, investigations, and removal of unlicensed work.

title: Leadership board/gifts
summary: Authorizes the Washington state leadership board to solicit gifts, grants, and endowments from public or private sources.

title: Postsecondary closures
summary: Requires colleges that close or discontinue programs to offer teach-outs or transfer agreements, refund students, and void related student debt.

title: Language access
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Government and administration
summary: Requires the Office of Equity to create language-access guidelines for state agencies, collect agency implementation reports, and propose fixes for interpreter and translator shortages.

title: Theater licenses/alcohol
summary: Creates a spirits, beer, and wine license for small theaters, conditioned on alcohol control plans, ID scanners, and staff training.

title: Real estate appraisals
summary: Addresses legal actions arising from real estate appraisal activity; the short text does not specify substantive changes.

title: Wage enforcement discretion
summary: Lets the Labor Department investigate wage complaints with set deadlines, tolls wage claim limitations, seeks penalties for willful violations, and requires a public complaint-priority process.

title: Unpaid wage recovery
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Creates a Wage Recovery Program that lets the Department pay unpaid low-wage workers early, in exchange for waiving appeal and private lawsuit rights, funded by wage civil penalties.

title: Residential dev./zones
summary: Bars large cities from excluding housing in commercial zones or requiring mixed-use or ground-floor retail as a condition of residential development.

title: Retail pricing
topics: AI and technology; Consumer protection and business
summary: Bans surveillance-based and surge pricing in grocery retail, delays electronic shelf labels in large stores until 2030, requires a Commerce study, and enforces violations under the Consumer Protection Act.

title: LEOFF 2 retiree/police chief
summary: Allows retired LEOFF 2 members to serve as police chiefs in small police departments.

title: Data broker registry
topics: AI and technology; Consumer protection and business
summary: Requires data brokers to register annually with the Department of Licensing starting 2028, disclosing data practices and opt-out options, with public posting of registrations.

title: Youth development fund
summary: Creates a youth development fund account to increase access to positive youth development programs.

title: Paid leave benefits
summary: Concerns paid family medical leave benefits, but the text does not say whether it expands, restricts, or otherwise changes them.

title: State energy code costs
summary: Aims to control costs imposed by the state energy code, but the text gives no specific changes.

title: Insurer taxes
summary: Expands the B&O tax exemption for insurance premiums, applies it retroactively to 2019, waives certain penalties, and adds a Workforce Education Investment Surcharge exemption for insurers.

title: Rural hospital payments
summary: Makes payments for services provided by rural emergency hospitals subject to legislative appropriation.

title: Public space/local use laws
summary: Bars local governments from enforcing laws against life-sustaining activities on public property unless adequate alternative shelter is available, with defenses and private injunctive suits.

title: Ex. medical placement
summary: Adds an alternative qualifying condition for extraordinary medical placement of incarcerated individuals, widening eligibility for medical release or placement.

title: WaTech/PRA exemption
summary: Exempts information submitted to WaTech for Digital Experience Platform services from public disclosure under the Public Records Act.

title: Apprenticeships/wellness
summary: Requires building-trade apprenticeships to include behavioral health and wellness training starting 2027, and lets electricians and plumbers count up to four such hours toward continuing education.

title: Crime victims & witnesses
summary: Aims to support crime victims and witnesses through victim-centered, trauma-informed responses; specific mechanisms are not described.

title: Asbestos training rules
summary: Concerns the Department of Labor and Industries' authority to adopt rules regulating asbestos training.

title: Removal of vehicles
summary: Lets tow operators immediately remove unattended vehicles that obstruct streetcar operation or threaten safety in streetcar rights-of-way in cities over 700,000.

title: EFSEC tribal consultation
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Requires EFSEC to offer government-to-government consultation with affected federally recognized tribes on energy site applications, and exempts those meetings from the Open Public Meetings Act.

title: Child welfare response
summary: Aims to address rising child maltreatment fatalities by supporting families that have already received a child welfare response.

title: Nursing education programs
summary: Changes standards for nursing education programs; the summary gives no detail on the specific changes.

title: Conservation districts
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Drops the farm-operator requirement for some conservation district supervisors, lets districts opt into Title 29A elections, and requires supervisors and certain candidates to file financial disclosures.

title: Transfers to charities
summary: Requires holders of property with charitable beneficiary designations to notify charities after an owner's death and transfer the property to them on affidavit.

title: Real estate disclosure form
summary: Changes the seller disclosure statement for residential property with heating oil tanks to point buyers to state remediation assistance, effective for sales on or after January 1, 2027.

title: Local gov./sales & use tax
summary: Removes certain sales and use tax exemptions to raise local government funding.

title: AI training data
summary: Requires generative AI developers to publish training-data documentation, enforceable under the Consumer Protection Act.

title: Interstate cannabis market
summary: Prepares for a legal interstate cannabis market; the text gives no operative provisions showing what changes.

title: Adult family home licensure
summary: Creates exemptions from adult family home licensing for certain foster family home licensees and child-specific license holders who cared for former foster youth.

title: Sex offender reg. compliance
summary: Requires certain persons to be in full compliance with sex offender and kidnapping offender registration requirements.

title: Sex offender information
summary: Expands the information that sex offenders and kidnapping offenders must provide when registering.

title: Office of independent inves.
summary: Expands the Office of Independent Investigations' jurisdiction and notification duties over police force incidents involving deaths, and exempts its investigative records from public disclosure.

title: EFSEC application review
summary: Streamlines energy facility siting by limiting adjudication topics, granting SEPA categorical exemptions and deeming design-standard compliance to mitigate impacts, and mandating expedited processing for solar, wind, storage and transmission projects.

title: Community cust. supervision
summary: Requires DOC to supervise certain stalking offenders on community custody who are assessed as high risk to reoffend against the same victim, regardless of risk classification.

title: Imminent physical harm/child
summary: Defines 'imminent physical harm' for child removal decisions as substantial risk of serious harm, including conditions like substance use and emotional neglect.

title: Real estate/exclusive market
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Consumer protection and business; Housing
summary: Bars real estate brokers from exclusive-group marketing of residential property unless it is also marketed publicly, with DOL discipline and WLAD unfair-practice liability.

title: Plumbing contractors
summary: Limits plumbing license suspensions for three infractions to residential work; non-residential work requires five infractions in five years, and single inspections count as one.

title: War on terror memorial
summary: Establishes a global war on terror memorial on the state capitol campus.

title: Large energy use facilities
summary: Defines 'emerging large energy use facility' (20+ MW data processing or hosting sites) and 'ELEUF tariff or policy' for utility electricity rates; creates no obligations.

title: Rodenticides
summary: Bans use of anticoagulant rodenticides and bromethalin rodenticides from 2027 through 2028, with an emergency-use exception, and orders reports and a study.

title: High cap. transit permits
summary: Gives municipalities enhanced permitting tools for high capacity transit projects; the text gives no further detail on funding or requirements.

title: Electric vehicles/sale
summary: Concerns electric vehicle sales and the relationship between manufacturers and vehicle dealers; the text does not state specific changes.

title: Utilities/education entities
summary: Requires utilities to offer discounted rates to entities providing public elementary and secondary education.

title: Emergency meetings
summary: Lets county governing bodies hold emergency meetings remotely or outside the county seat, and act without first offering public listening access.

title: Firearms background checks
summary: Lets the Washington State Patrol set firearms background check fees at a level that covers program administration costs.

title: Preventive dental care
summary: Aims to advance oral health equity and protect access to preventive dental care; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Community reinvestment prg.
summary: Creates a Community Reinvestment Program with a participatory plan, a work group on joint Equity-Commerce administration, and a WSIPP study, using existing appropriations.

title: Security guards board
summary: Creates a security guard standards board to set minimum pay, paid leave, benefits and training rules, with penalties for violations and fees funding the board.

title: Heritage orchard program
summary: Directs WSU to create a Heritage Orchard Program with a registry of heritage orchards and a list of rare apple varieties, contingent on budget funding.

title: Prostitution
summary: Expands the patronizing and prostitution offenses, raises fines and felony penalties for repeat patronizing, directs fee revenue to survivor-led services, and limits some arrests.

title: Eventual tenant ownership
summary: Expands opportunities for tenants to own their homes through eventual tenant ownership programs under the federal low-income housing tax credit.

title: Real estate excise taxes/GMA
summary: Lets fully planning GMA counties and their cities impose REET 2 real estate excise tax without voter approval.

title: DCYF accountability board
summary: Renames the DCYF Oversight Board as the Accountability Board, states its oversight purpose, and places it in the Office of Financial Management for administrative purposes.

title: Aquatics/sports PFD deadline
summary: Repeals the deadline for creating a regional aquatics and sports public facilities district, leaving its creation open without a time limit.

title: Quality assurance fee
summary: Freezes the hospital quality assurance fee rate at its July 2025 level and requires periodic adjustment of Medicaid add-on payments to match available fee revenue.

title: Nitrous oxide sale
summary: Makes it a gross misdemeanor to sell, distribute or offer nitrous oxide canisters or flavored nitrous oxide devices.

title: Sexually violent predators
summary: Modifies procedures for releasing sexually violent predators to less restrictive alternative placements.

title: Military families/education
summary: Requires school districts to admit military-connected children across district lines, accept early and flexible applications, and transfer their IEPs and 504 plans.

title: Postsecondary/med. abortion
summary: Addresses access to medication abortion at public postsecondary institutions; the summary does not state the specific change.

title: Wineries/restaurant license
summary: Lets licensed domestic wineries hold spirits, beer and wine restaurant licenses at additional winery locations, with the same privileges as standard restaurant licenses.

title: Emissions/trade-exposed
summary: Addresses emissions from emissions-intensive, trade-exposed facilities under the Climate Commitment Act; the summary does not state the change.

title: Part-time faculty pay
summary: Requires community and technical college part-time faculty pay to rise to 85% of full-time tenured faculty pay by 2030-31, with SBCTC progress reports.

title: Inmate funds
summary: Raises the inmate indigency threshold to $100, requires periodic CPI-based increases, and mandates public posting of the indigent rate.

title: EMT recertification
summary: Requires EMTs certified more than ten years in Washington to recertify every six years.

title: Peace officer use of force
summary: Changes the standard used to judge whether a peace officer's use of force is reasonable.

title: Animal testing alternatives
summary: Prohibits drug developers and testing facilities from using animal tests when a validated alternative exists, with violations treated as Consumer Protection Act violations.

title: County clerk fees
summary: Modifies and updates the statutory fees county clerks charge for preparing certain documents.

title: Upper Columbia water rights
summary: Requires Ecology to start a general water rights adjudication of the upper Columbia River, with a two-stage pilot for serving summonses and a later evaluation report.

title: Coronary interventions
summary: Requires the Department of Health to adopt by July 2027 certificate-of-need criteria for elective coronary interventions at ambulatory surgical facilities.

title: Health carrier overpayments
summary: Standardizes how health carriers must recover overpayments; the text gives no further detail on the rules.

title: Federal custody contracts
summary: Concerns contracts between the federal government and county or municipal jails to hold people in federal custody; the text gives no details.

title: Health care market standards
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Expands health care material-change notice rules to hospital ownership, asset sales, and nonprofit-to-for-profit conversions, adds filing fees, and extends the Attorney General's review period.

title: Cardiac emerg. plans/schools
summary: Requires schools to adopt cardiac emergency response plans.

title: Free transit/CTC students
summary: Adds community and technical college students to the riders transit agencies must carry free to qualify for state grants.

title: School district solvency
summary: Addresses financial solvency of school districts; the text gives no specific mechanism or amount.

title: Transportation contracting
summary: Authorizes WSDOT and Sound Transit to use a MATOC alternative process for awarding transportation construction contracts, with rosters, notice, and reporting requirements.

title: Insurance mortgagee clauses
summary: Concerns mortgagee clauses in insurance; the text gives no detail on specific changes.

title: Tribal fishing rights
summary: Repeals Initiative Measure No. 456 in its entirety; the bill's title concerns tribal fishing rights.

title: Traditional health/medicaid
summary: Directs the Health Care Authority to seek a federal waiver so Medicaid covers traditional health care practices delivered through Indian Health Service or tribal facilities.

title: Washington state public bank
summary: Creates a Washington state public bank; the text gives no details on its powers, capitalization or rules.

title: Sp. ed. evaluation reports
summary: Gives parents access to special education evaluation reports for their children.

title: Mental health sentencing alt
summary: Concerns the mental health sentencing alternative; the text gives no detail on what changes.

title: Affordable housing funding
summary: Requires revenue from the short-term rental tax to be used for affordable housing programs.

title: Pediatric transitional care
summary: Concerns licensing of facilities that provide pediatric transitional care services; the summary does not state any specific change.

title: LEOFF 2/standby pay
summary: Adds standby pay to basic salary for calculating benefits in the LEOFF Plan 2 retirement system.

title: Local effort assistance
summary: Increases state local effort assistance to K-12 districts so it aligns with enrichment levies.

title: Unemployment comp. notices
summary: Lets the Office of Administrative Hearings serve unemployment hearing notices and orders electronically through July 2029 without parties' consent.

title: Health plan certification
summary: Concerns the health plan certification process; the text gives no details on what changes.

title: UW investments
summary: Requires the University of Washington to place its endowment with the Washington State Investment Board for investment.

title: Local government procurement
summary: Lets county governments skip competitive bidding and advertising for many purchases and public works contracts, and removes some county purchasing requirements.

title: College scholarships/private
summary: Caps Washington College Grant and College Bound Scholarship maximum awards at private four-year colleges to averages of public institution awards.

title: Prosthetics/public employees
summary: Extends insurance coverage of prosthetic limbs and custom orthotic braces to public and school employees.

title: LEOFF 2/lump sum benefit
summary: Clarifies eligibility rules for tiered multiplier and alternative lump sum benefits in LEOFF Plan 2 pensions.

title: Digital school transcripts
summary: Establishes a statewide digital transcript data-sharing environment; the text gives no detail on access, privacy, or funding.

title: Evidence of medical expenses
summary: Concerns the evidence admissible to prove medical, hospital, or similar expenses from an injury.

title: Voting services
summary: Requires county auditors to hold tribal outreach meetings on reservation voting centers and drop boxes, and directs the Secretary to create an electronic ballot return portal for certain voters.

title: Grocery stores & pharmacies
topics: Consumer protection and business; Housing; Taxes and budget
summary: Requires advance notice before grocery or pharmacy closures in certain areas, lets localities zone for grocery use and levy an excise tax on vacant former grocery properties.

title: Deceased candidates
summary: Sets procedures for handling ballots and candidacy when a candidate for a city, town, or special district office dies before an election.

title: Environmental reporting
summary: Reduces utility reporting: EIA reports become biennial and RECs are reported as retired, and heat-day disconnection reports and the electricity adequacy report are eliminated.

title: Address confidentiality prg.
summary: Concerns Washington's address confidentiality program; the text gives no details of what changes.

title: Hospital inspections
summary: Changes hospital inspection rules: allows accreditation inspections to count toward state inspections every 36 months and lets DOH pause unannounced inspections during emergencies.

title: Fish and wildlife commission
summary: Adds four tribal commissioner and four alternate seats to the Fish and Wildlife Commission, raising membership from nine to thirteen, and changes quorum and appointment rules.

title: Public media grants
summary: Creates Commerce-run public media broadcaster and digital equity grant programs to expand internet and noncommercial media access, funded partly by gifts and grants.

title: Schools/local effort assist.
summary: Increases state local effort assistance payments to school districts, which equalize local levy funding.

title: Electric utility investments
summary: Adds investment options electric utilities can use under the 20 percent alternative compliance option of the Clean Energy Transformation Act.

title: Fire dept. civil service
summary: Concerns civil service positions in city and town fire departments; the summary gives no specifics on what changes.

title: Local lodging excise taxes
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets large-county cities impose a up-to-4% lodging tax, lets certain public facilities districts impose lodging taxes without voter approval, and exempts some from the 11.5% cap.

title: Farm machinery sales tax
summary: Creates a sales and use tax exemption for qualifying farm equipment bought by eligible farmers, expiring October 1, 2036, with a JLARC evaluation by 2035.

title: State nickname
summary: Designates "The Evergreen State" as Washington's official state nickname, with no duty to update existing materials.

title: Year-round Pacific std. time
summary: Implements year-round Pacific standard time, ending seasonal clock changes for daylight saving time.

title: Immigration enforcement
summary: Concerning federal immigration enforcement; the summary gives no details of what the bill changes.

title: School security grants
summary: Creates a grant program to fund school security and preparedness infrastructure.

title: School emergency response
summary: Requires school districts, charter schools and tribal compact schools to adopt specified emergency response systems and report progress to OSPI, which will report to the Legislature.

title: Jail system
