summary: Creates a Washington Jail Council within the Governor's office, subject to appropriations, to promote jail transparency, humane conditions, and rehabilitative reform.

title: Corporation acts
summary: Clarifies corporate share option, share exchange, and conversion rules, and lowers the shareholder vote needed to approve voluntary dissolution to a majority.

title: Chronically absent students
summary: Defines chronic absence as missing 10% of school days, funds ESD training on early warning systems, and expands dropout reengagement and Building Bridges supports, subject to appropriations.

title: Public school tools
summary: Creates a temporary, appropriation-dependent OSPI grant program helping K-12 schools fund math and ELA assessment and diagnostic tools, expiring December 31, 2028.

title: Student transp. vehicles
summary: Expands pupil transportation funding formulas to cover non-school-bus vehicles and exempts small student transport vehicles (10 or fewer persons) from school bus and CDL requirements.

title: Election security cameras
summary: Creates a grant program to fund election security cameras, adding funding without changing voting rules.

title: Ballot drop box labeling
summary: Requires counties to prominently display ownership and tampering-crime warning messages on every visible side of ballot drop boxes.

title: Interscholastic athletics
summary: Concerns how interscholastic athletics are organized; the text gives no specific change to current law.

title: Campaign signage map
summary: Directs the state Department of Transportation to create a map showing where campaign signs may be placed.

title: Election security
topics: AI and technology; Elections and voting
summary: Requires state approval of voting-related equipment and software, mandatory breach disclosure for election database vendors, and county cybersecurity measures by July 2027.

title: EFSEC governor approval
summary: Removes the governor from the project approval process at the Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council to speed up energy facility siting.

title: Prearrang. funeral services
summary: Exempts certain funeral merchandise and transportation agreements from prearranged funeral contract rules and lowers the required trust share to 80 percent, letting funeral homes keep more money.

title: Uniformed & overseas voting
summary: Adopts the Uniform Military and Overseas Voters Act, extending federal protections for service and overseas voters to state elections.

title: County weed boards
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration
summary: Changes county noxious weed control board membership from five to four districts plus an at-large member, and loosens nomination notice and application requirements.

title: Prepacked medication distr.
summary: Allows hospitals and health care entities to dispense prepackaged medications in larger supplies when pharmacy access is limited or packaging can't be reduced.

title: Senior citizens/prop. taxes
summary: Provides property tax relief to senior citizens; the summary gives no details on eligibility or amounts.

title: Retention of court exhibits
summary: Shortens the required court exhibit retention period from six years to five years.

title: Law enf. hiring
summary: Concerns hiring practices for law enforcement agencies and prosecutor offices; the summary gives no specifics on what changes.

title: Domestic workers
summary: Establishes employment and labor protections for domestic workers, including independent contractors, with remedies via L&I complaints or private lawsuits.

title: Wine/alcohol tax exemption
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Exempts the first 20,000 gallons of wine sold by a Washington winery from tax, reducing state excise revenue.

title: Educational interpreters
summary: Requires PESB to set performance standards and certificates for educational interpreters, mandates certification for school district interpreters by 2027-28, and publishes certification data.

title: Motor vehicle sales tax
summary: Dedicates the state sales tax collected on motor vehicles to transportation purposes.

title: Law school loan repayment
summary: Creates a law school loan repayment program for Washington public defenders and prosecutors, subject to appropriation, with a service obligation and repayment penalties.

title: Unlawful camping
summary: Concerns unlawful camping; the title and summary give no details on what the bill changes.

title: DOC release transportation
summary: Changes DOC release transportation rules: drops the $100 least-expensive cap, lets the superintendent approve or deny costs, and limits out-of-state transport with exceptions.

title: Vital records access
summary: Waives vital record fees for certain low-income parents enrolling children in early learning or school, and requires ECEAP providers and public schools to accept alternative age documents for enrollment.

title: Confinement health coord.
summary: Creates a Council of Health Care Coordination to coordinate health of people housed in confinement facilities, with state agency and stakeholder members.

title: Juvenile rehab. ombuds
summary: Expands the Office of the Family and Children's Ombuds to cover youth in juvenile rehabilitation facilities and gives it physical and online access to those records and facilities.

title: Biosolids/PFAS chemicals
summary: Ecology must convene an advisory committee, then set PFAS sampling or testing requirements for biosolids by 2028, analyze PFAS levels, and report by 2029.

title: System improvement team
summary: Removes SYNC's expiration date and requires it to submit a biennial report to the Legislature starting November 1, 2026.

title: Voter education
summary: Addresses voter education for jurisdictions changing how they select candidates; the summary gives no operative details.

title: Statewide emissions data
summary: Requires Ecology and Commerce to annually report statewide greenhouse gas emissions totals to the Governor and Legislature, starting in 2026.

title: Uniform custodial trust act
summary: Adopts the Uniform Custodial Trusts Act, governing how custodial trusts are created, managed, and terminated for minors and incapacitated beneficiaries.

title: Hate crime offense
summary: Clarifies the state's hate crime offense; the text gives no detail on what changes.

title: DOC WMS employee arbitration
summary: Removes the exclusion that kept Washington Management Service members at the Department of Corrections from interest arbitration eligibility.

title: Uniformed personnel
summary: Expands the definition of uniformed personnel to include small-town, small-county, and airport law enforcement officers, giving them interest arbitration rights.

title: Unemp ins/strikes & lockouts
summary: Lets workers on strike receive up to four weeks of unemployment benefits after a disqualification period, and removes the lockout disqualification, from 2026 through 2035.

title: Autonomous vehicles
summary: Sets vehicle and operator requirements for autonomous vehicles; the summary gives no detail on the specific rules.

title: PTSD/correctional workers
summary: Creates a presumption that PTSD is an occupational disease for Department of Corrections facility workers in workers' compensation, with exceptions for good-faith employment actions.

title: Supp. retirement bargaining
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Lets public employers bargain over contributions to supplemental retirement benefits run by unions, and limits the bargaining exclusion to Department of Retirement Systems plans.

title: Battery stewardship/EVs
summary: Adds electric vehicle batteries to Washington's battery stewardship program starting in 2029, requiring stewardship organizations to submit a plan for them.

title: Kimchi day
summary: Designates November 22nd as Kimchi Day, a legislatively recognized day, with no policy effect.

title: Signature gathering/protests
summary: Establishes legal protections for citizens who take part in the initiative and referendum process, such as signature gathering and protests.

title: Initiative sig. challenges
summary: Requires notifying legislators when initiative signatures are challenged. The bill is procedural and does not change initiative rules.

title: Sunshine committee
summary: Changes the Public Records Exemptions Accountability Committee's required meeting schedule to at least four meetings annually.

title: Presidential primary privacy
summary: Moves the presidential primary party declaration inside the return ballot envelope and requires a reminder that it must be completed for the ballot to count.

title: Nursing assistant regulation
summary: Moves nursing assistant disciplinary and regulatory authority from the Department of Health to the Nursing Board, expands the Board to 17 members, and eliminates a career advancement report.

title: Law enf. juvenile contact
summary: Requires police to give detained juveniles access to the Youth Access to Counsel line and clarifies that officers may contact juvenile witnesses and victims.

title: PFD formation
summary: Concerns the formation of public facilities districts; the text gives no details of powers or rules.

title: Winery tax exemption
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Gives small wineries producing under 20,000 gallons a year a reduced per-liter wine and cider tax rate and exempts them from most other excise taxes.

title: Agritourism
summary: Exempts agritourism buildings used six months or less a year from commercial building permit code standards, except life and fire safety requirements.

title: WSP firearms records system
summary: Lets the Washington State Patrol keep conducting firearm background checks when state record systems are unavailable.

title: Agricultural real estate
summary: Concerns ownership of agricultural real estate; the title alone does not show what change, if any, it makes.

title: Recycling rates
summary: Requires Ecology to publish statewide lists of recyclable materials for curbside and drop-off collection, and to complete a needs assessment by 2027.

title: Ferry captains
summary: Lets Washington State Ferries captains vote on joining a combined Masters, Mates and Pilots bargaining unit, effective 2026 if approved.

title: Law enf. hiring grants
summary: Creates a CJTC grant program funding up to 75% of entry-level salaries for local and tribal officers, conditioned on policy, training and compliance requirements.

title: Public works wages
summary: Requires public works contracts to adjust laborer, worker, and mechanic minimum hourly wages annually to the latest prevailing wage rate, with some exceptions.

title: Child care workforce board
summary: Establishes a child care workforce standards board; the text does not describe its powers or any rule changes.

title: Freight railroad infra.
summary: Provides B&O or public utility tax credits to railroad companies for certain short line maintenance, new rail, and modernization costs, subject to caps.

title: Rare diseases adv. council
summary: Creates an advisory council within UW's School of Medicine to study and advise on rare diseases, with annual reports starting December 1, 2026.

title: Traveling animal acts
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Bans elephants, bears, nonhuman primates, non-domestic felines and their hybrids from traveling animal acts, with gross misdemeanor penalties, and lets cities and counties adopt stricter rules.

title: Law enf. misconduct
summary: Lets the Attorney General investigate and sue local police and corrections agencies for constitutional or state-law violations, and requires a model accountability policy.

title: Impaired driving
summary: Lowers the legal blood alcohol limit for DUI offenses from 0.08 to 0.05 and requires a statewide public information campaign on the change.

title: Public employ. eligibility
summary: Sets citizenship or federal work authorization as the eligibility standard for certain public safety and civil service jobs and deputy prosecutors, including current employees.

title: Voters' pamphlets
summary: Requires the Secretary of State to print and distribute voters' pamphlets, and excuses county pamphlets from duplicating state pamphlet information on measures and candidates.

title: Interchange fees on tips
topics: Consumer protection and business; Labor and employment
summary: Bars card networks, issuers, and processors from charging interchange fees on sales tax and tip amounts, requires refunds, and sets $1,000 per-transaction penalties.

title: Synthetic opioids/endanger.
summary: Expands the controlled-substance endangerment statute to explicitly cover fentanyl and synthetic opioids, increasing criminal exposure for related conduct.

title: Abandoned vehicle auctions
summary: Taxes abandoned vehicle auction proceeds as vehicle sales rather than towing and storage, applying sales and B&O taxes, with a surplus-funds deduction.

title: Motor vehicles sales tax use
summary: Dedicates the sales tax collected on motor vehicles to highway uses.

title: Seed contract payment
summary: Sets contract terms and payment deadlines for turf seed sales, and lets WSDA suspend dealer licenses for unpaid producers.

title: Prenatal and postnatal care
summary: Requires nongrandfathered health plans to cover in-network prenatal and postnatal care without cost sharing starting 2026, and pregnancy-related prescriptions without cost sharing starting 2027.

title: Nonspot shrimp pot license
summary: Creates a limited-entry non-spot shrimp pot license for Puget Sound, capped at five combined licenses with fees, conversion and transfer rules.

title: Agency voter registration
summary: Lets state agencies, HBE, and online agency sites feed automatic and online voter registration, and clarifies registration for people designated through DOC.

title: Agricultural real estate
summary: Concerns ownership of agricultural real estate; the summary gives no specific change to ownership rules.

title: DSHS overpayments
summary: Lets DSHS waive collection of overpayments from certain long-term care and developmental disability clients, and requires rules setting when waivers apply.

title: Financial education
summary: Requires districts to offer high school financial education and makes it a graduation requirement for the class of 2033, with SBE recommendations and plans due by 2026.

title: Unattended motor vehicles
summary: Exempts remote-started vehicles that are locked with keys out from the unattended-vehicle definition, while keeping driver notice and aid duties.

title: Extended foster care/housing
summary: Creates a DCYF rental assistance program for foster and at-risk youth, up to 36 months and capped at age 21, with rent limited to a share of income.

title: Health carrier reimbursement
summary: Requires Medicaid-paid hospitals to contract with health carriers serving state employee benefit plans upon receiving a good faith offer.

title: Health carrier reporting
summary: Allows the insurance commissioner to require health carriers to annually report primary care expenditures, and makes those reports public.

title: Closed retirement plans
summary: Merges three closed pension plans into Legacy Retirement System, adds retiree COLAs, and suspends unfunded liability contribution rates through 2029.

title: PEBB & SEBB consolidation
summary: Consolidates the PEBB and SEBB public employee benefit programs into a new Washington Employees and Retirees Benefits Board with a modified membership.

title: CTC legal education programs
summary: Directs the state community college board to support new ABA-approved paralegal programs in eastern and central Washington, and requires three colleges to offer a prelaw associate's degree, subject to appropriation.

title: Public utility tax, counties
summary: Authorizes counties to impose a public utility tax.

title: Rural county coroners
summary: Requires the Legislature to appropriate funds through fiscal 2030 covering new or increased county coroner duties for counties under 40,000 population.

title: Professional engineers' reg.
summary: Revises professional engineer and land surveyor registration rules, including education equivalency, verification, fees, certificate validity, and Board pro tem appointments.

title: Motor vehicle emissions
summary: Bars Ecology from adopting California vehicle emission standards, repeals the state's ZEV requirements, and limits state rules to federal Clean Air Act standards.

title: Farm machinery sales tax
summary: Exempts small farmers with under $2 million in annual sales from sales tax on qualifying farm equipment costing $10,000 or more, expiring October 2035.

title: Pregnancy loss
summary: Removes coroner jurisdiction over pregnancy-loss remains, requires correctional facilities to report miscarriage and stillbirth counts annually, and repeals the crime of concealing birth.

title: Sexually explicit depictions
summary: Expands sexual exploitation of a minor crimes, drops identification requirements for fabricated depictions, and extends the statute of limitations from three to ten years.

title: School construction debt
summary: Lets school districts issue nonvoted construction bonds, shortens the required time out of binding conditions from three years to two, and bars SCAP aid for those projects.

title: Natural death act/pregnancy
summary: Removes pregnancy references from the model advance directive form under Washington's Natural Death Act.

title: Girls' athletic activities
summary: Title and summary indicate a measure to protect competitiveness in girls' interscholastic athletics; the text does not state the specific rules.

title: Weapons in certain areas
summary: Adds weapon bans at children's park facilities, state and local public buildings, and county fairs, with exemptions and updated signage rules.

title: Firearms dealers
summary: Makes the State Patrol the regulator for firearm dealer licenses, including processing, compliance and revocation, amends license fees, and requires dealer training.

title: In-home care training
summary: Standardizes basic training and certification requirements for long-term care workers who provide in-home care to family members, including spouses or domestic partners.

title: Worker leave/hate crimes
summary: Extends domestic violence leave and safety accommodation rights to hate crime victims and their family members, and bars employer discrimination or retaliation against them.

title: Public risk pool records
summary: Creates new Public Records Act exemptions for public risk pool rate formulae, data, and actuarial analyses and reports.

title: Sentence review/deportation
summary: Requires expedited clemency review for applicants facing deportation and makes all applicants eligible for pardons and restoration of rights regardless of immigration status.

title: Immigration status coercion
summary: Bars employers from threatening workers' immigration status to deter wage or labor-standard complaints, with per-act penalties enforced by L&I.

title: Sexually explicit depictions
summary: Expands criminal offenses for digitally fabricated obscene depictions of minors, narrows defenses, extends the statute of limitations to 10 years, and broadens sexual exploitation conduct.

title: Eid al-Fitr & Eid al-Adha
summary: Designates Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha as legislatively recognized days in Washington, with no policy effect.

title: Local gov. vehicle insurance
summary: Requires local governments to provide underinsured motorist coverage, at least $25,000 per person and $50,000 per accident, for employees operating government vehicles.

title: Service contracts
summary: Revises financial responsibility rules for vehicle service contract and protection product providers, adding reimbursement insurance flexibility plus consumer disclosure and direct-claim rights.

title: Mortgage lending fraud acc.
summary: Raises the mortgage lending fraud account surcharge on deeds of trust from $1 to $5 and removes the sunset on the surcharge and account.

title: Tribal elder tuition waivers
summary: Allows community and technical colleges to waive tuition and fees for tribal elders over 55 from eligible tribes, with State Board rulemaking.

title: Recording fees/escrow tax
summary: Excludes escrow agents' document recording fees from sales and B&O taxes when separately identified, and exempts this exclusion from JLARC review and the ten-year expiration.

title: Prescribing psychologists
summary: Creates a certification pathway letting licensed psychologists prescribe psychotropic medications, with training requirements and an opioid prescribing limit.

title: Plan 1 retiree COLAs
summary: Gives eligible PERS and TRS Plan 1 retirees a one-time 3% increase in 2025 and annual cost-of-living adjustments starting in 2026.

title: Retirement benefits/death
summary: Changes when Department of Retirement Systems benefits stop after a retiree or beneficiary dies, and when survivor benefits start, effective January 1, 2026.

title: Service grant program
summary: Creates a grant program paying eligible students, including those ineligible for federal aid due to immigration status, for community or volunteer service hours starting 2025-26.

title: Marriage/medical emergency
summary: Allows marriage licenses to be used immediately when a physician or specialist certifies imminent risk or capacity, and limits a surviving spouse's estate benefits if consent was coerced or lacked capacity.

title: Agriculture impacts
summary: Titled 'Agriculture impacts,' the bill states a goal of protecting agriculture; the text gives no operative provisions.

title: International medical grads
summary: Eliminates the one-year residency requirement for internationally trained physicians' limited licenses, requires only USMLE Steps 1 and 2, and allows up to eight years of renewals.

title: Academic employee bargaining
summary: Grants collective bargaining rights under PECBA to employees enrolled in academic or certificate programs at four Washington public universities, excluding managers and certain others.

title: Learning assistance program
summary: Raises learning assistance hours for high-poverty schools to 1.6 weekly and adopts a tiered model based on free and reduced-price meal eligibility starting 2026-27.

title: Fertility-related services
summary: Requires large group health plans, including public employee plans, to cover fertility preservation starting 2026 and infertility diagnosis and treatment starting 2027.

title: Uniform antitrust premerger
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Requires merging parties with Washington ties to file federal HSR premerger forms with the Attorney General, with confidentiality protections and penalties up to $10,000 per day.

title: Discrimination in schools
summary: Adds ethnicity, homelessness, immigration or citizenship status, and neurodivergence as protected classes in public school nondiscrimination rules, and separates gender identity and expression from sexual orientation.

title: SNF & rehab network adequacy
summary: Requires HCA to set Medicaid managed care network adequacy standards for nursing homes and rehabilitation hospitals (IRFs) by 2028, applying to contracts from 2028.

title: Residential services rate
summary: Requires DSHS to use King County's classification for Snohomish County community residential provider rates, contingent on funding in the omnibus appropriations act.

title: Student mental health net.
summary: Creates subject-to-appropriations student mental health programs, including OSPI statewide coordination, regional school-based behavioral health assistance, and a school planning grant program.

title: Collector vehicle licenses
summary: Ends the insurance exemption for collector vehicles, requires a second registered vehicle for collector plates, and moves the horseless carriage age cutoff to pre-1916 vehicles.

title: Juvenile detention, medical
summary: Requires the Health Care Authority to implement federal Medicaid reentry services for juveniles, including pre- and post-release screening and case management, and clarifies Medicaid suspension for DCYF confinement.

title: Common interest communities
summary: Extends WUCIOA provisions on meetings, EV charging, heat pumps, and small-community rules to HOA statutes, and revises unit owner meeting and voting procedures.

title: Child care licensing fees
summary: Prohibits the Department of Children, Youth, and Families from charging licensees fees to obtain a child care license.

title: Religious foods/correctional
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to make reasonable efforts to provide free religious celebration meals to incarcerated people, with partner nonprofits and donated foods allowed.

title: Small claims actions notice
summary: Revises the required notice contents for small claims court actions.Text is a short title and summary only.

title: Sentencing guide/caregivers
summary: Adds a defendant's status as a primary parent, guardian, or caregiver to the factors courts may use for a below-standard-range sentence, with exclusions.

title: Chinese Americans/schools
summary: Requires schools to designate time for Chinese American History Month and to teach the Chinese Exclusion Act in social studies, using a state-developed curriculum.

title: Curriculum establishment
summary: Addresses school districts' authority to establish their own curriculum; the text gives no details of any change.

title: Student given names
summary: Requires public schools to use students' given names, framed as protecting parents' and guardians' rights.

title: Sex ed./parent approval
summary: Requires parental or guardian approval before a child may take part in comprehensive sexual health education.

title: Public facilities districts
summary: Requires counties with a convention and trade center to spend public facilities district lodging tax revenue on affordable housing and community-initiated equitable development.

title: Reentry council members
summary: Increases the Washington Statewide Reentry Council to 22 members and lets certain members receive compensation and reimbursement.

title: Firearm purchase
summary: Enhances requirements for purchasing, transferring and possessing firearms; specific provisions are not described in the summary.

title: Disability insurer filings
summary: Requires experience-rated group disability insurers to file their full rating formulas and credibility methods, detailed enough for the Commissioner to replicate premiums.

title: Eminent domain purchase back
summary: Requires school districts to offer former owners a chance to buy back condemned or threatened-condemned property not used for school purposes, with waiver and exception provisions.

title: Ethics in public service
summary: Raises the gift threshold to $100, adds gift exemptions, and removes the $5,000 cap on ethics-violation costs while keeping the penalty cap.

title: St. agency tortious conduct
summary: Provides for legislative hearings to oversee tortious conduct by state agencies; the text gives no further detail.

title: State spending prgs. review
summary: Implements a periodic review of state spending programs; the text gives no details of any resulting changes.

title: Government efficiency portal
summary: Creates a portal to identify opportunities for increased government efficiency.

title: Criminal insanity
summary: Directs a review of state laws on criminal insanity and competency to stand trial, with no stated change to current rules.

title: GMA housing element
summary: Requires cities and counties to submit housing elements and development regulations to Commerce for compliance review, and bars them from taking effect until approved.

title: Early childhood court prg.
summary: Expands Early Childhood Court eligibility to families with children under age 6, up from under age 3.

title: Juvenile access to attorney
summary: Concerns juvenile access to an attorney; the summary gives no details of what changes.

title: Annual state spending growth
summary: Caps annual state spending growth at median worker wage growth and directs excess revenues to property tax relief.

title: Journal access/state empl.
summary: Directs the Washington State Institute for Public Policy to study funding and mechanisms for giving state employees electronic access to peer-reviewed journals, reporting by December 2026.

title: DCYF to DOC transfer, age 18
summary: Transfers certain individuals from the Department of Children, Youth, and Families to the Department of Corrections at age 18.

title: County auditor duties
summary: Moves the Board of County Commissioners' clerk duty from the county auditor to a board-designated employee and requires auditors to audit disbursements and fund transfers.

title: Salmon recovery projects
summary: Makes the salmon habitat restoration permit pathway permanent, adds more project types, and streamlines DNR and WDFW application timing and submission.

title: Elevators/smaller apartments
summary: Directs the state building code council to allow smaller passenger elevators in small apartment buildings and convenes a task force to review elevator safety requirements.

title: Habitat restoration material
summary: Lets DNR sell up to $250,000 of valuable materials for habitat restoration by direct sale, barred from resale, with treble damages for timber violations.

title: Student athlete insurance
summary: Allows public four-year universities to offer and pay for insurance covering current and, under rule, former intercollegiate student athletes.

title: Trick-or-treat day
summary: Establishes an annual trick-or-treat day in Washington, a designation with no regulatory or funding effect.

title: Transportation budget, supp.
summary: Makes additive 2025-2027 transportation budget appropriations, with committee amendments netting a $1 million increase.

title: Transportation budget
summary: Provides transportation agency and program appropriations for the 2025-27 biennium and adjusts 2023-25 appropriations.

title: Health care work violence
summary: Addresses workplace violence in health care settings; the text gives no specific requirements.

title: Child fatalities
topics: Children and families; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Renames child mortality reviews to child fatality reviews, extends them to ages up to 19, and makes identifying records confidential and admissible in criminal cases.

title: Student navigational support
summary: Creates a subject-to-appropriation financial aid completion and enrollment program, staffed by outreach specialists working with high schools in each ESD.

title: Deer and elk damage
summary: Requires at least 20 percent of deer and elk crop-damage claim funds to go to frontier one counties, with leftover funds open to other claimants.

title: Operating budget, supp.
summary: Modifies the 2023-2025 state operating budget appropriations for various agencies and programs.

title: Operating budget
summary: Enacts the 2025-27 biennial operating appropriations and 2023-25 supplemental appropriations for state agencies and programs.

title: State actuary appointment
summary: Eliminates the SAAC and moves appointment, removal and salary-setting authority for the state actuary to the PFC, requiring a four-member vote.

title: Testimony of children
summary: Raises the age limit to 16 for admitting child hearsay statements about sexual or physical abuse, expands hearsay for violent offenses, and broadens closed-circuit testimony for children.

title: DNR boundary line surveys
summary: Concerns boundary line surveys on public lands owned or managed by the Department of Natural Resources; the text gives no further detail.

title: Wolf predation
summary: Changes how WDFW calculates indirect wolf damage claims for livestock, using losses from the first confirmed depredation year, and removes indeterminate-cause claims in wolf-occupied areas.

title: Fire district civil service
summary: Concerns civil service systems for fire protection districts; the summary gives no detail on what changes.

title: County comprehensive plans
summary: Changes the timing of county and city comprehensive plan reviews to ten years from the previous adoption date or the staggered deadlines.

title: Wood burning devices
summary: Tightens wood burning device emission standards, bars installing or selling noncompliant devices, adds coal to banned fuels, and allows pellet stove restrictions.

title: Photovoltaic modules
summary: Delays Washington's photovoltaic module stewardship deadlines to 2030-2031, creates an advisory committee, and requires recommendations and reports.

title: Prompt pay/capital projects
summary: Requires state and local governments to pay undisputed public works invoices within 30 days, with 1% monthly interest on late payments.

title: Professional dev. resources
summary: Requires considering experiences of marginalized and underrepresented groups when identifying professional development resources on certain topics.

title: Sodium nitrite
summary: Restricts sales of sodium nitrite above 10% to business buyers, requires warning labels, record-keeping, and civil penalties for violations.

title: Education complaint process
summary: Establishes a complaint process to address willful noncompliance with certain state education laws.

title: Schools/gender inclusive
topics: Children and families; Civil rights and liberties; Education
summary: Requires school districts to adopt gender-inclusive policies on names, pronouns, athletics, restrooms and dress, bars staff from disclosing student gender identity without consent, and protects employees from retaliation.

title: Parents rights in education
summary: Revises parental education rights: changes record access timelines and fees, removes medical treatment notice, narrows criminal-action and law-enforcement notices, and revises campus-removal notice.

title: Incarcerated parents
summary: Allows the Department of Corrections to contract with nonprofits or volunteers for midwifery and doula services for incarcerated individuals, and updates gendered and outdated terminology.

title: Tobacco & nicotine products
summary: Bans retail sale, display and advertising of flavored tobacco, nicotine, vapor and entertainment vapor products from January 2026, with signage, penalties and a DOH awareness campaign.

title: Minimum parking requirements
summary: Caps local parking minimums for housing and commercial uses and bars parking requirements for many categories of buildings and projects.

title: International med. pathways
summary: Removes exceptions to a residency requirement for certain permanent immigrants seeking medical practice, as described in a one-line summary.

title: School district elections
summary: Concerns school district elections, but the text gives no details of what would change.

title: Student transportation
summary: Aims to provide adequate and predictable student transportation; the text does not state specific mechanisms or amounts.

title: Broadband repair loans
summary: Expands the state broadband loan program to fund repair and replacement of middle and last mile infrastructure, prioritizing areas that would otherwise go unserved.

title: Competency-based education
summary: Defines competency-based (mastery-based) education and related terms like competencies; the text alone changes no requirements.

title: School building energy perf.
summary: Lets K-12 schools and districts request ten-year extensions of Clean Buildings Performance Standard compliance dates, with no administrative penalty for requesting.

title: Dockworkers/PFML premiums
summary: Extends the PFML employer definition to cover employer representatives of dockworkers, who take on premium and reporting duties for those workers.

title: School district materials
summary: Increases per-student maintenance, supplies and operating cost allocations for school districts, including an added 9-12 amount, restricted to those costs.

title: Remote testing
summary: Lets districts offer online-school students the option to take statewide standardized tests remotely starting 2027-28, and directs OSPI to set implementation rules.

title: State gen. obligation bonds
summary: Authorizes the State Finance Committee to issue up to $4.7 billion in general obligation bonds for capital projects.

title: Capital budget
summary: Sets the 2025-27 biennial capital budget appropriations and 2025 supplemental capital appropriations for the 2023-25 biennium.

title: Gambling commission/PRA
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Consumer protection and business
summary: Exempts proprietary financial and security information held by the gambling commission from public inspection and copying.

title: Local government planning
summary: Requires cities and counties to amend noncompliant growth plans or regulations before the Growth Management Hearings Board can find them compliant, and removes a provision allowing invalidity to be lifted.

title: Driver training alternative
summary: Allows drivers facing a 60-day license suspension for repeated moving violations to complete a safe driving course instead, ending the suspension once one course per five years is completed.

title: DCYF oversight board comp.
summary: Allows lived-experience members of the DCYF oversight board to receive compensation and travel reimbursement for their service.

title: Veteran medical foster homes
summary: Exempts veteran medical foster homes from adult family home requirements while applying long-term care worker rules, vulnerable adult status, and caregiver disqualification standards.

title: Psychedelic substances
summary: Creates a state-licensed regulated psilocybin program for adults 21 and older, with licensed facilitators and service centers supervising therapeutic sessions.

title: Judicial orders
summary: Revises protection order procedures, including who may seek renewal, when minors can petition at 18, and how ex parte orders may be modified or terminated.

title: Wildlife safe passages
summary: Creates a wildlife habitat connectivity strategy and action plan run by WSDOT and WDFW, plus two treasury accounts for corridors and crossings.

title: Ibogaine-assisted therapy
summary: Directs the University of Washington to run a three-year randomized study comparing ibogaine-assisted therapy with standard treatment for opioid use disorder.

title: College grant award amounts
summary: Ties state college grant award amounts to institutions signing an affidavit attesting to nondiscrimination policies, reducing awards for non-signers and those under certain settlements or court orders.

title: Cannabis advertising
summary: Raises the number of permitted cannabis retailer advertising signs to four and adds limits on advertising content, trade name signs, and below-cost pricing.

title: Media service subscriptions
summary: Requires electronic media subscription services to pay pro rata refunds when consumers cancel, while keeping automatic renewals allowed and subject to the Consumer Protection Act.

title: Clean energy fund program
summary: Creates a Commerce-administered clean energy loan program, funded through a new account, for clean energy, EV charging, grid and nuclear projects.

title: L&I law enforcement
summary: Adds the Department of Labor and Industries to the statutory list of limited authority law enforcement agencies.

title: Ninth grade success grants
summary: Creates a subject-to-appropriation grant program for public high schools to fund ninth grade success teams that support at-risk incoming students.

title: DD parental caregivers
summary: Directs DDA to seek federal approval so parents providing extraordinary personal care to minor children with developmental disabilities can be paid through the waiver.

title: Water adjudication in WRIA 1
summary: Lets adjudication claim forms filed in WRIA 1 after June 1, 2023 satisfy statement-of-claim requirements, and protects water rights existing before July 27, 1997.

title: Fentanyl possession
summary: Creates or increases penalties for possessing fentanyl, according to the bill title and summary.

title: Mobile market programs
summary: Creates a DOH Mobile Market Program giving WIC and SFMNP participants nutrition access, subject to federal USDA funding and nonprofit operation rules.

title: Vehicle debris escape
summary: Requires trucks hauling dirt, gravel or similar aggregate on paved public highways to use a load cover, phased in by 2028, with exemptions for public entities.

title: Green energy/community
summary: Creates green energy community funds to support school districts and nonprofits in communities hosting renewable energy projects.

title: Pregnancy accommodations
summary: Requires employers, including small and religious ones, to paid break and travel time for expressing milk, expands pregnancy accommodations, and moves enforcement to L&I.

title: Vehicle and driver licensing
summary: Revises vehicle and driver licensing rules, including CDL conviction reporting with no diversion, odometer exemption years, remote hearings, and license plate authority.

title: Partial confinement
summary: Extends the maximum partial confinement and Community Parenting Alternative period from the final 12 to the final 18 months of a sentence, and removes the residential parenting provision.

title: City small works rosters
summary: Modifies small works roster requirements that cities use for public works contracting.

title: Personal property distraint
summary: Lets county treasurers cancel small personal property taxes when collection costs exceed the tax, and requires owners to request excess sale proceeds, which expire after three years.

title: Residential tenants
summary: Caps residential rent and fee increases at 7 percent per year, bars increases in a tenant's first year, and adds notice rules and tenant termination rights, with several exemptions.

title: Criminal fingerprinting
summary: Lets judges order fingerprinting of gross misdemeanor defendants lacking prints and expands police authority to fingerprint adults cited or summoned on criminal charges.

title: Officer certification
summary: Defines the terms 'certified' and 'commissioned' for the Criminal Justice Training Commission chapter on officer certification.

title: Candidate filing
summary: Lets filing officers list similarly named candidates consecutively and makes filing a candidacy with intent to mislead voters, using a well-known candidate's surname, a crime.

title: Physician res./international
summary: Creates a grant program to fund residency positions that train international medical graduates, overseen by the Washington Medical Commission.

title: Child sex dolls
summary: Title suggests a measure about child sex dolls, but the bill text is only a title and a note that it was not considered.

title: Health disparities council
summary: Renames and restructures the health disparities council, adding members and youth representatives, and tasks it with a statewide health justice and equity vision and recommendations.

title: Opioid overdose/civil commit
summary: Expands the grounds for involuntary commitment to include recent opioid overdose revival when the person is not receiving essential care.

title: Juvenile attorney exceptions
summary: Creates exceptions to juvenile access to an attorney; the summary does not specify the exceptions or their scope.

title: Confinement fees & expenses
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Requires free voice calls and free tablets for people in state prisons, bars DOC from profiting from calls, and expands contract fee disclosure and usage reporting.

title: Essential needs program uses
summary: Expands Essential Needs (HEN) housing aid to eligible elderly or disabled adults without a DSHS referral, allows direct cash assistance, and removes the 7 percent administration cap.

title: Washington health trust
summary: Directs development of a Washington health trust; the text gives no details on its structure, funding, or rules.

title: Snowmobile registration fees
summary: Raises the annual registration fee for vintage snowmobiles from $12 to $18.

title: Public school statutes
summary: Lets PASS program award funds be used for high school and beyond plans and repeals several outdated School Code provisions.

title: Anesthetics/greenhouse gases
summary: Concerns emissions of greenhouse gases used for anesthetic purposes; the text does not specify the requirements.

title: Unattended child in vehicle
summary: Concerns making it an offense to leave a child unattended in a vehicle; the text gives no details on penalties.

title: Reckless driving, speed
summary: Adds driving more than 30 mph over the posted speed limit to the conduct that constitutes reckless driving.

title: Hospital medical records
summary: Requires hospitals to keep all medical records for at least 26 years from creation, in any retention medium.

title: Anaphylaxis med. in schools
summary: Lets trained school staff give any single-use premeasured epinephrine for suspected anaphylaxis, without a student prescription, and extends liability protections and the rules to all public schools.

title: Fusion energy facilities
summary: Adds fusion energy facilities to the optional EFSEC certification process, requires radiation-control licenses, and specifies that energy plants include fission nuclear facilities.

title: Behavioral health resources
summary: Creates a confidential, anonymous behavioral health screening and counseling program for credentialed health professionals, funded by a uniform credentialing fee surcharge.

title: Health premiums/lobbying
summary: Restricts how health care premium dollars may be used, prohibiting their use for political lobbying.

title: WIC hematological screening
summary: Exempts staff at WIC clinics from medical assistant requirements when they only perform hematological finger, heel or toe-stick screening.

title: Legislature oath of office
summary: Authorizes county commissioners to administer oaths of office to state legislators.

title: Energy facility site eval.
summary: Limits EFSEC public hearings to land-use-inconsistent projects, sets approval criteria for clean energy facilities, and repeals expedited processing.

title: Naselle Youth Camp property
summary: Transfers ownership of the Naselle Youth Camp property from the state to the Chinook Indian Nation.

title: Bridge collisions
summary: Creates a work group to recommend measures addressing bridge collisions caused by large commercial vessels.

title: Kit home siting
summary: Allows local governments to permit factory-built kit homes of 800 square feet or less as emergency housing, subject to periodic inspection.

title: Squatters
summary: Seeks to improve legal processes to deter squatters on property.

title: Lodging tax revenues
summary: Expands the permissible uses of lodging tax revenue to include capital expenditures on tourism facilities owned by nonprofits.

title: Assembly halls/property tax
summary: Removes the 1-acre land limit on the assembly halls property tax exemption, starting with taxes due in 2027.

title: Special education services
summary: Extends special education and related services for students with disabilities to age 22 or high school graduation, and orders a transition-planning plan update.

title: Health care information
summary: Strengthens patients' rights over their health care information; the summary gives no specific mechanism.

title: Juvenile detention
summary: Concerns juvenile detention while a crime awaits disposition; the text gives no specifics on what changes.

title: ISRB hearings/victims
summary: Concerns victims' participation in hearings conducted by the indeterminate sentence review board; the text does not state how participation changes.

title: Juvenile firearm sentencing
summary: Modifies sentencing standards for juvenile firearm offenses; the summary does not say whether penalties increase or decrease.

title: Medicaid concurrent enroll.
summary: Implements state auditor recommendations to reduce improper payments for people concurrently enrolled in Medicaid, per the bill's brief text.

title: Commercial fishing bait tax
summary: Exempts bait sold for commercial fishing from retail sales and use tax, with a DOR exemption certificate required, through January 1, 2037.

title: Juvenile correctional pop.
summary: Lets people 18 and older in juvenile DCYF custody request transfer to adult DOC custody, with a three-day reconsideration period and no review board hearing.

title: Nonconsumptive hydropower
summary: Allows water right permits for nonconsumptive hydropower in water resource areas where minimum instream flows are not being met.

title: Insurance statutes
summary: Omnibus insurance housekeeping bill: repeals obsolete studies and reports, adds a hearing aid coverage mandate, and makes some insurer data confidential or less public.

title: Special education funding
summary: Raises special education funding multipliers to 1.32, removes the enrollment cap, lowers safety net thresholds, and adds statewide oversight and IEP system duties.

title: Tax compacts/capital invest.
summary: Raises the cap on tribal sales-tax distributions under compacts to 100 percent of state sales and use taxes for tribes completing qualified capital investments.

title: Electrical inspector exp.
summary: Expands the minimum experience requirements for electrical inspectors to count certain out-of-state experience toward qualification.

title: Early release petitions
summary: Lets people convicted of crimes committed before age 18 petition for early release after age 24, capped at 35 petitions yearly until 2035, with optional rental vouchers.

title: Death penalty
summary: Allows prosecutors to seek the death penalty against incarcerated offenders who commit murder.

title: Unlawful firearm possession
summary: Requires mandatory one year of community custody for unlawful firearm possession sentences, and DOC supervision for first and second degree offenders regardless of risk level.

title: Sentence modification
summary: Gives judges discretion to modify sentences in the interest of justice.

title: Educator support/nurses
summary: Requires school districts receiving BEST program funding to prioritize trained mentors for novice school nurses in their first three years.

title: School nurse requirement
summary: Requires first-class school districts to employ a school nurse.

title: School safety/penalties
summary: Expands and toughens interference and intimidation offenses protecting school staff, students and athletic officials, adds school exclusion after conviction, and removes mandatory student suspension language.

title: Violence prevention services
summary: Concerns the availability of community violence prevention and intervention services; the summary gives no specific mechanism or funding.

title: Body cameras/corrections
summary: Concerns body-worn cameras within corrections agencies; the short summary does not state the specific requirements.

title: Passport to careers program
summary: Requires the Office of Student Financial Assistance to deposit Passport to Careers Program money into the State Financial Aid Account with the state treasurer.

title: Institution reimburse. rates
summary: Modifies reimbursement rates for services related to institutions; the summary does not say whether rates rise or fall.

title: Juvenile rehab. to 25 repeal
summary: Repeals prior legislation that extended juvenile rehabilitation jurisdiction to age 25; the text gives no further detail.

title: Juvenile rehabilitation
summary: Requires DCYF to set juvenile institution bed-capacity rules, manage population at set thresholds, transfer some adult-convicted residents to DOC, and create an infraction system.

title: Child care provider qualif.
summary: Concerns qualifications for child care providers, but the text does not specify what changes.

title: Virtual currency kiosks
summary: Regulates virtual currency kiosks by capping daily transactions at $2,000 and fees, requiring NMLS reporting, and mandating fraud warnings and detailed receipts.

title: Vessel length/nonresident
summary: Raises the nonresident vessel permit length cap from 200 to 300 feet, sets per-foot fees for larger entity-owned vessels, and directs proceeds to youth swim grants.

title: Missing children adv. board
summary: Creates an advisory board to the Missing and Exploited Children Task Force.

title: Energy storage siting/EFSEC
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Prevents EFSEC from overriding local land use plans or zoning ordinances that forbid electricity storage facilities in critical areas.

title: Solid waste management
summary: Requires packaging and paper product producers to join or register with producer responsibility organizations, which must register with Ecology, with a sales ban on non-compliant producers from 2029.

title: Law enf. officers/increase
topics: Government and administration; Housing; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets cities and counties levy a 0.10% sales tax to hire law enforcement officers and fund some criminal justice programs.

title: State hospitals/police costs
summary: Creates and continues police community partnership programs at Eastern and Western State Hospitals, funded up to $750,000 per biennium per facility, with annual reporting.

title: Ignition interlock assist.
summary: Directs the Department of Licensing to adopt rules capping indigent drivers' ignition interlock financial assistance at two vehicles per person or household.

title: County board vacancies
summary: Repeals the statutory methods for filling vacancies on county commissioner boards.

title: Farm machinery sales tax
summary: Creates a sales and use tax exemption for qualifying farm machinery and equipment.

title: Controlled subs. dismissal
summary: Lets courts dismiss drug possession charges if the person completes a court-approved substance use disorder treatment program and the court finds the interests of justice warrant it.

title: Long-term services trust
summary: Amends the WA Cares long-term care program: restricts out-of-state and visa-holder participation, tightens benefit eligibility to 90-day ADLs, and redirects certain funds to the account.

title: Family & medical leave rates
summary: Changes how the PFML premium rate is set, adding a four-month reserve target in 2030 and eliminating the statutory rate formula, with the 1.2 percent cap kept.

title: Prevailing wage/public works
summary: Concerns prevailing wage requirements for public works projects; the summary gives no specifics on what changes.

title: Professional accounts
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Repeals six Department of Licensing accounts, moves their balances into one Account, and requires annual expenditure and revenue reporting on the professions using it.

title: Sexual assault/rights
summary: Updates Washington's sexual assault survivor bill of rights; the text does not specify the changes.

title: Juvenile offenses
summary: Requires a court finding before juvenile commitment and mid-point review hearings, while expanding eligibility for community-based disposition alternatives.

title: Early learning facilities
summary: Expands early learning facility grant and loan eligibility to full-day and extended-day conversions and emergency grants, and adds tribal compact schools as eligible recipients.

title: Mobile home community sale
summary: Revises mobile home community sale notice rules: removes separate sale notice, adds notice to tenant organizations, local governments and housing authorities.

title: Radiologic technologists
summary: Lets radiologic technologists perform IV contrast procedures under virtual direct supervision instead of in-person direct supervision.

title: St. Edward state park
summary: Removes the Parks Commission's authority to enter a 62-year lease for property at Saint Edward state park.

title: Gov. services/tribal lands
summary: Lets a federally recognized tribe and an adjacent city agree to extend urban governmental services onto abutting tribal-jurisdiction property until December 31, 2028.

title: Unmanned aircrafts/foreign
summary: Prohibits state purchases of small unmanned aircraft made or assembled by covered foreign entities.

title: Yakima basin water plan
summary: Extends the Yakima basin Integrated Plan's permit-securing milestones for water supply facilities from 2025 to 2035, and adds an interest payment on certain community forest loans.

title: Homelessness/tribal colleges
summary: Expands an existing program to include public tribal colleges located in Washington and accredited by NWCCU or a recognized accreditor.

title: Salmon recovery accelerator
summary: Establishes an ORIA environmental accelerator giving regulatory flexibility and 60-day relief decisions for CCA-funded salmon recovery and resiliency projects.

title: Pension credit for leave
summary: Allows LEOFF Plan 2 members on authorized leave to buy up to two years of pension service credit upon retiring, based on their salary at the time of leave.

title: Special education funding
summary: Removes the 16 percent special education funding cap, lets the superintendent reserve funds for statewide activities, and lowers the safety net eligibility threshold.

title: Guaranteed admissions prg.
summary: Creates a guaranteed admissions program requiring school data-sharing agreements, student notifications at certain times, and annual WAGAP reports from 2027 to 2032.

title: Motorcycles/weight fees
summary: Lowers the vehicle weight fee for motorcycles from $35 to $25, regardless of scale weight.

title: Child care subsidy rates
summary: Concerns child care subsidy rates; the text gives no detail on what would change.

title: Cash & food assistance/work
summary: Increases work participation requirements for able-bodied working-age adults receiving cash and food assistance.

title: Net nanny operations
summary: Ends sex offender registration after five crime-free years, and sets three-year supervision for certain Net Nanny offenders with no prior predatory history.

title: Rental agreement provisions
summary: Expands the list of rental agreement provisions that landlords are prohibited from including under the Residential Landlord-Tenant Act.

title: Capital gains tax
summary: Adjusts Washington capital gains tax rules on loss carryforwards, retirement plans, spousal combination, penalties, amendments, and broker reporting.

title: Local tax rate changes
summary: Requires local governments to give the DOR written notice, with supporting ordinance documents, when changing local sales and use tax rates, and sets bond-retirement notice timing.

title: Unclaimed property
summary: Modifies provisions of the revised uniform unclaimed property act, a state administrative framework for dormant property.

title: EFSEC/services by local gov.
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Bars appeals of city or county actions under EFSEC agreements based on inconsistency with a local code that EFSEC's statutes preempt.

title: Background checks
summary: Requires fingerprint background checks for long-term care and child placement workers and providers, and sets administrator training and certification rules.

title: Surface mine reclamation
summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to tell applicants revising surface mine reclamation permits or plans what information they need, within 60 days.

title: Smokey Bear license plates
summary: Creates Department of Natural Resources Smokey Bear special license plates for vehicles.

title: Postsecondary/med. abortion
summary: Requires public college student health centers to offer medication abortion access, referrals, telehealth support, and a reproductive health services website.

title: Burrowing shrimp
summary: Directs research into integrated pest management to address burrowing shrimp impacts on bottom-culture shellfish farming.

title: Theft from first responders
summary: Expands first-degree theft and possession of stolen property to cover equipment stolen from fire stations and EMS facilities or vehicles.

title: Prior auth. APIs/health
summary: Requires health carriers and managed care plans to build prior authorization APIs meeting federal rules, with reduced-service denials treated as appealable adverse determinations starting 2027.

title: State cactus
summary: Designates the Columbia Plateau cactus as Washington's official state cactus.

title: Insulin emergency supply
summary: Creates an HCA emergency insulin program letting eligible people get one 30-day supply per 12 months for a $10 maximum out-of-pocket cost starting 2026.

title: Learning standards
summary: Requires the State Board of Education's graduation requirement recommendations to ensure students can demonstrate competency in computer science and financial education standards.

title: Earned wage access services
summary: Creates a state license requirement for earned wage access providers, with background checks, financial standards and bonding, and exempts their fees from loan and interest rules.

title: Smoke detector installation
summary: Makes the Washington State Patrol solely responsible for enforcing smoke detector installation laws, removing that authority from local fire officials, and requires WSP to develop education materials.

title: Spiked drink testing
summary: Requires liquor licensees to offer drug test devices for sale in areas restricted to people 21 and older, with expiration checks, signage, and a liability shield.

title: Insurance code violations
summary: Lets the insurance commissioner order restitution for insurance code violations, with 8% interest, payable within 30 days, excluding providers.

title: Mobile dwellings
summary: Requires cities and counties planning under the GMA to allow at least one mobile dwelling unit on qualifying residential lots in urban growth areas.

title: Eluding & resisting arrest
summary: Lets police impound vehicles used in attempted eluding, bars redeeming the vehicle for 72 hours for some owners, and allows forfeiture after repeat eluding convictions.

title: DNR civil enforcement appeal
summary: Expands the Pollution Control Hearings Board's jurisdiction to hear appeals of DNR civil penalties for burning permit and silvicultural burning violations.

title: Rural nursing education
summary: Establishes a Department of Health Rural Nursing Education Program to provide distance nursing education and support services for rural communities.

title: Isolated employees
summary: Adds training, panic-button recordkeeping, and civil penalties to Washington's isolated employee safety law, enforced by L&I starting July 2026.

title: Memory care services
summary: Requires assisted living facilities that market memory care to obtain DSHS certification, with staffing, training, and operating standards starting July 2026.

title: Veterans affairs adv. comm.
summary: Changes the membership of the Veterans Affairs Advisory Committee.

title: Minimum wage increases
summary: Ties future Washington minimum wage increases to the federal minimum wage rather than the current inflation-based method.

title: Sales tax exemptions
summary: Permanently exempts bottled water, prepared food, and clothing from state sales and use tax.

title: Children's product sales tax
summary: Permanently exempts from sales and use tax purchases of products for young children.

title: Legislators/state facilities
summary: Requires DOC, DCYF and DSHS to give legislators access to state facilities, including tours and constituent meetings, and to respond in writing if a requested visit cannot be scheduled.

title: NE WA wolf-livestock account
summary: Creates spending authority from a wolf-livestock account for wolf-livestock management and grants to Stevens and Ferry county sheriffs' offices for a local wildlife specialist.

title: Essential worker health care
summary: Creates a DSHS program distributing supplemental payments to nursing home employers that fund employee health coverage through qualified health funds, subject to appropriation.

title: Access to personnel records
summary: Concerns access to personnel records, but the text gives no details on what the bill changes.

title: Student mobile device use
summary: Revises digital citizenship to include mobile device norms, directs OSPI to post related research and best practices, and requires a 2026 report on school phone-limit policies.

title: Organized retail theft
summary: Addresses organized retail theft; the title-only text does not specify any change to penalties or enforcement.

title: Organized retail theft
summary: Creates a sentencing enhancement that increases penalties for organized retail theft.

title: Assault rifles/CPL holders
summary: Exempts concealed pistol license holders from the state ban on importing firearms classified as assault rifles.

title: Firearm background checks
summary: Concerns the background check system for firearms transfers, but the summary does not say what changes.

title: Dental insurance practices
summary: Bars dental-only plans from denying claims solely for same-day procedures, allows credit card claim payments with fee notice, and creates a collaborative forum.

title: Free school meals
summary: Requires schools to provide free breakfast and lunch to any requesting student from 2026-27, adds a state per-meal reimbursement, and extends learning assistance and bonus funding.

title: Diabetes and obesity
summary: Requires health plans to cover obesity treatment, including surgery and medications, and directs HCA to seek federal approval to cover it in Medicaid.

title: Gray wolf management
summary: Allows WDFW to manage gray wolves in qualifying counties as if delisted as state endangered, using a county-triggered work group and management plan.

title: Higher education safety
summary: Requires college IDs to list a survivor support hotline, gives sexual assault survivors kit-preservation and notice rights, and bars institutions from pressuring students into nondisclosure agreements.

title: Criminal justice trainings
summary: Expands sexual assault investigation training to Title IX investigators and requires patrol officers to complete victim-centered, trauma-informed training every three years.

title: Actuarial pension funding
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lowers employer and Plan 2 member pension contribution rates for 2026 and suspends unfunded liability rates for four years for several state retirement systems.

title: Career & tech. ed./6th grade
summary: Lets districts offer exploratory career and technical education to sixth graders, excludes them from CTE allocation counts, and treats middle and high school CTE as one program for accounting.

title: Clean energy development
summary: Aims to accelerate development of clean energy and transmission; the summary gives no specific mechanism.

title: Environmental crimes
summary: Creates tiered felony and gross misdemeanor criminal penalties for knowing or negligent violations of water pollution and clean air laws.

title: ASAM 4 treatment criteria
summary: Delays by two years, from 2026 to 2028, the date when Medicaid managed care organizations and health carriers must start using ASAM Criteria Fourth Edition.

title: Crime victim services
summary: Requires the state treasurer to deposit set aggregate amounts each fiscal year into the VOCA account for victim services.

title: Reg. businesses/card fees
summary: Modernizes payment rules by expanding consumer-friendly transaction options for registered tow operators and regulated businesses, with card fees as the apparent focus.

title: Sheriffs, chiefs, etc.
summary: Modernizes, harmonizes and clarifies Washington laws governing sheriffs, police chiefs, marshals and police matrons. The summary gives no substantive changes.

title: Library funding alternate
summary: Amends the definition of recreational facilities to include community centers, which could include public libraries that use less than half their space for such facilities.

title: Victim of rape/pregnancy
summary: Allows exceptional (above-standard) sentences for offenses that result in pregnancy of a rape victim.

title: Law enf. community grants
summary: Removes the sunset on the Community Engagement Grant Program and directs Commerce to create a Community Immersion Law Enforcement Grant Program.

title: Alcohol taxes and fees study
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Directs the Washington State Institute for Public Policy to study and report on the state's alcohol taxation and fee system.

title: Youth mental health/schools
summary: Lets educational service districts arrange in-school placements of social worker associates and MSW candidates, and directs PESB to adopt placement rules.

title: Port commissioner terms
topics: Elections and voting; Government and administration
summary: Lets port districts put a ballot measure to voters to extend port commissioner terms from four to six years.

title: Wine & spirit sales limits
summary: Removes the 24-liter per-sale limit on certain alcohol products for holders of specified liquor licenses, including spirits retail licenses.

title: Medicaid access program
summary: Creates a covered lives assessment on Medicaid managed care organizations and health carriers, and raises Medicaid professional services rates to Medicare equivalents.

title: Even-numbered year elections
summary: Moves local government general elections to even-numbered years to increase voter participation.

title: Transportation/tribal rep.
summary: Requires local planning to coordinate with affected tribes and creates a Tribal Traffic Safety Coordinator Program within the Traffic Safety Commission.

title: Clergy, duty to report abuse
topics: Children and families; Civil rights and liberties
summary: Requires clergy to report suspected child abuse or neglect, and removes the exemption for information learned through privileged communications.

title: Cruelty to animals
summary: Addresses animal cruelty prevention, but the text gives no details of what it would change.

title: Motor vehicle dealers
summary: Repeals an exemption that let certain vehicle manufacturers with a 2014 dealer license compete with new motor vehicle dealers.

title: PFML grants/school districts
summary: Expands access to paid family and medical leave program grants for small school districts.

title: Parks & rec./interest arb.
summary: Adds Parks and Recreation Commission employees to those eligible for interest arbitration under the PSRA.

title: Environmental justice
summary: Bars new air-pollution permits for major sources in the most burdened census tracts and requires environmental justice impact statements for certain projects in pollution-burdened communities.

title: Self-insurer withdrawal
summary: Requires L&I to pay compensation for terminated self-insurers and makes decertified groups reimburse L&I through quarterly charges, with rules to follow.

title: Ballot measure petitions
summary: Requires petition circulators to sign expanded declarations and requires the Secretary of State to reject petition signatures whose residence address does not match voter registration records.

title: Salmon recovery projects/tax
summary: Exempts from sales and use tax the inputs needed for salmon recovery projects.

title: Riparian programs review
summary: Requires the Joint Legislative Audit and Review Committee to review Washington's riparian programs, with a preliminary report due December 2025 and a final report by June 2027.

title: Definition of timberland
summary: Expands the timberland definition for real estate excise tax rates, so certain forest lands transferred to governmental entities qualify when managed as designated forestland.

title: Schools/sexual assault
summary: Aims to support sexual assault survivors in public K-12 schools; the text gives no specific mechanisms or changes.

title: Corp. practice of medicine
summary: Restricts medical practice ownership to licensed medical providers and limits management services organizations' control over clinical decisions and practice shares.

title: DOC behavioral health cert.
summary: Requires DOH and DOC to adopt behavioral health standards for correctional facilities, with annual DOH inspections and DOC reimbursement of inspection costs.

title: Liquor revenue/local gov.
summary: Restores liquor sales revenue distributions to local governments, reversing a prior reduction in those payments.

title: Access to recreation sites
summary: Raises the Discover Pass fee to $45, adds a third plate space, and makes the lifetime disabled veteran pass equivalent to a Discover Pass.

title: Sustainable farms grants
topics: Consumer protection and business; Environment and energy
summary: Removes compost spreading equipment from eligible grant uses and requires grant projects to be prioritized by their carbon emissions reduction.

title: BSA transfers
summary: Concerns transfers from the budget stabilization account; the short text does not specify amounts or purposes.

title: Rainier school
summary: Subject to appropriations, requires relocating residents of Rainier School to other settings.

title: DDA no-paid services
summary: Limits DDA case resource management for No-Paid Services clients, removing client contact duties and barring services to inactive clients.

title: Prior authorization/health
summary: Adds requirements for insurer prior authorization: disclosure of reviewer credentials, public posting of policy changes, electronic systems, and limits on AI-based denials.

title: FAA medical certificates
summary: Makes employees in FAA medical certification review eligible for paid family and medical leave and requires employers to pay 50% of wages after leave is exhausted.

title: CTC faculty w/o tenure limit
summary: Requires community and technical colleges to cap courses taught by non-tenure-track faculty at 45 percent by 2030 and report annually to the Legislature.

title: Veterans w/ disabilities/tax
summary: The bill concerns property tax exemptions for veterans with disabilities, but the summary gives no details of the change.

title: Liquor licenses
summary: Concerns liquor licenses, but the text gives no detail on what would change.

title: Local news journalism
topics: AI and technology; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a state grant program funding local civic journalists and imposes a 1.22% gross-income surcharge on large social media and search platforms starting 2027 to fund it.

title: Wholesale power purchases
summary: Concerns how electric utilities make wholesale power purchases under the Washington Clean Energy Transformation Act; the text gives no specific change.

title: Financial aid eligibility
summary: Revises Washington College Grant award tiers and redefines the Bridge Grant as a $500 annual grant for low-income students.

title: Cannabis industry agreements
topics: Consumer protection and business; Criminal justice
summary: Prohibits retail cannabis licensees and their owners from agreements giving financial interests across more than five retail cannabis licenses.

title: Public defense services
summary: Concerns public defense services, but the text gives no specifics on what it changes.

title: Estate tax exclusion amount
summary: Indexes Washington's estate tax exclusion amount to Seattle-area CPI inflation starting in 2026, and makes that adjustment permanent.

title: EV charging/state expense
summary: Concerns the state paying for electricity used by electric vehicle charging stations.

title: Nursing home rate rebase
summary: Delays the scheduled rebasing of nursing home Medicaid payment rates until 2028.

title: Wage and salary disclosures
summary: Creates a written-notice process for job posting pay-transparency violations and bars penalties if employers correct the posting within 14 days.

title: DOC healthy env. pilot
summary: Creates a four-year DOC pilot at the Penitentiary East Complex with contact officers, de-escalation training, facility improvements, and annual recidivism reporting.

title: Veteran parking privileges
summary: Allows veterans with a 70% or higher disability rating who use a service animal to apply for disability parking privileges.

title: Pilates studios, etc./tax
summary: Exempts gymnastics and Pilates class charges from retail sales and use tax, and sets the B&O rate for those classes at facilities not primarily used for fitness.

title: Interfund loans/schools
summary: Lets financially distressed school districts take interest-free interfund loans from capital funds and seek state authorization to sell property.

title: Detached ADUs
summary: Establishes limitations on detached accessory dwelling units located outside urban growth areas.

title: Social equity impact/audits
summary: Extends the deadline for legislative bodies to hold public hearings on performance audit findings.

title: CBA financial feasibility
summary: Concerns the financial feasibility of collective bargaining agreements; the text gives no specific changes.

title: Child care providers
summary: Aims to increase affordable child care options by reducing barriers for providers, with no specific mechanism stated.

title: Vehicle noise cameras
summary: Authorizes local cameras with microphones to ticket street racing and vehicle noise violations, only in designated enforcement zones, with audio limited to violation moments.

title: Charter school contracts
summary: Lets charter school contracts exempt schools from basic education requirements and makes charter schools eligible for OSPI and SBE waivers, with SBE consultation on related contract terms.

title: Reports of fire losses
summary: Gives insurers 90 days after closing a fire-loss claim to report, instead of promptly, and sends reports to the OIC instead of the State Patrol chief.

title: Veteran benefits access
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Extends veteran and service-member benefit definitions to Space Force, NOAA, and USPHS members and some spouses, covering retirement, civil service, licensing, and employment preferences.

title: Small businesses/residential
summary: Requires cities to allow small neighborhood businesses in residential zones, excluding drive-throughs, while letting cities set compatibility limits like hours, noise, signage and alcohol.

title: Collective bargaining/AI use
summary: Requires public employers covered by PECBA and PSRA to bargain over adopting or modifying AI that affects employees' wages or performance evaluations.

title: Digital electronics/repair
topics: AI and technology; Consumer protection and business
summary: Requires manufacturers to provide parts, tools and documentation to independent repairers, bars parts pairing, and makes violations Consumer Protection Act violations enforced by the attorney general.

title: UW health sciences campus
summary: Establishes a health sciences campus of the University of Washington; the text gives no funding or operational details.

title: Energy independence act
