summary: Removes the annual renewable energy targets that qualifying utilities must meet under the Energy Independence Act, and strips related references from state law.

title: Court alternatives/youth
summary: Expands juvenile diversion eligibility and removes diversions from juvenile criminal history, and creates a community diversion grant program subject to funding.

title: Children in crisis program
summary: Extends the children's crisis rapid care team and project director duties to 2027 and replaces old reporting with an annual Governor report.

title: Community inclusion services
summary: Aims to improve community inclusion services for people with developmental disabilities; the provided text gives no specifics.

title: State building code council
summary: Changes the membership of the state building code council; the summary does not describe any change to building rules.

title: Utility wildfire mitigation
summary: Requires investor-owned utilities to file wildfire mitigation plans with the UTC, updated at least every three years, and gives the UTC approval authority.

title: Tax and revenue laws
summary: Makes technical tax changes: codifies medical supply sales tax reporting, clarifies rural data center exemption employment rules, and shifts the tax exemption study deadline.

title: License plate production
summary: Requires DOL to adopt rules extending temporary license plate expirations during permanent plate shortages and to develop a mitigation plan that may use third-party plate production.

title: DOC employee bargaining
summary: Requires one master collective bargaining agreement for DOC employees and exempts certain DOC bargaining units from coalition bargaining rules.

title: Gubernatorial emergencies
summary: Lets the Legislature terminate gubernatorial states of emergency and executive orders, by concurrent resolution in session or by leaders' written notice otherwise.

title: Collective bargaining reorg.
summary: Reorganizes the public employee collective bargaining act into seven subchapters and repeals obsolete sections, without changing substance.

title: Worship/access interference
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Creates a new offense for intentionally blocking access to or disrupting religious services at places of worship, with civil remedies for those harmed.

title: Noncompetition agreements
summary: Voids all noncompetition covenants, including for independent contractors and performers, requires employer notice by 2027, and allows private enforcement actions.

title: Hydrofluorocarbons
summary: Phases down hydrofluorocarbon use by restricting refrigerants above set global warming potential limits starting in 2027, 2030 and 2033.

title: Thermal coal divestment/SIB
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Bars the State Investment Board from new thermal coal investments and requires full divestment from thermal coal companies and funds holding them by 2030.

title: Single license plates
summary: Expands single-license-plate eligibility to passenger cars, SUVs, off-road vehicles, and light trucks, buses, and for-hire vehicles, with owners paying fees as if two plates were issued.

title: Accounts
topics: AI and technology; Taxes and budget
summary: Modifies the Broadband Mapping Account and redirects certain dedicated revenue sources, according to a short summary.

title: College promise pilot
summary: Creates a College Promise Pilot in Eastern Washington providing up to $5,000 yearly in tuition aid, a high school tuition program, reporting, and a private match requirement, subject to appropriations.

title: Fund-raising events
summary: Concerns requirements for fundraising events held by bona fide charitable or nonprofit organizations; the text does not specify the changes.

title: Special license plates
summary: Creates a moratorium on new special license plates until 2029 and requires a DOL workgroup to review existing special plate provisions.

title: Distributed energy resources
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets utilities meet clean energy targets with conservation and demand response, quadruples credit for certain distributed generation, exempts distributed solar from SEPA review, and keeps agrivoltaics on farmland from triggering added tax.

title: Commission on boys and men
summary: Establishes a Washington state commission on boys and men. The text gives no duties, funding, or policy changes.

title: High-hazard facility wages
summary: Concerns wages for journeypersons working in high-hazard facilities; the summary does not state the specific wage change.

title: Dialysis/certificate of need
summary: Exempts certain dialysis services from Washington's certificate of need requirements.

title: Counselors, etc. committee
summary: Concerns the advisory committee for mental health counselors, marriage and family therapists, and social workers; the text does not state any change.

title: Sewage-containing spills
summary: Increases public transparency about sewage-containing spills, according to the bill's title and summary.

title: Quantum economic development
summary: Creates a quantum economic development committee staffed by Commerce and a subject-to-appropriation grant program to help applicants win federal quantum technology grants.

title: Psychiatric pharmacists
summary: Allows board-certified psychiatric pharmacists to be licensed as agency-affiliated counselors, expanding who can provide counseling.

title: Public defense recruitment
summary: Directs the Office of Public Defense to create a training program for new mitigation specialists and paralegals and a paralegal pool for contracted public defense counsel.

title: Dairy inspection program
summary: Extends the expiration date of the in-state milk processing assessment that supports the dairy inspection program from 2025 to 2031.

title: Cancer research endowment
summary: Revises the Andy Hill Cancer Research Endowment's administrator rules, exempts community outreach grants from matching and review requirements, and updates Board membership after the Fred Hutchinson merger.

title: Cannabis industry
summary: Removes unspecified barriers facing the cannabis industry; the text gives no details on which rules change.

title: Broadcasters
summary: Moves the radio and television broadcasting B&O tax into a new section, defines broadcasting, and exempts it from tax preference review and its 10-year expiration.

title: Newspaper tax preference
summary: Clarifies newspaper and printing businesses must file annual tax reports, and sets a 0.484 percent B&O rate for those found ineligible for the newspaper exemption.

title: Call center retention
topics: Government and administration; Labor and employment
summary: Requires call center employers relocating jobs abroad to give 120 days' notice, with penalties, bars them from state grants and loans, and requires state call center contracts to be performed in the U.S.

title: Community authority funding
summary: Establishes state funding for community preservation and development authorities approved under RCW 43.167.060.

title: Intensive rural dev. areas
summary: Concerns residential development in limited areas of more intensive rural development; the summary gives no detail on the specific changes.

title: Vehicle inspection backlog
summary: Exempts all-terrain vehicles, wheeled all-terrain vehicles, and utility type vehicles declared a total loss or salvaged from VIN inspection requirements.

title: Industrial insurance/duties
topics: Consumer protection and business; Labor and employment
summary: Extends the good-faith duty and certification-withdrawal penalty for repeat violations to all workers' compensation self-insurers and third-party administrators.

title: CDL federal standards
summary: Directs the Department of Licensing to update CDL eligibility rules to clarify how federal domicile and immigration-status standards affect receiving or renewing a license.

title: Wildfire costs/securitizing
summary: Lets utilities finance wildfire and other disaster costs through rate recovery bonds, with UTC approval and customer charges that cannot be avoided.

title: Electric transmission system
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration
summary: Creates the Washington Electric Transmission Authority to plan, coordinate and build new transmission, prioritizing renewable grid access, with eminent domain and other powers.

title: Water-sewer district surplus
summary: Raises the dollar thresholds for water-sewer districts to sell surplus personal property without notice and real property privately.

title: Ag. cannabis workers
summary: Concerns collective bargaining rights for agricultural cannabis workers; the summary gives no details on the specific changes.

title: Rental housing market
summary: Bans landlord coordination services that use automated systems to recommend rents, renewal terms, or occupancy levels across multiple landlords, enforceable by the Attorney General and private suits.

title: Detached ADUs
summary: Lets counties allow detached accessory dwelling units outside urban growth areas, subject to water, septic, size, siting and short-term rental conditions.

title: Middle housing
summary: Allows counties to authorize up to four middle-housing units per lot in urban growth areas and LAMIRDs, with standards no stricter than single-family homes.

title: Farm holdings
summary: Concerns farm holdings, but the bill text gives no detail on what it would change.

title: Law enforcement arbitration
summary: Lets law enforcement officers pursue grievance arbitration under their union contracts and removes a limit on arbitrator term expirations.

title: Organic, etc. agriculture
summary: Aims to expand opportunities for organic, regenerative, climate-smart, and sustainable agricultural producers; no operative details are given.

title: Salmon recovery maintenance
summary: Creates a salmon recovery maintenance account and directs SRFB to consider long-term maintenance plans when funding habitat projects.

title: Responsible bidder criteria
summary: Modifies the responsible bidder criteria that contractors must meet to bid on public works projects.

title: Mental health services
summary: Aims to improve access to mental health and substance use disorder services; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Authorized PEBB benefits
summary: Changes which benefits the Public Employees' Benefits Board may offer; the text provides no further detail.

title: Open space incidental use
summary: Reduces the penalty for removing land from the Current Use Valuation Program from seven years of taxes owed to four years.

title: Medical debt
summary: Bars hospitals, providers and collection agencies from reporting medical debt to credit bureaus, and makes such reported debt void and unenforceable.

title: Behavioral health/schools
summary: Expands children's access to behavioral health services by placing licensed clinicians inside schools.

title: Use of dogs to hunt
summary: Removes county employees' exemption to hunt bear, cougar, or bobcat with dogs, but lets WDFW authorize county cougar public-safety responses with dogs.

title: History & heritage education
summary: Bill title and one-line description reference preserving history and heritage education; the text gives no specific rules or funding.

title: Tow truck payments/indigent
summary: Creates a DOL-run program to reimburse tow companies for towing and storage of indigent owners' vehicles, letting those owners reclaim vehicles without paying, funded from surplus auction proceeds.

title: Livestock identification
summary: Extends the expiration dates for livestock inspection and call-out fees and the Livestock Identification Advisory Committee from July 2026 to July 2030.

title: Motion picture captioning
summary: Requires movie theaters to offer closed captioning and set numbers of open-captioned screenings, with record-keeping for compliance.

title: Agricultural overtime
summary: Lets agricultural employers choose 12 weeks a year to employ workers up to 50 hours a week before overtime applies.

title: DCYF/financial stability
summary: Bars DCYF from using foster youth's benefits to reimburse care costs and requires DCYF to screen for and apply for SSI and Social Security benefits.

title: State sandstone
summary: Designates Wilkeson Sandstone as the official state sandstone of Washington, a symbolic designation with no policy effect.

title: Jail searches/gender
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Requires local jails to adopt search and privacy standards for transgender and intersex detainees, limiting cross-gender searches and viewing by opposite-gender staff.

title: Prescribed fire claims
summary: Creates a pilot program, run by ORM with DNR, to reimburse property and economic losses from certified prescribed fires and cultural burns, subject to available funding, through 2033.

title: Tourism promotion
summary: Creates a tourism industry advisory group to study and recommend a self-supported assessment to fund statewide tourism promotion, and extends its administrative funding to June 2026.

title: Hospital price transparency
summary: Requires hospitals to publish standard charges and shoppable services data per federal rules, and to submit machine-readable price files to the Department of Health annually starting July 2027.

title: Lead-based paint
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Revises Washington's lead-paint and renovation certification programs by removing fixed fees and inspection notice rules, adding enforcement referrals, and barring penalties duplicating EPA action.

title: Life insurance/suicide limit
summary: Shortens the suicide exclusion period on individual, industrial, and credit life insurance policies from two years to one year, starting for policies issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.

title: Home buying by entities
summary: Prohibits large investment entities and firms holding over 100 Washington single-family homes from buying additional single-family residential properties, with exceptions, enforced under the Consumer Protection Act.

title: Housing & shelters
summary: Requires cities and counties to allow STEP housing permits through administrative approval, with Commerce dispute review and revenue withholding for noncompliance.

title: Contraceptive coverage
summary: Extends the 12-month contraceptive supply requirement to all contraceptive prescriptions, not just refills.

title: DOC body scanner program
summary: Requires DOC to set up body scanners at two prisons to reduce strip searches and contraband, offer SUD assessment and treatment, and report annually.

title: Child care rate model
summary: Requires the biennial child care rate report to include cost-of-quality studies, including a living-wage-based model recommended by the early educator design team.

title: Employee driving requirement
summary: Bars employers from requiring a driver's license for jobs or posting that requirement, unless driving is essential, and adds L&I enforcement and penalties.

title: Recycling & waste reduction
summary: Creates a beverage container refund program requiring producers to join registered recycling refund PROs, pay costs, and face a sales ban if noncompliant.

title: Public employee bargaining
summary: Revises public-sector union rules: eases unit mergers, limits PERC intervention, strengthens PERC subpoena enforcement, and bars employers from requiring waiver of statutory claims in grievance settlements.

title: Complex care serv./children
summary: Supports caregivers who provide complex care services to children with heightened medical needs; details are not given in the text.

title: Universal communications
summary: Expands permitted uses of the Universal Communications account to cover service upgrades, reliability and infrastructure maintenance, and sets eligibility requirements for telecom providers.

title: Residential private schools
summary: Starting July 2026, DCYF must license the living accommodations of residential private schools unless exempted, and conduct negotiated rulemaking with the SBE.

title: Massage therapy coverage
summary: Requires the state Medicaid agency to cover medically necessary massage therapy for pain, with a provider referral, starting January 1, 2027.

title: Child welfare housing assist
summary: Lets DCYF continue housing assistance after child welfare services end, requires serving eligible families on waiting lists, subject to appropriation, and expands reporting.

title: Child care center siting
summary: Requires cities to allow child care centers as outright permitted uses in most zones, except industrial, light industrial and open space zones.

title: Conservation district limits
summary: Sets maximum per-parcel conservation district rates by county population, with periodic consumer price index adjustments and revised collection cost-retention rules.

title: Low-proof alcohol beverages
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Excludes low-proof beverages from spirits license fees and certain spirits taxes, while imposing a new $2.50 per gallon tax on their sales.

title: House-banked card rooms
summary: Allows house-banked card rooms to use centralized surveillance systems.

title: Pharmacist scope of practice
summary: Expands pharmacists' scope of practice to improve access to care and help manage chronic diseases.

title: Clean buildings standard
summary: Adds alternative compliance metrics, exemptions and extensions to the clean buildings standard, requires utilities to share energy data for tier 2 buildings, and bars passing penalties to tenants.

title: Community solar
summary: Concerns fair access to community solar; the summary gives no detail on specific rules or changes.

title: Community centers/prop. tax
summary: Expands the community center property tax exemption to cover nonprofit university surplus property converted into community centers, for taxes due 2026 through 2035.

title: School staff salary alloc.
summary: Raises state minimum salary allocations for classified school staff in stages from 2025-26, splitting administrative and other classified staff categories in 2027-28.

title: Sales tax sourcing impact
topics: Government and administration; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets large qualifying cities levy a sales tax up to 0.3% for up to 20 years, with required budget public-process steps.

title: Ocean vessels/environment
summary: Requires ocean-going vessels in Washington's regulated waters to use fuel with 0.1% or less sulfur starting 2028, with detailed recordkeeping.

title: Wrongly convicted persons
summary: Broadens state compensation for wrongly convicted people by expanding actual innocence definitions, covering civil detention, and limiting attorney general challenges to claims.

title: Traffic safety
summary: States a general goal of improving traffic safety; the text gives no specific rule changes.

title: State capitol campus
summary: Adjusts capital project responsibilities for the state capitol campus and changes membership of the State Capitol Committee and its design subcommittee.

title: Higher ed. gov./students
summary: Requires community and technical college boards to have a student trustee, sets appointment and eligibility rules, and restricts state funds for trustee travel.

title: Donate life license plate
summary: Directs special license plate proceeds to fund organ donation awareness and encourage positive sentiment toward donor registration.

title: Layoffs
summary: Requires employers with 50 or more full-time employees to give 60 days' written notice to ESD and affected workers before a mass layoff or business closing.

title: Tobacco, nicotine, & vapor
summary: Concerns regulation of tobacco, alternative nicotine, and vapor products; the summary gives no specific changes.

title: State patrol longevity bonus
summary: Expands the WSP longevity program to more commissioned employees, paying one-time retention incentives of $3,750 per quarter by June 30, 2025.

title: Transp. electrification
summary: Requires that EV charger installations at state-owned facilities be performed by EVITP or similarly certified installers.

title: ADU tax exemptions
summary: Extends the ADU property tax exemption to mid-sized counties, requiring annual applications, tenant income affidavits, and 12-month leases, through 2034.

title: Penalties/certain offenses
summary: Increases penalties for certain offenses, according to its one-sentence description.

title: Home care worker background
summary: Streamlines the background check process for home care workers.

title: Child abuse & DV/standards
summary: Establishes standards for civil proceedings and unprofessional conduct involving child abuse and domestic violence; the text is too brief to determine specific changes.

title: Domestic violence/custody
summary: Changes how child custody is handled when a parent has a history of domestic violence; details are not specified in the text.

title: Spring blade knives
summary: Removes spring blade knives from the statutory list of dangerous weapons, so they are expressly not dangerous weapons.

title: Firearms/individual right
summary: Title-only bill about individuals' rights to bear arms; the text does not state any specific change to current law.

title: Property distrib./divorce
summary: Lets divorcing parties enforce court orders on real property, requires creditors to follow them, and directs courts to weigh sale costs and homelessness risk for family homes.

title: Natural resources board/OSPI
summary: Short title only: concerns efficient administration of state education agencies and a natural resources board, with no operative details.

title: Unauthorized persons/removal
summary: Bill title indicates it concerns removing unauthorized persons, but the text gives no details on who is covered or what the removal process involves.

title: Paid family & medical leave
summary: Expands Washington paid family leave eligibility and job protections to more employers and workers, and requires employers to keep health coverage during protected leave.

title: Students/unemployment ins.
summary: Repeals the law that disqualifies certain students from receiving unemployment insurance benefits.

title: Future fund pilot project
summary: Concerns a Washington future fund pilot project; the text provides no further detail on its design or funding.

title: HS completers/CTC tuition
summary: Removes the age-19 minimum for community and technical colleges to waive high school diploma or certificate course fees.

title: College bound scholarship
summary: Expands College Bound Scholarship eligibility to students who have received a high school equivalency certificate.

title: County local roads
summary: Concerns county local roads, but the text gives no detail on what the bill changes.

title: Family home prov./military
summary: Exempts certain military-area family home child care providers, certified by a federal military service, from DCYF licensing, while requiring DCYF to investigate abuse referrals there.

title: Solar energy systems/schools
summary: Requires new school buildings to include installed solar energy systems.

title: Cannabis revenue/local gov.
summary: Shifts cannabis tax revenue from the state general fund to local governments, raising local shares from fiscal year 2026 through 2030.

title: Workers' compensation
summary: Sets tiered workers' compensation wage-replacement rates by family status, from 60% to 75% of wages, and adds payments to children's legal custodians.

title: Job applicants and employees
summary: Expands protections for job applicants and employees under the Washington Fair Chance Act, which limits employers' use of criminal history.

title: Transportation funding/CCA
summary: Funds the state transportation system using revenues from the Climate Commitment Act.

title: School library info and tech
summary: Requires every student to have access to a school library information and technology program, adds district policy duties, and lets some second-class districts use noncertificated staff to oversee it.

title: Kit homes/building codes
summary: Requires the State Building Code Council to adopt rules for kit homes of 800 square feet or less by March 31, 2027.

title: Multifamily housing/tax
summary: Creates a sales and use tax incentive for multifamily affordable housing projects.

title: Historic landmark desig.
summary: Concerns historic landmark designations, but the text gives no detail on what changes.

title: Zoning regulations
summary: Requires cities to allow ground-floor housing in transit station areas, caps pedestrian-corridor designations, eases street-level use rules, and allows taller, denser mass timber buildings.

title: Adopt-a-highway program
summary: Conditions WSDOT's Adopt-a-Highway program on appropriations and requires annual reports on participants' contractual compliance and contractor use.

title: Pregnancy/emerg. treatment
summary: Requires hospitals to treat pregnant patients with emergency medical conditions, including termination when the standard of care calls for it, or transfer them.

title: Growth management plans
summary: Delays comprehensive plan review deadlines for listed counties and cities and sets later compliance timing for minimum density, design review and accessory dwelling unit rules.

title: UGA subdivision process
summary: Requires GMA cities to adopt unit lot subdivision procedures on set deadlines, with plat notes, and bars them from refusing applications solely for lacking those procedures.

title: State clam
summary: Designates the Pacific razor clam as the official state clam of Washington.

title: Health care entity registry
summary: Creates a health care entity registry; the summary gives no details on who must register or what it requires.

title: Students/apprenticeships
summary: Title-only bill concerning students attending approved apprenticeship programs; the text does not state any specific change.

title: Horse racing
summary: Loosens Washington horse racing rules by removing race-day and simulcast limits, allowing handicapping contests, and changing commission governance and fund uses.

title: Goals of a basic education
summary: Modifies the statutory goals of basic education in Washington; the summary gives no specific changes.

title: Bingo gambling/senior groups
summary: Permits senior-focused groups to conduct certain bingo gambling activities.

title: Assaulting law enf. officers
summary: Increases the criminal penalty for assaulting a law enforcement officer.

title: Natural resources careers
summary: Directs OSPI to select a nonprofit partner to continue and expand a youth natural resources career program, subject to appropriations, with reporting to the Legislature.

title: State health plan
summary: Directs OFM to develop a statewide health resources strategy and report on it through 2032, with public comment, without changing health care rules.

title: Direct transfer to treatment
summary: Lets courts release bailed defendants on recognizance and stay prosecution if they enter inpatient or residential substance use or co-occurring treatment with an escort.

title: Tribes/K-12 instruction
summary: Requires school districts to add the Since Time Immemorial tribal sovereignty curriculum to social studies by 2026, consult tribes, and report compliance to the Legislature.

title: Exterior cladding materials
summary: Prohibits cities and counties from requiring or excluding exterior cladding materials that comply with the state building code.

title: School construction projects
summary: Requires school districts to make contractors on large school construction assistance projects over $35 million agree to project labor agreements with labor organizations.

title: Electric security alarms
summary: Requires local governments without rules on electric security alarms to allow them, including on outdoor storage properties, subject to safety and height standards.

title: History instruction
summary: Requires school districts to adopt policies and provide K-12 instruction on Asian American, Pacific Islander, Latino, and Black American history within social studies courses, with annual reporting.

title: Parenting plan limitations
summary: Concerns limitations in parenting plans, but the text gives no detail on what changes.

title: Affordable housing funding
summary: Lets cities, counties and towns impose a short-term rental tax of up to 4 percent, with revenue dedicated to housing services and facilities.

title: HIV antiviral drugs/medicaid
summary: Requires Washington's Health Care Authority to cover all FDA-approved HIV antiviral drugs for Medicaid enrollees without prior authorization or step therapy.

title: Labor standards
summary: Requires employers and TNCs to provide paid vacation leave, guarantees five days of paid bereavement leave, and lets L&I issue stop work orders for violations.

title: Health/contract terminations
summary: Bars health carriers, providers, and facilities from publicly discussing a possible contract termination until 45 days before the termination date, with exceptions.

title: Corp. homeowner registration
summary: Creates a Corporate Homeowner Registration Program and a state treasury account to administer its funds.

title: Safe system approach strat.
summary: Modifies state transportation law on active transportation facilities, roundabout definitions and rules of the road, and WSDOT Complete Streets mitigation via local facilities.

title: Critical energy infra./PRA
summary: Concerns disclosure of critical energy infrastructure information, with the PRA tag indicating a public records exemption for such information.

title: Fishing and hunting licenses
summary: Sets Washington fishing and hunting license fee amounts for residents, nonresidents, seniors and youth.

title: OII expansion/prosecutions
summary: Renames the police investigations office as OIIP and creates an independent prosecutor with final charging authority over police deadly-force cases.

title: Tribal warrants
summary: The bill concerns tribal warrants, but the text gives no detail on what it would change.

title: Electric vehicle batteries
summary: Seeks to improve end-of-life management of electric vehicle batteries; the text gives no specific requirements.

title: Affordable housing dev.
summary: Requires the Washington Center for Real Estate Research to produce biennial analyses of county housing units, housing needs, and progress on affordable and emergency housing.

title: Health carriers & providers
summary: Concerns relationships between health carriers and contracting providers; the short text does not specify any changes.

title: Insurance & credit study
summary: Requires the Insurance Commissioner to study insurers' use of credit history and other rate factors, then report policy options to the Legislature by 2026.

title: Livestock wolf predation
summary: Creates a three-year WDFW pilot letting livestock owners and their agents lawfully kill the first wolf returning to a predation site, with reporting and carcass surrender required.

title: Affordable housing/sales tax
summary: Lets cities and counties create a sales and use tax remittance program that exempts affordable housing developers from sales tax on qualifying projects.

title: Zero emissions vehicles/sale
summary: Bill concerning zero emissions vehicle sales, with requirements applying to manufacturers and vehicle dealers; the text does not state the specific change.

title: School levies & local effort
summary: Changes school enrichment levy caps to 30% of levy base starting 2026 and revises local effort assistance eligibility and matching amounts.

title: Biosimilar medicines
summary: Lets pharmacists substitute interchangeable biosimilars more freely, drops substitution-instruction and signature-line requirements, and lets carriers require trying a biosimilar first from 2027.

title: Shared streets
summary: Lets cities designate nonarterial streets as shared streets with a 10 mph speed limit option, and requires annual reports on crashes and violations.

title: Interstate teacher compact
summary: Repeals the Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact, with the withdrawal taking effect six months after enactment.

title: Water recreation facilities
summary: Concerns water recreation facilities, but the text gives no detail on what it would change.

title: JLARC studies
summary: Modifies the provisions governing studies conducted by the Joint Legislative Audit and Review Committee (JLARC).

title: Commercial fishery licenses
summary: Creates a limited Hood Canal beach seine salmon license with fees, caps the number at five, and requires converting a Puget Sound commercial salmon license.

title: TNCs/large-scale events
topics: Consumer protection and business; Government and administration; Transportation
summary: Makes TNC price-gouging violations during large events and emergencies Consumer Protection Act violations, requires driver-pay receipts, and lets cities geofence pickup zones at major events.

title: Alternative jet fuels
summary: Promotes the production and use of alternative jet fuels in Washington; the text gives no specific mechanism.

title: Cardiac and stroke outcomes
summary: Bill text is a title only, stating a goal of improving cardiac and stroke outcomes without specifying any mechanism.

title: Juvenile attorney access
summary: Gives juveniles access to attorneys when contacted by law enforcement.

title: Transit-oriented development
summary: Requires cities and counties with major transit stations to adopt 20-year multifamily property tax exemption programs in station areas, with affordable housing units counted toward the exemption.

title: Microenterprise home kitchen
summary: Creates a new category of microenterprise home kitchen operation, defined as a food facility run from a person's primary residence, excluding cottage food operations.

title: Long-term care ombud funding
summary: Requires the LTC Ombuds Program, with Commerce and OFM, to develop a recommendation for adequate funding to meet its statutory duties.

title: Free speech info./higher ed.
summary: Requires higher education institutions to provide free speech information to students.

title: Free speech policy/higher ed
summary: Requires public colleges and universities to adopt free speech policy statements.

title: Cultural resources/land use
summary: Requires GMA counties and cities to adopt tribe-consulted archaeological and cultural resource ordinances by 2029 to keep SEPA categorical exemptions, and creates a task force.

title: Equine industry
summary: Creates an equine regulatory account, funded by up to $1.5 million yearly from the treasury and sales tax revenue, to pay federal HISA fees and compliance costs.

title: Land use permitting workload
summary: Streamlines local land use permitting by expanding binding site plan use, barring condo-specific permitting burdens, and limiting permit decision deadline extensions.

title: Multiunit housing/SEPA
summary: Creates a SEPA categorical exemption for multiunit housing development within incorporated urban growth areas, removing certain environmental review requirements.

title: Residential development
summary: Requires fully planning cities and counties to use only clear and objective residential development standards by 2029, with Commerce publishing model code provisions.

title: Impact fees
summary: Expands impact fee deferral for housing developers by repealing the deferral cap, lien, and admin fee, while adding interest, penalties, and buyer disclosure.

title: Residential housing permits
summary: Vests residential projects in the zoning rules in effect when a complete permit application is filed, and bars treating unpaid fees or unposted notices as invalidating it.

title: WA saves trust account
summary: Renames the Washington Saves Administrative Treasury Trust Account to the Washington Saves Administrative Trust Account.

title: Juvenile detention/CHINS
summary: Allows CHINS petitions so detained juveniles without a releasable parent can get emergency hearings and possible DCYF custody or approved placement.

title: College admission criteria
summary: Addresses transparency in college admissions, but the provided text is only a short title with no operative details.

title: In-state resident enrollment
summary: Sets minimum in-state resident enrollment thresholds that public universities must meet.

title: Foster care/rights of child
summary: Declares rights for youth in foster care, including equal treatment, sibling contact, and extended foster care, and requires DCYF to issue a rights pamphlet by September 2025.

title: Sporting event raffles
summary: Addresses electronic raffles at live sporting events; the short summary does not say whether they would be allowed or restricted.

title: Diet pills and supplements
summary: Bans selling or giving away over-the-counter diet pills and weight-loss or muscle-building supplements to anyone under 18.

title: Public records exemptions
summary: Concerns recommendations from the public records exemptions accountability committee; the text does not state any change to exemptions.

title: Electric vehicle fires
summary: Directs development of best practices for responding to electric vehicle fires. It does not change any rules.

title: State clam/Pacific geoduck
summary: Designates the Pacific geoduck as the official clam of the state of Washington.

title: Wage replacement
summary: Creates a state wage replacement program funded by a small employer surcharge, paying unemployment-style benefits starting 2027, including to some workers barred from UI for lack of work authorization.

title: Safe excavation
summary: Updates excavation safety rules: adds an online locator notice platform, sets notice timing and marking duties, and requires physical exposure before directional boring.

title: Lead in cookware
topics: Consumer protection and business; Health care
summary: Raises the allowable lead limit in cookware from 5 ppm to 90 ppm in 2026, then 10 ppm in 2028, and narrows the restriction's scope.

title: Prosthetic limb coverage
summary: Requires most group health plans to cover prostheses, custom orthotic braces, repairs, and replacements, and to report claims data to the insurance commissioner.

title: Farm fuel users
summary: Removes the five-year limit on the expanded fuel tax exemption for farm product transport and states intent to pay farm fuel users.

title: Back country search & rescue
summary: Creates a state grant program to support backcountry search and rescue organizations and volunteers.

title: Confidentiality/interstate
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Health care
summary: Requires businesses to notify the Attorney General when legal process over protected health care lacks an attestation, and extends limits on officials' cooperation with outside inquiries to agents.

title: Subdivision of land
summary: Streamlines plat and subdivision approval by limiting required public hearings, meetings and design review, and allowing administrative approval with notice to neighbors.

title: Community solar projects
topics: Environment and energy; Labor and employment
summary: Expands the community solar program by raising the project size cap to 999 kW, adding administrators, and creating new precertification and power purchase incentives, with labor standards for larger projects.

title: Alt. on-site sewage systems
summary: Concerns approval of certain alternative on-site sewage systems; the summary does not state whether approval rules are loosened or tightened.

title: Mt. St. Helens license plate
summary: Creates Mount St. Helens special license plates for vehicle owners.

title: Media literacy & civic ed.
summary: Promotes student access to information about media literacy and civic education; the text gives no mechanism or rule change.

title: Hospital exec. excise tax
summary: Imposes an excise tax on annual compensation of highly paid hospital employees to fund health care access.

title: Children of murdered parents
summary: Provides tuition and fee waivers at public colleges and universities for children of murdered parents.

title: Energy facilities/water
summary: Requires applicants to prove an adequate water supply before new energy facilities can be permitted.

title: Blood donation/school instr.
summary: Encourages schools to teach blood donation awareness alongside bone marrow donation, optionally within a required health class, using approved nationally recognized providers.

title: Medicaid clients/metrics
summary: Directs HCA to create a plan to incentivize Medicaid managed care and fee-for-service providers to improve cancer screening, prenatal and postpartum care measures, with annual reporting.

title: Child fatality reviews
summary: Expands child fatality and near-fatality reviews to cover youth in DCYF care and juvenile rehabilitation facilities, and grants OFCO access to those facilities and case systems.

title: Gift card criminal conduct
summary: Aims to deter criminal conduct involving gift cards; the text gives no specifics on the penalties or mechanisms.

title: Estate tax/extraordinary rev
summary: Redirects extraordinary estate tax revenue into the developmental disabilities community services account, funding those services.

title: Assaulting outreach workers
summary: Concerns criminal penalties for assaulting outreach workers; the text does not say whether penalties are added or changed.

title: Affordable housing/REET
summary: Expands the real estate excise tax exemption to cover any ownership housing that affordable homeownership facilitators provide to low-income households, through 2030.

title: ABLE accounts
summary: Creates a state ENABLE account for ABLE savings accounts, depositing $1,000 into each eligible account and covering some administrative fees.

title: Supply chain competitiveness
summary: Creates a Supply Chain Competitiveness Infrastructure Program offering grants and loans for port-related supply chain infrastructure, with DOT setting priorities and criteria.

title: Cannabis local excise tax
summary: Authorizes counties, and then cities, to impose a local excise tax of up to 2 percent on retail cannabis sales, subject to voter approval.

title: Garnishment exemptions
summary: Raises the exempt amounts of personal property and financial accounts shielded from consumer-debt garnishment, makes protections permanent, adds indexing, and exempts alimony.

title: Environment/port districts
summary: Directs UW to study aviation air quality and noise impacts near Sea-Tac and has Commerce convene a work group to inform mitigation strategies.

title: Fish and wildlife officers
summary: Adds lieutenants and captains of fish and wildlife officers to those eligible for interest arbitration under the public employee bargaining law.

title: Student restraint, isolation
summary: Bans certain restraints and isolation of students in schools, limits when physical restraint and isolation are allowed, and funds demonstration projects.

title: Child care centers/buildings
summary: Requires occupancy load for child care centers in mixed-use buildings to count only the areas where child care is provided.

title: Aquatic lease inflation rate
summary: Switches the inflation index for water-dependent aquatic land leases from PPI to CPI and removes DNR's duty to pick a substitute index.

title: Plasma donation/physicians
summary: Allows certain health professions to act as physician substitutes for plasma source donation centers.

title: Workforce education account
summary: Directs advanced computing surcharge revenue to computing degree programs, creates apprenticeship tuition grants, and requires colleges to grant credit for apprenticeship instruction.

title: Housing shortage/local share
summary: Requires local governments with permitting authority to approve enough new homes through 2035, evaluate codes, track permit denials, and risks withholding REET earnings from noncompliant jurisdictions.

title: Water & sewage system access
summary: Allows water and sewer extensions outside city and urban growth boundaries for existing development, and bars growth board and boundary review board challenges to approved extensions.

title: Landlord-tenant/preemption
summary: Bars cities, counties and towns from regulating landlord-tenant agreements for most private rental housing, while allowing voluntary rent-control agreements.

title: Utility connection charges
summary: Allows large eastern Washington counties to waive utility connection charges for affordable, supportive or emergency housing if developers record covenants restricting use and income.

title: CTC online course offerings
summary: Allows community and technical colleges to market online courses beyond their districts, and bars them from competing for enrollment.

title: Impaired driving
summary: Concerns impaired driving, but the text gives no specifics on what it would change.

title: Child sex abuse
summary: Addresses reporting of child sex abuse, but the text gives no detail on who must report or what changes.

title: Mental health internships
summary: Creates a public school-based mental health internship grant program, administered by PESB, to help schools attract and pay full-time school psychology interns.

title: Intercity passenger rail
summary: Sets 2035 performance targets for Amtrak Cascades rail service, requires WSDOT to prioritize them and report annually on progress.

title: Newborn screening additions
summary: Establishes a process for adding conditions to Washington newborn screenings, emphasizing timely, efficient, and evidence-based additions.

title: Irrigation dist. elections
summary: Lets any qualified irrigation district elector vote absentee, drops the inconvenience and witness requirements, and allows boards to hold mail-only elections.

title: Fuel tax assistance grants
summary: Creates a subject-to-appropriation grant program helping rural school districts over 450 square miles cover higher fuel costs, administered by OSPI.

title: Broadband grant & loan prg.
summary: Removes incorporated businesses, partnerships, and LLCs as eligible entities for the state broadband grant and loan program.

title: Home care aide certification
summary: Lets long-term care workers delay home care aide certification past 200 days while the State Auditor audits I-1163 training requirements, and directs DOH to adopt implementing rules.

title: Manufacturing/sales tax
summary: Creates a sales and use tax exemption for manufacturing facilities and green manufacturing facilities.

title: Manufacturing facilities/tax
summary: Concerns manufacturing facilities and their tax treatment; the provided text does not specify the changes.

title: Manufacturing/B&O tax
summary: Creates a business and occupation tax exemption for manufacturing facilities and green manufacturing facilities.

title: Electronic admission tickets
summary: Requires ticket sellers to immediately deliver electronic admission tickets once payment is confirmed.

title: Associate development orgs
summary: Removes reporting requirements for associate development organizations on businesses receiving retention, expansion and recruitment services, including those outside the largest city in a county.

title: Residential landlord-tenant
summary: Creates a task force to study the Residential Landlord-Tenant Act and report recommendations to the Legislature by July 1, 2027.

title: Multifamily tax exemption
summary: Repeals location limits on counties that may designate residential targeted areas for the multifamily property tax exemption, widening which counties can offer it.

title: Mobility equipment repair
summary: Limits what original equipment manufacturers must provide for mobility equipment repair and allows attorney general enforcement under the Consumer Protection Act.

title: DDA employment services age
summary: Requires DDA to provide employment services and community inclusion access to clients starting at age 20, sets hours by needed assistance, and renames community access.

title: Employment training program
summary: Extends the B&O tax credit for businesses in the customized employment training program to July 2031 and changes the SBCTC reporting requirements.

title: Health carrier payment times
summary: Requires health carriers, public-employee plans, and managed care organizations to report claims payment timeliness data to OIC or HCA, with annual agency reports starting in 2027.

title: Electioneering/auditors
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Elections and voting
summary: Extends the prohibition on influencing voters to cover county election office buildings and their adjacent routinely used county parking lots.

title: Theft in the 3rd degree
summary: Amends Washington's third-degree theft law, but the text provided does not say how.

title: Foreclosure mediation prg.
summary: Expands the foreclosure mediation program to cover HOA and condo assessment delinquencies, adds meet-and-confer and document steps, reporting, and a Commerce resource center.

title: Performance audits/tax share
summary: Increases the share of sales tax revenue dedicated to funding performance audits.

title: Constitutional rights
summary: Addresses federal orders that the bill's title says violate the US or Washington Constitution or judicial precedent; the text gives no operative detail.

title: Drivers' licenses/blood type
summary: Allows applicants to optionally include verified blood type on driver's licenses and identicards, with a one-time fee of up to $2 and public education.

title: Utility relocation
summary: Directs WSDOT to coordinate utility owners on fish barrier removal projects and to maximize federal funding that can cover utility relocation costs.

title: Continuing care oversight
summary: Makes violations of the CCRC statutes unfair or deceptive acts under the Consumer Protection Act, exposing operators to CPA enforcement.

title: Seattle Reign FC lic. plate
summary: Creates a Seattle Reign FC special license plate and directs its proceeds to the RAVE Foundation for girls, women, and environmental and equity programs.

title: Teacher residency & apprent.
summary: Defines a teacher residency as a mentored, full-year teacher preparation model offered by schools and approved teacher preparation programs.

title: Boiler operator cert.
summary: Creates a boiler operator certification program, which would require boiler operators to hold certification.

title: Young driver safety
summary: Bill text is only a title and one line stating its aim to improve young driver safety; no specific provisions are given.

title: Mental health treatment/tax
summary: Allows local mental health and chemical dependency sales tax revenue to fund new construction of treatment facilities, not just modifications to existing ones.

title: Social services/property tax
summary: Exempts nonprofit-owned property from property tax when it is loaned or leased to government, tribes, or nonprofits providing social services, without the usual expiration or review.

title: Municipal gas utilities/CCA
summary: Changes the Climate Commitment Act compliance obligation for certain municipal gas utilities; the text does not specify how.

title: Intensive rural development
summary: Allows new commercial or industrial development, other than retail or food service, within rural LAMIRD outer boundaries when the local legislative authority finds it economically necessary.

title: Medical cannabis database
summary: Lets the Liquor and Cannabis Board use the medical cannabis database to verify certain excise tax exemptions.

title: Prevailing wage/records
summary: Adds Taft-Hartley trusts and joint labor-management committees as prevailing wage interested parties entitled to certified payroll records, limited to wage-complaint use.

title: Toll rate setting process
summary: Creates a new process for the Washington State Transportation Commission to set toll rates.

title: Municipal solid waste
summary: Delays coverage of waste-to-energy facilities used by county and city solid waste programs under the emissions program from 2027 to 2036.

title: Health care marketplace
summary: Concerns notice or oversight of material changes to the operations and governance of health care marketplace participants; the summary gives no operative detail.

title: Traffic infraction penalties
summary: Doubles penalties for using a personal electronic device while driving in school, playground, or crosswalk speed zones, with no waivers and fines going to the School Zone Safety Account.

title: Child custody determinations
summary: Establishes procedures for determining child custody; the text is too brief to show any substantive change.

title: Subscriber emails/PRA
summary: Exempts email addresses of people who subscribe to local agency updates from public records disclosure under the Public Records Act.

title: Online services/minors
topics: AI and technology; Children and families
summary: Requires operators of addictive social media feeds to estimate minor users' ages and limits how personal data collected for age estimation may be used or retained.

title: Public health clinics/tax
summary: Concerns county property tax levies that would fund public health clinic purposes.

title: Diesel vessels/state ferries
topics: Environment and energy; Government and administration; Transportation
summary: Creates a new ferry vessel procurement process, exempts Washington State Ferries from procurement statutes, and lets WSDOT postpone Jumbo Mark II conversion.

title: Self-service storage/tax
summary: Taxes self-storage space rentals as retail sales starting 2026, subject to B&O retailing and sales tax, with revenue intended for affordable housing.

title: Industrial stormwater permit
summary: Creates a presumption that entities covered by the industrial stormwater general permit are in compliance under certain circumstances.

title: Chemical abortion
summary: Bill concerning chemical abortion; the provided text does not state what it would change.

title: Bail bond agents/immigration
summary: Adds using bail recovery authority to enforce civil immigration warrants, and sharing a defendant's immigration status, to bail bond licensees' unprofessional conduct list.

title: Juvenile convictions/score
summary: Applies the exclusion of certain juvenile convictions from adult offender scores retroactively, regardless of when the underlying offense occurred.

title: Transit conduct/ferries
summary: Expands the legal definition of transit authority to include the Washington State Ferries.

title: Driver course/work zones
summary: Requires drivers under 26 to pass a free online work zone and first responder safety course before licensing, funded partly by work zone camera revenue.

title: TRS & SERS/plan 2 transfer
summary: Gives TRS Plan 3 and SERS Plan 3 members never offered a choice the option to irrevocably transfer to Plan 2 for future service.

title: Local gov. hearing examiners
summary: Requires larger nonrural counties and cities over 2,000 population to adopt hearing examiner systems for quasi-judicial permit and land use decisions.

title: Uniform debt default act
summary: Requires creditors suing to collect consumer debt to meet detailed complaint, documentation, and notice rules before obtaining a default judgment.

title: Automobile insurance
summary: Requires auto policies with physical damage coverage to include an appraisal clause and sets timelines and appraiser selection rules for resolving claim valuation disputes.

title: Local farming grant program
summary: Creates an ESD-administered grant program for farmers to support local hiring, reduce transportation pollution, and build food sovereignty and climate resilience.

title: Airpark covenants
summary: Exempts city-owned property from airpark covenants that are more restrictive than the city's zoning ordinance.

title: Dual credit programs
summary: Aims to improve student access to dual credit programs, including career and technical education dual credit.

title: Housing on college lands
summary: Lets community and technical colleges lease or transfer underused land for affordable housing, at reduced value, and exempts those leases from leasehold excise tax.

title: Transportation revenue
summary: Creates new transportation revenue sources based on motor vehicle use of public roadways.

title: Residential energy storage
summary: Requires the WSU Energy Program to run a residential battery incentive program, with large utilities required to participate and smaller ones optional.

title: Fish and wildlife commission
summary: Concerns membership of the Fish and Wildlife Commission; the summary does not say what changes.

title: Housing permitting
summary: Bars local governments from charging permit applicants for third-party peer review when in-house licensed staff have already reviewed the materials.

title: Dev. disabilities/rec checks
summary: Concerns background record checks for certain volunteers and contractors who will have access to children or people with developmental disabilities.

title: Tenant assistance program
summary: Redirects portions of document recording fees through 2032 to fund housing authority grants for tenant rental assistance payments.

title: Housing supply/GMA
summary: Requires counties to track progress on permitting new housing and lets the Governor sanction localities that fail to increase housing supply under GMA goals.

title: Updating comprehensive plans
summary: Adds housing-permit-related comprehensive plan amendments to the items that may be considered more than once a year.

title: Interstate bridge toll bonds
summary: Authorizes up to $2.5 billion in bonds, repaid from tolls, fuel taxes and state credit, to fund the Interstate Bridge Replacement project.

title: Imitation firearm labeling
summary: Defines imitation firearms, including BB devices, toy guns and replicas, and lists exemptions for collector replicas and spot marker guns.

title: Child neglect cases
summary: Seeks to improve responses and outcomes in child neglect cases; the summary gives no specific mechanism or funding.

title: National board bonuses
summary: Reduces the annual National Board Certificate bonus and the poverty-school additional bonus for certificated instructional staff to $3,000, with inflation adjustments after 2025-26.

title: Retired employees/work
summary: Extends to 2030 the allowance letting retired public pension members work up to 1,040 hours a year without losing benefits.

title: Public facilities districts
summary: Bill concerning public facilities districts; the provided text gives no details of what it changes.

title: Eviction reform
summary: Revises unlawful detainer and residential landlord-tenant rules, tightening tenant answer and hearing requirements and removing an arrest requirement for eviction over assault.

title: Housing court commissioners
summary: Allows superior courts to appoint housing court commissioners to assist with unlawful detainer (eviction) cases, with required training and impartiality standards.

title: Impaired driving
summary: Bill concerning impaired driving; the text gives no details of what it would change.

title: Law enforcement memorial
summary: Addresses which names are included on the Washington state law enforcement memorial. It is a commemorative measure with no policy effect.

title: Legislative comparison study
summary: Requires a legislative comparison study; the text gives no details on scope, responsible agency, or funding.

title: Invol. treatment counsel
summary: Assigns county and state responsibility for appointed counsel in involuntary treatment cases, shifting costs between counties, BHASOs, HCA and the Office of Public Defense.

title: EV charger property crime
summary: Until 2028, the EV charging council must address EV charger property crime through an advisory or ad hoc committee, subject to appropriation.

title: Affordable housing/exemption
summary: Lets affordable housing projects meeting the 12-year MFTE criteria use any of the four previous building and energy code standards, or current codes.

title: Impact fees
summary: Lets local governments impose a voter-approved sales tax up to 1 percent, but only after substantially cutting impact fees on development.

title: Housing opportunity zones
summary: Lets cities designate commercial sites such as malls and vacant stores as housing development opportunity zones, with project areas defined by existing parcel improvements.

title: State facility EV charging
summary: Authorizes the state to provide charging for privately owned EVs at state offices, with fees deposited into the Motor Vehicle Fund, and removes a pro-EV policy declaration.

title: Government services delivery
summary: Concerning government services delivery improvement; the text gives no specific policy changes.

title: Child care & early dev.
summary: Delays and scales back child care and ECEAP expansions, removes some eligibility, raises copayments, and makes several programs subject to appropriations.

title: Public housing task force
summary: Creates a public housing task force to study publicly owned mixed-income housing and report recommendations to the Legislature and Governor in 2026.

title: Washington state public bank
summary: Creates a Washington state-owned public bank; the text gives no details on powers, funding or rules.

title: Residential dev./commercial
summary: Creates incentives for residential development on underutilized commercial properties in exchange for public benefits.

title: Working minors
summary: Raises and sets minimum penalties for minor work violations and requires revoking minor work permits for repeat or serious-harm violations.

title: Auto. traffic safety revenue
summary: Requires half of local traffic safety camera infraction revenue to go to the State Motor Vehicle Fund, ahead of existing distribution rules.

title: Cannabis licensees/distance
topics: Criminal justice; Government and administration; Housing
summary: Bars cities, towns and counties from requiring cannabis retail stores to sit more than 250 feet from other cannabis retailers.

title: Art purchase program
summary: Establishes a state program to let people purchase art, according to a short title and one-line summary.

title: GA building/reentry center
summary: Establishes a colocated community facility and work release center in the General Administration building on the Capitol campus.

title: Dependency/attorney appt.
summary: Phases in statewide appointment of attorneys in dependency cases, county by county, from 2022 through 2032.

title: 988 line tax
summary: Directs 988 crisis line tax revenue to fund hotlines first and allows contracting for LGBTQ youth crisis services if federal support ends.

title: Law enf. aviation support
summary: Creates a Military Department grant program funding local sheriff and police helicopter aviation support units, contingent on specific funding by June 30, 2026.

title: Ambulance transport fund
summary: Removes the expiration date for the ambulance transport fund, so the fund would continue without a sunset.

title: Psychiatric pharmacists
summary: Concerns psychiatric pharmacists; the text provides no detail on what would change.

title: Passive investment vehicles
summary: Clarifies how the business and occupation tax applies to investment income of passive investment vehicles managed by certain B&O-taxed persons.

title: Federal employee hiring pref
summary: Gives certain displaced federal employees hiring preference for Washington state government jobs.

title: Working families' tax credit
summary: Extends Working Families' Tax Credit eligibility to workers 18 or older regardless of qualifying children, effective January 2026, contingent on budget funding.

title: Transition to kindergarten
summary: Limits Transition to Kindergarten program funding, starting with the 2025-26 school year, to the amount in the omnibus appropriations act.

title: Primary residence/tax
summary: Creates a primary residence property tax exemption equal to the greater of $100,000 or 60% of county median home value.

title: WFTC increase/tenants
summary: Adds an up-to-$300 Working Families Tax Credit refund for renters with 183+ days of primary residence leases, contingent on a constitutional amendment and budget funding.

title: Student enrollment
summary: Reduces state funding enrollment counts for school districts whose Alternative Learning Experience enrollment exceeds 15 percent of total or FTE enrollment.

title: Transportation procurement
summary: Creates a public-private partnership framework for transportation projects and sets WSDOT procurement options for large highway projects, plus a study of alliance contracting.

title: Investment income/B&O tax
summary: Clarifies the scope of the business and occupation tax deduction for investment income.

title: Public safety/local tax
topics: Government and administration; Housing; Taxes and budget
summary: Lets counties and cities impose a 0.3% public safety sales tax without voter approval through 2027, with revenue usable for behavioral health, diversion, and related local programs.

title: American dream homes
summary: Aims to promote housing affordability by incentivizing construction of 'American dream homes'; the text gives no mechanism or funding details.

title: Payment card processing/tax
summary: Establishes a 3% B&O tax rate on payment card processing, with a permanent deduction for interchange fees, network fees, and certain retained processor fees.

title: Maple syrup processing
summary: Addresses maple syrup processing operations, but the text gives no specifics on what would change.

title: African diaspora heritage
summary: Establishes an African diaspora heritage week, a commemorative designation with no policy effect.

title: Student transport. vehicles
summary: Reduces state reimbursements to school districts that receive grants or rebates to replace the same student transportation vehicle; requires reporting.

title: FDA labeling
summary: Conforms state labeling rules to Food and Drug Administration labeling standards, according to a short title with no detailed text.

title: Impaired driving
summary: Concerns impaired driving, but the text gives no specifics on what it would change.

title: Vaccination status
summary: Prohibits using a person's vaccination status in certain administrative and legal proceedings.

title: Agency demographic data
summary: Requires state agencies to collect voluntary demographic data under OMB SPD 15 standards by 2030, with public reporting and OFM exemptions and variances.

title: Higher education costs
summary: Changes Washington College Grant awards: raises income eligibility, alters private and apprenticeship maximums, eliminates for-profit awards, and adds a six-year limit on College Bound funds.

title: Liquor license fees
summary: Raises state fees for almost all liquor licenses, permits, and endorsements.

title: Wildfire BSA appropriations
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Appropriates $77.687 million from the BSA to DNR to cover 2024 fire season suppression costs, without changing the balanced budget requirement.

title: Budget savings
summary: Seeks budget savings by changing certain policies that have not yet taken effect; details are not in the text provided.

title: State financial aid/credits
summary: Restores a cap limiting state financial aid to 125 percent of the credits needed to graduate.

title: CTC employee COLAs
summary: Changes the cost-of-living index used for annual raises for community and technical college employees from Seattle-area CPI to IPD.

title: Higher education funding
summary: Increases state funding to expand access to higher education.

title: State employee compensation
summary: Temporary compensation reductions for state government employees during the 2025-2027 fiscal biennium.

title: Public employee health plans
summary: Concerns employer contributions and incentives for public and school employee health benefit plans; the summary gives no specifics on the changes.

title: Tax preferences
summary: Repeals certain tax preferences; the summary does not identify which preferences or their dollar effect.

title: Sales and use tax rate
summary: Sets Washington's state sales and use tax rate at 6 percent beginning January 1, 2027.

title: Payroll expense tax
summary: Creates a 5% employer payroll expense tax on wages above the Social Security wage base, exempts employers under $7 million in wages, and credits eligible city payroll taxes.

title: Intangible assets tax
summary: Imposes a new state tax of $5 per $1,000 on Washington residents' intangible assets, such as publicly traded stocks, bonds, ETFs and mutual funds.

title: Property tax
summary: Expands property tax exemptions and income thresholds for qualifying retirees and consolidates the state levy into a single revenue-neutral rate.

title: Youth behavioral health acc.
summary: Creates a youth behavioral health account funded by a new business and occupation tax on social media platforms.

title: Transportation funding bonds
summary: Authorizes up to $7 billion in general obligation bonds for highway projects and raises State Route 520 bond authorization by $500 million.

title: Transportation resources
summary: Raises state fuel taxes, electric and hybrid vehicle fees, title and registration fees, and rental car and peer-to-peer sharing taxes, with revenue going to Move Ahead WA accounts.

title: Transportation funds
summary: Redirects sales tax revenue and shifts transportation and general fund money through transfers, sweeps, and deferral changes for 2025-2029.

title: Tobacco & nicotine products
summary: Regulates tobacco and nicotine products; the summary gives no specific rules, so the direction of change is unknown.

title: Fish habitat restoration
topics: Environment and energy; Taxes and budget
summary: Creates a 2.01053% light and power utility tax and authorizes up to $5 billion in bonds to fund salmon and steelhead habitat restoration under the federal injunction.

title: Yakima Valley School
summary: Concerns the Yakima Valley School, a state facility for people with developmental disabilities; the text gives no specific changes.

title: Revenue voluntary disclosure
summary: Creates a voluntary disclosure program within the Department of Revenue for taxpayers.

title: Health plan incentives
summary: Eliminates the SmartHealth wellness incentive program for state employee health plans (PEBB and SEBB) starting January 2028, while honoring incentives already earned through 2027.

title: Health carrier surpluses
summary: Requires OIC to find nonprofit health carriers with excessive surplus and collect 10 percent of the excess for the Cascade Care Savings Program.

title: Cost savings
summary: Repeals certain annual reports and an advisory committee to generate cost savings for the state.

title: Operating budget
summary: Sets Washington's 2025-2027 operating budget appropriations and adjusts 2023-2025 supplemental operating appropriations.

title: Zero-emission vehicle prg.
summary: Imposes a new excise tax on banking, pooling and selling surplus zero-emission vehicle credits, with revenue to the General Fund and EV incentive accounts.

title: K-12 education funding
summary: Replaces the fixed 101% property tax growth limit with inflation plus population growth, capped at 103%, and raises K-12 enrichment levy and state LEA thresholds.

title: Tax rates/cap. gains, estate
summary: Raises Washington capital gains tax rates to 7% and 9.9% above $1 million, and raises estate tax rates while increasing the exclusion to $3 million.

title: Excise taxes
topics: Consumer protection and business; Taxes and budget
summary: Taxes certain nicotine products as other tobacco products, adds a cigarette tax, and requires a one-time 2026 sales tax prepayment from large retailers.

title: Business and occupation tax
summary: Adds a 0.5% B&O surcharge on large taxpayers, raises several existing B&O surcharge rates and the Advanced Computing cap, and modifies the investment income deduction.

title: Sale of juice grapes
summary: Adds juice grapes to the state Agricultural Marketing and Fair Practices Act and sets timelines for grape sale negotiations around harvest.

title: Election security
summary: Creates the State Elections Confidence Using Rigorous Examination Act; the text provided does not describe its specific provisions.

title: DOC transfers/immigration
summary: Facilitates transfers of certain people in Department of Corrections custody, apparently in connection with immigration; the summary gives no detail.

title: Paid protestor services/tax
summary: Subjects paid protestor services to state retail sales and use taxes by classifying them as temporary staffing services.

title: Freight rail dependent use
summary: Repeals local authority to allow freight rail dependent uses on resource lands near short line railroads and in rural lands.

title: Advanced nuclear energy
summary: Commerce must develop and publish a nuclear power strategic framework by December 2026, contingent on outside funding covering all costs.

title: Missing persons alert system
summary: Concerns a missing persons alert system, but the text gives no details on what it would change.

title: Patient advocates
summary: Concerns patient advocates, but the text gives no details on what the bill would change.

title: Fifth-wheel travel trailers
summary: Allows fifth-wheel travel trailers up to 46 feet overall on public highways and defines how that length is measured.

title: Leadership board/gifts
topics: Children and families; Government and administration
summary: Authorizes the Washington State Leadership Board to accept private gifts and grants for youth leadership programs, requires reporting to OFM, and removes expired sports mentoring references.

title: Postsecondary/med. abortion
summary: Concerns access to medication abortion at public postsecondary educational institutions; the summary does not state the specific change.

title: Veterans/discharge def.
summary: Allows veterans' civil service preference to be claimed using a predischarge certification, with later proof of discharge required and agency verification rules.

title: College scholarships/private
summary: Changes the maximum Washington College Grant and College Bound Scholarship award amounts for students at four-year not-for-profit institutions.

title: Attorney general inv. ID
summary: Authorizes the attorney general's office to issue confidential identification to its investigators.

title: Political affil./hate crimes
summary: Clarifies that hate crime laws cover crimes motivated by the victim's political affiliation.

title: Uniform mortgage mod. act
summary: Establishes uniform legal rules so mortgage modifications keep the original lien and priority, without creating a novation, and defines covered modifications.

title: Motor vehicle arb. fee
summary: Raises the motor vehicle arbitration fee charged on new vehicle sales or leases from $3 to $6.

title: Pets in unattended vehicles
summary: Makes it lawful to leave a vehicle's engine running while unattended for up to 30 minutes to keep a pet comfortable.

title: Retirement funds/expenses
summary: Ends a temporary allowance for trust fund interest to cover 2025-27 loss-prevention costs and permanently lets that interest pay for fraud-prevention work.

title: Lump sum retirement payments
summary: Raises the monthly minimum benefit threshold for Plan 2 retirees to elect a lump-sum payment from $50 to $250, adjusted annually at DRS discretion.

title: Superior court judge/Skagit
summary: Adds one superior court judge position in Skagit County.

title: Guardianship, etc.
summary: Revises adult guardianship and conservatorship procedures, requiring appointed attorneys for objecting respondents at public expense and expanding supported decision-making provisions.

title: Board of natural resources
summary: Requires the Governor to appoint two tribal representatives to the Board of Natural Resources, selected with input from federally recognized tribes.

title: County ferry districts
summary: Lets county ferry districts operate ferries beyond passenger-only service, such as auto ferries.

title: Campaign finance schedule
summary: Sets a new schedule for campaign finance filings: January participation statements, monthly expenditure reports, and extra pre-election reports in July, September, and October.

title: Financial aid applications
summary: Requires the high school and beyond plan platform to import financial aid application data and inform students about the Washington Opportunity Scholarship.

title: Campaign memorabilia
summary: Exempts display of memorabilia from past, inactive campaigns in legislative offices from the ban on using public resources for campaigns.

title: Signature gatherers
topics: Civil rights and liberties; Criminal justice
summary: Creates penalties for harassing initiative and referendum signature gatherers and adds protections for them.

title: Storage space rentals
summary: Allows electronic self-storage rental agreements and sets a uniform termination process, including a 15-day notice period before owners may dispose of remaining property.

title: Health carrier payments
summary: Requires health insurance carriers to request any additional information needed to process a claim within 21 days.

title: Sex offender placements
summary: Adds community notification and protections tied to less restrictive alternative placements for sex offenders living in the community.

title: Workers' comp. medical care
summary: Lets injured workers choose providers, allows out-of-network treatment when no network provider is available, and bars employers from coercing provider choice.

title: School district impact fees
summary: Concerns school district impact fees; the text gives no details on what the bill changes.

title: Financial education
summary: Requires high schools to provide financial education and makes it a graduation requirement starting with the class of 2033.

title: Signature gathering
summary: Establishes protections for citizens who take part in the initiative and referendum process, such as signature gathering.

title: Sea lion predation donations
summary: Adds a donation option at vessel registration that directs funds to the sea lion predation control account to help preserve salmon.

title: Immigrant workers
summary: Requires employers to notify workers and representatives of federal I-9 inspections and results, limits verification beyond federal law, and bars voluntary consent to federal record access.

title: Public official notification
summary: Creates a voluntary statewide system to alert enrolled public officials when a targeted threat is confirmed, administered by the military department.

title: Sexually violent predators
summary: Modifies the procedures for releasing sexually violent predators to less restrictive alternative placements.

title: Law enf. face coverings
summary: Bans peace and federal officers from wearing face coverings while interacting with the public, with exceptions, and lets detained people sue masked officers.

title: Lubricant emissions
summary: Exempts emissions associated with lubricants from coverage under Washington's cap-and-invest program.
